source: Structure from vedabase.io (BBT), 27 Sep 2026; notes in our own words

children.note: The Gita taught in seven classes by Sri Gauranga Das (Gita Week playlist), mapped verse by verse with links to the videos.
Krishna’s teaching to Arjuna: 18 chapters, 700 verses, with Srila Prabhupada’s purports. Open the map for chapter-by-chapter key verses.
The ripened fruit of the Vedas: 12 cantos, 335 chapters, 18,000 verses on the Lord, His devotees and the cosmos, with Srila Prabhupada’s purports.
The life and teachings of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu, by Krishnadasa Kaviraja Gosvami: Adi, Madhya and Antya lila, 66 chapters, with purports.
Srila Prabhupada’s three main works, which he called the foundation of his mission.

children.topic: Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead
children.note: A summary study of the Tenth Canto: Krishna’s pastimes from His birth in Mathura to His return to Dvaraka, told as a story.
A summary of Sri Caitanya’s teachings to Rupa, Sanatana, Ramananda Raya, Sarvabhauma and Prakasananda, drawn from Caitanya-caritamrta.
Forty-eight texts on the autumn season from the Tenth Canto, each a picture of the world and a lesson, with paintings.
Books that tell the pastimes and teachings in story form.
A summary study of Rupa Gosvami’s Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu: what devotional service is, its stages, and the five kinds of loving relationship.
Rupa Gosvami’s Upadesamrta: eleven verses of practical instruction for a devotee, from controlling the tongue to Radha-kunda.
Eighteen mantras of the Isa Upanisad: everything belongs to the Lord, and the difference between knowledge and ignorance.

children.topic: Bhakti: The Art of Eternal Love
children.note: A short introduction to bhakti drawn from The Nectar of Devotion: what it is, its benefits, and the six features of pure devotion.
The Hare Krishna mantra explained, with conversations including George Harrison and John Lennon, and techniques for chanting.
The science of bhakti: what to do, and what to avoid.
Interviews, lectures, essays and letters: reincarnation, the spiritual master, yoga, karma, Krishna and Christ, and the perfection of life.
A short book on the soul, death, and how to reach the spiritual sky beyond the universe.
What the Gita says about yoga: rejected by Arjuna, then defined as devotion — the highest yogi thinks of Krishna within.
Lectures on the sixth and eighth chapters of the Gita: yoga as action, mastering the mind, meditation, and remembering Krishna at death.
Lectures on the ninth chapter of the Gita: the most confidential knowledge, open to everyone.
Five short chapters: the highway to happiness, chanting, seeing Krishna everywhere, the roads of the foolish and the wise.
A conversation in Mayapur between Srila Prabhupada and a young Peace Corps worker, Bob Cohen, covering the basics of Krishna consciousness.
Talks and interviews: superconsciousness, the pleasure principle, reincarnation, the spiritual master, and material problems with spiritual solutions.
Srila Prabhupada answers a psychology questionnaire on religion, progress, the caste system, and the purpose of society.
The story of Ajamila from the Sixth Canto: death, the Yamadutas and Visnudutas, and the power of the holy name.
Short books for a newcomer, mostly from lectures and conversations.
Queen Kunti’s prayers to Krishna from the First Canto, with Srila Prabhupada’s commentary: the original person, dangers as blessings, unalloyed devotion.
Lord Kapila teaches His mother Devahuti (Third Canto): the guru, the Lord’s activities, meditation, and devotional service as the final perfection.
Prayers and teachings from the Bhagavatam with Srila Prabhupada’s commentary.

children.topic: Meditate on Krishna, cause of all causes
children.note: Vyasa opens by bowing to Krishna as the self-sufficient origin of creation who first gave Vedic knowledge to Brahma. (SB 1.1 1)
This scripture throws out materially motivated dharma and gives the highest truth, enough on its own to bring one to God. (SB 1.1 2)

children.topic: Ripe fruit of the Vedic tree
children.note: The sages are invited to taste the Bhagavatam, sweetened further by passing through the lips of Sukadeva. (SB 1.1 3)
The sages describe the people of this age as short-lived, lazy, misguided and always agitated, so they need a simple essence. (SB 1.1 10)

children.topic: Even unconscious chanting frees the soul
children.note: Chanting Krishna's name, even by accident, releases one from the tangle of birth and death; fear itself fears that name. (SB 1.1 14)

children.topic: Where has dharma gone after Krishna left?
children.note: The sages' final question: now that Krishna has returned to His abode, who shelters religious principles? (SB 1.1 23)

The Bhagavatam opens with Vyasa's invocation of Krishna as the source of everything. At Naimisaranya, Saunaka and the sages ask Suta Gosvami to distill the essence of all scripture for the short-lived, troubled people of Kali-yuga.

children.topic: Real dharma is unmotivated, uninterrupted devotion
children.note: The highest occupation for everyone is loving service to God that asks nothing in return and never stops; only this satisfies the self. (SB 1.2 6)

children.topic: Duty without taste for Krishna is useless
children.note: Any work done according to one's position is wasted labor if it does not awaken attraction for hearing about the Lord. (SB 1.2 8)

children.topic: Human life is for inquiring about truth
children.note: Desires should not aim at sense pleasure; one should want only enough health to pursue inquiry into the Absolute. (SB 1.2 10)
Those who know the Absolute call the same nondual reality by three names, according to how deeply it is realized. (SB 1.2 11)

children.topic: Krishna in the heart cleans away desires
children.note: When one develops the urge to hear about Him, the Lord within clears worldly cravings out of the heart. (SB 1.2 17)

children.topic: Regular Bhagavatam classes fix loving service
children.note: Attending Bhagavatam classes and serving pure devotees nearly destroys all that troubles the heart and makes devotion permanent. (SB 1.2 18)

Suta Gosvami praises Sukadeva and answers the sages: the true dharma of humanity is unmotivated, uninterrupted devotion to Krishna. Hearing about Him cleans the heart, removes lust and ignorance, and reveals Him as Brahman, Paramatma and Bhagavan.

children.topic: 3 · Kṛṣṇa Is the Source of All Incarnations

children.note: The second purusa form is the indestructible source from which demigods, humans and all other beings emerge. (SB 1.3 5)
The Lord's avatars are beyond counting, compared to rivulets pouring from an inexhaustible lake. (SB 1.3 26)
The famous verdict: all listed avatars are parts or parts of parts, but Krishna Himself is the source who descends to protect the faithful. (SB 1.3 28)

children.topic: Only devotees know the creator fully
children.note: Those who serve Krishna's feet with unreserved, favorable, constant devotion can understand His full glory and power. (SB 1.3 38)

children.topic: Bhagavatam is God in book form
children.note: This scripture, compiled by Vyasa, is God appearing as a book, meant for everyone's ultimate good. (SB 1.3 40)

children.topic: A sun rising after Krishna's departure
children.note: When Krishna left with religion and knowledge, this Purana rose like the sun to give sight to those blinded by Kali-yuga. (SB 1.3 43)

Suta lists the purusa incarnations and twenty-two avatars from the Kumaras to Buddha and Kalki, then declares Krishna the original Godhead of whom all others are portions. He ends by tracing how Vyasa gave the Bhagavatam to Sukadeva and Pariksit.

children.topic: Naked bathers hid from Vyasa, not Suka
children.note: The maidens covered themselves before Vyasa but not before his son, because Sukadeva saw no difference between male and female. (SB 1.4 5)

children.topic: Suka stays only as long as milking
children.note: Sukadeva would pause at a householder's door just long enough to milk a cow, purely to sanctify the home. (SB 1.4 8)

children.topic: Vyasa foresees Kali's faithless, short-lived people
children.note: Through his vision Vyasa saw people would lose goodness, patience and lifespan, and so he worked for everyone's welfare. (SB 1.4 17-18)

children.topic: Mahabharata written for women and workers
children.note: Out of compassion Vyasa composed the Mahabharata so that those outside Vedic study could also reach life's goal. (SB 1.4 25)
Though fully equipped with Vedic knowledge and vast works, Vyasa senses something essential is missing. (SB 1.4 30)
Vyasa suspects his dissatisfaction comes from not clearly presenting bhakti, which is dear to both the Lord and perfected souls. (SB 1.4 31)

Saunaka asks about Sukadeva and Pariksit. Suta explains how Vyasa saw the coming degradation of Kali, divided the Vedas, wrote the Mahabharata for the less qualified, yet still felt empty inside. Narada then arrives at his hermitage on the Sarasvati.

children.topic: 5 · Nārada’s Instructions on Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam for Vyāsadeva
You have not described the Lord's glories
children.note: Narada tells Vyasa plainly that philosophy which does not please the Lord's senses is worthless, whatever its scope. (SB 1.5 8)

children.topic: Godless words are a pilgrimage for crows
children.note: Literature that ignores the Lord's glories is compared to a crow's gathering place; swanlike souls find no joy there. (SB 1.5 10)

children.topic: Even imperfect verses about Krishna cause revolution
children.note: Writing filled with the Lord's names and pastimes reforms a misguided civilization and is accepted by honest people even if poorly composed. (SB 1.5 11)

children.topic: Even liberation looks poor without God
children.note: Self-knowledge free of matter still lacks beauty if it has no place for the infallible Lord, let alone fruitive work. (SB 1.5 12)

children.topic: A fallen devotee never truly loses
children.note: One who leaves worldly duty for devotion and slips while immature still gains, while the dutiful nondevotee gains nothing. (SB 1.5 17)

children.topic: Narada purified by sages' food remnants
children.note: Taking the sages' leftovers once with permission cleared Narada's sins and made the transcendentalist's nature attractive to him. (SB 1.5 25)

Narada diagnoses Vyasa's despondency: he has not broadcast Krishna's glories, and words without the Lord are a crows' pilgrimage. Narada then tells how, as a maidservant's son, he served Vedantist sages and gained taste for hearing about Krishna.
Meditating on the Lord's feet with a mind melted by love, Narada wept and Krishna at once appeared within his heart. (SB 1.6 16)

children.topic: You will not see Me again this life
children.note: The Lord tells Narada that those not yet fully free of material taint can hardly see Him, so this single vision must suffice. (SB 1.6 21)

children.topic: One glimpse to sharpen your longing
children.note: The single vision was given to increase Narada's hankering, because greater longing for God frees one from other desires. (SB 1.6 22)

children.topic: Even a few days' service fixes intelligence
children.note: Brief service to the Absolute gives firm intelligence and leads to becoming the Lord's associate after leaving this world. (SB 1.6 23)

children.topic: Narada roams the earth chanting, satisfied
children.note: Ignoring worldly formalities, Narada travels everywhere chanting the Lord's names and fame, humble and free of envy. (SB 1.6 26)

children.topic: Chanting is the boat across nescience
children.note: Narada testifies that constant chanting of the Lord's activities carries anxious, sense-driven people across the ocean of ignorance. (SB 1.6 34)

Narada continues his life story: after his mother dies of snakebite, he wanders north, meditates under a banyan tree and briefly sees Krishna in his heart. A voice says he will not see the Lord again that life; he dies chanting and is reborn as Brahma's son.

children.topic: Just hearing this book sprouts love
children.note: Simply listening to the Bhagavatam awakens devotion to Krishna and extinguishes lamentation, illusion and fear. (SB 1.7 7)

children.topic: Even liberated souls are attracted to Krishna
children.note: The atmarama verse: self-satisfied sages still crave to serve the Lord because His qualities attract everyone. (SB 1.7 10)
Krishna tells Arjuna that Asvatthama, fearing death, has fired a weapon he cannot withdraw. (SB 1.7 27)

children.topic: Whom a religious warrior never kills
children.note: Krishna lists those a dharmic fighter spares: the careless, drunk, mad, sleeping, afraid, chariotless, women, children and surrendered. (SB 1.7 36)
A brahmana's kin must not be killed, yet an aggressor must; Arjuna must satisfy Draupadi, Bhima and Krishna at once. (SB 1.7 53-54)

children.topic: Shaving, not killing, for a fallen brahmana
children.note: The prescribed punishment for a brahmana's unworthy relative is to cut his hair, take his wealth and expel him, never execution. (SB 1.7 57)

Vyasa compiles the Bhagavatam and teaches it to Sukadeva. Suta then narrates how Asvatthama beheads Draupadi's sleeping sons, fires a brahmastra at Arjuna, is captured, and, after Draupadi pleads for mercy, is punished by having his hair and jewel cut off.

children.topic: 8 · Prayers by Queen Kuntī and Parīkṣit Saved
Krishna shields the embryo of Uttara
children.note: Residing in every heart as Paramatma, the Lord covers Uttara's womb with His own energy to save the Kuru line. (SB 1.8 14)

children.topic: God hidden like an actor in costume
children.note: Kunti says the Lord is veiled by deluding energy, unrecognized by the foolish just as an actor in disguise goes unnoticed. (SB 1.8 19)

children.topic: Let calamities come again and again
children.note: Kunti welcomes repeated dangers because each one brought Krishna's presence, which ends the cycle of birth and death. (SB 1.8 25)

children.topic: Only the materially exhausted approach You
children.note: Good birth, wealth, learning and beauty make people unable to call on God sincerely; the Lord is easy for the humble. (SB 1.8 26)

children.topic: Let my mind flow like the Ganges
children.note: Kunti prays that her attraction be drawn to Krishna alone, unbroken, as the Ganges runs to the sea. (SB 1.8 42)

children.topic: Cannot wash blood with animal sacrifice
children.note: Yudhisthira argues that killing men cannot be atoned by killing animals, as mud cannot filter muddy water. (SB 1.8 52)

As Krishna prepares to leave for Dvaraka, He saves Uttara's unborn child from Asvatthama's brahmastra. Queen Kunti offers her famous prayers, welcoming calamities that bring Krishna near. Yudhisthira, guilt-ridden over the war's killing, cannot be consoled.

children.topic: 9 · The Passing Away of Bhīṣmadeva in the Presence of Lord Kṛṣṇa
All this is inevitable time's doing
children.note: Bhisma explains the Pandavas' sufferings as the work of time, which carries everyone along as wind moves clouds. (SB 1.9 14)

children.topic: No one knows the Lord's plan
children.note: Even great philosophers who inquire exhaustively remain bewildered about what Krishna intends. (SB 1.9 16)

children.topic: Equal to all, yet He came to me
children.note: Though Krishna is impartial, He graciously stands before Bhisma at death because Bhisma is His unflinching servant. (SB 1.9 22)

children.topic: Bhisma invests his whole mind in Krishna
children.note: Bhisma withdraws thinking, feeling and willing from all duties and places them in the self-satisfied Lord who descends for play. (SB 1.9 32)

children.topic: Krishna breaks His vow to keep Bhisma's
children.note: Bhisma cherishes how Krishna leapt from the chariot with a wheel, charging him like a lion, to honor Bhisma's promise. (SB 1.9 37)

children.topic: One sun, seen differently by all
children.note: Bhisma meditates on the one Lord in every heart, understanding that different perceptions do not divide Him. (SB 1.9 42)

Yudhisthira visits Bhisma dying on his bed of arrows. Bhisma teaches him about time and the Lord's plan, instructs him on dharma, then fixes his mind on Krishna standing before him, recalling Him on the battlefield, and leaves his body at the solstice.

children.topic: 10 · Departure of Lord Kṛṣṇa for Dvārakā
Clouds rain and cows give freely
children.note: In Yudhisthira's kingdom rain fell as needed, the earth produced abundantly and cows wet the pastures with milk. (SB 1.10 4)

children.topic: How could they bear His separation?
children.note: Those who once hear Krishna's glories cannot stop; how much harder for the Pandavas, who lived, ate and slept beside Him. (SB 1.10 11-12)

children.topic: Rooftop ladies' talk beats Vedic hymns
children.note: The women of Hastinapura, absorbed in Krishna's qualities, spoke of Him in words more attractive than Vedic chants. (SB 1.10 20)

children.topic: Only pure devotees see His form
children.note: The ladies say Krishna's transcendental form is seen by devotees cleansed through strict service and self-control, the sole purifying path. (SB 1.10 23)

children.topic: He descends when rulers become animals
children.note: Whenever kings live like beasts, the Lord manifests His power and mercy in various forms across the ages. (SB 1.10 25)

children.topic: Krishna stops each evening for rites
children.note: Even on His journey, welcomed everywhere, the Lord halted at sunset to perform His regular evening duties. (SB 1.10 36)

Under Yudhisthira's reign nature gives abundantly. After some months Krishna departs Hastinapura; the Pandavas nearly faint with separation. The ladies on the rooftops glorify Him as the original Godhead as He travels through many provinces to Dvaraka.

children.topic: You are our mother, father and guru
children.note: The Dvaraka citizens address Krishna as their mother, well-wisher, father, spiritual master and deity, asking for continued mercy. (SB 1.11 7)

children.topic: Every moment apart is like millions of years
children.note: The citizens say that when Krishna is away their eyes become useless, as if the sun had vanished. (SB 1.11 9)

children.topic: He greets even the lowest with respect
children.note: Krishna bows, embraces, shakes hands, smiles and blesses everyone who comes to receive Him, regardless of rank. (SB 1.11 22)

children.topic: His feet: refuge of pure devotees
children.note: The Lord's chest houses Laksmi, His face feeds the eyes, His arms shelter demigods, His feet shelter those who speak only of Him. (SB 1.11 26)
Though constantly beside Him, the queens find Krishna's feet ever fresh; even restless Laksmi cannot leave them. (SB 1.11 33)

children.topic: Untouched by matter, like His devotees
children.note: The Lord's divinity is that material qualities never affect Him, and those sheltered in Him share that freedom. (SB 1.11 38)

Krishna blows His conch as He nears Dvaraka; the citizens rush out saying His absence feels like ages. The decorated city welcomes Him, His mothers embrace Him, and His sixteen thousand queens shed tears. Suta explains the Lord is never touched by matter.

children.topic: Heavenly opulence could not satisfy Yudhisthira
children.note: Though even the demigods envied his wealth, Yudhisthira was content only in serving the Lord. (SB 1.12 6)

children.topic: Thumb-sized Lord seen in the womb
children.note: The unborn child sees a blackish, four-armed Lord in yellow dress and golden helmet, whirling a club to burn away the weapon. (SB 1.12 8)

children.topic: He will be famed as Visnu-protected
children.note: The brahmanas declare the child will be known as saved by the Lord and grow into a top-class devotee. (SB 1.12 17)
They foretell that news of death by a brahmana's curse will break his attachments and turn him to surrender. (SB 1.12 27)
By questioning Sukadeva about the self, Pariksit will renounce everything and attain a fearless life. (SB 1.12 28)
He is called Pariksit because he will search every person for the being he saw before birth, constantly contemplating Him. (SB 1.12 30)

Pariksit in Uttara's womb sees a thumb-sized four-armed Lord dispelling the brahmastra's heat. At his birth the brahmanas predict he will rival Rama and Arjuna, be cursed by a brahmana's son and learn from Sukadeva. Yudhisthira performs three horse sacrifices.

children.topic: Devotees turn any place into pilgrimage
children.note: Yudhisthira tells Vidura that saints carrying the Lord in their hearts sanctify wherever they go. (SB 1.13 10)

children.topic: Time creeps up on the family-attached
children.note: Eternal time silently overcomes those too absorbed in household affairs to notice its approach. (SB 1.13 17)

children.topic: Living like a dog on Bhima's leftovers
children.note: Vidura shocks Dhrtarastra by pointing out he clings to life on the charity of those he once tried to kill. (SB 1.13 23)

children.topic: First-class man leaves home for God
children.note: Vidura defines the best person as one who recognizes the misery of this world and leaves home depending on the Lord within. (SB 1.13 27)

children.topic: The Lord plays with us like toys
children.note: Narada explains that the supreme will brings people together and separates them like a player with his pieces. (SB 1.13 43)
Narada states the harsh law of nature: the weak sustain the strong, so no one can really protect anyone. (SB 1.13 47)

Vidura returns from pilgrimage and bluntly tells blind old Dhrtarastra to leave home before death arrives. Dhrtarastra and Gandhari slip away at night. When Yudhisthira laments, Narada explains the Lord's control over all and foretells Dhrtarastra's yogic end.
Yudhisthira notices seasons disrupted and people becoming greedy, angry, deceitful and dishonest in their livelihoods. (SB 1.14 3)

children.topic: Cheating even among friends and family
children.note: Every dealing becomes polluted with fraud and strain, even between spouses, parents, children and brothers. (SB 1.14 4)

children.topic: All our fortune came from Krishna's mercy
children.note: Yudhisthira credits kingdom, wives, victories and future destinations entirely to the Lord's causeless grace. (SB 1.14 9)
Yudhisthira reads the omens as signs that the earth will no longer be marked by Krishna's lotus feet. (SB 1.14 21)

children.topic: Krishna and Balarama protect the Yadus
children.note: The two Lords remain among the Yadus for the universe's welfare, and their kinsmen enjoy life as in the spiritual sky. (SB 1.14 35-36)

children.topic: Have you lost your dearest friend?
children.note: After many questions, Yudhisthira concludes that only losing Krishna could explain Arjuna's dejection. (SB 1.14 44)

Arjuna leaves for Dvaraka and is gone seven months. Yudhisthira sees terrifying omens in nature and society and fears Krishna has departed. When Arjuna returns pale and weeping, Yudhisthira asks after every Yadu relative before naming his real fear.

children.topic: Krishna, my intimate friend, has left me
children.note: Arjuna tells the King that the Lord who treated him as a friend is gone, and with Him all his wondrous power. (SB 1.15 5)

children.topic: Enemies spared me by His mercy
children.note: Arjuna recalls how foes never struck him when he left the chariot, and regrets treating the worshipable Lord as a driver. (SB 1.15 17)
Arjuna's bow, arrows and chariot are now like ghee poured on ashes or seeds sown in barren ground. (SB 1.15 21)

children.topic: The Gita relieves the burning heart
children.note: Arjuna turns to Govinda's instructions because they soothe the heart in every circumstance of time and place. (SB 1.15 27)

children.topic: Kali arrives the day Krishna departs
children.note: From the moment the Lord left in His own form, the age of Kali became fully manifest for the unwise. (SB 1.15 36)

children.topic: Pandavas reach Goloka in their own bodies
children.note: By constant remembrance the Pandavas attained Krishna's abode, closed to the materially absorbed, without giving up their bodies. (SB 1.15 47-48)

Arjuna recalls every victory Krishna gave him and says without Him his bow and chariot are useless. He reports the Yadus destroyed and Krishna gone, then finds peace in the Gita. Yudhisthira enthrones Pariksit and the Pandavas leave for the spiritual world.

children.topic: 16 · How Parīkṣit Received the Age of Kali
Devotees lick honey from His feet
children.note: Saunaka asks only for topics connected to Krishna, since anything else wastes a precious life. (SB 1.16 6)

children.topic: No death while Yamaraja is here
children.note: With the lord of death invited to the assembly, everyone should seize the chance to hear the deathless nectar of the Lord's pastimes. (SB 1.16 8)

children.topic: Nights in sleep, days in vain
children.note: Lazy, short-lived people squander their nights sleeping and their days on work that leads nowhere. (SB 1.16 9)

children.topic: Krishna served the Pandavas as a servant
children.note: Hearing how the Lord acted as driver, messenger and watchman for his family, Pariksit is overwhelmed with devotion. (SB 1.16 16)
The bull Dharma has lost three legs and wonders whether Earth grieves for him, for the abandoned sacrifices, or for famine. (SB 1.16 20)
Earth lists truthfulness, cleanliness, mercy, self-control, tolerance and many more virtues that reside fully in Krishna. (SB 1.16 26-30)

Pariksit rules well and, while touring, catches a sudra dressed as a king beating a cow and bull. Suta relates how Dharma, the one-legged bull, asks mother Earth why she grieves; she lists the Lord's qualities and mourns His departure from her surface.

children.topic: A king's first duty: relieve suffering
children.note: Pariksit says a ruler's fame, life and next birth vanish if the helpless are terrorized, so he must punish the violent. (SB 1.17 10-11)

children.topic: Philosophers argue about who causes distress
children.note: Dharma notes various thinkers blame the self, higher powers, karma or nature, so the culprit is hard to name. (SB 1.17 19)

children.topic: Four legs: austerity, cleanliness, mercy, truth
children.note: Pariksit identifies Dharma's legs and says three were broken by arrogance, sexual craving and drunkenness. (SB 1.17 24)

children.topic: Truth alone remains, and Kali attacks it
children.note: Only the leg of truthfulness still stands, and deceitful Kali is working to destroy even that. (SB 1.17 25)

children.topic: Kali's four homes: gambling, drink, sex, slaughter
children.note: The King permits Kali to live only where gambling, intoxication, prostitution and animal killing take place. (SB 1.17 38)

children.topic: A fifth home: wherever gold is
children.note: At Kali's request Pariksit adds gold, since gold breeds lying, drunkenness, lust, jealousy and hostility. (SB 1.17 39)

Pariksit confronts the sudra beating bull Dharma and cow Earth. The bull's lost legs are austerity, cleanliness and mercy, ruined by pride, lust and intoxication. Kali surrenders and is confined to gambling, drink, prostitution, slaughter and gold.

children.topic: 18 · Mahārāja Parīkṣit Cursed by a Brāhmaṇa Boy
Pariksit sees the good in Kali-yuga
children.note: Like a bee taking only nectar, the King knew that in this age good intentions bear fruit at once while bad acts must be performed. (SB 1.18 7)

children.topic: A moment with a devotee beats heaven
children.note: The sages say brief association with the Lord's devotee outweighs heaven or liberation, let alone worldly wealth. (SB 1.18 13)

children.topic: A dead snake on the sage's shoulder
children.note: Feeling neglected, the angry King drapes a lifeless snake on meditating Samika with his bow and leaves. (SB 1.18 30)

children.topic: Srngi's curse: snakebird in seven days
children.note: The brahmana boy curses Pariksit to die from a snakebird's bite on the seventh day for insulting his father. (SB 1.18 37)

children.topic: Without monarchy, thieves devour the people
children.note: Samika explains the king represents the Lord; when kingship is abolished, rogues scatter the unprotected like lambs. (SB 1.18 43)
Samika models forbearance: devotees, even when insulted, cheated, cursed or killed, do not retaliate. (SB 1.18 48)

The sages ask Suta for Sukadeva's teachings. Suta tells how a hungry, thirsty Pariksit found sage Samika in trance, felt insulted, and hung a dead snake on him. Samika's son Srngi cursed him to die of snakebite in seven days; the sage grieved at the excess.

children.topic: Death news received as good news
children.note: Hearing of the curse, the King is glad, seeing it as the cause of his detachment from worldly things. (SB 1.19 4)

children.topic: The curse is the Lord's mercy
children.note: Pariksit understands that God came as a brahmana's curse to frighten him out of his attachment to family life. (SB 1.19 14)

children.topic: Wish for future births: love Krishna
children.note: If reborn, the King prays only for attachment to Krishna, the company of devotees and friendship with all beings. (SB 1.19 16)

children.topic: What must a dying man do?
children.note: Pariksit asks the sages to deliberate and tell him the duty of everyone, especially one about to die. (SB 1.19 24)

children.topic: Sukadeva sits, ready to answer anything
children.note: The pacified sage takes his seat, and the King bows and questions him politely, hands folded. (SB 1.19 31)

children.topic: What to hear, chant, remember, worship
children.note: Pariksit's core question: what a person should listen to, recite, keep in mind and worship, and what to avoid. (SB 1.19 38)

Pariksit repents, welcomes the curse as the Lord's mercy, and sits beside the Ganges, fasting to the end. Great sages gather and approve. The sixteen-year-old Sukadeva appears, and Pariksit asks him what a person about to die should hear, chant and remember.
How the Bhagavatam came to be spoken: the sages’ questions, Narada and Vyasa, the departure of Krishna, Pariksit cursed and Sukadeva’s arrival. 19 chapters.

children.topic: 1 · The First Step in God Realization
Nights in sleep or sex, days making money
children.note: Sukadeva describes the materialist's life: nights lost to sleep and sex, days to earning and family maintenance. (SB 2.1 3)

children.topic: Trusting body, children, wife as soldiers
children.note: Those ignorant of the self cling to fallible protectors and never see their own inevitable destruction. (SB 2.1 4)
Whatever the path, knowledge, yoga or duty, the highest achievement is to remember the Lord at life's end. (SB 2.1 6)

children.topic: Chanting is the fearless way for everyone
children.note: Chanting the Lord's name without stop suits the desireless, the desirous and the self-satisfied alike. (SB 2.1 11)

children.topic: One conscious moment beats a wasted life
children.note: A long life spent in ignorance is worthless; a single moment of full awareness starts the search for the highest good. (SB 2.1 12)
Told he had only a moment to live, Khatvanga dropped everything and took full shelter of the Lord. (SB 2.1 13)

Sukadeva praises Pariksit's question and contrasts it with lives wasted on money, sleep and sex. Remembering the Lord at death is life's perfection; chanting suits all. He teaches meditation on the virat-rupa, mapping planets and elements onto the Lord's body.
The enlightened person accepts minimum needs and sees extra endeavor as hard labor for nothing. (SB 2.2 3)
With trees, rivers, caves and the Lord's protection available, sages have no reason to court the money-proud. (SB 2.2 5)
Some meditate on the Lord within the heart, four-armed, holding lotus, disc, conch and club. (SB 2.2 8)
Meditation should begin at the Lord's lotus feet and rise limb by limb to His smiling face, purifying intelligence. (SB 2.2 13)

children.topic: No better deliverance than direct devotion
children.note: For souls wandering the universe, nothing is more auspicious than devotional service to Krishna. (SB 2.2 33)

children.topic: Hear, glorify and remember Him everywhere
children.note: Sukadeva's conclusion: every human must hear about, praise and remember the Lord always and in all places. (SB 2.2 36)

children.topic: 3 · Pure Devotional Service: The Change in Heart
Whatever you want, worship the Supreme
children.note: Whether full of desire, desireless or seeking liberation, the broad-minded person should worship the Personality of Godhead. (SB 2.3 10)

children.topic: The sun steals life, except from devotees
children.note: Each sunrise and sunset shortens everyone's life except one who spends time discussing the all-good Lord. (SB 2.3 17)

children.topic: Praised only by hogs and asses
children.note: Those who never hear Krishna's pastimes are praised only by animal-like people. (SB 2.3 19)

children.topic: Snake-hole ears and a frog's tongue
children.note: One who has never heard or loudly sung the Lord's glories has ears like holes and a tongue like a frog's. (SB 2.3 20)

children.topic: No devotee's dust means a dead body
children.note: A person who never took a pure devotee's foot dust or smelled tulasi from the Lord's feet is a breathing corpse. (SB 2.3 23)
If chanting the holy name brings no ecstasy, tears or standing hairs, the heart is hard as steel. (SB 2.3 24)

Sukadeva lists which demigods grant which desires but says the intelligent worship Krishna whatever they want. Saunaka asks Suta to continue, and Suta condemns lives without hearing of the Lord: ears like snake holes, hands like a dead man's, hearts of steel.
Through attraction to Krishna the King releases attachment to body, wife, children, palace, animals, treasury and kingdom. (SB 2.4 2)

children.topic: How does the Lord create universes?
children.note: Pariksit asks how the Lord's energies produce worlds that even great demigods cannot conceive. (SB 2.4 6)

children.topic: Hearing and worship erase all sins
children.note: Sukadeva bows to Krishna, about whom praise, remembrance, seeing, prayer, hearing and worship instantly cleanse sins. (SB 2.4 15)

children.topic: Great qualities are fruitless unless offered
children.note: Sages, philanthropists, philosophers and Vedic chanters gain nothing unless their gifts serve the Lord. (SB 2.4 17)

children.topic: Even Kiratas and Hunas are purified
children.note: Members of the lowest tribes and sinful races become pure by sheltering in the Lord's devotees. (SB 2.4 18)
By constantly thinking of Krishna's feet under authorities, the devotee sees the truth, while speculators invent Him at whim. (SB 2.4 21)

Pariksit, now fully detached, asks how the Lord creates, maintains and withdraws the universes. Before answering, Sukadeva offers a series of prayers glorifying Krishna, who purifies even the lowest tribes, and bows to Vyasa.

children.topic: Do you create alone, like a spider?
children.note: Narada wonders whether Brahma spins the universe from himself the way a spider spins its web. (SB 2.5 5)

children.topic: Brahma admits a power above him
children.note: Brahma says that without knowing the Lord beyond him, people are naturally fooled by his powerful acts. (SB 2.5 10)

children.topic: Maya makes us say I and mine
children.note: The illusory energy, ashamed to face the Lord, keeps the bewildered chattering about 'I' and 'mine'. (SB 2.5 13)

children.topic: Vedas, demigods, planets all for the Lord
children.note: Scripture, demigods, worlds and sacrifices exist to serve the Supreme Lord, like limbs of His body. (SB 2.5 15)

children.topic: All yoga and austerity aim at Narayana
children.note: Meditation, penance, knowledge and salvation itself are all directed toward reaching Narayana. (SB 2.5 16)

children.topic: From false ego, sky and sound appear
children.note: Creation begins as false ego in darkness produces the sky, whose subtle quality is sound. (SB 2.5 25)

Narada asks Brahma whether he alone creates. Brahma answers that he works only after the Lord, as the moon shines after the sun, and describes creation: modes, false ego, elements from sky to earth, mind, senses, and the virat-rupa with fourteen worlds.

children.topic: His feet shelter all from fear
children.note: The Lord's steps protect the upper, lower and heavenly worlds, and His lotus feet drive away every fear. (SB 2.6 7)

children.topic: Spiritual world is three-fourths of His energy
children.note: Beyond matter lies the vast spiritual sky for those never reborn; the attached must stay in the three worlds. (SB 2.6 20)

children.topic: Aloof from creation like sun from rays
children.note: All universes and elements come from the Lord, yet He stays separate as the sun is separate from its heat and light. (SB 2.6 22)

children.topic: Brahma's sacrifice from the Lord's limbs
children.note: Born on the lotus with no ingredients, Brahma had only the Lord's bodily parts from which to build his sacrifice. (SB 2.6 23)
Despite his austerity, mystic power and honor, Brahma admits he cannot comprehend the source of his own birth. (SB 2.6 35)

children.topic: Best to surrender at His feet
children.note: Brahma concludes surrender to the Lord's feet is all-auspicious, since even the Lord cannot measure His own limits. (SB 2.6 36)

Brahma maps the universal form: voice from His mouth, herbs from His breath, rivers from His veins. The spiritual world is three quarters of His energy. He made his first sacrifice from the Lord's limbs, admits he cannot fathom Him, and turns to the avatars.
The half-lion incarnation kills the demon king on His lap with His nails to end the demigods' fear. (SB 2.7 14)

children.topic: Vamana begs three steps from Bali
children.note: Appearing as Aditi's youngest son, the Lord asks Bali for three paces of land and takes the whole world. (SB 2.7 17)
When Indra floods Vraja for seven days, the boy Krishna holds up the hill on one hand to shelter the cows. (SB 2.7 32)
When God-talk vanishes and rulers are lowborn, the Lord appears as the final chastiser of the age. (SB 2.7 38)
Whoever the Lord favors for pure surrender can understand Him; those attached to the body cannot. (SB 2.7 42)

children.topic: Even outcastes and animals can be liberated
children.note: Anyone, of any birth, can know God by surrendering to pure devotees and following their example. (SB 2.7 46)

Brahma tells Narada the Lord's scheduled incarnations, from Varaha, Kapila, Nrsimha and Vamana to Rama, Krishna, Buddha and Kalki, then admits no one can measure the Lord; only surrendered souls know Him, and he asks Narada to spread the Bhagavatam.

children.topic: Hear Bhagavatam, Krishna appears in heart
children.note: Anyone who hears the Bhagavatam regularly and seriously soon finds Krishna manifest within the heart. (SB 2.8 4)

children.topic: Bhagavatam is autumn rain on muddy water
children.note: The sound form of Krishna enters a devotee's heart and washes away lust, anger and hankering. (SB 2.8 5)
Once the heart is cleansed by devotion, one never leaves Krishna's feet, like a weary traveler safely home. (SB 2.8 6)

children.topic: How does the soul get a body?
children.note: Pariksit asks whether the spirit soul, distinct from matter, receives its body by chance or by some cause. (SB 2.8 7)
Drinking the message of the infallible Lord from Sukadeva's lips, the fasting king feels no fatigue. (SB 2.8 26)

children.topic: 9 · Answers by Citing the Lord’s Version
Soul's bondage is like a dream
children.note: The pure soul's link with a material body is unreal, like a dreamer watching his own body act. (SB 2.9 1)
Perplexed on the lotus, Brahma hears two syllables meaning penance, the wealth of renunciants, and obeys. (SB 2.9 6)
In the Lord's abode passion and ignorance are absent, time has no sway and even demons worship as devotees. (SB 2.9 10)
The Lord tells Brahma that He creates, maintains and withdraws the cosmos through penance alone. (SB 2.9 24)
First seed verse: before, during and after the cosmos, only the Lord exists. (SB 2.9 33)

children.topic: Whatever seems real apart from Me is maya
children.note: Second seed verse: anything of value unrelated to the Lord is His illusion, a reflection in darkness. (SB 2.9 34)

Sukadeva tells how Brahma, hearing 'ta-pa', did penance, saw Vaikuntha and the four-armed Lord, and received the four seed verses of the Bhagavatam: the Lord exists before, during and after creation. Brahma passed this on to Narada, who taught Vyasa.

children.topic: 10 · Bhāgavatam Is the Answer to All Questions

children.note: Creation, subcreation, planets, protection, impetus, Manus, science of God, return home, liberation and the ultimate shelter. (SB 2.10 1)

children.topic: The supreme shelter is the Absolute Truth
children.note: The Supreme Soul is the origin, reservoir and final rest of the cosmos, the summum bonum of all topics. (SB 2.10 7)
The Supreme Person is not impersonal; He lies on the water born of Him, hence the name Narayana. (SB 2.10 11)

children.topic: Everything exists by His mercy alone
children.note: Matter, action, time, modes and living beings persist only while the Lord cares for them. (SB 2.10 12)

children.topic: His transcendental form is beyond matter
children.note: The Lord truly appears with His own name, qualities, pastimes and associates, unaffected by activity. (SB 2.10 36)

children.topic: The Lord does not directly engineer creation
children.note: Vedic accounts of His intervention only refute the idea that material nature creates on its own. (SB 2.10 45)

Sukadeva lists the ten topics of the Bhagavatam, explains adhyatmic, adhidaivic and adhibhautic, and narrates how Narayana's desires produced the senses, limbs and their presiding deities in the universal form; Saunaka then asks Suta about Vidura and Maitreya.
Sukadeva begins: the first step in God realisation, the universal form, the process of creation, and why the Bhagavatam answers every question. 10 chapters.

children.topic: Give up Duryodhana, save the family
children.note: Vidura warns his brother that sheltering a son envious of Krishna destroys all good fortune. (SB 3.1 13)
Duryodhana abuses Vidura as a maidservant's son and orders him expelled from the palace. (SB 3.1 15)
Pierced by harsh words, Vidura sets his bow at the door and departs, seeing it all as the Lord's energy. (SB 3.1 16)

children.topic: Akrura rolls in Krishna's footprint dust
children.note: Vidura asks about Akrura, who once fell in love-ecstasy on the road marked by Krishna's feet. (SB 3.1 32)
He appears to destroy the arrogant, and His human-like acts exist so that everyone can understand Him. (SB 3.1 44)

children.topic: Sing the glories of the unborn Lord
children.note: Vidura asks Uddhava to chant about Krishna, who appears out of mercy among His devotees, the Yadus. (SB 3.1 45)
Srila Prabhupada's recorded class: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 3.1.10. Tap the link to read the transcript and play the audio.
Recorded classes on this chapter, with transcript and audio on vedabase.io. Oldest first.

Sukadeva tells how Vidura advised Dhrtarastra to return Yudhisthira's kingdom, was insulted by Duryodhana and left for pilgrimage; at the Yamuna he meets Uddhava and asks after Krishna, the Yadus and the Pandavas, then asks him to sing the Lord's glories.

children.topic: The sun of the world has set
children.note: Uddhava says Krishna has departed and the snake of time has swallowed the Yadu house; what welfare remains? (SB 3.2 7)

children.topic: The fish cannot see the moon
children.note: The Yadus lived with Krishna daily yet failed to recognize Him as God, like fish seeing the moon's reflection. (SB 3.2 8)
Once one smells the dust of Krishna's feet, forgetting is impossible; a flick of His brow relieved the earth. (SB 3.2 18)
Krishna gave the poison-breasted demoness the status of a mother; who is more merciful than He? (SB 3.2 23)

children.topic: Even His enemies see Him on Garuda
children.note: Uddhava envies demons who, absorbed in enmity, see the Lord face to face with His disc in hand. (SB 3.2 24)
When Indra's rains flooded Vraja, Krishna held up the hill like an umbrella to shelter everyone. (SB 3.2 33)

Asked about Krishna, Uddhava falls silent in ecstasy, then laments that the world's sun has set. He recalls Krishna's prison birth, childhood in Vraja, Kaliya, Govardhana and the rasa dance, marvelling that even the Yadus missed His divinity.

children.topic: 3 · The Lord’s Pastimes Out of Vṛndāvana

children.note: Learning all Vedas by hearing them once, Krishna repays Sandipani by bringing his dead son from Yamaloka. (SB 3.3 2)
Among assembled kings, Krishna takes Bhismaka's daughter as His own, as Garuda snatched nectar. (SB 3.3 3)

children.topic: One Lord, many wives, one moment
children.note: Krishna expands into many forms to marry every rescued princess simultaneously by proper rites. (SB 3.3 8)

children.topic: The Yadus have become a burden
children.note: After Kuruksetra, Krishna sees His own powerful dynasty as an even heavier load on the earth. (SB 3.3 14)

children.topic: They will fall by their own quarrel
children.note: Krishna decides the Yadus can vanish only through a drunken brawl after His departure. (SB 3.3 15)
All beings' enjoyment is controlled by a higher power; faith in Krishna's acts comes only by devotion. (SB 3.3 23)

Uddhava recounts Krishna's Mathura and Dvaraka pastimes: killing Kamsa, marrying Rukmini and 16,000 princesses, slaying demons, the Kuruksetra war, installing Yudhisthira, and finally His plan that the Yadus, now a burden, perish through a drunken quarrel.

children.topic: I could not bear separation from Him
children.note: Knowing the Lord's plan to end the dynasty, Uddhava still followed, unable to leave His lotus feet. (SB 3.4 5)
Uddhava finds the Lord resting alone against a young tree, foot on thigh, serene despite leaving all. (SB 3.4 8)

children.topic: This is your last birth, Uddhava
children.note: Krishna tells Uddhava he has received His highest favor and may now go to Vaikuntha. (SB 3.4 12)

children.topic: I want only service, not liberation
children.note: Uddhava says devotees easily gain dharma, wealth, pleasure and liberation, but he prefers loving service. (SB 3.4 15)
Uddhava sends Vidura to Maitreya, who was instructed by the Lord Himself before He left the world. (SB 3.4 26)
Krishna keeps Uddhava in the world to spread knowledge of Him, since the modes never touch him. (SB 3.4 31)

Uddhava describes the Yadus' drunken destruction and finding Krishna alone under a banyan tree, where the Lord told him his life was his last, revealed the Bhagavatam knowledge, and sent him to Badarikasrama; Uddhava directs Vidura to Maitreya at the Ganges.
Vidura observes that fruitive activity never satisfies or ends distress, and asks how to live rightly. (SB 3.5 2)
Topics of the Lord, entering through the ears, sever one's bondage to family affection. (SB 3.5 11)
Vidura asks Maitreya to distill the essence of every topic: the Lord's glories. (SB 3.5 15)
Maitreya reveals Vidura, born to Vyasa, was the lord of death cursed by Mandavya Muni. (SB 3.5 20)
The demigods pray that the Lord's lotus feet shield surrendered souls from all material misery. (SB 3.5 39)

children.topic: His feet are within, yet unseen
children.note: Those bound by 'I and mine' cannot see the Lord's feet, though they reside within their own bodies. (SB 3.5 44)

At Hardwar Vidura asks Maitreya how to live for real happiness and begs for Krishna-katha. Maitreya honors him, then describes creation: the Lord alone, maya, mahat-tattva, false ego, mind, senses and elements, ending with the demigods' prayers.
When the Lord enters the elements through His potency, all beings stir into activity like sleepers waking. (SB 3.6 3)
The universal form is the Supersoul's first plenary portion, in whom the whole creation rests. (SB 3.6 8)
Vedic knowledge came from the virat's mouth; those devoted to it are teachers of all society. (SB 3.6 30)

children.topic: Worship the Lord through the guru
children.note: Since all social orders come from the Lord, self-realization means worshiping Him under a spiritual master. (SB 3.6 34)

children.topic: Hearing His glories is life's highest gain
children.note: Discussing the Lord's activities as arranged by learned sages fulfills the ear's true purpose. (SB 3.6 37)

children.topic: Bow down; He cannot be known
children.note: Words, mind and ego fail to grasp the Lord, so the sane response is simply to offer obeisances. (SB 3.6 40)

Maitreya explains how the Lord entered the twenty-three elements to form the gigantic virat-purusa, how demigods entered its mouth, eyes, ears and limbs, and how the four social orders arose from its mouth, arms, thighs and legs.

children.topic: God overcome by maya is illogical
children.note: Maitreya rejects the theory that the Supreme is bewildered by illusion yet also unconditioned. (SB 3.7 9)

children.topic: Dreaming your head is cut off
children.note: The soul's identity crisis has no real basis, like a dreamer who sees himself beheaded. (SB 3.7 10)
The self seems material only by association, as the moon's reflection shakes with the water. (SB 3.7 11)

children.topic: Chanting His name ends all misery
children.note: Just hearing and chanting Krishna's name and form stops unlimited suffering, what to speak of serving Him. (SB 3.7 14)

children.topic: Fools and sages are happy; middle suffers
children.note: Vidura notes the lowest fool and the fully transcendental are content, while those between them suffer. (SB 3.7 17)

children.topic: Devotees are the source of knowledge
children.note: Without pure devotees, no one could learn devotional service and detachment. (SB 3.7 39)

Vidura asks how the changeless Lord touches matter and why the pure soul suffers. Maitreya says bondage is illusion, like a moon trembling on water, removed by devotion. Satisfied, Vidura poses a long list of questions on creation and dharma.

children.topic: 8 · Manifestation of Brahmā from Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu

children.note: Sanat-kumara and the sages asked Sankarsana, seated at the universe's base, about Vasudeva, as Vidura now asks. (SB 3.8 3)

children.topic: Visnu asleep on Ananta, eyes half open
children.note: When the worlds are submerged, the Lord lies on the great serpent in His own potency, not fully asleep. (SB 3.8 10)
Unable to see from the lotus whorl, Brahma turns in every direction and grows a head for each. (SB 3.8 16)

children.topic: Who am I? Where is this lotus from?
children.note: Brahma, in ignorance, wonders about his own origin and reasons that the root must lie below in the water. (SB 3.8 18)

children.topic: Searching the lotus stem in vain
children.note: Brahma descends through the stem toward Visnu's navel but cannot find the root. (SB 3.8 19)

children.topic: After a hundred years, the Lord within
children.note: When his meditation matures, Brahma sees the Supreme in his heart, whom effort could not reveal. (SB 3.8 22)

Maitreya traces the Bhagavatam from Sankarsana through the Kumaras to Parasara, then tells how Visnu lay on Ananta, a lotus rose from His navel, and Brahma, born there, searched the stem in vain, meditated and saw the Lord in his heart.

children.topic: Anxiety until one takes His shelter
children.note: People guarding wealth, body and friends stay fearful until they surrender to the Lord's feet. (SB 3.9 6)

children.topic: Devotees see the Lord through the ears
children.note: By proper hearing the heart is cleansed and the Lord sits there in the form the devotee cherishes. (SB 3.9 11)

children.topic: His name at death washes all sin
children.note: Even unconsciously chanting the Lord's names while dying erases the sins of many births. (SB 3.9 15)

children.topic: Let me not become proud as creator
children.note: Brahma prays to serve the Lord in creation without being affected or thinking himself the doer. (SB 3.9 23)

children.topic: See Me in you, and you in Me
children.note: The Lord promises Brahma that in devotion he will see Him in himself, the universe and all beings. (SB 3.9 31)

children.topic: Be attached to Me, not the body
children.note: The Lord declares He is the Supersoul and dearest of all, the proper object of attachment. (SB 3.9 42)

Brahma prays to Garbhodakasayi Visnu, glorifying His eternal form, pitying suffering souls and asking to create without pride. The Lord says his wish is already granted and tells him to see Him everywhere through penance, knowledge and devotion.
Eternal time stirs the three modes and is the changeless, limitless tool of the Lord's material pastimes. (SB 3.10 11)
Besides the natural interaction of modes, there are nine kinds of creation and three of dissolution. (SB 3.10 14)
Immovable beings grow upward, are nearly unconscious, yet have inner feelings of pain. (SB 3.10 20)
The lower species, guided by smell, are ignorant and cannot remember anything in the heart. (SB 3.10 21)

children.topic: Humans think themselves happy in misery
children.note: The single human species, ruled by passion, feels content while living amid constant suffering. (SB 3.10 26)

After a hundred years of penance Brahma drinks up the wind and water, enters the lotus and divides it into fourteen worlds. Maitreya then defines eternal time and lists ten creations: six natural and four by Brahma, including plants, animals, humans and gods.

children.topic: 11 · Calculation of Time, from the Atom
Time is the Lord's invisible potency
children.note: Time is measured by atomic movement, yet it is the power of Hari, who controls all motion unseen. (SB 3.11 3)

children.topic: The sun shortens life to free us
children.note: The sun reduces everyone's lifespan to break material attachment and opens the way to heaven. (SB 3.11 15)
Satya lasts 4,800, Treta 3,600, Dvapara 2,400 and Kali 1,200 years of the demigods. (SB 3.11 19)
A thousand cycles of four yugas make Brahma's day; an equal night follows while he sleeps. (SB 3.11 22)

children.topic: Brahma's life is one blink for the Lord
children.note: Brahma's entire hundred years amount to less than a second for the unchanging Supreme Lord. (SB 3.11 38)
Time governs everything from atom to Brahma's life, yet is itself controlled by the Lord and cannot touch the liberated. (SB 3.11 39)

Maitreya measures time from the atom through truti, nimesa, muhurta, day, month and year, then the four yugas, Brahma's day of a thousand yuga cycles, the fourteen Manus, and Brahma's hundred-year life, which is one moment for the Supreme Lord.

children.topic: 12 · Creation of the Kumāras and Others

children.note: Ordered to beget children, the four sages decline, being attached to Vasudeva and set on liberation. (SB 3.12 5)
Brahma's suppressed anger bursts from between his eyebrows as a blue-and-red child. (SB 3.12 7)
Brahma tells Rudra that austerity alone approaches the Lord who is in every heart yet beyond the senses. (SB 3.12 19)
Marici and the sages tell Brahma that desiring his own daughter is unworthy of the universe's chief. (SB 3.12 30)

children.topic: Brahma abandons his body as fog
children.note: Ashamed before his sons, Brahma gives up that body, which spreads out as dangerous darkness. (SB 3.12 33)
Two forms separate from Brahma's body: the first Manu, Svayambhuva, and his queen Satarupa. (SB 3.12 54)

children.topic: 🎬 We Must Accept Some Sort of Tapasya
children.note: Vanimedia clip 0145 (subtitled in many languages): Srimad-Bhagavatam 3.12.19 Lecture in Dallas on March 3, 1975 Imperfections of living being - Meditation on GodFreedom from materialism - Four regulative principles - Explanatory story

Maitreya describes Brahma's creations: the Kumaras who refuse to procreate, Rudra born from his anger and sent to penance, the ten sages, his shameful attraction to his daughter Vak, the Vedas and social orders from his mouths, and Manu with Satarupa.
Brahma tells Manu that guarding living beings is the best service to him and delights the Supreme. (SB 3.13 12)

children.topic: Labor is futile if Janardana is displeased
children.note: The Lord receives all sacrifice; one who fails to satisfy Him neglects his own true interest. (SB 3.13 13)

children.topic: A thumb-sized boar from Brahma's nose
children.note: While Brahma ponders how to lift the earth, a tiny boar appears from his nostril and swells to the sky. (SB 3.13 18)

children.topic: Earth on the tusks, demon slain
children.note: Varaha easily raises the earth from the water on His tusks and, blazing with anger, kills Hiranyaksa in the deep. (SB 3.13 31)

children.topic: You are the Vedas in a boar's form
children.note: The sages praise the Lord as the personified sacrifice whose body holds the oceans in its pores. (SB 3.13 34)
Only a non-human would ignore life's goal and reject narrations of the Lord that end all suffering. (SB 3.13 50)

Brahma tells Manu to rule and protect while worshiping the Lord. When the earth sinks, a thumb-sized boar leaves Brahma's nostril, grows huge, dives in, hoists the earth on His tusks, kills Hiranyaksa; sages praise Varaha as sacrifice personified.

children.topic: 14 · Pregnancy of Diti in the Evening

children.note: Diti tells Kasyapa that desire torments her like a mad elephant battering a banana tree. (SB 3.14 10)

children.topic: A wife helps conquer the senses
children.note: Kasyapa says sheltering in a wife lets a householder master the senses, like a fort commander repelling raiders. (SB 3.14 20)

children.topic: Siva roams with ghosts at twilight
children.note: Kasyapa warns that this hour belongs to Siva, who travels on his bull with his ghostly companions. (SB 3.14 24)
Overcome by lust, Diti seizes Kasyapa's garment like a shameless prostitute, and he yields to fate. (SB 3.14 30)

children.topic: Two sons will torment the worlds
children.note: Kasyapa foretells that Diti's tainted womb will bear two contemptible sons who make the universe weep. (SB 3.14 39)

children.topic: Your grandson will be a great devotee
children.note: Because of Diti's repentance and faith, Prahlada will be born, famed equally with the Lord Himself. (SB 3.14 44-45)

Vidura asks why Varaha fought Hiranyaksa. Maitreya tells how Diti, lusty at dusk, forced Kasyapa to unite despite his warnings about Siva's hour. Kasyapa foretells two demon sons killed by the Lord, but consoles her with grandson Prahlada, a great devotee.

children.topic: 15 · Description of the Kingdom of God
Vaikuntha residents sing of the Lord
children.note: Inhabitants fly with their consorts, eternally chanting the Lord's glories, ignoring even honeyed flowers. (SB 3.15 17)
Fragrant celestial blooms honor tulasi's austerity, since the Lord wears her leaves as His garland. (SB 3.15 19)
Those who abandon talk of the spiritual world for mundane topics fall into deepest ignorance. (SB 3.15 23)

children.topic: Ecstasy in hearing wins the kingdom
children.note: People who tremble, breathe heavily and sweat hearing of the Lord reach His abode without other austerities. (SB 3.15 25)

children.topic: The doorkeepers cursed to the material world
children.note: The Kumaras decide the guards who see duality in Vaikuntha must fall to the world of three enemies. (SB 3.15 34)

children.topic: Born in hell, if we may serve You
children.note: The Kumaras accept any birth so long as their hearts, words and ears stay engaged with the Lord. (SB 3.15 49)

Diti's pregnancy darkens the universe; Brahma tells the demigods how the four Kumaras reached Vaikuntha, describes its forests and devotees, and how two doorkeepers blocked the sages and were cursed. The Lord Himself came out and the Kumaras prayed to Him.

children.topic: 16 · The Two Doorkeepers of Vaikuṇṭha, Jaya and Vijaya, Cursed by the Sages

children.note: The Lord takes His servants' offense as His own and asks the sages' forgiveness. (SB 3.16 4)

children.topic: Hearing My glories purifies even a dog-eater
children.note: Anyone who bathes in hearing the Lord's name is cleansed; He would cut off His own arm if it opposed devotees. (SB 3.16 6)

children.topic: I carry Vaisnava footdust on My head
children.note: The Lord, whose foot-wash is the Ganges, says He wears the dust of devotees' feet, so who would refuse? (SB 3.16 9)

children.topic: Brahmanas, cows and the helpless are My body
children.note: Those who see these as separate from the Lord are torn apart by the messengers of Yamaraja. (SB 3.16 10)
The Lord reveals the curse was His plan: the guards will be demons but return soon, absorbed in Him by anger. (SB 3.16 26)

children.topic: Yoga of anger brings you back
children.note: The Lord assures Jaya and Vijaya that angry concentration on Him will quickly cleanse their sin. (SB 3.16 31)

The Lord approves the Kumaras' curse on Jaya and Vijaya, treats the offense as His own and glorifies brahmanas and devotees. The awed sages submit. He sends the doorkeepers to demoniac births with a quick return; they become Diti's twins.

children.topic: 17 · Victory of Hiraṇyākṣa Over All the Directions of the Universe

children.note: At the demons' birth, cows yield blood, clouds rain pus, temple images shed tears and trees fall windless. (SB 3.17 13)
The elder twin, puffed up by his benediction, subdues the three worlds and fears death from no one. (SB 3.17 19)

children.topic: Demigods hide like snakes from Garuda
children.note: Proud of his strength and boon, Hiranyaksa terrifies the gods, who flee at his very sight. (SB 3.17 22)
Hiranyaksa mockingly bows at Varuna's feet and demands a battle from the guardian of the waters. (SB 3.17 27)
Varuna, curbing his anger, directs the demon to the most ancient person, whom even heroes praise. (SB 3.17 30)
Varuna predicts the Lord as Varaha will strip Hiranyaksa's pride and leave him dead on the field. (SB 3.17 31)

After a hundred-year pregnancy Diti bears Hiranyakasipu and Hiranyaksa amid terrible omens. Proud of Brahma's boon, Hiranyaksa roams with his mace seeking a fight, scatters the demigods and taunts Varuna, who says only Visnu can satisfy him in battle.

children.topic: 18 · The Battle Between Lord Boar and the Demon Hiraṇyākṣa

children.note: Seeing the boar carrying the earth on His tusks, Hiranyaksa laughs and belittles Him as an animal. (SB 3.18 2)
Varaha places the earth on the water and grants her His own energy to stay afloat as Brahma praises Him. (SB 3.18 8)

children.topic: We are jungle creatures hunting dogs
children.note: The Lord retorts that one free of death fears no abuse from a braggart bound by death's laws. (SB 3.18 10)
The Lord sidesteps the demon's mace-blow to His chest as a perfect yogi eludes death. (SB 3.18 15)

children.topic: Two bulls fighting for a cow
children.note: Both combatants, bleeding and enraged by the smell of blood, maneuver like bulls contending for a cow. (SB 3.18 19)
Brahma warns that the auspicious midday hour is ending and the demonic evening approaches. (SB 3.18 27)

Hiranyaksa finds Varaha lifting the earth, mocks Him as a beast and chases Him. The Lord sets the earth afloat, returns the taunts, and the two duel with maces, wounding each other. Brahma arrives and urges the Lord to finish him before evening falls.

children.topic: 19 · The Killing of the Demon Hiraṇyākṣa

children.note: Hiranyaksa refuses to strike the unarmed Lord, and this fair play stirs the Lord's fury. (SB 3.19 4)

children.topic: Mace kicked away with the left foot
children.note: The Lord playfully knocks down the demon's hurtling mace with His foot while he watches. (SB 3.19 9)

children.topic: Sky rains pus, hair and bones
children.note: The demon's magic darkens the heavens and pours filth from the clouds amid thunder and lightning. (SB 3.19 19)

children.topic: Felled like a tree in the wind
children.note: A casual slap at the ear root sends Hiranyaksa spinning; eyes bulging, limbs broken, he falls dead. (SB 3.19 26)

children.topic: Who could meet such a blessed death?
children.note: Brahma marvels that the demon died gazing at the face yogis seek in trance, struck by the Lord's own foot. (SB 3.19 28)

children.topic: Hearing this frees one from all sin
children.note: Whoever hears or chants the killing of Hiranyaksa is relieved of sinful reactions, even brahmana-killing. (SB 3.19 37)

Varaha loses His mace but the demon honors the duel, so the Lord takes Sudarsana. Hiranyaksa's mace, trident, fists and magic all fail; a slap below the ear kills him as he gazes at the Lord. Brahma marvels at such a death; hearing this tale removes all sin.
A lotus bright as a thousand suns rises from the Lord's navel, and Brahma is the first to emerge. (SB 3.20 16)
Brahma first creates tamisra, andha-tamisra, tamas, moha and maha-moha from his shadow. (SB 3.20 18)

children.topic: Hungry sons try to eat Brahma
children.note: Yaksas and Raksasas, born from Brahma's cast-off body of night, rush at their father shouting to devour him. (SB 3.20 20)
Pursued by lustful demons, Brahma flees to the Lord, who tells him to abandon his tainted body. (SB 3.20 28)
Mistaking dusk for an alluring woman, the deluded asuras take hold of her. (SB 3.20 37)
Feeling his purpose fulfilled, Brahma produces the Manus, who guide the welfare of the universe. (SB 3.20 49)

Vidura asks how the Prajapatis populated the universe. Maitreya lists Brahma's creations from discarded bodies: night with Yaksas and Raksasas, day with demigods, lustful demons chasing the twilight woman, Gandharvas, ghosts, Pitas, Siddhas, Nagas and Manus.

children.topic: My eyes have reached their goal
children.note: Kardama says seeing the Lord's form fulfills sight itself, a vision yogis seek for many lifetimes. (SB 3.21 13)
The Lord's feet ferry one across ignorance, yet fools ask them for pleasures even hell-dwellers can get. (SB 3.21 14)

children.topic: The wheel of time spares devotees
children.note: Time's wheel of thirteen spokes and 360 joints shortens all life but cannot touch the Lord's devotees. (SB 3.21 18)

children.topic: Creator like a spider spinning its web
children.note: The Lord creates, sustains and withdraws universes by His own energies, as a spider spins and swallows its web. (SB 3.21 19)

children.topic: I will be born as Devahuti's son
children.note: The Lord promises to appear through Kardama's wife and teach her the philosophy of ultimate categories. (SB 3.21 32)
Kardama tells Manu that if he did not patrol with chariot and bow, rogues would break all social laws. (SB 3.21 52-54)

Kardama Muni worships Visnu for ten thousand years at Bindu-sarovara and sees Him on Garuda. He asks for a wife; the Lord promises Manu's daughter Devahuti, nine daughters and His own birth as their son. Manu brings Devahuti; Kardama praises royal duty.

children.topic: 22 · The Marriage of Kardama Muni and Devahūti
Brahmanas the heart, kshatriyas the arms
children.note: Manu explains that priests and warriors spring from the Lord's body and are meant to guard one another. (SB 3.22 3)

children.topic: Never refuse a gift freely offered
children.note: Manu argues that turning away what comes unasked is unbecoming even for a fully detached person. (SB 3.22 12)
The sage accepts Devahuti but vows to take up pure devotional life once she has borne his offspring. (SB 3.22 19)
Manu weeps and drenches his daughter's head as he hands her to Kardama and turns for home. (SB 3.22 25)
Manu's immense reign is never wasted, since every moment is filled with hearing and remembering the Lord. (SB 3.22 36)
Maitreya asks how anyone fully surrendered to Krishna could be troubled by body, mind, nature or others. (SB 3.22 37)

Maitreya tells Vidura how Svayambhuva Manu offers his daughter Devahuti to the sage Kardama, who agrees on condition that he will renounce family life after fathering children. Manu returns home and reigns as a saintly king absorbed in Krishna.

children.topic: All gain vanishes at Vishnu's eyebrow
children.note: Kardama reminds Devahuti that material achievements are fragile, while her service has earned rare spiritual gifts. (SB 3.23 8)
Using yogic power the sage instantly produces an aerial palace that moves wherever he wishes. (SB 3.23 12)

children.topic: Nothing is hard for the surrendered
children.note: Maitreya observes that those who shelter at the Lord's feet find no goal beyond their reach. (SB 3.23 42)

children.topic: We wasted our time on the senses
children.note: Devahuti regrets that years of pleasure passed without cultivating knowledge of the Supreme. (SB 3.23 53)

children.topic: Company that binds, company that frees
children.note: Attachment for enjoyment enslaves, yet the same bond with a saintly person leads toward liberation. (SB 3.23 55)
Devahuti says work that fails to lead through religion, renunciation and finally devotion leaves a person effectively lifeless. (SB 3.23 56)

Devahuti serves Kardama devotedly until she wastes away; pleased, he grants her a flying palace, a rejuvenating bath in Bindu-sarovara and years of enjoyment, fathering nine daughters. As he prepares to leave, she laments time spent on the senses.

children.topic: Say 'Yes, sir' to father and guru
children.note: Brahma teaches that a son should carry out the orders of father or spiritual master with full deference. (SB 3.24 13)

children.topic: Kapila will uproot desire for work
children.note: Brahma foretells that the golden-haired incarnation will pull out the deep craving for material action. (SB 3.24 17)
Kardama marvels that the Supreme, sought by yogis for many lives, appears in his own home to support devotees. (SB 3.24 29)
Kapila declares His mission: to explain the philosophy of self-realization for those seeking freedom from desire. (SB 3.24 36)

children.topic: Go freely; conquer death by worship
children.note: Kapila sanctions Kardama's departure, telling him to offer every act to the Lord and gain eternal life. (SB 3.24 38)
Wandering as a sannyasi, Kardama loses false ego and attachment, his mind still and equal to all. (SB 3.24 44)

Kardama consoles Devahuti: the Lord Himself will be born as her son. Kapila appears; Brahma arrives, praises Kardama and has the nine daughters married to great sages. Kardama surrenders to Kapila, takes sannyasa and attains perfection.
Kapila says awareness drawn to the modes is conditioned life, but fixed on the Lord it is liberation itself. (SB 3.25 15)

children.topic: Attachment to devotees opens the door
children.note: The very attachment that binds one to matter frees one when redirected to self-realized souls. (SB 3.25 20)
A saint is tolerant, merciful, friendly to all beings, without enemies, peaceful and faithful to scripture. (SB 3.25 21)
Discussing the Lord's pastimes with pure devotees pleases the heart and gradually awakens real devotion. (SB 3.25 25)
Devotional service dissolves the subtle covering effortlessly, as stomach fire digests food. (SB 3.25 33)

children.topic: Wind, sun and death obey from fear
children.note: Kapila reveals that the elements and even death itself act only out of awe of His supremacy. (SB 3.25 42)

Devahuti begs Kapila to lift her out of ignorance. He teaches that consciousness turned to the Lord is liberation, describes the qualities of sadhus, urges attachment to their company, and declares that pure devotees want no reward but the Lord Himself.

children.topic: The Supreme Soul, beginningless and self-luminous
children.note: Kapila opens by describing the Lord as beyond the modes, everywhere perceivable, sustaining all by His effulgence. (SB 3.26 3)

children.topic: Forgetfulness makes the soul claim doership
children.note: Forgetting himself, the living being accepts material energy as his field and wrongly owns its actions. (SB 3.26 6)
Kapila sums up the categories, adding time as the mixing element that completes the count. (SB 3.26 15)
Since a cause lives in its effect, the traits of ether, air, fire and water all appear in earth. (SB 3.26 49)

children.topic: Only consciousness wakes the Cosmic Being
children.note: After every deity fails, the inner controller enters with reason and the universal form rises. (SB 3.26 70)

children.topic: Only the Supersoul rouses the sleeper
children.note: Just as senses cannot wake a sleeping man, the living being's assets act only when the Supersoul helps. (SB 3.26 71)

Kapila lays out Sankhya: the Lord accepts material nature as His pastime; from pradhana come mahat-tattva, false ego, mind, intelligence, senses and five elements, twenty-five in all with time. The universal form lies inert until the Supersoul awakens it.
The soul who claims nothing stays apart from the modes even while living in a material body. (SB 3.27 1)
The soul's wish to dominate matter keeps his conditioning alive, harming him like a bad dream. (SB 3.27 4)
A devotee is content with easy income, eats moderately, lives quietly and remains peaceful and compassionate. (SB 3.27 8)

children.topic: Can nature ever release the soul?
children.note: Devahuti asks how soul and matter, eternally attracted to each other, could possibly be separated. (SB 3.27 17)

children.topic: Fire consumes the sticks that fed it
children.note: Kapila says devotional service burns up nature's covering, as flames destroy the wood that started them. (SB 3.27 23)

children.topic: Devotee reaches the abode, never returns
children.note: By the Lord's mercy the doubt-free devotee goes to the blissful spiritual realm after death and never comes back. (SB 3.27 28-29)

Kapila explains that the soul, like the sun above its reflection, is untouched by nature, yet suffers by identifying with the body. Devahuti asks how the eternal soul-nature bond can break; Kapila answers that long, serious devotional hearing burns it away.

children.topic: 28 · Kapila’s Instructions on the Execution of Devotional Service

children.note: Breath control cleans the body, concentration removes sin, sense restraint cuts association, and meditation frees one from the modes. (SB 3.28 11)

children.topic: Meditate limb by limb, not all at once
children.note: Kapila advises fixing the mind on each feature of the Lord's form separately rather than a general view. (SB 3.28 20)

children.topic: Feet that shatter mountains of sin
children.note: The Lord's feet, source of the Ganges on Siva's head, smash the accumulated sins in the meditator's heart. (SB 3.28 22)

children.topic: His smile dries an ocean of tears
children.note: Meditating on Hari's benevolent smile removes the grief of all who bow to Him. (SB 3.28 32)

children.topic: Tears, thrilled hairs and a hooked mind
children.note: Steady practice awakens pure love; the body shows ecstasy and the mind, once bait, withdraws from matter. (SB 3.28 34)

children.topic: One fire in many kinds of wood
children.note: As fire appears differently in different fuel, one pure soul shows differently in bodies shaped by the modes. (SB 3.28 43)
