children.topic: 🎬 Devahuti's Position is a Perfect Women
children.note: Vanimedia clip 0217 (subtitled in many languages): Srimad-Bhagavatam 3.28.1 Lecture in Honolulu on June 1, 1975 Explanatory story - Description of human societyMisdirected civilization - Act in proper consciousness
Video of Srila Prabhupada teaching this chapter: full lectures and short subtitled clips from vanimedia.org.

Kapila teaches Devahuti the yoga of concentration: regulated duties, breath control and meditation on the Lord's form limb by limb, from lotus feet to smiling face. This ripens into love, tears and ecstasy, and the yogi sees the one soul in all beings.

children.topic: 29 · Explanation of Devotional Service by Lord Kapila

children.note: Pure bhakti arises when the mind is instantly drawn to the Lord's name and flows to Him uninterrupted, like river to sea. (SB 3.29 11-12)
Even when offered, the pure devotee declines every type of mukti, wanting only service. (SB 3.29 13)
Kapila says temple worship that disregards His presence in every being is mere mimicry. (SB 3.29 21)
Deity worship without knowing the Lord in all hearts is compared to offering ghee into dead ashes. (SB 3.29 22)

children.topic: None greater than the surrendered devotee
children.note: Kapila finds no one higher than one who dedicates all activity and life to Him without pause. (SB 3.29 33)

children.topic: Fear of time is not knowing the Lord
children.note: Time, which transforms all matter, is another feature of the Lord; only the ignorant dread it. (SB 3.29 37)

Devahuti asks about devotion, rebirth and time. Kapila classifies bhakti by the modes, describes pure devotion flowing like the Ganges, condemns temple worship that ignores the Lord in all beings, ranks living entities, and shows time as the Lord's feature.

children.topic: 30 · Description by Lord Kapila of Adverse Fruitive Activities

children.note: The materially absorbed person does not sense the mighty time that carries him along. (SB 3.30 1)
Deluded by maya, the conditioned soul enjoys his species and is reluctant to leave it, even a hellish one. (SB 3.30 5)

children.topic: Earns by violence, goes to hell alone
children.note: He gathers money by harm, eats little himself, and bears the sinful reaction for those he fed. (SB 3.30 10)
When he can no longer provide, his family withholds the respect they once showed, like farmers with worn oxen. (SB 3.30 13)
As police seize a criminal, Yama's agents bind the sinner's subtle body by the neck for punishment. (SB 3.30 20)

children.topic: Ill-gotten money is the passage fare
children.note: Wealth earned by envy of others becomes the ticket with which he departs alone for the darkest hell. (SB 3.30 31)

Kapila describes the materialist who ignores time, clings to family, earns by violence, grows old despised like a worn-out ox, dies in agony, and is dragged by Yamadutas over a burning road to hellish torments before slowly rising again to human birth.

children.topic: 31 · Lord Kapila’s Instructions on the Movements of the Living Entities
A bird in a cage remembers
children.note: Confined in the womb, the fortunate child recalls a hundred past births and grieves. (SB 3.31 9)
The unborn soul takes shelter of the Lord's feet, admitting his condition fits his past misdeeds. (SB 3.31 12)

children.topic: I would rather not be born
children.note: Fearing maya will seize him at birth, the child prefers the womb to falling back into the blind well of life. (SB 3.31 20)
Pushed out by the birth wind, the child falls in filth, loses his knowledge and cries under maya's spell. (SB 3.31 24)
Kapila says no attachment binds as completely as that to a woman or to men who dote on women. (SB 3.31 35)

children.topic: Neither dread death nor pamper the body
children.note: Knowing the soul's real nature, one should move through the world detached and firm in purpose. (SB 3.31 47)

Kapila traces the soul's journey: entering the womb, growing month by month, suffering there and praying to the Lord, then being born, forgetting all, and passing through childhood and youth. He warns against sensual company and defines birth and death.

children.topic: To the moon and back again
children.note: Ritualists devoted to gods and forefathers reach the moon, drink soma, and return to earth. (SB 3.32 3)

children.topic: Detached duty leads to God's kingdom
children.note: Working without ownership or ego purifies consciousness and easily brings one to the spiritual world. (SB 3.32 6)
Those who spurn the nectar of the Lord's pastimes for gossip about materialists are condemned by that comparison. (SB 3.32 19)

children.topic: Take shelter of His lotus feet
children.note: Kapila directly advises His mother to worship the Lord with love and be fixed in devotional service. (SB 3.32 22)
As one thing is perceived differently by different senses, the one Lord seems many through different scriptures. (SB 3.32 33)

children.topic: Once with faith, back to Godhead
children.note: Whoever meditates on, hears or chants about the Lord even once with love surely returns home. (SB 3.32 43)

Kapila contrasts householders chasing ritual results, who reach the moon or Pitrloka and fall back, with detached workers who reach the Lord. He urges Devahuti to shelter at the Lord's feet, shows all paths end in Him, and limits this teaching to the faithful.
Devahuti declares that one who once chants, hears, bows or remembers the Lord instantly qualifies for Vedic rites. (SB 3.33 6)
Whoever chants the holy name must already have performed all austerities, pilgrimages and Vedic study. (SB 3.33 7)
Kapila tells His mother the process He taught is simple and will liberate her even in this body. (SB 3.33 10)

children.topic: A cow grieving her lost calf
children.note: Though enlightened, Devahuti mourns her son's departure as a cow mourns a dead calf. (SB 3.33 21)
Following Kapila's instructions, she is soon freed from bondage and attains the Lord within. (SB 3.33 30)
Maitreya promises that anyone who hears the story of Kapila and His mother becomes a devotee and reaches the Lord's abode. (SB 3.33 37)

Devahuti praises Kapila, glorifying even a dog-eater who chants the holy name. Kapila assures her the path is easy and departs. She practices bhakti-yoga in Kardama's opulent ashram, attains liberation at Siddhapada, and Kapila settles by the ocean in trance.
Vidura and Maitreya: creation in detail, the Varaha and Kapila incarnations, and Lord Kapila’s teachings to His mother Devahuti. 33 chapters.

children.topic: Canto 4 · The Creation of the Fourth Order
1 · Genealogical Table of the Daughters of Manu

children.note: Atri's wife bears Soma, Dattatreya and Durvasa as partial forms of Brahma, Vishnu and Siva. (SB 4.1 15)

children.topic: Atri stands on one leg for a century
children.note: The sage controls his breath and attachments, eating only air, praying for a son like the Lord. (SB 4.1 19)

children.topic: We three are the one you meditated on
children.note: Brahma, Vishnu and Siva tell Atri they all came because they are the same person he worshipped. (SB 4.1 30)
Maitreya says anyone who faithfully hears of these dynasties is freed from sinful reactions. (SB 4.1 46-47)
The twin sage incarnation has appeared in the Yadu and Kuru lines to relieve the earth's burden. (SB 4.1 59)
Because Daksa kept insulting the faultless Siva, Sati gave up her body by yoga before maturing. (SB 4.1 66)

Maitreya lists the descendants of Manu's daughters: Akuti bears Yajna, Devahuti's nine daughters marry sages, and Atri's austerity brings Brahma, Vishnu and Siva to grant him Soma, Dattatreya and Durvasa. Nara-Narayana is born to Dharma; Sati is introduced.

children.topic: How could Daksa hate gentle Siva?
children.note: Vidura wonders how anyone could oppose the peaceful, self-satisfied guru of the world. (SB 4.2 2)
Daksa mocks Siva as an ash-smeared madman of crematoriums, auspicious only in name. (SB 4.2 14-15)

children.topic: Curse: no share of the sacrifice
children.note: Daksa declares that Siva, whom he calls the lowest demigod, will get no portion of the offerings. (SB 4.2 18)

children.topic: Daksa will have a goat's face
children.note: Nandisvara curses Daksa for bodily attachment and forgetting Vishnu, foretelling his goat head. (SB 4.2 23)
Bhrgu retorts that those vowed to Siva will become atheists who abandon scriptural rules. (SB 4.2 28)
Amid the cursing and counter-cursing, a saddened Siva says nothing and departs with his disciples. (SB 4.2 33)

Vidura asks why Daksa hated Siva. Maitreya recalls a sacrifice where Siva did not rise for Daksa; enraged, Daksa denounces Siva's habits and curses him out of the offerings. Nandisvara curses the brahmanas, Bhrgu curses Siva's followers, and Siva leaves.

children.topic: 3 · Talks Between Lord Śiva and Satī
No invitation needed for father's house
children.note: Sati argues one may visit a friend, husband, guru or father uninvited. (SB 4.3 13)
Siva explains that education, austerity, wealth, beauty, youth and lineage make the proud unable to see greatness. (SB 4.3 17)

children.topic: Kin's harsh words hurt more than arrows
children.note: Siva says an enemy's weapon wounds less than a relative's cruel speech, which festers day and night. (SB 4.3 19)

children.topic: Why the envious resent the realized
children.note: One driven by false ego cannot bear the glory of self-realized souls, as demons envy the Lord. (SB 4.3 21)
Siva reveals that he is ever engaged in offering obeisance to Krishna in pure consciousness. (SB 4.3 23)
Siva cautions that if Sati goes despite his advice, the humiliation she meets will be fatal. (SB 4.3 25)

Years later Daksa holds a grand sacrifice without inviting Siva. Sati, seeing her sisters fly to it, begs Siva to let her go. Siva smiles but warns that a relative's contempt cuts deeper than arrows and that attending would end in an insult equal to death.

children.topic: Sati storms off to her father's house
children.note: Overcome by anger and grief, she leaves Siva and heads to the sacrifice despite his warning. (SB 4.4 3)
Sati contrasts Daksa the fault-finder with Siva, who overlooks faults and praises any good quality. (SB 4.4 12)
Sati says the very name 'si-va' cleanses all sin, and only Daksa could envy such a pure being. (SB 4.4 14)
One hearing a guru blasphemed should block the ears and leave, or if able, punish the offender. (SB 4.4 17)

children.topic: Vomit poisoned food, discard this body
children.note: Sati resolves to give up the body received from a blasphemer, as one expels poison. (SB 4.4 18)
Meditating on Siva's feet, she is purified of all sin and consumes her body by the inner fire. (SB 4.4 27)

Torn, Sati goes to Daksa's sacrifice with Siva's attendants. Only her mother and sisters greet her; seeing no offering for Siva, she publicly rebukes her father, condemns her body born of him, and burns it in yogic fire. Bhrgu's Rbhus drive off Siva's ghosts.

children.topic: 5 · Frustration of the Sacrifice of Dakṣa

children.note: In fury Siva bites his lip, laughs like a madman and dashes a lightning-bright hair to the ground. (SB 4.5 2)

children.topic: Order: kill Daksa and his soldiers
children.note: The newborn giant asks his task and Siva names him chief of his associates and sends him to the sacrifice. (SB 4.5 4)
Daksa's wife declares the calamity is his doing, since innocent Sati died as her sisters watched. (SB 4.5 9)
Virabhadra blinds Bhaga, who had winked approval while Bhrgu cursed Siva. (SB 4.5 20)

children.topic: Teeth of Daksa and Pusa knocked out
children.note: Those who bared their teeth cursing or smiling at Siva lose them, as Baladeva once did to Dantavakra. (SB 4.5 21)
Unable to cut Daksa's neck by weapon or mantra, Virabhadra uses the animal-killing device. (SB 4.5 24)

Hearing of Sati's death from Narada, Siva tears out a hair and creates the giant Virabhadra, ordering him to destroy Daksa's sacrifice. Siva's hosts wreck the arena, maim Bhrgu, Bhaga and Pusa, and Virabhadra beheads Daksa on the animal-slaughter block.

children.topic: No happiness from offending the great
children.note: Brahma tells the demigods that blaspheming an exalted soul spoils any sacrifice they perform. (SB 4.6 4)

children.topic: Fall at Siva's feet without reservation
children.note: Brahma advises sincere surrender to Siva as the way to win his pleasure. (SB 4.6 5)

children.topic: Siva grave as time, free of anger
children.note: The demigods find Siva seated under the great banyan, serene and having given up wrath. (SB 4.6 33)

children.topic: Creator like a spider with its web
children.note: Brahma praises Siva as one who makes, sustains and withdraws the cosmos by his own expansion. (SB 4.6 43)
Those surrendered to Siva treat all beings equally and never rage like animals. (SB 4.6 46)

children.topic: Restore Daksa, Bhaga, Bhrgu and Pusa
children.note: Brahma pleads for Daksa's life, Bhaga's eyes, Bhrgu's mustache and Pusa's teeth. (SB 4.6 51)

The battered demigods approach Brahma, who says offending Siva brings no happiness and leads them to Kailasa. After a long description of that paradise, they find Siva under a banyan; Brahma praises him and begs him to restore Daksa and finish the sacrifice.
Siva rules that Daksa's burnt head will be replaced by a goat's, and Bhaga will see through Mitra. (SB 4.7 3)
Revived, Daksa thanks Siva for correcting rather than abandoning him despite his offense. (SB 4.7 13)

children.topic: Siva's mind fixed on Vishnu's feet
children.note: Siva explains he tolerates blasphemers because his consciousness rests at the Lord's lotus feet. (SB 4.7 29)

children.topic: Chanting the name removes all obstacles
children.note: The brahmanas pray that simply chanting Vishnu's holy name overcomes every hindrance. (SB 4.7 47)

children.topic: Seeing Brahma, Vishnu, Siva as one
children.note: Vishnu tells Daksa that whoever sees no separation between the three lords and Brahman finds peace. (SB 4.7 54)
Maitreya reports Sati took birth in the Himalayan kingdom and again married Siva. (SB 4.7 58)

Siva forgives and prescribes remedies: Daksa gets a goat's head and revives, his heart cleansed. The sacrifice resumes; Vishnu appears on Garuda and all pray. Vishnu teaches Daksa that He, Brahma and Siva are one, and Sati is reborn as Parvati to rewed Siva.

children.topic: 8 · Dhruva Mahārāja Leaves Home for the Forest
Suruci: you don't belong on that lap
children.note: The stepmother tells Dhruva that being born of another womb disqualifies him from the throne. (SB 4.8 11)

children.topic: Wishing harm on others harms oneself
children.note: Suniti first teaches her son never to desire misfortune for anyone, since pain rebounds. (SB 4.8 17)
Narada advises rejoicing at superiors, pitying inferiors and befriending equals to escape misery. (SB 4.8 34)

children.topic: I want a position no one has reached
children.note: Dhruva rejects consolation and asks for a path to glory beyond his father and grandfather. (SB 4.8 37)
Narada gives the twelve-syllable mantra and directs worship with offerings according to time and place. (SB 4.8 54)
Dhruva's concentration chokes the cosmic breath, and suffocating demigods run to the Lord. (SB 4.8 80)

Five-year-old Dhruva, spurned from his father's lap by stepmother Suruci, is sent by mother Suniti to worship the Lord. Narada tests then teaches him meditation and the twelve-syllable mantra. In Madhuvana his austerity grows until the universe cannot breathe.
Seeing the boy tongue-tied, the Lord graces him with the ability to pray. (SB 4.9 4)

children.topic: Bliss of bhakti beats Brahman bliss
children.note: Dhruva declares that hearing of the Lord surpasses impersonal merging, let alone fleeting heaven. (SB 4.9 10)

children.topic: Give me the company of devotees
children.note: Dhruva asks only for association with pure devotees, by which he can cross the fiery ocean of birth. (SB 4.9 11)
Vishnu awards Dhruva the unmoving planet around which all luminaries circle like bulls at a pole. (SB 4.9 20-21)
Dhruva laments that offered anything by the Lord, he asked for trifles, like a pauper begging husks. (SB 4.9 35)

children.topic: Honor flows to the Lord's friend
children.note: All beings naturally respect one in friendship with God, as water flows downhill. (SB 4.9 47)

Vishnu appears before Dhruva, touches his conch to the boy's forehead, and Dhruva prays with new wisdom. The Lord grants him the polestar and long rule, yet Dhruva regrets asking for perishable things. He returns home to a jubilant welcome and is crowned.

children.topic: 10 · Dhruva Mahārāja’s Fight with the Yakṣas

children.note: Dhruva's unmarried brother dies hunting in the Himalayas and his mother perishes in grief. (SB 4.10 3)
Overcome by sorrow and anger, Dhruva sets out in his chariot to conquer the Yaksa city. (SB 4.10 4)

children.topic: Chariot reappears like the sun from fog
children.note: Just as the Yaksas claim victory, Dhruva emerges unharmed from the storm of weapons. (SB 4.10 15)

children.topic: Rain of blood and body parts
children.note: Yaksa illusion showers Dhruva with gore and falling torsos to terrify him. (SB 4.10 24)
Maitreya notes the Yaksas' magic creates strange visions to unsettle those lacking discernment. (SB 4.10 28)

children.topic: The holy name protects from death
children.note: The sages assure Dhruva that chanting the Lord's name, as powerful as the Lord, saves from fierce death. (SB 4.10 30)

Dhruva marries and has children; his brother Uttama is killed by a Yaksa. Grieving and furious, Dhruva attacks Alakapuri, routs 130,000 Yaksas with his arrows, then is engulfed by their sorcery of blood rain and monsters until sages bless him with the Name.

children.topic: 11 · Svāyambhuva Manu Advises Dhruva Mahārāja to Stop Fighting

children.note: The moment the weapon is fixed, the Yaksa sorcery vanishes like pain when one knows the self. (SB 4.11 2)
Manu tells his grandson that needless rage is hellish and he has overstepped by killing the innocent. (SB 4.11 7)
The Lord is pleased when His devotee greets others with these four qualities. (SB 4.11 13)

children.topic: He kills yet is not the killer
children.note: Through time the Lord moves the modes; He seems to act but only His power works. (SB 4.11 18)

children.topic: The Yaksas did not kill your brother
children.note: Manu explains that birth and death come from the Supreme cause, not from these Yaksas. (SB 4.11 24)

children.topic: Anger, the chief enemy of realization
children.note: Manu prescribes his words as medicine and urges Dhruva to master wrath above all. (SB 4.11 31)

Dhruva fires the narayanastra, dispelling the illusion and slaughtering Yaksas. Svayambhuva Manu arrives with sages and stops him: the innocent must not die for one offender, anger is the path to hell, time alone kills, and Dhruva must appease Kuvera.

children.topic: 12 · Dhruva Mahārāja Goes Back to Godhead

children.note: Kuvera tells Dhruva neither he nor the Yaksas truly killed anyone; eternal time is the cause. (SB 4.12 3)

children.topic: Boon: unflinching remembrance of the Lord
children.note: Offered anything, Dhruva asks only for constant faith and memory of God to cross ignorance. (SB 4.12 8)

children.topic: Foot on the head of death
children.note: Boarding the celestial plane, Dhruva calmly steps on personified death as a stair. (SB 4.12 30)

children.topic: Mother Suniti follows in another plane
children.note: When Dhruva worries about leaving his mother, the associates show her ascending too. (SB 4.12 33)
Only those who constantly work for others' welfare can reach the self-luminous spiritual planets. (SB 4.12 36)
Narada marvels that five-year-old Dhruva defeated the Lord by the qualities of a devotee. (SB 4.12 42)

Kuvera blesses Dhruva, who asks only for steady remembrance of the Lord. Dhruva rules 36,000 years, retires to Badarikasrama, and in trance is fetched by Nanda and Sunanda in a Vaikuntha plane. He steps on death's head, sees his mother follow, reaches Vishnu.

children.topic: 13 · Description of the Descendants of Dhruva Mahārāja
Utkala liberated by the fire of bhakti
children.note: Dhruva's son Utkala lives in inner bliss, seeing only the Lord everywhere, and refuses the throne because devotion has burned away all material interest. (SB 4.13 8-9)
Utkala looks dull, deaf and crazy to shallow observers, but he is really like fire hidden under ashes, blazing within. (SB 4.13 10)

children.topic: Sages curse Vena, churn out Prithu
children.note: A sage's curse strikes like lightning; after Vena dies and chaos spreads, the sages churn his arm and Vishnu's partial form appears as Prithu. (SB 4.13 19-20)
The priests tell Anga that once Vishnu, the real enjoyer of sacrifice, is invited, every demigod comes along and accepts his share. (SB 4.13 33)

children.topic: A bad son destroys a home
children.note: Anga reflects that a sinful son ruins reputation, breeds quarrel in the household and leaves the parents in endless anxiety. (SB 4.13 44)

children.topic: Why a bad son can be better
children.note: Anga concludes a good son ties one to home while a bad son makes home hellish, so a wise man is easily detached from it. (SB 4.13 46)

Maitreya traces Dhruva's line: his son Utkala renounces the throne as a hidden saint, and the family runs down to the good King Anga, who gets the cruel son Vena through a sacrifice and, sickened by him, abandons his kingdom for the forest.

children.topic: Citizens like ants on a burning log
children.note: The sages see the people trapped between a tyrant king on one side and thieves on the other, with nowhere safe to turn. (SB 4.14 8)
A ruler is pious when his citizens follow varnashrama and worship the Supreme Lord through their own occupations. (SB 4.14 18)

children.topic: Please Vishnu and nothing is impossible
children.note: The sages explain that when the Lord served by all demigods is satisfied, every goal is reached, so the king should keep the yajnas going. (SB 4.14 20)

children.topic: Vena: all gods live in me
children.note: Vena claims that Vishnu, Brahma, Shiva, Indra and every other deity reside within the king's body, so he alone deserves the first offerings. (SB 4.14 26-27)
Already spiritually dead by blaspheming Vishnu, Vena is slain by the sages simply through their thunderous, angry speech. (SB 4.14 34)

children.topic: A brahmana must not neglect the poor
children.note: Even a peaceful, impartial brahmana loses spiritual power if he ignores suffering people, like water draining from a cracked pot. (SB 4.14 41)
Srila Prabhupada's recorded class: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 4.14.14. Tap the link to read the transcript and play the audio.
Recorded classes on this chapter, with transcript and audio on vedabase.io. Oldest first.

The sages crown Vena, who bans all sacrifice and demands worship of himself as the only god. When he mocks their advice and insults Vishnu, they slay him with a sound-curse. Later they churn his thigh and the dwarf Nishada is born, absorbing Vena's sins.

children.topic: Vishnu and Lakshmi born from Vena's arms
children.note: The sages recognise the male as an expansion of Vishnu's maintaining power and the female as the goddess of fortune who never leaves Him. (SB 4.15 3)

children.topic: Brahma reads the marks on Prithu's palm
children.note: Seeing Vishnu's disc-line on the right hand and lotuses on the soles, Brahma confirms Prithu is a partial incarnation of the Lord. (SB 4.15 9-10)

children.topic: Gifts from Brahma, Sarasvati, Vishnu, Lakshmi
children.note: The highest deities arm the new king with spiritual knowledge, a transcendental necklace, the Sudarshana disc and unending opulence. (SB 4.15 16)

children.topic: Prithu declines praise he has not earned
children.note: The king tells the reciters their praises do not fit him yet and would be better spent on someone who truly has those qualities. (SB 4.15 22)
Prithu argues that being praised for qualities one lacks is really an insult, and a fool who enjoys such praise is cheated. (SB 4.15 24)

Churning Vena's arms, the sages produce Prithu and Arci, partial forms of Vishnu and Lakshmi. Brahma sees Vishnu's marks on his palm, demigods shower gifts at his coronation, and Prithu refuses the reciters' praise since he has not yet earned it.

children.topic: 16 · Praise of King Pṛthu by the Professional Reciters

children.note: Prithu will spread mercy evenly like sunshine, and collect taxes only to return them in times of need, as the sun draws water and gives rain. (SB 4.16 6)
Even if a poor citizen tramples on the king's authority, Prithu will forgive him, patient as the earth that bears everything. (SB 4.16 7)

children.topic: Impartial even toward his own son
children.note: Prithu will punish his own son if guilty and spare an enemy's son if innocent, never bending justice for family. (SB 4.16 13)
The king will honour all women as mothers, treat his wife as half of himself, father his citizens and serve the Lord's preachers. (SB 4.16 17)

children.topic: Milking the earth, leveling the hills
children.note: The reciters foretell that Prithu will treat the earth as a cow to feed his people and flatten its surface with his bow like Indra's thunderbolt. (SB 4.16 22)
Prithu will perform a hundred ashvamedhas at the Sarasvati, and during the last one Indra will steal the horse. (SB 4.16 24)

Pleased by Prithu's humility, the reciters praise him as Vishnu's incarnation and foretell his reign: impartial like the sun, tolerant as the earth, milking the earth-cow, a hundred horse sacrifices, Indra's theft of the horse, and lessons from Sanat-kumara.

children.topic: 17 · Mahārāja Pṛthu Becomes Angry at the Earth
Starving citizens appeal to their king
children.note: Drying up like a tree burning from inside, the people tell Prithu he is both king and God's incarnation and must arrange their food and livelihood. (SB 4.17 10-11)

children.topic: Earth: I am the boat carrying everything
children.note: The cow-shaped earth warns Prithu that if he breaks her apart, he and his subjects will have nothing left to stand on. (SB 4.17 21)
The king charges the earth with taking her share of sacrifices while hiding the grains, so her disobedience deserves death. (SB 4.17 22)

children.topic: Killing the selfish is not killing
children.note: Prithu states that a ruler may execute anyone, of any sex, who lives only for himself without compassion, and it counts as no crime. (SB 4.17 26)

children.topic: You once lifted me as the boar
children.note: The earth reminds the Lord that in His boar form He raised her from the universal waters and created everything for the world's maintenance. (SB 4.17 34)
Made of the Lord's own energy, the earth admits she cannot grasp His contradictory activities, or even those of His devotees. (SB 4.17 36)

Vidura asks how the earth became a cow. Starving citizens beg Prithu for food; he aims his bow at the earth, who flees as a cow, pleads that she is a woman and the boat carrying everything, then surrenders with prayers recognizing him as Vishnu.

children.topic: 18 · Pṛthu Mahārāja Milks the Earth Planet

children.note: The earth asks Prithu to hear her patiently, since a wise person takes useful knowledge from any source, however humble. (SB 4.18 2)

children.topic: Mental speculators fail again and again
children.note: One who invents his own methods and rejects the sages' proven directions is repeatedly frustrated in his attempts. (SB 4.18 5)

children.topic: Why the earth hid her grains
children.note: Because kings stopped punishing thieves who used grain for sense enjoyment instead of sacrifice, the earth withheld her seeds. (SB 4.18 7)

children.topic: Bring a calf, a pot and a milkman
children.note: The earth tells Prithu how to draw milk from her: provide a suitable calf so her affection flows, plus a vessel and someone to milk. (SB 4.18 9-10)

children.topic: Manu as calf, grains as milk
children.note: Accepting her words, Prithu turns Svayambhuva Manu into a calf and milks every herb and grain from the earth into his cupped hands. (SB 4.18 12)
Before Prithu, settlements were haphazard; from his reign cities, villages and pastures were laid out by design. (SB 4.18 32)

The earth calms Prithu: follow the sages' methods, bring a calf, pot and milker. Prithu makes Manu the calf and milks out all grains; sages, demigods, demons, animals and mountains each milk their own needs. He then levels the earth and founds planned towns.

children.topic: 19 · King Pṛthu’s One Hundred Horse Sacrifices
Sacrifice makes the land a wish-cow
children.note: During Prithu's yajna the whole earth becomes like a kama-dhenu, supplying every daily need of life through sacrifice. (SB 4.19 7)
To steal the horse, Indra dresses as a liberated sage; the sage Atri sees through this cheating display of piety. (SB 4.19 12)
Vijitasva recovers the horse, and Maitreya notes that fake renunciants in the world today copy the costumes Indra invented then. (SB 4.19 22)

children.topic: Only sacrificial animals may be killed
children.note: When Prithu rises to kill Indra, the priests remind him that in a yajna only the sanctioned animals may be slain. (SB 4.19 27)
Brahma tells Prithu not to grieve over reversals arranged by destiny, since struggling against them drags one deeper into materialism. (SB 4.19 34)
Brahma urges Prithu, as Vishnu's incarnation, to halt the sacrifices so Indra's irreligious inventions do not multiply. (SB 4.19 38)

Prithu begins a hundred horse sacrifices; envious Indra twice steals the horse disguised as a false sannyasi. Prithu's son Vijitasva recovers it, Prithu moves to kill Indra, but Brahma halts everything at ninety-nine sacrifices and makes peace.

children.topic: 20 · Lord Viṣṇu’s Appearance in the Sacrificial Arena of Mahārāja Pṛthu
The truly advanced are never malicious
children.note: Vishnu says the best humans work for others' welfare and never harbour malice, because they know the soul is different from the body. (SB 4.20 3)

children.topic: The king shares one sixth of piety
children.note: A ruler who protects his people earns a sixth of their pious credit, but one who only taxes them inherits their sins instead. (SB 4.20 14)
The Lord, charmed by Prithu's behaviour, offers any boon and says He stays in the heart of one who is equipoised in all conditions. (SB 4.20 16)

children.topic: A million ears to hear Your glories
children.note: Prithu rejects liberation by merging and asks only for a million ears to hear about the Lord's feet from pure devotees. (SB 4.20 24)

children.topic: Only an animal leaves devotee association
children.note: Whoever once hears the Lord's glories among pure devotees and still leaves their company is no better than an animal. (SB 4.20 26)

children.topic: Give me what a father would give
children.note: Prithu asks the Lord not to offer material boons but to bestow whatever He judges best, as a father cares for a son unasked. (SB 4.20 31)

Vishnu appears with Indra after the ninety-ninth sacrifice, asks Prithu to forgive him, and teaches him to rule with equal vision beyond bodily identity. Prithu embraces Indra, refuses merging into God and begs instead for a million ears to hear His glories.
A king who collects revenue but fails to train citizens in their duties takes on their sins and loses his own fortune. (SB 4.21 24)

children.topic: Serving the Lord cleans lifetimes of dirt
children.note: The urge to serve the Lord's feet washes the mind like Ganges water flowing from His toes, cleansing countless births of contamination. (SB 4.21 31)

children.topic: Serve the Lord with mind, words and work
children.note: Prithu asks his citizens to offer their thoughts, speech, bodies and the fruits of their occupations to the Lord without reservation. (SB 4.21 33)
Tolerance, penance and knowledge make brahmanas and Vaishnavas more powerful than kings, so rulers must never offend them. (SB 4.21 37)

children.topic: The Lord prefers eating through devotees
children.note: Though He accepts fire offerings, the Lord enjoys food far more when it passes through the mouths of sages and devotees. (SB 4.21 41)

children.topic: A son delivers Vena from hell
children.note: The assembly confirms that the Vedic promise about a putra is proven: Prithu has rescued his cursed father Vena from the darkest hell. (SB 4.21 46)

Prithu returns to a festive capital and addresses a great assembly: a king who taxes without teaching duty inherits his citizens' sins, so all should serve the Lord through their work and honor brahmanas and Vaishnavas. All agree Prithu has delivered Vena.

children.topic: 22 · Pṛthu Mahārāja’s Meeting with the Four Kumāras
A house that shuts out devotees
children.note: However opulent, a home where the Lord's devotees are never welcomed is to be seen as a tree full of poisonous snakes. (SB 4.22 11)

children.topic: Life's goal: detach from body, attach to God
children.note: Sanat-kumara states the scriptural conclusion that human welfare lies in leaving the bodily concept and growing firm attachment to the Lord. (SB 4.22 21)
Progress requires shunning those absorbed in sense pleasure and money, and even their associates, until one cannot live without hearing about Hari. (SB 4.22 23)
The greatest obstacle to one's own interest is finding any other subject more attractive than realizing the self. (SB 4.22 32)
Of religion, wealth, pleasure and liberation, only liberation matters most, since death destroys the other three. (SB 4.22 35)

children.topic: The Lord's feet are the boat
children.note: The ocean of ignorance is full of sharks; rather than harsh austerities, simply take shelter of the Lord's feet to cross it safely. (SB 4.22 40)

The four Kumaras descend; Prithu welcomes them and asks how souls burning in material life reach the goal. Sanat-kumara prescribes hearing about the Lord, avoiding sense-enjoyers and sheltering at His feet. Prithu offers them everything and rules unattached.
Prithu disciplines speech, senses, semen and breath in the forest with no aim other than pleasing Krishna. (SB 4.23 7)
Seeing Krishna in his heart, Prithu abandons other yoga and jnana practices, realizing that only krishna-katha dispels illusion. (SB 4.23 12)

children.topic: Leaving the body as its master
children.note: Prithu hands all designations back to the Lord of maya and departs as a prabhu, freed by knowledge, renunciation and devotion. (SB 4.23 18)

children.topic: Arci served like Lakshmi serves Vishnu
children.note: The demigods' wives glorify Queen Arci for serving her husband with mind, speech and body just as the goddess of fortune serves the Lord. (SB 4.23 25)

children.topic: Wasting a human life is self-cheating
children.note: One who gets a human body, the chance for liberation, and spends it on laborious fruitive work is cheating and envying himself. (SB 4.23 28)
Regularly reading or telling Prithu's story increases unwavering attraction to the Lord's feet, the boat across ignorance. (SB 4.23 39)

Aging Prithu shares out his wealth, retires to the forest, performs severe austerities, sees the Lord in his heart and leaves the body through yoga. Queen Arci enters his pyre and reaches his destination; Maitreya lists the fruits of hearing this history.

children.topic: 24 · Chanting the Song Sung by Lord Śiva
Krishna's devotee is dearest to Shiva
children.note: Shiva declares that anyone surrendered to Krishna, the controller of nature and souls, is most dear to him. (SB 4.24 28)
A hundred lifetimes of duty may earn Brahma's post, but one directly surrendered to Vishnu goes to the spiritual world immediately. (SB 4.24 29)

children.topic: Show me the form Your devotees love
children.note: Shiva asks to see not any form but the one specially cherished by the Lord's dear devotees, which alone fully satisfies the senses. (SB 4.24 44)

children.topic: Time cannot touch the surrendered soul
children.note: Time destroys the universe with a twitch of its brow, yet it does not approach one sheltered fully at the Lord's feet. (SB 4.24 56)

children.topic: A moment with a devotee changes everything
children.note: Even a brief chance meeting with a devotee frees one from attraction to karma and jnana, let alone to the mortal demigods' boons. (SB 4.24 57)
Shiva promises that devotional service, though difficult, becomes easy for anyone who simply recites or reads this prayer of his. (SB 4.24 76)

Maitreya follows Prithu's line to King Pracinabarhi, whose ten sons, the Pracetas, meet Lord Shiva at a lotus lake. Shiva tells them Vishnu's devotees are dearest to him and teaches them his Rudra-gita prayer to the Lord, promising it brings the Lord's mercy.

children.topic: 25 · The Descriptions of the Characteristics of King Purañjana

children.note: Narada asks the king what fruitive rituals can achieve, since life's real aims, ending distress and gaining happiness, lie beyond them. (SB 4.25 4)

children.topic: Slaughtered animals wait with iron horns
children.note: Narada shows the king the animals he sacrificed hovering in the sky, ready to gore him after death for the pain he caused. (SB 4.25 8)
The story opens with a famous king whose constant companion, Avijnata, is understood by no one, a hint of the Supersoul. (SB 4.25 10)
Wandering south of the Himalayas, Puranjana finds a splendid nine-gated city with every facility, the body he will inhabit. (SB 4.25 13)

children.topic: I do not know who made me
children.note: The lady admits she knows neither her parents nor her companions' origins, only that she exists here now, the voice of blind intelligence. (SB 4.25 33)

children.topic: A pet animal dancing for its wife
children.note: Captivated by his wife, Puranjana loses his whole existence, following her orders like a trained animal against his own will. (SB 4.25 62)

Narada asks Pracinabarhi what his animal sacrifices earn and shows him the slain beasts waiting for revenge. He begins the Puranjana allegory: a king with an unknown friend finds a nine-gated city, weds its lady, and lives a hundred years led by her moods.

children.topic: 26 · King Purañjana Goes to the Forest to Hunt, and His Queen Becomes Angry

children.note: Puranjana's chariot with five horses, two wheels, three flags, one driver and eleven commanders maps the body's senses, karma, modes and mind. (SB 4.26 1-3)
Scripture allows a meat-hungry king to hunt only sanctioned animals, a regulation meant to curb the excess of passionate men. (SB 4.26 6)
Acting on one's own whims out of pride binds one to nature's modes, sending the soul up and down from stool-germ to Brahmaloka. (SB 4.26 8)

children.topic: A home without wife is a wheelless chariot
children.note: Puranjana finds his household joyless and reflects that without a devoted wife or mother the home cannot function. (SB 4.26 15)
Puranjana confesses he hunted without asking his queen, yet pleads that no woman would refuse her lusty husband, showing lust masked as regret. (SB 4.26 26)

Puranjana rides his five-horse chariot to hunt and mercilessly kills animals, an image of the body driven by the senses. Returning refreshed, he finds his queen sulking on the bare ground and flatters her back, confessing he offended her by leaving unasked.

children.topic: 27 · Attack by Caṇḍavega on the City of King Purañjana; the Character of Kālakanyā

children.note: Absorbed in his wife's charms, Puranjana loses good sense and forgets that each passing day and night cuts his lifespan without profit. (SB 4.27 3)

children.topic: Youth gone in half a moment
children.note: With a heart full of lust and sin, the king enjoys his wife and finds his fresh young life over almost instantly. (SB 4.27 5)
The Gandharva king with his 360 warriors and as many women, the days and nights of the year, plunder the city's enjoyments. (SB 4.27 13)

children.topic: The serpent fights alone for a century
children.note: The five-hooded snake, the life air, defends the city single-handed against 720 attackers for a hundred years and grows weak. (SB 4.27 16)
When Narada refuses the daughter of Time, she curses him never to stay long in one place, explaining his constant travel. (SB 4.27 22)

children.topic: Fear adopts old age as sister
children.note: The Yavana king Bhaya accepts Kalakanya as his sister and, with his brother Prajvara, plans to attack the world unseen. (SB 4.27 30)

Puranjana wastes half his life in sex, begets 1,100 sons and 110 daughters, and performs animal sacrifices. Candavega's 360 Gandharva pairs attack his city, weakening the five-hooded serpent. Kalakanya, rejected by Narada, marries Bhaya the Yavana king.

children.topic: 28 · Purañjana Becomes a Woman in the Next Life

children.note: Dragged off by the Yavana, Puranjana in ignorance still fails to remember the Supersoul, his eternal well-wisher. (SB 4.28 25)
The animals Puranjana killed in sacrifice now gore him with their horns, like axes chopping him apart. (SB 4.28 26)

children.topic: Reborn as a woman by remembering his wife
children.note: Because Puranjana dies thinking of his wife, his next birth is as a beautiful princess, the daughter of King Vidarbha. (SB 4.28 28)

children.topic: Do you not recognise Me, your friend?
children.note: The brahmana asks the grieving widow who she is and reminds her that she once consulted Him often, her eternal companion. (SB 4.28 52)

children.topic: Two swans in the Manasa lake
children.note: The Supersoul explains that He and the soul live together in the heart like two swans, yet have wandered far from their real home for ages. (SB 4.28 54)

children.topic: Man, woman or eunuch: only the body
children.note: Gender identities come from the body created by illusion, the Lord's own potency; both He and the soul are pure spirit. (SB 4.28 61)

Old age and death's soldiers wreck Puranjana's city; dragged away thinking of his wife, he is reborn as Vaidarbhi, wife of Malayadhvaja. Widowed, she meets the unknown brahmana friend who reveals they are two swans in one heart and decodes the allegory.

children.topic: 29 · Talks Between Nārada and King Prācīnabarhi

children.note: Narada reveals that Avijnata is the Supreme Lord, the soul's eternal friend, unknown because material names and qualities cannot reach Him. (SB 4.29 3)

children.topic: Body as chariot, senses as horses
children.note: The chariot is the body, horses the senses, wheels good and bad karma, flags the three modes, rope the mind, driver the intelligence. (SB 4.29 18-20)
Nobody welcomes old age, but death, the Yavana king, gladly accepts her as his sister. (SB 4.29 22)

children.topic: Only waking ends a bad dream
children.note: No new karma can cancel old karma; material life is a dream of ignorance that ends only when one awakens to Krishna consciousness. (SB 4.29 34)

children.topic: The deer between tiger and hunter
children.note: The soul enjoys the garden of family life like a grazing deer, unaware of the tiger before it and the hunter of death behind. (SB 4.29 53)
Like a caterpillar gripping a new leaf before leaving the old, the soul, driven by the mind's desires, secures its next body before death. (SB 4.29 76-77)

Narada decodes the allegory: Puranjana is the soul, the city the body, the queen intelligence, the gates the senses, Candavega time, Kalakanya old age. Only devotion ends the dream of karma; the subtle body carries one to rebirth. The king leaves for penance.

children.topic: The Lord loves their brotherly unity
children.note: Vishnu says He is pleased above all that the brothers are united in one occupation, devotional service, and invites them to ask a boon. (SB 4.30 8)

children.topic: Chant Shiva's prayers morning and evening
children.note: The Lord promises His blessings, fulfilled desires and good intelligence to anyone who offers Him Shiva's song twice daily. (SB 4.30 10)
Devotees find their service always new because the Supersoul keeps refreshing it; in that brahma-bhuta state they neither lament nor rejoice. (SB 4.30 20)
Having reached the Lord's feet, the Pracetas ask what more they could want, like a bee that never leaves the celestial tree. (SB 4.30 32)
For as long as they must wander in bodies, the Pracetas pray only for the company of those who discuss the Lord's pastimes. (SB 4.30 33)

children.topic: A moment with a devotee beats heaven
children.note: For mortals, even a moment's association with a pure devotee outweighs heavenly planets or merging into Brahman. (SB 4.30 34)

After ten thousand years chanting Shiva's song under the sea, the Pracetas see Vishnu on Garuda. He blesses their unity, gives them Marisha as wife and promises their return to Him. They pray only for devotee association; later Daksha is born from Marisha.
The Pracetas admit that attachment to household affairs nearly erased the instructions they received from Shiva and Vishnu. (SB 4.31 6)
Narada asks what use severe penance, hearing, speech, intelligence and strength are if they are not used in devotional service. (SB 4.31 11)

children.topic: Yoga, sannyasa, study: useless without Hari
children.note: Every spiritual practice, however important, achieves nothing unless it leads to understanding the Supreme Lord. (SB 4.31 12)

children.topic: Water the root, feed the tree
children.note: As watering the root nourishes every branch and feeding the stomach enlivens the limbs, worshipping the Lord satisfies all demigods. (SB 4.31 14)
Narada says the Lord is quickly pleased by kindness to all beings, satisfaction in any condition and restraint of the senses. (SB 4.31 19)

children.topic: The self-sufficient Lord depends on devotees
children.note: Though needing nothing, the Lord becomes dependent on His devotees and ignores even Lakshmi and the kings who chase her favour. (SB 4.31 22)

Retiring after ages at home, the Pracetas admit to Narada they nearly forgot Shiva's and Vishnu's teachings. Narada teaches that without devotion all austerity and learning are useless: water the root and the whole tree is fed. Enlightened, Vidura heads home.
The daughters of Manu, Daksa’s sacrifice, Dhruva Maharaja, King Prthu, the story of Puranjana and the Pracetas. 31 chapters.

children.topic: No one can defy the Lord's order
children.note: Brahma tells Priyavrata that no austerity, learning, yoga, strength, wealth or religion lets anyone, from Brahma to an ant, escape the Lord's command. (SB 5.1 12)

children.topic: The liberated soul treats karma as a dream
children.note: Even a liberated person keeps the body given by past karma but views its joys and pains as an awakened man views last night's dream. (SB 5.1 16)

children.topic: Six co-wives follow you to the forest
children.note: An uncontrolled man fears bondage even in the forest, since the mind and five senses travel with him, while a self-controlled householder is safe. (SB 5.1 17)

children.topic: Householder as king in a fortress
children.note: One who conquers mind and senses at home is like a king secure in his fort, and once lust subsides he can go anywhere without danger. (SB 5.1 18)

children.topic: One holy name frees even an outcaste
children.note: A devotee conquers hunger, thirst, grief, illusion, old age and death, and even an untouchable is freed by uttering the Lord's name once. (SB 5.1 35)

children.topic: A dancing monkey in his wife's hands
children.note: Priyavrata rebukes himself for sinking into sense enjoyment like a covered well and becoming his wife's performing monkey. (SB 5.1 37)

Pariksit asks how the devotee Priyavrata could rule and enjoy family life. Sukadeva tells how Brahma himself ordered him to take the throne; Priyavrata rules brilliantly, carves seven oceans chasing the sun, then condemns his own indulgence and renounces all.
Understanding Agnidhra's wish for a son, Brahma dispatches the finest dancing girl of his court to the prince's meditation grove. (SB 5.2 3)

children.topic: Your eyes are two feathered arrows
children.note: Agnidhra praises the Apsara's glances as shaftless, lotus-feathered arrows, admitting he cannot fight such prowess. (SB 5.2 8)
Sukadeva notes that Agnidhra, clever as a demigod, knew how to win women with sweet talk and thus gained Purvacitti's favour. (SB 5.2 17)
Still longing for Purvacitti after she leaves, Agnidhra dies thinking of her and joins her on the planet of the forefathers. (SB 5.2 22)

Agnidhra rules Jambudvipa and worships Brahma for a son. Brahma sends the Apsara Purvacitti, whom the meditating prince, mistaking her for a sage, courts with poetic praise. They live together for ages and beget nine sons who each get a region of Jambudvipa.

children.topic: 3 · Ṛṣabhadeva’s Appearance in the Womb of Merudevī, the Wife of King Nābhi

children.note: Sacrifice has seven ways to please God, yet none guarantees Him; He appears for Nabhi only out of affection for His devotee. (SB 5.3 2)

children.topic: Tulasi and water please Him most
children.note: The priests say the Lord is fully satisfied by simple offerings of tulasi leaves, water and fresh sprigs made by devotees with choked voices. (SB 5.3 6)

children.topic: Help us remember You at death
children.note: Fearing that hunger, fever or stumbling at death may blot out the Lord's name, the priests pray for His help to remember Him then. (SB 5.3 12)

children.topic: Begging a rich man for grain
children.note: Nabhi asks only for a son from the Lord who could grant heaven or liberation, like approaching a millionaire for a handful of rice. (SB 5.3 13)
The Lord says no one equals Him, yet the qualified brahmanas' words must not fail, since He regards them as His mouth. (SB 5.3 17)

children.topic: I will be born of Merudevi
children.note: Finding no equal to give Nabhi, Vishnu promises to expand Himself and appear in the womb of Merudevi. (SB 5.3 18)

King Nabhi and Merudevi worship Vishnu for a son, and the four-armed Lord appears at the sacrifice. The priests pray that He needs no rituals, ask to remember Him at death, and beg pardon for calling Him for a mere son. Vishnu agrees to be born as their child.

children.topic: 4 · The Characteristics of Ṛṣabhadeva, the Supreme Personality of Godhead

children.note: When jealous Indra withholds rain, Rishabhadeva simply smiles and by His own yoga-maya pours water on His land, Ajanabha. (SB 5.4 3)
The sages' verse honours Nabhi because his devotion moved the Supreme Lord to accept birth as his son. (SB 5.4 6)
Rishabha's eldest son Bharata, an exalted devotee, is the reason this land is called Bharata-varsha. (SB 5.4 9)

children.topic: God acting as an ordinary soul
children.note: Though eternal, blissful and untouched by birth, death, age or disease, Rishabhadeva lives as if a conditioned soul to teach by example. (SB 5.4 14)
Whatever a great personality does, ordinary people imitate, which is why the Lord teaches by His own conduct. (SB 5.4 15)
Under Rishabha's rule everyone was so satisfied and affectionate toward the king that nobody thought to ask for anything at all. (SB 5.4 18)

Rishabhadeva is born with divine marks, answers Indra's drought by raining on Ajanabha, and is enthroned by Nabhi, who retires to Badarikashrama. He models householder life, begets a hundred sons including Bharata and nine great devotees, and teaches them.

children.topic: 5 · Lord Ṛṣabhadeva’s Teachings to His Sons
Human life is not for hog-like pleasure
children.note: Rishabhadeva opens by saying a human body should be used for austerity and devotion, since sense pleasure is available even to dogs and hogs. (SB 5.5 1)

children.topic: Serving great souls opens the door to liberation
children.note: Freedom from bondage comes through serving spiritually advanced mahatmas, while keeping company with sex-minded people leads straight to hell. (SB 5.5 2)

children.topic: Ignorance keeps the soul taking new bodies
children.note: Until a person inquires into spiritual life, his karma-colored mind stays impure and he must keep accepting material bodies. (SB 5.5 5)

children.topic: Male-female attraction is the root knot
children.note: The attraction between man and woman ties the heart to body, home, property and relatives, feeding the illusion of I and mine. (SB 5.5 8)

children.topic: Do not become a guru who cannot deliver
children.note: No one should take the role of teacher, father, husband, mother or worshipable deity unless he can free his dependents from repeated birth and death. (SB 5.5 18)

children.topic: Respect every being, for I dwell within
children.note: Rishabhadeva asks his sons never to envy any creature but to honor all beings at every moment, since honoring them is honoring him. (SB 5.5 26)

Rishabhadeva tells his hundred sons that human life is for austerity and devotion, not animal-like sense pleasure, and that serving great souls opens liberation. He names Bharata as heir, then wanders as an avadhuta, silent and abused, absorbed in bliss.

children.topic: Never trust the mind, stay vigilant
children.note: Like a hunter who never trusts captured animals, advanced souls keep constant watch on the mind rather than placing faith in it. (SB 5.6 2)

children.topic: Even Shiva and Saubhari were agitated
children.note: The restless mind can cheat anyone at any moment, as shown when Shiva was stirred by Mohini and Saubhari Muni fell from yoga. (SB 5.6 3)

children.topic: The mind breeds lust, anger and fear
children.note: Lust, anger, pride, greed, grief, illusion and fear all spring from the mind, so no learned person puts faith in it. (SB 5.6 5)

children.topic: Rishabhadeva's body burns in a forest fire
children.note: While wandering near Kutakachala, a fire sparked by wind-rubbed bamboos consumes the forest and Rishabhadeva's body. (SB 5.6 8)

children.topic: King Arhat concocts a rival religion
children.note: Hearing of Rishabhadeva's ways, King Arhat imitates them and, exploiting Kali-yuga, starts an atheistic creed opposed to the Vedas. (SB 5.6 9)
Bathing in devotional service, devotees enjoy such bliss that they refuse liberation even when the Lord Himself offers it. (SB 5.6 17)
