The Lord appears before the demigods and, after Brahma's prayers, tells them to ally with the demons and churn the Milk Ocean with Mandara and Vasuki, calmly and unafraid of poison. Indra wins Bali over; when Mandara crushes both sides, God revives them.

children.topic: 7 · Lord Śiva Saves the Universe by Drinking Poison
Lord smiles and takes the snake's tail
children.note: When the proud demons demand Vasuki's head, the Lord quietly accepts and grasps the tail, the demigods following Him. (SB 8.7 4)

children.topic: The Lord becomes a tortoise to lift Mandara
children.note: As the unsupported mountain sinks, the Lord takes a wonderful tortoise form, enters the water and raises it on His back. (SB 8.7 8)

children.topic: Ocean first yields the halahala poison
children.note: The churning agitates all sea creatures and, before any nectar, produces a fiercely dangerous poison. (SB 8.7 18)
Siva tells Bhavani that shielding struggling living beings is his duty as their protector. (SB 8.7 38)

children.topic: Helping others pleases Hari, so I drink
children.note: Siva reasons that benevolent work pleases the Lord and everyone else, so he resolves to swallow the poison himself. (SB 8.7 40)

children.topic: Suffering for others is the highest worship
children.note: Great souls willingly accept pain on behalf of the people; this is called the best way to worship the Lord in every heart. (SB 8.7 44)

Churning begins with Vasuki as rope; the demons insist on the head end. Mandara sinks and the Lord lifts it as a tortoise. The ocean first yields the halahala poison, and Siva, after the demigods' prayers, drinks it out of compassion, gaining a blue throat.

children.topic: 8 · The Churning of the Milk Ocean
Laksmi rises like lightning from the ocean
children.note: The goddess of fortune, devoted only to the Lord's enjoyment, appears with a brilliance surpassing lightning on marble. (SB 8.8 8)
Surveying the assembly, Laksmi finds that austerity, knowledge and greatness all coexist with anger, desire or dependence. (SB 8.8 20)
After deliberation she accepts the Lord, who is self-sufficient and needs nothing yet owns all qualities and powers. (SB 8.8 23)
A portion of Vishnu, expert in medicine, rises from the ocean carrying a full jug of amrita. (SB 8.8 34)

children.topic: I will bewilder the demons by quarrel
children.note: When the demons grab the nectar, the Lord promises the sad demigods He will set the asuras fighting among themselves. (SB 8.8 37)
The Lord assumes the form of a supremely beautiful woman whose every feature captivates the mind, to recover the nectar. (SB 8.8 41-46)

Renewed churning yields the surabhi cow, Uccaihsrava, Airavata, gems, parijata, Apsaras and then Laksmi, who finds every candidate flawed and picks Vishnu. Varuni goes to the demons; Dhanvantari brings nectar, the demons snatch it and the Lord becomes Mohini.

children.topic: A wise man never trusts a woman
children.note: Mohini teases the demons that she is only a prostitute and asks why they place such faith in her. (SB 8.9 9)

children.topic: Accept whatever I do, fair or unfair
children.note: Holding the jug, Mohini agrees to distribute the nectar only if the demons promise to accept even a dishonest division. (SB 8.9 12)

children.topic: Nectar to demons is milk to snakes
children.note: Knowing demons are crooked by nature, the infallible Lord judges it unsafe to give them any share of the nectar. (SB 8.9 19)

children.topic: Demons charmed and cheated of their share
children.note: Mohini soothes the demons with sweet words, then pours the nectar for the demigods seated apart, freeing them from old age and death. (SB 8.9 21)
Disguised as a demigod, Rahu sips nectar; the sun and moon expose him and the Lord severs his head, which lives on as a planet. (SB 8.9 25)
Demigods and demons shared time, place and labor, but only those sheltered at the Lord's feet obtained the nectar's fruit. (SB 8.9 28)

The quarrelling demons ask Mohini to divide the nectar; she warns that women are untrustworthy, then takes it on condition they accept whatever she does. She serves only the demigods; Rahu sneaks a sip and is beheaded. The Lord reveals His form and the lesson.

children.topic: 10 · The Battle Between the Demigods and the Demons
Non-devotees churned but could not drink
children.note: Despite full effort in the churning, the demons missed the nectar because they were not devoted to Vasudeva. (SB 8.10 1)
Bali commands from the Vaihayasa craft built by Maya Danava, armed for every combat and flickering between visible and invisible. (SB 8.10 16-18)

children.topic: Duels in pairs: Bali versus Indra
children.note: The great warriors fight one on one, Bali against Indra, Karttikeya against Taraka, Varuna against Heti and so on. (SB 8.10 28)

children.topic: Bali vanishes and conjures a mountain
children.note: Losing the arrow duel, Bali resorts to demonic illusion, raising a phantom mountain over the demigod army. (SB 8.10 45)

children.topic: Illusions vanish like a dream on waking
children.note: The moment the Lord enters the field the demons' magic dissolves; simply remembering Him frees one from every danger. (SB 8.10 55)

Envious of the demigods' gain, the demons attack on the Milk Ocean's shore. Sukadeva describes both armies on exotic mounts, Bali on his Vaihayasa airplane, paired duels, and Bali's illusions of mountains, fire and flood, dispelled when Vishnu arrives.

children.topic: Indra blocks mechanical trips to heaven
children.note: Indra says he throws down those who try to reach higher planets or liberation by mystic power or machines. (SB 8.11 5)

children.topic: Time hands out fame, victory and death
children.note: Bali replies that everyone on the battlefield is under eternal time and receives victory, defeat and death in turn. (SB 8.11 7)

children.topic: The wise neither rejoice nor lament
children.note: Bali calls Indra unlearned for gloating, since those who see time's movements stay even in gain and loss. (SB 8.11 8)
Because Bali's harsh words were true, Indra took them calmly, like an elephant unbothered by its driver's goad. (SB 8.11 11)
Blessed to die by nothing wet or dry, Namuci is beheaded by Indra with foam, which is neither. (SB 8.11 40)

children.topic: Narada tells the demigods to stop fighting
children.note: Sent by Brahma, Narada reminds the demigods they have the nectar and Narayana's protection, so they should end the war. (SB 8.11 44)

Revived by the Lord, the demigods rout the demons. Indra and Bali trade rebukes on fate before Indra fells him; Jambha, Bala and Paka die, and Namuci, immune to wet and dry weapons, is slain with foam. Narada halts the slaughter; Sukracarya revives the dead.

children.topic: 12 · The Mohinī-mūrti Incarnation Bewilders Lord Śiva
Cause and effect are one, like gold
children.note: Siva declares that as ornament and mine share the same gold, the Lord and His creation are one; dualities come only from ignorance. (SB 8.12 8)

children.topic: Even Siva and Brahma are bewildered
children.note: Siva admits that he, Brahma and the sages, though born of goodness, cannot understand creation under the Lord's illusory energy. (SB 8.12 10)

children.topic: Showing the form that lusty men love
children.note: Vishnu agrees to reveal to Siva the form especially cherished by those driven by lust. (SB 8.12 16)
Exchanging glances with the ball-playing girl, Siva forgets his own identity, his wife and his companions. (SB 8.12 22)

children.topic: Siva's seed becomes gold and silver mines
children.note: Wherever Siva's semen fell during the chase, deposits of gold and silver came into being afterwards. (SB 8.12 33)

children.topic: If maya deludes me, what of others?
children.note: Siva tells Bhavani that even he, a chief expansion of the Lord, was fooled by His energy, so ordinary beings have no chance. (SB 8.12 43)

Hearing of Mohini, Siva visits Vishnu with Uma, praises Him and asks to see the female form. Vishnu vanishes and appears as a girl playing ball; Siva loses his senses and chases her, his seed becoming gold and silver mines, until he sees through the illusion.

children.topic: Vamana, youngest Aditya, in this manvantara
children.note: In the present age the Lord appears as the dwarf Vamana, son of Kasyapa and Aditi, youngest of the Adityas. (SB 8.13 6)

children.topic: Bali will be Indra in the eighth manvantara
children.note: Under Savarni Manu, Bali Maharaja, son of Virocana, will hold the post of heavenly king. (SB 8.13 12)

children.topic: Three paces cost Bali the worlds, then perfection
children.note: Bali lost everything by giving Vishnu three steps of land, but that total surrender will bring him life's perfection. (SB 8.13 13)

children.topic: Bound by love, installed in Sutala
children.note: The Lord affectionately bound Bali and placed him in Sutala, where he lives more comfortably than Indra. (SB 8.13 14)

children.topic: Fourteen Manus make one day of Brahma
children.note: The reigns of all fourteen Manus together span a thousand yuga cycles, one kalpa or day of Brahma. (SB 8.13 36)

Sukadeva names the seventh Manu Sraddhadeva's sons, sages and Indra, and the Lord's advent as Vamana. He previews Manus eight to fourteen with their demigods, sages and partial incarnations, noting Bali as the next Indra. Fourteen Manus fill one day of Brahma.

children.topic: The Lord appoints Manus, Indras and sages
children.note: All universal administrators receive their posts from the Supreme Lord in incarnations such as Yajna. (SB 8.14 2)

children.topic: One Lord teaches knowledge, karma and yoga
children.note: Hari appears as Siddhas like Sanaka, sages like Yajnavalkya and yogis like Dattatreya to teach the different paths. (SB 8.14 8)
Bewildered by maya, people research and philosophize to find the Absolute Truth, yet they cannot see Him that way. (SB 8.14 10)

Pariksit asks who directs the Manus. Sukadeva explains that the Lord's incarnations like Yajna appoint Manus, sages, Indras and demigods, who restore dharma each cycle, while the Lord Himself teaches as Sanaka, Yajnavalkya and Dattatreya and acts as king.

children.topic: 15 · Bali Mahārāja Conquers the Heavenly Planets
Why beg like a pauper, then arrest?
children.note: Pariksit wants to know why the owner of everything asked Bali for three paces and still bound him after receiving the gift. (SB 8.15 1-2)

children.topic: Chariot and horses rise from the sacrificial fire
children.note: From the Visvajit yajna emerge a gold-covered chariot, horses like Indra's and a lion-marked flag for Bali. (SB 8.15 5)

children.topic: No sinner or envious person enters Indra's city
children.note: Indrapuri's residents are free of envy, violence, pride, lust and greed; no one with such faults can enter. (SB 8.15 22)

children.topic: Only the Lord can defeat brahma-tejas
children.note: Brhaspati tells Indra that Bali, empowered by the Bhrgu brahmanas, can be conquered by no one but the Supreme Lord. (SB 8.15 29)

children.topic: He will fall when he insults the brahmanas
children.note: Brhaspati foresees that Bali's brahmana-given power will vanish, with his allies, once he offends those same brahmanas. (SB 8.15 31)

Pariksit asks why the Lord begged land from Bali then bound him. Sukadeva begins: revived by Sukracarya, Bali performs the Visvajit sacrifice, gains a celestial chariot and weapons, and marches on Indra's glorious city. The demigods flee; Bali rules all.

children.topic: 16 · Executing the Payo-vrata Process of Worship
A home that turns guests away
children.note: Kasyapa warns that a household where a guest leaves without even water is no better than a jackal's hole in a field. (SB 8.16 7)

children.topic: Illusion binds the world through children
children.note: Hearing Aditi's plea, Kasyapa smiles at how Vishnu's maya ties the whole world through parental love. (SB 8.16 18)

children.topic: Worship Vasudeva, the giver of all good
children.note: Kasyapa directs Aditi to serve the Lord in everyone's heart, since only He can bring real blessings and defeat all enemies. (SB 8.16 20)

children.topic: Devotion never fails; other paths are useless
children.note: Kasyapa's verdict: bhakti to the Lord infallibly grants one's desires, and every other method is a waste of effort. (SB 8.16 21)
Prasada must reach the poor, the blind, non-devotees and outcastes alike, because the Lord is pleased when all are fed. (SB 8.16 56)

children.topic: Payo-vrata: the sacrifice containing all sacrifices
children.note: This vow is called sarva-yajna because performing it accomplishes every other sacrifice, austerity and charity at once. (SB 8.16 60)

Aditi grieves that the demons have driven her sons from heaven. Kasyapa tells her only Vishnu's devotional service can help and teaches her the payo-vrata: twelve days on milk alone, worshiping Keshava with mantras, feasts for brahmanas and prasada for all.

children.topic: 17 · The Supreme Lord Agrees to Become Aditi’s Son
A pleased Lord gives everything, easily
children.note: Aditi prays that when the Lord is satisfied, long life, wealth, knowledge and mystic powers come easily, so defeating rivals is trivial. (SB 8.17 10)
The Lord explains that force will not work now because the demon chiefs are protected by brahmanas whom He always favors. (SB 8.17 16)

children.topic: Worship of Me is never wasted
children.note: Because Aditi's vow has pleased Him, the Lord vows to find a way to help her, since His worship always bears fruit. (SB 8.17 17)
The Lord agrees to take birth from Aditi, crediting Kasyapa's austerity, in order to protect her other sons, the demigods. (SB 8.17 18)
The Lord tells Aditi not to reveal His promise to anyone, since confidential plans succeed when kept quiet. (SB 8.17 20)

children.topic: The Lord, sole boat for drowning demigods
children.note: Brahma prays that just as a boat saves a drowning man, the Lord alone can shelter the demigods stripped of heaven. (SB 8.17 28)

Aditi performs the payo-vrata with full concentration and Vishnu appears before her. Reading her heart, He promises to be born as her son through Kasyapa to restore the demigods, and Brahma prays to the Lord now within Aditi's womb.
The Lord appears at the auspicious Abhijit moment in the month of Bhadra, and all the planets turn charitable. (SB 8.18 5)

children.topic: Vishnu becomes Vamana like an actor
children.note: Having shown His eternal four-armed form, the Lord takes the role of a brahmana dwarf before His parents' eyes. (SB 8.18 12)

children.topic: Vamana's first alms from mother Bhagavati
children.note: At the thread ceremony Kuvera gives the begging pot and Shiva's consort personally offers the Lord His first alms. (SB 8.18 17)

children.topic: Earth sinks under the dwarf's footsteps
children.note: Hearing of Bali's sacrifice, Vamana sets out to bless him, and the ground gives way beneath each of His steps. (SB 8.18 20)

children.topic: Bali follows Shiva, takes foot-water on his head
children.note: Knowing that Shiva carries the Ganges from Vishnu's toe, Bali reverently places the Lord's foot-washing water on his own head. (SB 8.18 28)
Bali offers Vamana cows, gold, houses, villages, elephants, even a bride, sensing the boy has come to ask for something. (SB 8.18 32)

Vishnu appears from Aditi's womb in His four-armed form, then becomes Vamana, a dwarf brahmacari. After His sacred thread ceremony He walks to Bali's ashvamedha at Bhrigukaccha, where the delighted Bali washes His feet and offers Him anything He wants.

children.topic: 19 · Lord Vāmanadeva Begs Charity from Bali Mahārāja

children.note: Chased by the demon, Vishnu decides to enter his enemy's own heart, where a man who sees only outward cannot find Him. (SB 8.19 9)

children.topic: Three paces of land is all I ask
children.note: Vamana requests from the munificent king only as much ground as three of His own small steps can cover. (SB 8.19 16)

children.topic: Three worlds cannot fill uncontrolled senses
children.note: Vamana replies that a person without self-control stays hungry even after owning everything in the three worlds. (SB 8.19 21)
One should accept what fate provides, because discontent never leads to happiness even for the ruler of three worlds. (SB 8.19 24)
A contented brahmana grows in spiritual strength, while a greedy one loses it like fire sprinkled with water. (SB 8.19 26)
Sukracarya reveals to Bali that the brahmacari is the Supreme Lord born of Kasyapa and Aditi to serve the demigods. (SB 8.19 30)

Vamana praises Bali's generous family, recalls Hiranyaksha and Hiranyakasipu, and asks for just three paces of land, teaching that greed can never be satisfied. Bali agrees, but Sukracarya warns that the dwarf is Vishnu and argues that a promise may be broken.

children.topic: Earth can bear anything but a liar
children.note: Bali insists no sin equals falsehood, quoting mother earth, who can carry any weight except an untruthful man. (SB 8.20 4)

children.topic: Cheating a brahmana worse than hell
children.note: Bali fears neither hell, poverty nor death as much as he fears deceiving a brahmana who has come to beg. (SB 8.20 5)

children.topic: Give now what death will take anyway
children.note: Since death strips everyone of wealth, Bali reasons it is wiser to please the Lord with riches he must lose regardless. (SB 8.20 6)

children.topic: Blessing or punishment, I obey Vishnu
children.note: Bali resolves to give the land whether Vishnu has come to bless him or to punish him as an enemy. (SB 8.20 11)

children.topic: Heaven praises Bali's gift to his enemy
children.note: The Gandharvas and Kinnaras celebrate that Bali gave all three worlds knowing Vishnu was on his rivals' side. (SB 8.20 20)

children.topic: Second step covers heaven; nothing left
children.note: Vamana's second stride spans the higher planets up to Satyaloka, so no place remains for the promised third step. (SB 8.20 34)

Bali refuses to break his word even to Vishnu, saying nothing is worse than a lie; Sukracarya curses him. Bali offers the land, and Vamana expands into the universal form, covering earth with one step and heaven with the second, leaving nowhere for the third.

children.topic: 21 · Bali Mahārāja Arrested by the Lord

children.note: Water from Brahma's pot that bathed the Lord's feet becomes the Ganges, flowing from the sky to purify all three worlds. (SB 8.21 4)
Bali's followers decide that slaying the disguised Vishnu is their duty and take up weapons against Him. (SB 8.21 13)

children.topic: No effort can overrule the Supreme
children.note: Bali tells his soldiers that human power cannot defeat the Lord who grants happiness and distress to everyone. (SB 8.21 20)

children.topic: Time cannot be beaten by any means
children.note: Neither armies, counsel, diplomacy, forts, mantras nor herbs can overcome the time factor that represents the Lord. (SB 8.21 22)

children.topic: Garuda arrests Bali with Varuna's ropes
children.note: After the sacrifice ends, Garuda understands his master's wish and binds the demon king. (SB 8.21 26)

children.topic: Where shall I place My third step?
children.note: Vamana points out that two steps have covered the universe and asks Bali to think where the third can go. (SB 8.21 29)

Brahma washes Vamana's foot, producing the Ganges, and the demigods worship Him. Bali's demons attack but are beaten by Vishnu's associates; Bali stops them, saying time now favors the gods. Garuda binds Bali, and Vamana demands his third step.

children.topic: Place Your third step on my head
children.note: Bali asks Vamana to complete the promise by stepping on his head so that his word will not become false. (SB 8.22 2)
Bali says losing wealth, going to hell or being bound troubles him less than the shame of a broken promise. (SB 8.22 3)
Prahlada praises the Lord for both raising Bali to heaven and removing his wealth, since opulence had darkened his vision. (SB 8.22 16)

children.topic: Opulence makes even the wise forget
children.note: Prahlada observes that material wealth bewilders even learned, self-controlled men away from self-realization. (SB 8.22 17)

children.topic: I favor a man by taking everything
children.note: The Lord tells Brahma that wealth makes fools proud and defiant, so His special mercy is to remove their possessions first. (SB 8.22 24)

children.topic: Bali will be Indra under Savarni Manu
children.note: For his tolerance the Lord grants Bali a post the demigods cannot reach: heaven's throne in the next manvantara. (SB 8.22 31)

Bound Bali offers his head for the third step, fearing only dishonor. Prahlada and Vindhyavali arrive; Brahma asks for his release. The Lord explains He strips wealth from those He favors, then grants Bali Sutala and future kingship of heaven.

children.topic: 23 · The Demigods Regain the Heavenly Planets
Even an attempted bow bears fruit
children.note: Bali marvels that his mere attempt to offer obeisances brought a mercy never given to the demigods themselves. (SB 8.23 2)

children.topic: Causeless mercy on a family of demons
children.note: Prahlada asks how rogues born among demons received the Lord's grace, answering that His mercy needs no cause. (SB 8.23 7)

children.topic: The Lord is like a desire tree
children.note: Prahlada explains that favoring devotees is not partiality; the Lord responds to each according to what they seek. (SB 8.23 8)

children.topic: The holy name makes all faultless
children.note: Sukracarya declares that errors in mantras, time, place or paraphernalia vanish when the Lord's name is chanted. (SB 8.23 16)

children.topic: Vamana hands the worlds back to Indra
children.note: Having begged all of Bali's land, the Lord returns to His brother Indra everything the demons had taken. (SB 8.23 19)

children.topic: Hearing of incarnations leads back to Godhead
children.note: Sukadeva promises that hearing the Lord's uncommon deeds raises one to heaven or even to the spiritual world. (SB 8.23 30)

Bali is released and enters Sutala with Prahlada, who marvels at the Lord's mercy on demons. Sukracarya says chanting the holy name removes all sacrificial faults. Vamana returns heaven to Indra, and the demigods accept Upendra as their protector.
The Lord descends to protect cows, brahmanas, demigods, devotees, the Vedas and the principles of religion. (SB 8.24 5)

children.topic: Transcendental in any form, like air
children.note: Whether appearing human or animal, the Lord stays above the modes, just as air is unchanged by what it passes through. (SB 8.24 6)

children.topic: Do not throw Me to the sharks
children.note: The little fish begs the merciful king not to drop Him back into the river where larger creatures could eat Him. (SB 8.24 14)

children.topic: Tie the boat to My horn with Vasuki
children.note: The Lord instructs Satyavrata to fasten the ark to His horn using the serpent Vasuki when the flood winds toss it. (SB 8.24 36)
Satyavrata prays that people ignorant of life's goal choose fools as teachers, while he accepts the all-seeing Lord. (SB 8.24 50)
Sukadeva closes by bowing to the Lord who posed as a fish, restored the Vedas to Brahma and taught Satyavrata. (SB 8.24 61)

Pariksit asks why the Lord became a fish. Sukadeva tells how Hayagriva stole the Vedas and how a tiny fish in Satyavrata's palms outgrew every reservoir, then warned of a flood. Tied by Vasuki to a boat, the king hears the Lord's teachings in the deluge.
The Manus, Gajendra the elephant, the churning of the ocean, Mohini, Bali Maharaja and Vamana, and Matsya the fish. 24 chapters.

children.topic: Only the Lord existed before creation
children.note: Sukadeva begins the dynasty by recalling that at the end of the previous age nothing but the Supreme Person remained. (SB 9.1 8)

children.topic: A daughter instead of a son
children.note: Because the priest was distracted by Sraddha's wish, Manu's sacrifice produced Ila, and Manu questioned his guru. (SB 9.1 16)
Pleased with Vasistha's prayers, the Lord changes the girl into a fine prince named Sudyumna. (SB 9.1 22)
The moment Sudyumna enters the Sukumara forest at Meru's base, he and his horse change into female forms. (SB 9.1 26)

children.topic: Shiva's vow: any male becomes female
children.note: To please Parvati after sages walked in on them, Shiva declared that every man entering the forest would turn into a woman. (SB 9.1 32)

children.topic: Male one month, female the next
children.note: Satisfied by Vasistha yet bound by his word, Shiva lets Sudyumna alternate sex each month and rule the kingdom. (SB 9.1 38-39)

Pariksit asks about Vaivasvata Manu's dynasty. A priest's error gives Manu a daughter, Ila, whom Vasistha turns into Sudyumna. Entering Shiva's forbidden forest, Sudyumna becomes a woman, bears Pururava to Budha, then alternates sex monthly by Shiva's grace.

children.topic: 2 · The Dynasties of the Sons of Manu
Prsadhra beheads the cow by mistake
children.note: Rushing at a tiger in the dark, the cowherd prince swings his sword and cuts off the cow's head instead. (SB 9.2 5-6)

children.topic: Vasistha curses him to shudra birth
children.note: Though the killing was unintentional, the family priest condemns Prsadhra to lose his kshatriya status in the next life. (SB 9.2 9)

children.topic: Accepting the curse with folded hands
children.note: Prsadhra neither argues nor laments; he bows to his guru's words and takes up lifelong celibacy. (SB 9.2 10)

children.topic: A saint enters the forest fire
children.note: Fully absorbed in the Lord, Prsadhra uses a blazing forest fire to give up his body and reach the spiritual world. (SB 9.2 14)

children.topic: Kavi renounces the kingdom in youth
children.note: Manu's youngest son leaves for the forest before adulthood, meditating on the Lord within his heart until perfection. (SB 9.2 15)

Sukadeva traces Manu's sons. Prsadhra, guarding cows at night, mistakenly kills a cow and is cursed to shudra birth, but accepts it, becomes a devotee and leaves his body in a forest fire. Kavi renounces early; the lines of Karusa, Narisyanta and Dista follow.

children.topic: 3 · The Marriage of Sukanyā and Cyavana Muni

children.note: Not knowing they are the sage's eyes in an anthill, the girl pricks the luminous points with a thorn and they bleed. (SB 9.3 4)
Sukanya adapts to the irritable old sage's moods and serves him attentively without confusion. (SB 9.3 10)

children.topic: Three identical youths rise from the lake
children.note: Cyavana and the two Ashvini-kumaras emerge equally beautiful, dressed alike with earrings and lotus garlands. (SB 9.3 15)

children.topic: This young man is your son-in-law
children.note: Rebuked as unchaste, Sukanya smiles and tells her father the handsome youth beside her is Cyavana himself. (SB 9.3 22)
When Indra tries to strike the sage for offering soma to the Ashvinis, Cyavana freezes his raised arm. (SB 9.3 25)
Brahma laughs and tells Kakudmi that every suitor he had in mind, and their descendants, died ages ago. (SB 9.3 32)

Princess Sukanya pierces the glowing eyes of aged Cyavana Muni and is given to him in marriage. The Ashvini-kumaras restore his youth, she picks him out from the identical trio, and her father is amazed. Revata's son Kakudmi later gives Revati to Balarama.

children.topic: 4 · Ambarīṣa Mahārāja Offended by Durvāsā Muni
Every sense engaged in Krishna's service
children.note: Ambarisa uses mind, words, hands, ears, eyes, touch, smell, tongue and legs only in activities connected with the Lord. (SB 9.4 18-20)

children.topic: Water: both eating and not eating
children.note: Consulting brahmanas, the king breaks the fast with water alone to honor Dvadashi without dishonoring his guest. (SB 9.4 39-40)
The Lord's disc, standing guard for the devotee, incinerates the fiery creature as a forest fire destroys a snake. (SB 9.4 48)

children.topic: I am controlled by My devotees
children.note: Vishnu tells Durvasa He is not independent: He lives in the hearts of desireless devotees and loves even their devotees. (SB 9.4 63)

children.topic: Devotee in My heart, I in his
children.note: The Lord declares that pure devotees know nothing but Him, and He likewise knows no one but them. (SB 9.4 68)

children.topic: Austerity is dangerous in an ungentle man
children.note: Vishnu warns that learning and penance, though auspicious, become harmful when held by someone lacking gentleness. (SB 9.4 70)

After Nabhaga's story, Sukadeva describes King Ambarisa, who engages every sense for Krishna. He breaks a Dvadashi fast with water before Durvasa eats; the sage's demon is burnt by the Sudarsana disc, which then chases Durvasa to Brahma, Shiva and Vishnu.
Ambarisa asks the disc, the Lord's weapon against the envious, to show mercy to Durvasa for his whole family's sake. (SB 9.5 9)

children.topic: My family's merit in exchange for his relief
children.note: The king offers all the piety of his dynasty's charity and sacrifices to free the sage from the burning. (SB 9.5 10)

children.topic: Today I saw a devotee's greatness
children.note: Durvasa admits that though he offended the king, Ambarisa prayed for his welfare, revealing what devotees are. (SB 9.5 14)
Durvasa asks what could be impossible for the Lord's servants, when merely hearing His name cleanses a person. (SB 9.5 16)

children.topic: One year on water, no credit taken
children.note: After feeding the returned sage, Ambarisa sees his own power came from the Lord and claims nothing for himself. (SB 9.5 24)

children.topic: Remembering Ambarisa makes one a devotee
children.note: Sukadeva promises that anyone who recites or even thinks of this story becomes a pure devotee. (SB 9.5 27)

Durvasa falls at Ambarisa's feet; the king prays to the Sudarsana disc, which stops burning the sage. Durvasa praises the devotee's greatness, eats and blesses him. Ambarisa, who fasted a year awaiting him, later retires to the forest to meditate on Vasudeva.
Puranjaya agrees to fight the demons only if Indra carries him; ordered by Vishnu, the proud Indra turns into a bull. (SB 9.6 14)
Finding the king drank the wife's sanctified water, the brahmanas bow to the Lord's will rather than protest. (SB 9.6 29)

children.topic: You may drink me, says Indra
children.note: With no mother for the crying newborn, Indra puts his finger in the baby's mouth, giving the child his name Mandhata. (SB 9.6 31)
Meditating underwater, the sage sees fish in sex, desires the same pleasure, and asks Mandhata for a daughter. (SB 9.6 39-40)

children.topic: Fire fed with fat never stops
children.note: Despite endless enjoyment with fifty wives, Saubhari remains unsatisfied, like a flame kept burning by drops of fat. (SB 9.6 48)
Saubhari concludes that a seeker of liberation must avoid sex-minded people and fix the mind on the Lord's feet. (SB 9.6 51)

Sukadeva follows Iksvaku's line: Vikuksi exiled for eating a rabbit, Puranjaya riding Indra as a bull, Mandhata born from his father's side. Sage Saubhari, aroused by watching fish mate, takes fifty princesses, then regrets his fall and returns to austerity.

children.topic: Trisanku hangs head-down in the sky
children.note: Cursed to be an outcaste, he is sent to heaven bodily by Visvamitra, pushed back by the gods, and stays suspended. (SB 9.7 5-6)

children.topic: A son promised as sacrifice to Varuna
children.note: Childless Hariscandra vows to offer his future son to Varuna, and Rohita is born by that blessing. (SB 9.7 9)
Attached to Rohita, Hariscandra invents one excuse after another to make Varuna wait for the sacrifice. (SB 9.7 15)
After six years in the forest, Rohita purchases Ajigarta's second son and presents him to his father for the yajna. (SB 9.7 20)
Seeing the king and queen truthful and patient, the sage teaches them the knowledge that fulfills human life. (SB 9.7 24)

Sukadeva lists Mandhata's descendants: Purukutsa in Rasatala, Trisanku hanging upside down in the sky, and Hariscandra, who promises his son Rohita to Varuna but keeps delaying. Rohita buys Sunahsepha as substitute; Visvamitra then enlightens the king.

children.topic: 8 · The Sons of Sagara Meet Lord Kapiladeva

children.note: His co-wives' poison fails to kill the unborn child, who is born with it and so receives the name Sagara. (SB 9.8 4)

children.topic: Sixty thousand sons burnt by their own fire
children.note: Misled by Indra, Sagara's sons insult Kapila and are consumed by heat rising from their own bodies. (SB 9.8 11)

children.topic: Kapila did not burn them in anger
children.note: Sukadeva rejects the idea that Kapila's glance killed them, since a body of pure goodness cannot show ignorant anger. (SB 9.8 12)
Kapila's philosophy is a sturdy boat for crossing material existence; such a sage sees no friend or enemy. (SB 9.8 13)

children.topic: Covered by the modes, we cannot see You
children.note: Amsuman prays that souls under the three modes perceive only nature's workings, never the Lord within their hearts. (SB 9.8 22)

children.topic: Only Ganges water can deliver them
children.note: Kapila returns the horse and tells Amsuman that his burnt forefathers can be saved by nothing except the Ganges. (SB 9.8 28)

Born with poison, Sagara becomes emperor and holds a horse sacrifice. Indra steals the horse; Sagara's sixty thousand sons find it near Kapila, attack Him and are burnt by their own fire. Amsuman prays to Kapila and learns only the Ganges can save them.

children.topic: Who will cleanse the sins bathers leave?
children.note: Mother Ganges worries that people's sins will accumulate in her water and asks Bhagiratha how she can be freed. (SB 9.9 5)

children.topic: Pure devotees will bathe in you
children.note: Bhagiratha answers that saintly devotees carrying the Lord in their hearts will neutralize all the sins she collects. (SB 9.9 6)

children.topic: Shiva holds the Ganges on his head
children.note: Asked to break her fall, Shiva agrees and reverently bears the river that sprang from Vishnu's toes. (SB 9.9 9)

children.topic: The human body is meant for all
children.note: The brahmana's wife pleads that killing a human body untimely destroys every benefit that life could give. (SB 9.9 28)

children.topic: Only one moment left to live
children.note: Told by the demigods that a single moment remains, Khatvanga drops everything and fixes his mind on the Lord's feet. (SB 9.9 42)

children.topic: Give up the imaginary city, surrender
children.note: Khatvanga likens the material world to a phantom town on a hill and resolves to abandon attachment and surrender. (SB 9.9 47)

Bhagiratha's austerity brings the Ganges to earth, Shiva bearing her fall, and Sagara's sons are delivered. Sukadeva then tells of Saudasa, cursed by Vasistha to be a man-eater and by a brahmana's wife, and of Khatvanga, who attains the Lord in one moment.

children.topic: 10 · The Pastimes of the Supreme Lord, Rāmacandra
Leaving the kingdom like a liberated soul
children.note: To honor His father's promise, Rama abandons throne, friends and home as easily as a freed soul leaves the body. (SB 9.10 8)

children.topic: Ravana steals Sita like a tiger
children.note: With both brothers away, Ravana carries off Sita as a tiger takes unguarded sheep, and Rama shows the pain of attachment. (SB 9.10 11)

children.topic: The ocean asks for a bridge
children.note: The ocean personified invites Rama to cross but begs Him to build a bridge so His fame will spread through the ages. (SB 9.10 15)

children.topic: You stole My wife like a dog
children.note: Rama rebukes Ravana as a dog that steals food in the householder's absence and vows to punish him like Yamaraja. (SB 9.10 22)
Rama's arrow pierces Ravana like a thunderbolt and he falls from his airplane, blood pouring from ten mouths. (SB 9.10 23)

children.topic: No disease, old age or unwanted death
children.note: Under Rama's rule every bodily and mental misery vanished, and nobody died who did not wish to. (SB 9.10 53)

Sukadeva briefly tells Rama's pastimes: breaking Shiva's bow, exile, Sita's abduction by Ravana, the bridge over the ocean, the killing of Ravana, and the return to Ayodhya where Bharata offers back His sandals. Rama's reign makes Treta-yuga like Satya-yuga.

children.topic: Your light in our hearts is enough
children.note: The brahmanas return Rama's gifts, saying His presence dispelling their ignorance is the greatest donation. (SB 9.11 6)
Fearing the talk of ignorant men, the Lord sends His wife away and she takes shelter in Valmiki's ashram. (SB 9.11 10)
Entrusting her twins to Valmiki, Sita meditates on Rama's feet and disappears into the ground. (SB 9.11 15)
Sukadeva notes that this attachment troubles even the great controllers, let alone ordinary householders. (SB 9.11 17)

children.topic: Rama needed no monkeys to win
children.note: Killing Ravana and bridging the sea are not His true glory; the Lord has no equal and required no help. (SB 9.11 20)

children.topic: Hearing Rama's pastimes frees from envy
children.note: Whoever listens to Rama's story is cured of envy and released from the bondage of karma. (SB 9.11 23)

Rama performs sacrifices and gives the whole earth to the priests, who return it. Overhearing a citizen slander Sita, He sends her, pregnant, to Valmiki's ashram, where Lava and Kusa are born; Sita later enters the earth. Rama finally returns to Vaikuntha.

children.topic: 12 · The Dynasty of Kuśa, the Son of Lord Rāmacandra

children.note: A disciple of Jaimini, this king masters mystic yoga and passes adhyatma-yoga, which loosens the heart's knots, to Yajnavalkya. (SB 9.12 3-4)
Perfected in yoga, Maru survives to this day and will revive the sun dynasty at the end of Kali-yuga. (SB 9.12 6)
Sukadeva reminds the king that Abhimanyu slew this Iksvaku descendant in battle. (SB 9.12 8)

children.topic: Sumitra, last of the solar kings
children.note: The dynasty of the sun-god will come to an end with King Sumitra, after whom no more sons are born. (SB 9.12 16)

Sukadeva lists Rama's descendants through Kusa down to Brhadbala, whom Pariksit's father Abhimanyu killed, then names the future kings of the solar line from Brhadrana to Sumitra, with whom the Iksvaku dynasty will end in Kali-yuga.

children.topic: Life is flickering; Nimi does not wait
children.note: Knowing life is brief, Nimi starts his sacrifice with other priests rather than waiting for Vasistha. (SB 9.13 3)

children.topic: Nimi curses his guru in return
children.note: Accusing Vasistha of losing his sense out of greed for Indra's fees, the king pronounces that his guru's body will also fall. (SB 9.13 5)

children.topic: Devotees use the body for service
children.note: Nimi contrasts Mayavadis who dread rebirth with devotees who are fearless and turn the body into an instrument of service. (SB 9.13 9)

children.topic: The body is like a fish's anxiety
children.note: Nimi refuses a material body, calling it the root of grief and fear, like a fish that lives always in dread of death. (SB 9.13 10)

children.topic: Janaka born from the churned body
children.note: The son produced from Nimi's corpse is called Janaka, Vaideha and Mithila, and founds the city of Mithila. (SB 9.13 13)
All the Mithila kings knew their spiritual identity, so they lived free of duality without leaving household life. (SB 9.13 27)

King Nimi begins a sacrifice without Vasistha; the two curse each other and both bodies fall. Nimi refuses a new body, preferring to serve the Lord in spirit; sages churn his corpse and produce Janaka. The Mithila line, with Sita's father Siradhvaja, follows.

children.topic: Soma abducts Tara out of pride
children.note: Puffed up after his Rajasuya, the moon-god forcibly takes Brhaspati's wife, sparking a war among the gods. (SB 9.14 4)

children.topic: Tara admits the child is Soma's
children.note: Questioned privately by Brahma, Tara whispers that the baby belongs to the moon-god, who claims him. (SB 9.14 13)
She will eat only food cooked in ghee and must never see Pururava naked except during intercourse. (SB 9.14 22)

children.topic: Naked, sword in hand, into the night
children.note: Stung by Urvasi's taunts, Pururava chases the lamb-thieves without dressing, and the Gandharvas' flash exposes him. (SB 9.14 30)

children.topic: Do not let the foxes eat you
children.note: Urvasi tells the despairing king to master his senses and warns that a woman's heart is like a fox's. (SB 9.14 36)

children.topic: Pururava starts fire sacrifice in Treta
children.note: Treating the fire from the aranis as his son, Pururava inaugurates karma-kanda yajna and reaches Gandharvaloka. (SB 9.14 49)

The lunar dynasty begins: Soma kidnaps Brhaspati's wife Tara, whose son Budha fathers Pururava. Urvasi lives with Pururava on conditions, leaves when he is seen naked chasing Gandharvas, and warns him about women. Seeking her, he founds fire sacrifice.
Satyavati eats her mother's kshatriya-charged oblation, so her line will produce a fierce warrior instead of a sage. (SB 9.15 9)
Scholars accept him as Vasudeva's incarnation who ended Kartavirya's dynasty and purged rulers twenty-one times. (SB 9.15 14)

children.topic: Arjuna dams the Narmada with his arms
children.note: Playing with women in the river, the proud thousand-armed king stops its flow, flooding Ravana's camp. (SB 9.15 20)
Drunk on power, Kartaviryarjuna has his men drag the crying cow and her calf away to Mahismati. (SB 9.15 26)

children.topic: Arms lopped off like serpent hoods
children.note: After destroying his arrows, Parasurama's axe severs all of Kartaviryarjuna's thousand arms. (SB 9.15 34)
Jamadagni teaches his son that a brahmana's duty is to cultivate forgiveness, which pleases the Lord. (SB 9.15 40)

Sukadeva traces Pururava's line to Jamadagni and his son Parasurama. Thousand-armed Kartaviryarjuna steals Jamadagni's wish-fulfilling cow; Parasurama slaughters his armies and beheads him, but Jamadagni calls it a sin and sends him to atone at holy places.

children.topic: 16 · Lord Paraśurāma Destroys the World’s Ruling Class
Parasurama kills his mother and brothers
children.note: Confident in his father's power, he immediately executes Jamadagni's order against his mother and disobedient brothers. (SB 9.16 6)

children.topic: Boon: let them live, forgetting death
children.note: Offered any blessing, Parasurama asks that his mother and brothers be restored with no memory of being killed. (SB 9.16 7)
Kartaviryarjuna's sons ignore the wife's begging and cut off the meditating sage's head, carrying it away. (SB 9.16 12)

children.topic: Twenty-one purges, nine lakes of blood
children.note: Using his father's murder as the pretext, Parasurama rids the earth of sinful kings repeatedly and fills lakes at Samanta-pancaka. (SB 9.16 18-19)

children.topic: Parasurama still lives on Mount Mahendra
children.note: Having laid down his weapons, he remains a peaceful brahmana honored by Siddhas, Caranas and Gandharvas. (SB 9.16 26)

children.topic: Visvamitra curses fifty sons as mlecchas
children.note: When his elder sons refuse Sunahsepha as their eldest brother, the sage condemns them to become opposed to Vedic culture. (SB 9.16 33)

Parasurama beheads his mother and brothers on his father's order, then asks for their revival. Kartaviryarjuna's sons murder Jamadagni; Parasurama purges the kshatriyas twenty-one times and revives his father. Visvamitra adopts Sunahsepha, curses defiant sons.

children.topic: 17 · The Dynasties of the Sons of Purūravā

children.note: Dhanvantari, founder of medical science, appears in Kasi's line as a form of Vasudeva; remembering his name frees one from disease. (SB 9.17 4)
At the demigods' request Raji defeats the demons and hands heaven back, yet a fearful Indra surrenders the kingdom to him again. (SB 9.17 13)
Brihaspati's oblations make Raji's sons abandon morality, and once degraded they are easily wiped out by Indra. (SB 9.17 15)

Sukadeva traces the lines of Pururava's sons: Kasi's dynasty with Dhanvantari the physician incarnation, Alarka's 66,000-year reign, and King Raji, who won heaven for Indra and whose sons later lost it after Brihaspati made them fall.
Nahusa's eldest son declines kingship, understanding that political power blocks self-realization. (SB 9.18 2)

children.topic: Sarmistha throws Devayani in a well
children.note: A quarrel over a swapped dress ends with the angry princess stripping Devayani and casting her into a well. (SB 9.18 17)

children.topic: Sukracarya curses Yayati with old age
children.note: Learning of the king's affair with Sarmistha, the sage condemns him to sudden old age and invalidity. (SB 9.18 36)

children.topic: Yadu declines his father's old age
children.note: Yadu argues one cannot renounce without first enjoying, so he refuses to accept the burden of age. (SB 9.18 40)
Puru ranks sons by obedience: the best anticipates his father's wish, while one who refuses an order is worthless. (SB 9.18 44)
Even with borrowed youth and a whole world to enjoy, Yayati's senses find no lasting satisfaction after a millennium. (SB 9.18 51)

Yayati becomes king after Nahusa's fall. He rescues Devayani from a well and marries her, secretly fathers sons with Sarmistha, and is cursed with old age by Sukracarya. Only Puru agrees to trade his youth, and Yayati enjoys for a thousand years.
Yayati admits he is like the goat in his story, captivated by beauty and forgetful of his real spiritual task. (SB 9.19 12)

children.topic: Butter on fire: desire never ends
children.note: Trying to end lust by enjoying it only feeds it, just as ghee makes a fire burn higher. (SB 9.19 14)
Even invalids cannot drop sense cravings, so anyone wanting real happiness must consciously renounce them. (SB 9.19 16)
After a millennium of pleasure Yayati confesses his hunger for enjoyment has only increased daily. (SB 9.19 18)

children.topic: Leaving pleasure like a fledged bird
children.note: Yayati drops his lifelong habits in an instant, the way a bird abandons the nest once its wings have grown. (SB 9.19 24)

children.topic: Family life is a tourist hotel
children.note: Devayani realizes worldly relationships are as temporary as guests in an inn, fixes her mind on Krishna, and is liberated. (SB 9.19 27-28)

Disgusted with lust, Yayati tells Devayani the parable of the he-goat who forgot self-realization for she-goats. He teaches that desire grows with enjoyment, returns Puru's youth, crowns him emperor, and both king and queen attain liberation.
Sakuntala's silence counts as consent, and Dusmanta weds her at once by chanting omkara in the Gandharva style. (SB 9.20 16)

children.topic: A son belongs to his father
children.note: A heavenly voice tells Dusmanta that a child truly belongs to the father, so he must accept his son and honor Sakuntala. (SB 9.20 21)
Bearing Krishna's disc on his palm, Bharata rules the world and performs over a hundred horse sacrifices along the Ganges and Yamuna. (SB 9.20 24-26)
Bharata's deeds are as unreachable as touching heaven with one's hands; none before or after can match them. (SB 9.20 29)
Despite unrivaled power and family, Bharata finally views it all as a hindrance to spiritual life and stops enjoying it. (SB 9.20 33)

Sukadeva describes the Puru dynasty: King Dusmanta secretly marries Sakuntala at Kanva's hermitage, later rejects her until a voice from the sky confirms his son. That son, Bharata, becomes a matchless emperor, and Bharadvaja is given to him by the Maruts.
Never earning for himself, Rantideva shares whatever comes with guests, staying calm even as his family starves for 48 days. (SB 9.21 3-5)

children.topic: Let me suffer for all beings
children.note: Rantideva wants neither mystic powers nor liberation, only to stay among the living and bear their distress so they may be relieved. (SB 9.21 12)

children.topic: Water for a candala cures all
children.note: By offering his last water to a struggling outcaste, the king feels freed of hunger, thirst, fatigue and grief. (SB 9.21 13)
Brahma, Siva and others reveal that they had come disguised as the brahmana, sudra and candala to test the king. (SB 9.21 15)

children.topic: Maya vanishes before a pure devotee
children.note: Because Rantideva is desireless and Krishna conscious, the illusory energy cannot even appear before him. (SB 9.21 17)

Sukadeva narrates the Bharata line, centering on King Rantideva, who after a 48-day fast gives all his food and water to successive guests, wishing only to suffer for others. The demigods reveal themselves; the chapter ends with the Pancala kings and Krpa.
Born as two separate halves and abandoned, the child is playfully fused into one by the demoness Jara. (SB 9.22 8)
Twelve rainless years lead the brahmanas to tell Santanu he must return the throne to his elder brother Devapi. (SB 9.22 14-15)
Sukadeva reveals his own birth from Vyasa and how the sage entrusted this scripture to him because he was free from desire. (SB 9.22 21-24)
After the Kuru dynasty fell, Krishna's mercy shielded the unborn Pariksit from Asvatthama's weapon. (SB 9.22 34)
Angered by his father's death from Taksaka, Pariksit's son will perform a sacrifice to destroy all snakes. (SB 9.22 36)

Sukadeva lists the descendants of Ajamidha and the Kuru line: Jarasandha's strange birth, Santanu and Devapi, Bhisma, Vyasa's birth from Satyavati, the Pandavas and Kauravas, Pariksit's own birth and rescue, and the future kings down to Ksemaka.

children.topic: 23 · The Dynasties of the Sons of Yayāti

children.note: A childless charioteer discovers Kunti's abandoned infant in a basket on the Ganges and raises him as his own. (SB 9.23 13)
The Yadu dynasty's history is so pious that simply hearing it frees a person from sinful reactions. (SB 9.23 18-19)
The Supersoul of all beings chooses the Yadu dynasty to appear in His original humanlike form. (SB 9.23 20-21)
No ruler equaled him in sacrifice, charity, austerity, mystic power, learning, strength or mercy. (SB 9.23 25)
By the demigods' grace the barren Saibya bears Vidarbha, who later marries the girl once called her daughter-in-law. (SB 9.23 38)

Sukadeva covers the lines of Anu, Druhyu and Turvasu, including Romapada, Rsyasrnga and Karna's adoption, then begins the pious Yadu dynasty: Kartaviryarjuna's greatness, the Yadava, Madhava and Vrsni branches, and Jyamagha's barren queen who bears Vidarbha.

children.topic: 24 · Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead
The sun-god gives Kunti a son
children.note: Testing Durvasa's boon, Kunti summons Surya, who insists on giving her a child while preserving her virginity. (SB 9.24 34)
Among Devaki's eight sons come Sankarsana and finally Krishna Himself, with Subhadra as Pariksit's grandmother. (SB 9.24 53-55)
Whenever religion declines and irreligion rises, the supreme controller descends by His own will. (SB 9.24 56)

children.topic: Demons in government destroy each other
children.note: God arranges for militarized demonic rulers to fight among themselves, lightening the earth's burden. (SB 9.24 59)
Krishna acted so that future devotees in Kali-yuga could be freed from misery simply by remembering Him. (SB 9.24 61)
Krishna's smiling, ornamented face delights everyone; devotees even resent the creator for the blink that interrupts their sight. (SB 9.24 65)

Sukadeva completes the Yadu genealogy down to Vasudeva, Devaki and Kunti, who receives Karna from the sun-god, then explains why Krishna appears: to restore religion, relieve the earth of demons and bless devotees, whose eyes resent even blinking.
The dynasties of the sun and the moon: Sudyumna, Ambarisa, Lord Ramacandra, Pururava, Parasurama, and the birth of the Yadus. 24 chapters.

children.topic: 1 · The Advent of Lord Kṛṣṇa: Introduction
Who but a butcher stops hearing?
children.note: Descriptions of the Lord are medicine for suffering souls; only a self-killer would turn away from them. (SB 10.1 4)
Fasting before death, Pariksit says the nectar of Krishna topics keeps his hunger and thirst from troubling him. (SB 10.1 13)
Like the Ganges, inquiry into Krishna purifies the speaker, the questioner and the listening public. (SB 10.1 16)
As Kamsa drives the wedding chariot, an invisible voice declares that Devaki's eighth child will be his killer. (SB 10.1 34)

children.topic: Death is born with the body
children.note: Vasudeva reasons with Kamsa that whoever is born must die, today or after centuries, so killing gains nothing. (SB 10.1 38)

children.topic: The mind shapes the next body
children.note: One's thoughts at death determine the next body; the soul changes bodies only because of a flickering mind. (SB 10.1 42)

Pariksit asks to hear Krishna's pastimes. Sukadeva tells how Brahma relayed Visnu's plan to relieve the earth, how a sky voice warned Kamsa that Devaki's eighth child would kill him, and how Vasudeva's wisdom and promise saved her until Kamsa jailed them both.

children.topic: 2 · Prayers by the Demigods for Lord Kṛṣṇa in the Womb

children.note: The Lord announces He will appear as Devaki's son while Yogamaya takes birth as Yasoda's daughter. (SB 10.2 9)
Eating, sleeping or walking, Kamsa sees his enemy everywhere and so thinks of Krishna constantly, though with hatred. (SB 10.2 24)

children.topic: Satyam param: the Lord is truth
children.note: The demigods praise the Lord as the unfailing truth behind creation, maintenance and destruction, inaccessible to hypocrites. (SB 10.2 26)

children.topic: Crossing the ocean like a calf's hoofprint
children.note: Meditating on the Lord's feet as a boat, following the mahajanas, one crosses nescience as easily as a puddle. (SB 10.2 30)
Loving devotees who slip do not fall like nondevotees; the Lord keeps them and they advance fearlessly. (SB 10.2 33)
Speculation cannot reveal the Lord's name and form; only devotional service discloses them. (SB 10.2 36)

Kamsa persecutes the Yadus. Krishna orders Yogamaya to move Sesa from Devaki's womb to Rohini's and to be born as Yasoda's daughter. Krishna enters Vasudeva's heart and then Devaki, and Brahma, Siva and the demigods secretly pray to the Lord in her womb.

children.topic: The Lord rises like the full moon
children.note: Amid gentle thunder and flowers, Visnu appears from Devaki in the dark of night like the moon rising in the east. (SB 10.3 7-8)
The newborn holds conch, disc, club and lotus, with Srivatsa, Kaustubha and yellow dress, astonishing His father. (SB 10.3 9-10)

children.topic: Devaki asks Him to hide His form
children.note: Fearing Kamsa, Devaki begs the Lord to withdraw His four-armed Visnu form and look like a normal baby. (SB 10.3 30)
In a past life the couple performed austerities for twelve thousand celestial years wanting the Lord as their son. (SB 10.3 36)

children.topic: Love Me as son, know Me as God
children.note: Krishna tells His parents that loving Him as their child while knowing His supremacy will bring them back to Godhead. (SB 10.3 45)
Guards sleep, locked iron doors swing open, and Sesa's hoods shield Vasudeva and the baby from the rain. (SB 10.3 48-49)

At an auspicious midnight Krishna appears to Vasudeva and Devaki as four-armed Visnu. Both parents pray; Krishna recalls their past lives as Prsni and Sutapa, then becomes a normal baby. Vasudeva carries Him to Gokula and brings back Yasoda's girl.
Slipping from Kamsa's grip, Yogamaya appears in the sky as the armed goddess Durga. (SB 10.4 9)

children.topic: Your killer is already born elsewhere
children.note: Durga mocks Kamsa: killing her is pointless, since his destined enemy has already taken birth somewhere else. (SB 10.4 12)
Kamsa reasons that bodies appear and vanish like earthen pots while the soul, like the earth, is never destroyed. (SB 10.4 19)
One who thinks he kills or is killed remains in bodily darkness and keeps suffering material reactions. (SB 10.4 22)

children.topic: Seeing difference breeds fear and envy
children.note: Vasudeva explains that people who divide 'mine' from 'yours' fall prey to grief, fear, greed and madness. (SB 10.4 27)
One who harasses great souls loses longevity, beauty, fame, religion and promotion to higher worlds. (SB 10.4 46)

Kamsa tries to kill Devaki's newborn girl, but she rises as Durga and says his killer is born elsewhere. Remorseful, Kamsa frees the couple and Vasudeva teaches him about the soul, yet next morning his ministers push him to kill infants and harass brahmanas.

children.topic: 5 · The Meeting of Nanda Mahārāja and Vasudeva

children.note: Time, bathing, ritual, austerity, charity and satisfaction purify various things, and self-realization purifies the soul. (SB 10.5 4)
The men of Vraja celebrate Krishna's birth by joyfully smearing each other with yogurt, milk and butter. (SB 10.5 14)
Nanda's house is eternally the Lord's abode, and with Krishna's arrival the goddess of fortune sports there. (SB 10.5 18)
Vasudeva compares relatives to sticks in a current, pulled apart by their differing karma and the flow of time. (SB 10.5 25)
Nanda consoles Vasudeva that children come and go by unseen destiny, and whoever understands this stays unbewildered. (SB 10.5 30)

Nanda celebrates Krishna's birth with lavish charity and a festival in Gokula, where cowherds splash each other with butter and curd. In Mathura to pay taxes, Nanda meets Vasudeva, who asks after both boys and urges him to hurry home because of danger.

children.topic: 6 · The Killing of the Demon Pūtanā
A sleeping snake on her lap
children.note: Putana lifts the child destined to kill her as carelessly as one who mistakes a snake for a rope. (SB 10.6 8)

children.topic: Krishna sucks out poison and life
children.note: Angered, the baby squeezes the poisoned breast and draws out both the poison and the witch's life. (SB 10.6 10)
Witches, ghosts and evil planets that torment children all flee when the name of Visnu is uttered. (SB 10.6 27-29)
Because Krishna sucked her breast, Putana's sins vanished and her burning corpse smelled like aguru incense. (SB 10.6 34)

children.topic: Even a murderous witch gains perfection
children.note: If Putana attained the highest goal by offering her breast with evil intent, what awaits mothers who offer with love? (SB 10.6 35-36)
Anyone who faithfully hears how Krishna killed Putana develops attachment for Govinda. (SB 10.6 44)

The witch Putana enters Gokula as a beauty, offers baby Krishna her poisoned breast, and dies as He sucks out her life. The gopis chant protective mantras over Krishna; Putana's burning body smells of incense, for she won a mother's place in the spiritual sky.

children.topic: 7 · The Killing of the Demon Tṛṇāvarta

children.note: Pariksit notes that hearing Krishna's boyhood deeds is so pleasing it removes mental dirt and material attachment. (SB 10.7 1-2)
Crying for milk, the baby kicks the handcart so that wheels, axle and pots scatter everywhere. (SB 10.7 7)

children.topic: Krishna grows heavy as a mountain
children.note: Yasoda suddenly cannot bear her one-year-old's weight and sets Him down, remembering Narayana. (SB 10.7 18)
The whirlwind demon cannot shake off the child at his throat and falls lifeless onto the rocks of Vraja. (SB 10.7 28)

children.topic: The innocent protected, the sinful destroyed
children.note: The cowherds see the law of nature: a devotee is always guarded and a cruel demon is killed by his own sin. (SB 10.7 31)
As Krishna yawns after nursing, Yasoda sees sky, planets, oceans, mountains and all living beings inside His mouth. (SB 10.7 35-36)

At the utthana ceremony baby Krishna kicks over a cart; a year later the whirlwind demon Trnavarta carries Him into the sky but is choked by His weight and falls dead. While nursing Him, Yasoda sees the whole universe in Krishna's yawning mouth.

children.topic: 8 · Lord Kṛṣṇa Shows the Universal Form Within His Mouth

children.note: Garga reveals that this son appeared in three colors in past ages and now comes in a blackish form. (SB 10.8 13)
Garga concludes that Krishna is as good as Narayana in qualities and power, so Nanda must raise Him carefully. (SB 10.8 19)
The gopis tell Yasoda how Krishna frees calves, steals curd and butter, feeds monkeys and breaks the pots. (SB 10.8 29)

children.topic: I never ate dirt, look yourself
children.note: Accused by His friends, Krishna insists they are liars and invites His mother to inspect His mouth. (SB 10.8 35)

children.topic: Yasoda sees everything in His mouth
children.note: In the opened mouth Yasoda sees space, planets, elements, the modes, time, karma and even Vrndavana with herself. (SB 10.8 37-39)

children.topic: The Vedas' subject, her ordinary boy
children.note: The Supreme Person studied through all Vedic literature is treated by Yasoda simply as her own child. (SB 10.8 45)

Garga Muni secretly names Rama and Krishna and predicts Krishna's greatness. The brothers crawl, walk and steal butter; the gopis complain playfully to Yasoda. Accused of eating dirt, Krishna opens His mouth, Yasoda sees the universe, then forgets by Yogamaya.
Left unsatisfied when Yasoda tends boiling milk, Krishna smashes the yogurt pot with a stone and eats butter alone. (SB 10.9 6)
The Lord whom meditators cannot catch runs in fear from a mother with a stick, and she pursues Him. (SB 10.9 9)
No matter how many ropes Yasoda ties together, each remains short by exactly two fingers' width. (SB 10.9 16)
Seeing His mother sweating and exhausted, the Lord becomes merciful and lets Himself be tied. (SB 10.9 18)

children.topic: The Lord controlled by His devotee
children.note: Though the universe and all demigods obey Him, Krishna shows here that He submits to those who love Him. (SB 10.9 19)
Yasoda's son is available to spontaneous loving servants, not to speculators, ascetics or those who identify with the body. (SB 10.9 21)

While Yasoda churns butter, Krishna breaks the yogurt pot and feeds monkeys. She chases and catches Him, but every rope is two fingers short until He agrees to be bound. Sukadeva explains the Lord is conquered only by love, then introduces the arjuna trees.

children.topic: 10 · The Deliverance of the Yamala-arjuna Trees

children.note: Narada says riches confuse intelligence more than looks, birth or learning, leading to wine, women and gambling. (SB 10.10 8)

children.topic: The body ends as worms, stool or ash
children.note: Whatever one's status, the body one kills animals to maintain will finally become worms, excrement or ashes. (SB 10.10 10)

children.topic: Poverty is ointment for proud eyes
children.note: Reducing the arrogant rich to poverty helps them see reality and feel the pain of others. (SB 10.10 13)
Sadhus freely associate with the poor, whose hearts are quickly cleansed of material desire, not with the proud rich. (SB 10.10 17)
Hauling the heavy mortar roped to His waist, the little boy pulls down both arjuna trees with a great crash. (SB 10.10 27)
Krishna says that as sunlight ends darkness, meeting a surrendered devotee frees one from material bondage. (SB 10.10 41)

Narada finds Kuvera's drunken sons naked with women and curses them to become trees for their own good, teaching that wealth blinds while poverty humbles. Krishna drags the mortar between the arjuna trees, fells them, and freed Nalakuvara and Manigriva pray.

children.topic: Krishna dances for half a sweet
children.note: The all-powerful Lord dances and sings like a wooden doll when the gopis bribe Him with sweets and clapping. (SB 10.11 7)
Krishna barters a few spilled grains for fruit, and the vendor's basket instantly turns to gold and gems. (SB 10.11 11)
The wise elder recommends moving to Vrndavana, rich in grass, gardens and hills for cows, gopas and gopis. (SB 10.11 28)

children.topic: Calf demon thrown into a tree
children.note: Krishna grabs the disguised demon by tail and hind legs, whirls him dead and hurls him into a kapittha tree. (SB 10.11 43)
When the duck demon attacks again, Krishna grips both halves of his beak and splits him as easily as a blade of grass. (SB 10.11 51)

children.topic: Demons die like flies in fire
children.note: Nanda marvels that every fierce killer sent for Krishna perishes on arrival, like moths flying into flame. (SB 10.11 56)

Nanda frees Krishna from the mortar; the boys' story is disbelieved. A fruit seller's basket fills with jewels. Upananda persuades the cowherds to move to Vrndavana, where Krishna tends calves, kills the calf demon Vatsasura and splits Bakasura's beak.

children.topic: 12 · The Killing of the Demon Aghāsura

children.note: Yogis who master the mind for lifetimes cannot touch dust from the Lord's feet, yet Vraja's people saw Him daily. (SB 10.12 12)
Seeking revenge for Putana and Baka, the demon lies on the road as a mountain-sized serpent with open mouth. (SB 10.12 16)

children.topic: Boys laugh and enter the mouth
children.note: Confident Krishna will kill any threat as He killed Baka, the boys clap, laugh and walk into the python. (SB 10.12 24)

children.topic: Krishna swells and chokes the demon
children.note: Krishna enlarges Himself in Aghasura's throat until the demon's life air bursts out the top of his head. (SB 10.12 31)
A brilliant effulgence leaves the corpse, waits in the sky, and merges into Krishna as the demigods watch. (SB 10.12 33)
If Aghasura was liberated by thinking of the Lord even by force, devotees who always remember Him are certain of it. (SB 10.12 39)

On a picnic the cowherd boys mistake the python-shaped Aghasura for scenery and walk into his mouth. Krishna follows, swells in the demon's throat and kills him, reviving the boys. Aghasura's light merges into Krishna; Pariksit asks why the tale came late.

children.topic: 13 · The Stealing of the Boys and Calves by Brahmā

children.note: Krishna sits at the center of the lunch circle like a lotus whorl, every boy hoping He will glance his way. (SB 10.13 8)

children.topic: Brahma steals the boys and calves
children.note: Wanting to test Krishna's power after Aghasura, Brahma spirits away the calves and boys while Krishna searches. (SB 10.13 15)

children.topic: Krishna becomes every boy and calf
children.note: Krishna expands into the exact bodies, sticks, flutes, names and habits of all the missing boys and calves. (SB 10.13 19)

children.topic: Parents love their sons like Krishna
children.note: For one year the affection of Vraja's parents for their own children swells daily, because those children are now Krishna. (SB 10.13 26)
Before Brahma's eyes all the boys and calves appear as bluish, four-armed Visnu forms with conch, disc, mace and lotus. (SB 10.13 47-48)

children.topic: Brahma falls like a golden rod
children.note: Overwhelmed, Brahma leaps from his swan and touches Krishna's feet with all four crowns, bathing them with tears. (SB 10.13 62)

After the forest lunch Brahma steals the calves and boys. Krishna expands into exact copies of each, and for a year Vraja's parents and cows love them more than ever. Balarama grows puzzled; Brahma returns, sees every boy as Visnu and falls at Krishna's feet.
Those who drop speculation and devote body, words and mind to Krishna's stories win the Lord no one can conquer. (SB 10.14 3)
Giving up devotion for dry knowledge yields only trouble, like beating chaff and expecting grain. (SB 10.14 4)
One who waits for Krishna's mercy, tolerating past reactions while offering respects, makes liberation his rightful claim. (SB 10.14 8)
Brahma, seven spans tall in one pot-like universe, marvels that countless universes drift through Krishna's pores like dust. (SB 10.14 11)

children.topic: Any birth, just let me serve
children.note: Brahma prays to be a devotee in any life, even as an animal, so long as he serves Krishna's feet. (SB 10.14 30)

children.topic: The ocean becomes a calf's hoofprint
children.note: For those who take the boat of Murari's feet, the material ocean shrinks to a puddle and Vaikuntha is the goal. (SB 10.14 58)

Brahma prays to Krishna: devotion conquers Him, speculation is threshing empty husks, universes pass through His pores, Vraja's residents are most fortunate. Krishna returns the boys, who felt the year as a moment; Sukadeva explains why Krishna is dearest.

children.topic: 15 · The Killing of Dhenuka, the Ass Demon

children.note: Krishna points out the fruit-laden trees bending to touch His brother's feet, seeking release from their ignorance. (SB 10.15 5)

children.topic: The earth blessed by His touch
children.note: Krishna says the land is fortunate to feel His feet, glances and, above all, His embrace of the gopis that Laksmi craves. (SB 10.15 8)
When His elder brother tires, Krishna personally rubs His feet and serves Him as He rests on a friend's lap. (SB 10.15 14)

children.topic: Balarama whirls Dhenuka into a palm
children.note: Seizing the ass demon by the hooves, Balarama spins him with one hand and flings him dead into a treetop. (SB 10.15 32)

children.topic: Gopis drink His face with bee-like eyes
children.note: The women of Vrndavana relieve their day's separation by gazing at Mukunda, and He accepts their shy glances as worship. (SB 10.15 43)
Cows and boys who drink the poisoned Yamuna fall dead, and Krishna restores them to life with a compassionate look. (SB 10.15 49-50)

Now cowherds, Krishna and Balarama roam Vrndavana, Krishna praising the trees, bees and animals honoring His brother. At the boys' request they enter Talavana, where Balarama whirls the ass demon Dhenuka into the palms. Krishna later revives poisoned boys.

children.topic: Krishna leaps from the kadamba tree
children.note: Seeing the Yamuna poisoned, Krishna climbs a tall kadamba, tightens His belt and dives into the deadly water. (SB 10.16 6)
Having given Krishna their very selves, the cowherds faint from grief at the sight of Him motionless in Kaliya's coils. (SB 10.16 10)
After exhausting the serpent by circling, Krishna mounts his heads and dances, His feet reddened by their jewels. (SB 10.16 26)
With all his hoods trampled and vomiting blood, Kaliya finally recognizes Narayana and takes shelter within his mind. (SB 10.16 30)
The serpent's wives say those who gain the dust of Krishna's feet want neither kingship, Brahma's post nor liberation. (SB 10.16 37)
Krishna sends Kaliya back to Ramanaka Island, promising that Garuda will not attack a snake marked with His feet. (SB 10.16 63)

Krishna leaps into Kaliya's poisoned lake, is coiled by the serpent while Vraja grieves, then dances on Kaliya's hoods until the snake surrenders. Kaliya's wives beg mercy, and Krishna banishes the serpent to the sea, marked by footprints so Garuda spares him.
Proud Kaliya alone eats the monthly offerings meant for Garuda, openly defying the carrier of Vishnu. (SB 10.17 4)
The sage decrees that Garuda will die if he ever again eats fish in that lake, so the bird can never enter it. (SB 10.17 11)
Krishna emerges adorned in jewels and garlands, and the stunned cowherds revive like senses returning to a fainted man. (SB 10.17 13-14)

children.topic: Nanda gives charity for Krishna's safety
children.note: On the brahmanas' advice, Nanda gladly donates cows and gold so his son may stay free from danger. (SB 10.17 18)

children.topic: We can never leave Your feet
children.note: Trapped by fire, the Vrajavasis beg Krishna's shelter, declaring His lotus feet remove all fear. (SB 10.17 24)
Seeing His devotees in distress, the unlimited Lord simply drinks up the blazing fire. (SB 10.17 25)

Sukadeva tells Pariksit why Kaliya hid in the Yamuna: he stole the serpents' tribute to Garuda, was beaten, and fled to a lake Garuda could not enter due to Saubhari's curse. Krishna returns from the lake, Vraja revives, and at night He swallows a forest fire.

children.topic: 18 · Lord Balarāma Slays the Demon Pralamba
Summer turns to spring for Krishna
children.note: Because the Lord lives there, harsh summer shows the gentle qualities of spring in Vrindavana. (SB 10.18 3)
Celestials secretly join the village to worship Krishna and Balarama, who themselves play as cowherd boys. (SB 10.18 11)
The all-seeing Lord recognizes the demon but pretends friendship while planning how to finish him. (SB 10.18 18)
Carrying Balarama, Pralamba slows under the crushing weight and reveals his huge, blazing true form. (SB 10.18 26)
Remembering His own strength, the fearless Balarama angrily strikes the demon's head with His hard fist. (SB 10.18 28)

children.topic: Boys embrace Balarama as if reborn
children.note: Overwhelmed with love, the cowherd boys glorify Balarama and hug Him as though He had returned from death. (SB 10.18 31)

Summer in Vrindavana feels like spring because Krishna and Balarama are present. During carrier games at the Bhandira tree, the demon Pralamba disguised as a cowherd carries Balarama away; Balarama grows heavy, then smashes the demon's head with His fist.

children.topic: Krishna calls each cow by name
children.note: The Lord's voice rumbles like a cloud, and the lost cows joyfully answer when they hear their own names. (SB 10.19 6)

children.topic: We are souls surrendered to You
children.note: The boys plead that Krishna's own friends must not perish, declaring themselves fully surrendered to Him. (SB 10.19 10)

children.topic: Close your eyes, do not fear
children.note: The boys obey, and the master of mystic power opens His mouth and drinks the terrible fire. (SB 10.19 12)

children.topic: Boys wonder if Krishna is a demigod
children.note: Rescued by the Lord's internal potency, the cowherd boys can only guess that Krishna must be divine. (SB 10.19 14)

children.topic: A moment without Govinda seems ages
children.note: For the young gopis, even a brief absence of Krishna feels like a hundred ages. (SB 10.19 16)

While the boys play, the cows stray into the Munja forest and a fire surrounds everyone. The terrified boys surrender to Krishna, who tells them to close their eyes; He swallows the fire and returns them to the Bhandira tree. They think He must be a demigod.

children.topic: 20 · The Rainy Season and Autumn in Vṛndāvana
Clouds cover sky like modes cover soul
children.note: Dense monsoon clouds hide the sky's light just as the three modes of nature obscure the spirit soul. (SB 10.20 4)

children.topic: Clouds give their lives like merciful men
children.note: Wind-driven clouds pour themselves out for the world's benefit, like generous people who sacrifice everything. (SB 10.20 6)
Hills bear the pounding rain calmly, just as devotees absorbed in the Lord stay peaceful under every attack. (SB 10.20 15)

children.topic: Rainbow without a string, Lord without modes
children.note: Indra's bow rests on no string; likewise the Lord appears in matter yet stays free of material qualities. (SB 10.20 18)

children.topic: Fish do not see the water shrinking
children.note: Fish in drying pools miss the loss, like family men who never notice their remaining lifetime slipping away. (SB 10.20 37)

children.topic: Autumn moon relieves like wisdom relieves
children.note: The cool moon ends the sun's torment, as knowledge ends bodily misidentification and Krishna ends the gopis' separation. (SB 10.20 42)

Sukadeva describes the rainy season and autumn in Vrindavana, turning each natural scene into a lesson: clouds as charitable souls, muddy roads as neglected scriptures, autumn clarity as devotion. Krishna and Balarama enjoy the forest through both seasons.

children.topic: 21 · The Gopīs Glorify the Song of Kṛṣṇa’s Flute

children.note: Peacock feather, yellow cloth and Vaijayanti garland: Krishna fills His flute with the nectar of His lips. (SB 10.21 5)

children.topic: Eyes that see Krishna are fortunate
children.note: The gopis declare there is no greater sight for anyone with eyes than the two sons of Nanda entering the forest. (SB 10.21 7)

children.topic: What good deeds did the flute do?
children.note: The gopis envy the bamboo flute, which alone drinks Krishna's lips while its bamboo ancestors weep in joy. (SB 10.21 9)
Birds perch with closed eyes, absorbed only in the flute song, and the gopis compare them to great sages. (SB 10.21 14)

children.topic: Rivers embrace His feet with waves
children.note: Hearing the flute, rivers whirl in desire and offer lotus flowers while clasping Krishna's feet. (SB 10.21 15)
The hill serves Krishna, Balarama and the cows with water, grass, caves and fruit, rejoicing at Their touch. (SB 10.21 18)

As Krishna enters the autumn forest playing His flute, the gopis of Vraja privately praise its song. They envy the flute's access to His lips and describe how peacocks, deer, cows, birds, rivers, clouds and Govardhana Hill all respond to Him in ecstasy.

children.topic: 22 · Kṛṣṇa Steals the Garments of the Unmarried Gopīs
Katyayani, make Nanda's son my husband
children.note: Each girl worships the goddess with this single prayer, absorbing her mind entirely in Krishna. (SB 10.22 4)

children.topic: Krishna climbs the kadamba with their clothes
children.note: Laughing with His friends, Krishna takes the garments up a tree and teases the bathing gopis. (SB 10.22 9)
Krishna says the girls must bow with joined palms above their heads to atone before reclaiming their clothes. (SB 10.22 19)

children.topic: Desire for Me does not breed lust
children.note: Like roasted grain that cannot sprout, longing fixed on Krishna never grows into material craving. (SB 10.22 26)
Krishna sends the girls home, promising they will enjoy the coming nights in His company. (SB 10.22 27)

children.topic: Live for the welfare of others
children.note: Pointing to trees, Krishna teaches that every being should use life, wealth, mind and words to help others. (SB 10.22 35)
Srila Prabhupada's recorded class: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 10.22.35. Tap the link to read the transcript and play the audio.
Recorded classes on this chapter, with transcript and audio on vedabase.io. Oldest first.

The unmarried gopis worship Katyayani for a month to get Krishna as husband. Krishna steals their clothes at the Yamuna, makes them come out and bow, then promises they will enjoy His company. Later He praises trees as models of selfless giving.
Absorbed in petty desires and elaborate ritual, the priests refuse the boys and fail to see who is asking. (SB 10.23 9)

children.topic: Wives flow to Krishna like rivers
children.note: The brahmanas' wives carry four kinds of food to their beloved as naturally as rivers run to the sea. (SB 10.23 19)

children.topic: Nothing is dearer than the self
children.note: Krishna explains that body, wife, wealth and friends are dear only because of the self within. (SB 10.23 27)

children.topic: Love grows by hearing, not proximity
children.note: Hearing, seeing the Deity, meditating and chanting develop love for Krishna, so He sends the wives home. (SB 10.23 33)

children.topic: To hell with our birth and learning
children.note: The remorseful brahmanas curse their lineage, celibacy and ritual skill, all useless since they opposed the Lord. (SB 10.23 40)
Untrained in any purification, the wives have firm devotion, while the brahmanas with every rite have none. (SB 10.23 43-44)

Hungry cowherd boys beg food from ritualistic brahmanas, who ignore them, but the brahmanas' wives rush to Krishna with food, abandoning their families. Krishna sends them home, teaching that love grows by hearing, not proximity. The brahmanas repent.
Krishna asks Nanda to explain openly, since saintly persons see all equally and hide nothing. (SB 10.24 4)

children.topic: Birth and death come by karma
children.note: Krishna argues that happiness, fear and security all arise from one's own actions, not from Indra. (SB 10.24 13)
One should honor one's own duty and nature, since whatever maintains us is our true worshipable deity. (SB 10.24 18)

children.topic: What has Indra to do with rain?
children.note: Clouds pour rain by the mode of passion, so Krishna asks why Indra should get the credit. (SB 10.24 23)

children.topic: Let the sacrifice go to Govardhana
children.note: Krishna proposes using Indra's paraphernalia to honor the cows, brahmanas and the hill instead. (SB 10.24 25)
