Krishna assumes a huge form, declares Himself the hill, and eats the abundant offerings to instill faith. (SB 10.24 35)

Seeing preparations for Indra's sacrifice, Krishna questions Nanda, argues that karma and nature, not Indra, govern life, and proposes worshiping the cows, brahmanas and Govardhana instead. Vraja agrees; Krishna appears as the hill and eats the offerings.
Drunk on his own power, Indra rages that Vraja has surrendered to a mere human child and insulted the gods. (SB 10.25 3)

children.topic: Krishna, save the cows from Indra
children.note: Shivering under hail and wind, the people of Vraja cry out to Krishna, who loves His devotees. (SB 10.25 13)

children.topic: I will destroy Indra's false pride
children.note: Krishna resolves to counteract the storm and cure demigods who foolishly think themselves lords of the universe. (SB 10.25 16)

children.topic: I have vowed to protect My devotees
children.note: Krishna calls the cowherds His own family and reminds Himself of His promise to shelter them. (SB 10.25 18)
Krishna picks up Govardhana with one hand as easily as a child lifts a small mushroom. (SB 10.25 19)
Forgetting hunger, thirst and comfort, Krishna stands holding the mountain while Vraja gazes at Him. (SB 10.25 23)

Furious Indra sends the clouds of devastation to flood Vraja. The cowherds and cows beg Krishna's shelter, and He lifts Govardhana Hill with one hand, holding it for seven days while everyone stands beneath. Indra withdraws and the demigods praise Krishna.
The cowherds marvel that a small boy held Govardhana like an elephant holding a lotus. (SB 10.26 3)

children.topic: Why can't we stop loving Him?
children.note: The cowherds wonder why their affection for Krishna and His for them is so spontaneous and unbreakable. (SB 10.26 13)
Garga said the child took white, red and yellow forms before and now appears in blackish hue. (SB 10.26 16)
Just as Vishnu's presence protects the demigods, those attached to Krishna are never overcome by enemies. (SB 10.26 21)
Garga told Nanda his son matches Narayana in qualities, opulence and fame, so nothing He does should surprise. (SB 10.26 22)
Sukadeva sums up: seeing His sheltered devotees suffer, Krishna smiled and lifted the hill with one hand. (SB 10.26 25)

Astonished cowherds ask Nanda how a seven-year-old could lift Govardhana and recall Krishna's feats since infancy. Nanda repeats Garga Muni's words: this child appears in every age and is equal to Narayana. The doubts of Vraja are dispelled.

children.topic: 27 · Lord Indra and Mother Surabhi Offer Prayers
Time punishes the proud for their good
children.note: Indra calls Krishna the father, guru and time itself, whose incarnations humble those who think themselves masters. (SB 10.27 6)
Blinded by ruling power, Indra offended the Lord and now prays that his mind never be so impure again. (SB 10.27 8)

children.topic: I stopped your sacrifice out of mercy
children.note: Krishna tells Indra he was drunk on heavenly opulence and needed to remember the Lord always. (SB 10.27 15)

children.topic: The Lord drags down the intoxicated
children.note: One blinded by power cannot see Krishna's rod nearby, so for his welfare Krishna removes his position. (SB 10.27 16)

children.topic: Surabhi asks Krishna to be our Indra
children.note: The mother of cows requests Krishna to rule for the sake of cows, brahmanas and all saintly beings. (SB 10.27 20)
Surabhi bathes Him with milk, Indra with Ganga water from Airavata, and they give Him the name Govinda. (SB 10.27 22-23)

Ashamed Indra bows to Krishna, admits his pride, and hears that the sacrifice was stopped out of mercy. Mother Surabhi asks Krishna to be the cows' Indra; she bathes Him with milk and Indra with Ganga water, naming Him Govinda as nature overflows with joy.

children.topic: 28 · Kṛṣṇa Rescues Nanda Mahārāja from the Abode of Varuṇa

children.note: Varuna rejoices that seeing Krishna completes his purpose, since those who accept His feet cross material existence. (SB 10.28 5)
Apologizing for his ignorant servant, Varuna begs mercy and asks Krishna to take Nanda home. (SB 10.28 8)

children.topic: Will He give us His abode?
children.note: Hearing of Varuna's reverence, the cowherds conclude Krishna is God and eagerly hope for His transcendental realm. (SB 10.28 11)

children.topic: People wander without knowing their goal
children.note: Krishna reflects that souls move among higher and lower births by desire, never knowing their true destination. (SB 10.28 13)
Dipped in Brahma-hrada, Nanda and the men see the planet of the Absolute Truth just as Akrura will later. (SB 10.28 16)
In that abode the cowherds are amazed to see Krishna Himself surrounded by the Vedas offering prayers. (SB 10.28 17)

Bathing in the Yamuna at an inauspicious hour after Ekadasi, Nanda is seized by Varuna's servant. Krishna goes to Varuna's court, is worshiped, and brings Nanda home. The cowherds then long for Krishna's abode, and He shows them the spiritual world.

children.topic: 29 · Kṛṣṇa and the Gopīs Meet for the Rāsa Dance

children.note: Hearing Krishna's flute, the women of Vrindavana leave everything and hurry to Him, unknown to each other. (SB 10.29 4)

children.topic: Any strong feeling for Krishna absorbs the mind
children.note: Whether lust, anger, fear, affection or friendship, whoever fixes emotion on Hari becomes absorbed in Him. (SB 10.29 15)

children.topic: Love comes by hearing, not nearness
children.note: Krishna tells the gopis that devotion grows through hearing, seeing, meditating and chanting, so go home. (SB 10.29 27)

children.topic: You are the real husband of all
children.note: The gopis accept the duty to serve husbands but say that service truly belongs to Krishna, the Self of all. (SB 10.29 32)

children.topic: Our feet won't move from Yours
children.note: Krishna has stolen their minds and hands from housework; the gopis ask how they could ever go back. (SB 10.29 34)

children.topic: Krishna vanishes to remove their pride
children.note: Seeing the gopis proud of their good fortune, Krishna disappears at once to bless them further. (SB 10.29 48)

On an autumn full-moon night Krishna's flute draws the gopis from home. He tells them to go back to their husbands, but they reply that He is the true Self of everyone and beg to be His maidservants. He enjoys with them, then vanishes to curb their pride.
So absorbed in remembering Him, the gopis' bodies imitate His walk, smile and speech. (SB 10.30 3)
Like madwomen the gopis question trees about Him, though as Supersoul He pervades everything. (SB 10.30 4)

children.topic: What austerity did Mother Earth perform?
children.note: The gopis ask the earth how she earned the touch of Krishna's feet, recalling Vamana and Varaha. (SB 10.30 10)
Seeing a second set of footprints, the gopis conclude one girl pleased Govinda so much He took her alone. (SB 10.30 28)

children.topic: Climb on My shoulder; then He vanishes
children.note: When the proud gopi asks to be carried, Krishna agrees and immediately disappears, leaving her in remorse. (SB 10.30 38)
Returning to the riverbank, the gopis sit together meditating on Krishna and hoping He will come. (SB 10.30 44)

Bereft of Krishna, the gopis ask trees and the earth where He went, then act out His pastimes, each saying 'I am Krishna.' They track His footprints mixed with those of one special gopi, who was herself left when she grew proud. All return to the Yamuna bank.
The gopis say the goddess of fortune lives in Vraja because Krishna was born there, and they live only for Him. (SB 10.31 1)

children.topic: Not Yasoda's son but the witness within
children.note: The gopis know Krishna is the indwelling Supersoul who appeared at Brahma's request to protect the universe. (SB 10.31 4)

children.topic: Your narrations are life for sufferers
children.note: Stories of Krishna spread by sages destroy sin and bring fortune; those who broadcast them are most generous. (SB 10.31 9)

children.topic: A moment feels like an age
children.note: Without Krishna each instant seems a millennium, and even blinking eyelids steal the sight of His face. (SB 10.31 15)

children.topic: Who but a cheater would leave us?
children.note: The gopis rebuke Krishna for abandoning women who left husbands and children for Him at night. (SB 10.31 16)
The gopis place His soft feet gently on their breasts and worry that forest stones may wound them. (SB 10.31 19)

The gopis' songs of separation: they remind Krishna how His birth glorified Vraja, how He saved them from every danger, and how His feet, lips and flute torment and sustain them. They call Him a cheater yet worry that pebbles may hurt His tender feet.
Smiling in yellow cloth and garland, Krishna appears before the gopis as one who enchants even Cupid. (SB 10.32 2)
One gopi takes Him in through her eyes and holds Him inside, resembling a yogi in meditation. (SB 10.32 8)

children.topic: Who returns love and who does not?
children.note: The gopis ask Krishna to explain those who love only lovers, those who love everyone, and those who love none. (SB 10.32 16)

children.topic: Merciful ones love even the unresponsive
children.note: Krishna says the truly religious serve like parents, showing affection even to those who never reciprocate. (SB 10.32 18)

children.topic: I hide to intensify your love
children.note: Krishna withholds reciprocation so devotees, like a poor man who lost new wealth, think of nothing else. (SB 10.32 20)
Even in Brahma's lifetime Krishna cannot repay the gopis, so their own glorious deeds must be their reward. (SB 10.32 22)

Krishna reappears, smiling, and the weeping gopis revive, each greeting Him in her own way. Seated by the Yamuna they ask about kinds of reciprocation; Krishna explains He hid to intensify their love and admits He can never repay their spotless service.
Expanding Himself, Krishna stands beside each gopi so every girl thinks He is with her alone. (SB 10.33 3)
In the circle of dancing gopis Krishna shines like a dark jewel set in gold. (SB 10.33 6)

children.topic: How could the Lord touch others' wives?
children.note: Pariksit asks how the guardian of religion could apparently violate morality with the gopis. (SB 10.33 26-27)
Sukadeva answers that great controllers consume everything yet stay unpolluted by seeming transgressions. (SB 10.33 29)
One who is not Rudra cannot drink poison; imitating the Lord's conduct destroys an ordinary person. (SB 10.33 30)
Whoever faithfully hears these pastimes gains pure devotion and quickly overcomes the heart's disease of lust. (SB 10.33 39)

Krishna expands Himself between every pair of gopis and the rasa dance begins as demigods watch. After dancing and water play, Pariksit asks how the Lord could touch others' wives; Sukadeva says great controllers are never tainted and must not be imitated.

children.topic: 34 · Nanda Mahārāja Saved and Śaṅkhacūḍa Slain

children.note: Caught in the serpent's jaws, Nanda calls out to his son as a surrendered soul. (SB 10.34 6)

children.topic: Foot touch turns snake into Vidyadhara
children.note: Krishna's divine foot destroys the serpent's sins, and he rises as the shining celestial Sudarsana. (SB 10.34 9)
Sudarsana thanks the sages whose curse led him to the touch of the supreme guru's feet. (SB 10.34 14)

children.topic: Chanting His name purifies all who hear
children.note: Sudarsana reasons that if Krishna's name purifies chanter and hearer, His feet's touch is far greater. (SB 10.34 17)
Seeing Krishna and Balarama chasing him like Time and Death, the Yaksha abandons the women and runs. (SB 10.34 29)
After killing Sankhacuda, Krishna presents the demon's shining jewel to His elder brother before the gopis. (SB 10.34 32)

On a pilgrimage to worship Siva, Nanda is swallowed by a snake; Krishna's foot frees it, revealing the Vidyadhara Sudarsana, cursed for mocking sages. Later the Yaksha Sankhacuda abducts the gopis; Krishna kills him and gives his crest jewel to Balarama.

children.topic: 35 · The Gopīs Sing of Kṛṣṇa as He Wanders in the Forest

children.note: Hearing the flute, bulls, deer and cows stop chewing and freeze as if asleep or painted. (SB 10.35 4-5)
When Krishna calls the cows with His flute, the rivers stand still, waiting for the dust of His feet. (SB 10.35 6-7)

children.topic: Brahma and Siva bow to the flute
children.note: The gopis tell Yasoda that even the chief demigods cannot grasp Krishna's melodies and bow their heads. (SB 10.35 14-15)
Returning with the cows, Krishna's garland is powdered with hoof-dust and His fatigue makes Him more beautiful. (SB 10.35 22-23)
Sukadeva concludes that the women of Vrindavana spend each day festively singing of Krishna's pastimes. (SB 10.35 26)

While Krishna is away in the forest each day, the gopis sing of Him: His flute stuns bulls and deer, halts rivers, bewilders Brahma and Siva, and draws clouds to shade Him. They picture Him returning at dusk, dusty and tired, a festival for their eyes.

children.topic: 36 · The Slaying of Ariṣṭā, the Bull Demon
I am here to punish miscreants
children.note: Krishna calms Vraja and challenges the bull demon, declaring His purpose is to chastise the wicked. (SB 10.36 7)

children.topic: Arista beaten with his own horn
children.note: Krishna throws the bull down, wrings him like wet cloth, tears out a horn and beats him with it. (SB 10.36 13)
Narada tells Kamsa that Krishna is Devaki's son and Balarama Rohini's, hidden with Nanda by Vasudeva. (SB 10.36 17)

children.topic: Kill Them in a wrestling match
children.note: Kamsa orders Canura and Mustika to slay the boys under the pretext of a public wrestling contest. (SB 10.36 22-23)

children.topic: Akrura sent to bring the boys
children.note: Kamsa asks his trusted Akrura to drive to Nanda's village and return with Krishna and Balarama. (SB 10.36 30)

children.topic: Be equal in success and failure
children.note: Akrura tells Kamsa destiny decides results, so one should stay balanced, yet he agrees to go. (SB 10.36 38)

Krishna kills the bull demon Arista by tearing out his horn. Narada then tells Kamsa that Krishna and Balarama are really Vasudeva's sons. Kamsa chains Vasudeva, sends Kesi, plans a wrestling match and elephant ambush, and orders Akrura to fetch the boys.

children.topic: 37 · The Killing of the Demons Keśi and Vyoma

children.note: As the horse charges again, Krishna smiles and pushes His left arm into its mouth like a snake into a hole. (SB 10.37 5)

children.topic: No pride in killing an enemy
children.note: After Kesi dies, Krishna calmly accepts the demigods' flowers without any boast of His easy victory. (SB 10.37 8)
Narada praises Krishna as the Supersoul dwelling unseen in every heart, the witness and supreme controller. (SB 10.37 10-11)
Narada lists what he will see: Kamsa's death, Kalayavana, Naraka, the parijata, many marriages and more. (SB 10.37 15-20)
Narada predicts Krishna will drive Arjuna's chariot and destroy armies to relieve the earth's burden. (SB 10.37 21)
After killing Vyoma like a sacrificial animal, Krishna smashes the boulder and leads the boys to safety. (SB 10.37 33)

Krishna kills the horse demon Kesi by thrusting His arm down its throat. Narada arrives and foretells Krishna's deeds from Kamsa's death to Kurukshetra. Later the demon Vyoma hides cowherd boys in a cave during a game; Krishna slays him and frees them.

children.topic: What have I done to see Krishna?
children.note: Akrura wonders what austerity or charity earned him the fortune of seeing the Lord today. (SB 10.38 3)

children.topic: Words without Krishna decorate a corpse
children.note: Akrura reflects that descriptions of the Lord purify the world, while other speech is lifeless ornament. (SB 10.38 12)

children.topic: Krishna won't see me as an enemy
children.note: Though sent by Kamsa, Akrura trusts the omniscient Lord sees the true intent of every heart. (SB 10.38 18)

children.topic: The Lord reciprocates like a wish-tree
children.note: Krishna favors no one and neglects no one, yet answers each devotee's worship as heavenly trees fulfill wishes. (SB 10.38 22)

children.topic: Rolling in the dust of His footprints
children.note: Seeing Krishna's footprints, Akrura leaps from his chariot weeping and rolls in the dust of his master's feet. (SB 10.38 26)
Nanda asks Akrura how the Yadus survive under cruel Kamsa, who killed his own sister's infants. (SB 10.38 41)

Driving to Vraja, Akrura wonders what merit lets him see Krishna and imagines the Lord's welcome. He rolls in the dust of Krishna's footprints, is embraced by Krishna and hosted by Balarama, and Nanda asks how anyone survives under Kamsa.
Nothing is unattainable for one who pleases Krishna, yet His pure servants never ask Him for anything. (SB 10.39 2)
The gopis accuse fate of joining loving hearts and then senselessly tearing them apart like a child's game. (SB 10.39 19)
Playing on his name, the gopis say the man taking Krishna away is anything but kind. (SB 10.39 21)
Seeing the gopis lament, Krishna consoles them through a messenger with a loving vow to come back. (SB 10.39 35)
The gopis stand motionless, watching the chariot's flag and then its dust until nothing remains. (SB 10.39 36)
In the Yamuna Akrura beholds the four-armed dark-blue Lord lying on the lap of thousand-hooded Sesha. (SB 10.39 46-48)

Krishna hears Kamsa's plans from Akrura and laughs; Nanda orders Vraja to Mathura. The gopis blame Providence and 'cruel' Akrura as Krishna leaves, promising to return. Bathing in the Yamuna, Akrura sees Krishna and Balarama, then Vishnu reclining on Ananta.
Akrura bows to the original Person from whose navel-lotus Brahma appeared and made the universe. (SB 10.40 1)

children.topic: Worshipers of other gods worship You
children.note: Whoever turns to other deities is ultimately worshiping Krishna, the embodiment of all demigods. (SB 10.40 9)

children.topic: All paths flow to You like rivers
children.note: As mountain rivers filled by rain end in the sea, every path of worship finally reaches the Lord. (SB 10.40 10)

children.topic: The universal form of the Lord
children.note: Fire is His face, earth His feet, sun His eye, sky His navel, clouds His hair and rain His seed. (SB 10.40 13-14)

children.topic: Body, home and wealth are a dream
children.note: Akrura admits he foolishly treats family and money as real though they are as unreal as a dream. (SB 10.40 24)

children.topic: Chasing a mirage past real water
children.note: Like a fool who ignores a weed-covered pond to chase a mirage, Akrura has turned away from Krishna. (SB 10.40 26)

Akrura prays to the four-armed Lord: every path of worship, whether Vedic ritual, philosophy, Vaishnava scripture or Siva worship, finally reaches Krishna like rivers to the sea. He praises the universal form and avatars, admits his illusion, and surrenders.

children.topic: Seeing You, what is left to see?
children.note: Akrura says every wonder of earth, sky and water rests in Krishna, so nothing else amazes him. (SB 10.41 5)

children.topic: Without You I won't enter Mathura
children.note: Akrura pleads that Krishna, ever kind to devotees, should not abandon him but grace his home. (SB 10.41 11)

children.topic: First I must kill the Yadus' enemy
children.note: Krishna promises to visit Akrura's house only after satisfying His friends by finishing Kamsa. (SB 10.41 17)

children.topic: Mathura's women embrace Him through their eyes
children.note: Having long heard of Krishna, the city's ladies take Him into their hearts and forget the pain of His absence. (SB 10.41 28)
Insulted by the arrogant royal washerman, Krishna removes his head with just the tips of His fingers. (SB 10.41 37)

children.topic: Sudama asks for devotion, not wealth
children.note: Offered any boon, the garland-maker chooses unshakable devotion, friendship with devotees and compassion for all. (SB 10.41 51)

Krishna withdraws the vision and Akrura drives on to Mathura, begging the brothers to visit his home; Krishna agrees but only after killing Kamsa. In the city Krishna beheads a rude washerman, blesses a weaver, and grants garland-maker Sudama pure devotion.

children.topic: 42 · The Breaking of the Sacrificial Bow
Hunchback made beautiful by a touch
children.note: Krishna presses Trivakra's toes and lifts her chin; her crooked body becomes straight and lovely, showing what seeing Him brings. (SB 10.42 8)

children.topic: Bow snapped like a sugar cane
children.note: Krishna lifts the great bow with His left hand, strings it in an instant and breaks it in two as the guards watch. (SB 10.42 17)

children.topic: Citizens take the brothers for demigods
children.note: Seeing Their strength and beauty after the bow incident, the people of Mathura conclude the two boys must be gods. (SB 10.42 22)
Kamsa sees no head in his mirror, holes in his shadow and ghostly dreams; he cannot sleep for fear of death. (SB 10.42 28-31)

children.topic: The king trembles on his throne
children.note: Surrounded by ministers and vassal rulers at the arena, Kamsa still shakes inwardly with dread. (SB 10.42 35)

In Mathura Krishna straightens the hunchback Trivakra, breaks Kamsa's giant sacrificial bow and beats the guards. Kamsa, terrified by omens all night, sets up the wrestling festival where Nanda and the cowherds take their seats.

children.topic: Krishna kills the elephant with its tusk
children.note: Like a lion Krishna climbs the beast, tears out a tusk and slays both the elephant and its keepers. (SB 10.43 14)

children.topic: Each sees Krishna according to his heart
children.note: Wrestlers see a thunderbolt, women see Cupid, parents see a child, Kamsa sees death, yogis see the Absolute Truth. (SB 10.43 17)
The crowd concludes the two boys are portions of the Supreme Lord born in Vasudeva's house. (SB 10.43 23)
The citizens recount how Krishna held up the hill for a week and tamed Kaliya, protecting Gokula. (SB 10.43 26-27)
Krishna says boys should wrestle equals so the audience is not tainted by an unjust contest. (SB 10.43 38)

At the arena gate Krishna is attacked by the elephant Kuvalayapida; He toys with it, kills it and enters carrying a tusk. Onlookers see Him differently by their moods, recall His deeds, and Canura challenges the brothers to wrestle.

children.topic: Silence in an unjust assembly is sin
children.note: The women say a wise person avoids a gathering of wrongdoers, and if present must speak the truth. (SB 10.44 10)

children.topic: Gopis sing Krishna while doing chores
children.note: Milking, churning and sweeping, the women of Vraja chant about Krishna with choked voices and gain everything. (SB 10.44 15)

children.topic: Canura swung and hurled to death
children.note: Unmoved by the wrestler's blows, Krishna whirls Canura by the arms and throws him down dead like a fallen pillar. (SB 10.44 22-23)

children.topic: Kamsa dragged from the royal dais
children.note: Krishna seizes Kamsa by the hair, knocks off his crown and flings him onto the mat before falling on him. (SB 10.44 37)

children.topic: Constant fear of Krishna grants liberation
children.note: Because Kamsa always saw the Lord with disc in hand, even in dread, he attained a form like the Lord's. (SB 10.44 39)
Freed from chains, Devaki and Vasudeva know their sons as the Lords of the universe and stand with folded palms. (SB 10.44 51)

Krishna and Balarama kill the wrestlers Canura, Mustika and others while the women protest the unequal bout and praise Vraja. Krishna then leaps onto the dais, drags Kamsa down and kills him; Balarama slays his brothers and the parents are freed.

children.topic: A debt to parents no one can repay
children.note: Since parents give the body by which all goals are reached, even a hundred years of service cannot settle the debt. (SB 10.45 5)
One who can but does not support aged parents, wife, child, guru or the sheltered is called dead while breathing. (SB 10.45 7)
Krishna makes His grandfather king, noting that by Yayati's curse no Yadu may sit on the throne. (SB 10.45 13)

children.topic: How to serve a spiritual master
children.note: The brothers serve Sandipani as they would the Lord Himself, setting the perfect example for disciples. (SB 10.45 32)
Learning each subject on one hearing, Krishna and Balarama master all the arts and offer guru-dakshina. (SB 10.45 35-36)
Krishna commands the lord of death to return the boy bound by karma, and presents him to Sandipani. (SB 10.45 45)

Krishna covers His parents' awe with yoga-maya, teaches the duty owed to parents, crowns Ugrasena and sends Nanda home. Initiated by Garga, the brothers study under Sandipani, master sixty-four arts and bring back the guru's dead son from Yamaraja.

children.topic: I sustain those who give up everything
children.note: Krishna says the gopis abandoned body, home and duty for Him alone, and He personally maintains such devotees. (SB 10.46 4)
Nanda asks Uddhava whether Krishna thinks of His mother, friends, cows, Vrindavana and Govardhana. (SB 10.46 18)
Hearing of her son's deeds, Yasoda cries and milk streams from her breasts out of love. (SB 10.46 28)
Even an impure person who fixes the mind on Him at death burns all sins and reaches the supreme abode. (SB 10.46 32-33)

children.topic: Krishna dwells in all hearts like fire
children.note: Uddhava tells Nanda not to grieve; the Lord is within every being as fire lies hidden in wood. (SB 10.46 36)

children.topic: He is everyone's son and father
children.note: Krishna is not Nanda's child alone but the son, soul, father and mother of all living beings. (SB 10.46 42)

Krishna sends Uddhava to Vraja to console His parents and the gopis. Nanda asks whether Krishna remembers them and Yasoda weeps. Uddhava explains that Krishna is everyone's father and self, present in all hearts, and promises His return.
Taking a bee for Krishna's envoy, the gopi tells it not to touch her feet with kunkuma from a rival's breast. (SB 10.47 12)

children.topic: A drop of Krishna-katha ruins worldliness
children.note: Those who taste even once the nectar of His pastimes leave home and wander Vrindavana like begging birds. (SB 10.47 18)

children.topic: You are never apart from Me
children.note: Krishna's message: as the elements pervade all things, He is present in everyone's mind, senses and life. (SB 10.47 29)
Krishna stays away so the gopis' meditation on Him grows more intense and draws their minds nearer. (SB 10.47 35)

children.topic: Let me be dust in Vrindavana
children.note: Uddhava prays to become a bush or creeper there so the gopis' foot-dust may fall on him. (SB 10.47 61)
Uddhava bows again and again to the dust of the cowherd women whose loud glorification of Krishna cleanses everything. (SB 10.47 63)

The gopis meet Uddhava; one gopi pours out her hurt to a bee as Krishna's messenger. Uddhava delivers Krishna's message that He is never separated from them and praises the gopis' love above all, wishing to be dust at their feet.

children.topic: Choosing sense pleasure from the Lord
children.note: One who worships the rarely approached Lord and then asks for mundane enjoyment settles for a trifle. (SB 10.48 11)
Akrura says the Lord set the Vedic path and incarnates in goodness whenever atheists obstruct it. (SB 10.48 23)

children.topic: The grateful friend who gives Himself
children.note: To those who worship Him in friendship the Lord grants all desires, even His own self, without diminishing. (SB 10.48 26)

children.topic: Cut the ropes of family attachment
children.note: Akrura begs Krishna to sever illusory bonds to children, wife, wealth and body, all products of maya. (SB 10.48 27)

children.topic: Saints purify at once; tirthas take time
children.note: Holy rivers and deities purify slowly, but saintly devotees purify simply by being seen. (SB 10.48 31)

children.topic: Blind king ruled by wicked sons
children.note: Krishna notes Dhritarashtra is controlled by his sons and treats his brother's children unjustly. (SB 10.48 34)

Krishna visits Trivakra and fulfils her desire, then goes to Akrura's house, where Akrura offers prayers on the Lord's nature and incarnation. Krishna honours Akrura as guru and uncle and sends him to Hastinapura to check on the Pandavas.
Surrounded by enemies, Kunti asks whether Krishna will come to console her and her fatherless sons. (SB 10.49 10)
For those afraid of death and rebirth, Kunti sees no refuge other than Krishna's liberating feet. (SB 10.49 12)

children.topic: Treat Pandu's sons as your own
children.note: Akrura warns that partiality brings infamy now and hell later, so the king must be equal to all nephews. (SB 10.49 19)
Every creature enters and leaves alone and alone reaps the fruits of good and evil deeds. (SB 10.49 21)

children.topic: See the world as a dream
children.note: Akrura urges the king to view life as illusion and fantasy, control the mind and become peaceful. (SB 10.49 25)

children.topic: Lightning cannot stay in a cloud
children.note: Dhritarashtra confesses that good advice cannot stay in a heart swayed by love for his sons. (SB 10.49 27)

Akrura stays months in Hastinapura observing Dhritarashtra's partiality. Kunti weeps and prays to Krishna for shelter. Akrura counsels the blind king on justice and the aloneness of every soul; the king admits attachment binds him.

children.topic: 50 · Kṛṣṇa Establishes the City of Dvārakā

children.note: Krishna resolves that He has come to lighten the earth's burden, protect the pious and kill the wicked. (SB 10.50 9)

children.topic: Heroes act, they do not boast
children.note: Answering Jarasandha's taunts, Krishna says real fighters show prowess in deeds, not words. (SB 10.50 19)
Balarama binds the king, but Krishna stops him since Jarasandha still has a role to play. (SB 10.50 31)
Jarasandha loses the same way seventeen times but keeps attacking the Yadus protected by Krishna. (SB 10.50 41)

children.topic: A fortress built in the sea
children.note: Facing threats from two sides, Krishna has a twelve-yojana fort and wondrous city built in the ocean. (SB 10.50 49)

children.topic: Sudharma hall and parijata from Indra
children.note: Indra gives the assembly hall where mortals escape death's laws, plus the heavenly parijata tree. (SB 10.50 54)

Jarasandha besieges Mathura with 23 armies; Krishna and Balarama, with divine chariots, destroy them but release Jarasandha, who returns seventeen times. When Kalayavana arrives, Krishna builds Dvaraka in the sea and moves the Yadus there.
Kicked awake, Mucukunda looks at the barbarian and in an instant reduces him to ashes. (SB 10.51 12)
The demigods tell Mucukunda that irresistible time, which sweeps away all his contemporaries, is the Supreme Lord. (SB 10.51 19)

children.topic: Even I cannot count My births
children.note: Krishna tells Mucukunda His names, births and deeds are limitless beyond His own counting. (SB 10.51 36)

children.topic: Human life wasted like animal in a well
children.note: One who gains the rare human form but ignores the Lord's feet falls into the dark well of household life. (SB 10.51 46)

children.topic: King today, worms or ashes tomorrow
children.note: The body that rides golden chariots as 'king' is soon called feces, worms or ashes by time's power. (SB 10.51 50)
Mucukunda asks nothing but service to Krishna's feet; a wise man would not choose a boon that binds him. (SB 10.51 55)

Krishna lures Kalayavana into a cave where sleeping King Mucukunda's glance burns him to ash. Krishna reveals Himself; Mucukunda confesses wasted royal life, refuses material boons and asks only for service. Krishna blesses his future birth.
Pariksit says no experienced hearer tires of Krishna's pure, charming stories that wash away worldly stain. (SB 10.52 20)
Having fed and rested Rukmini's messenger, the Lord rubs his feet with His own hands before questioning him. (SB 10.52 29)
Krishna repeatedly honours brahmanas who are satisfied, humble and peaceful, the best well-wishers of all. (SB 10.52 33)

children.topic: Rukmini's shameless heart fixed on Krishna
children.note: Her letter opens: hearing of His qualities and beauty, she has placed her mind on Him without shame. (SB 10.52 37)

children.topic: Don't let the jackal take the lion's share
children.note: Rukmini pleads that Krishna come quickly and not let Sisupala touch what belongs to the hero. (SB 10.52 39)
Rukmini explains she will leave the palace to worship Girija before the wedding, when He can take her. (SB 10.52 42)

Mucukunda leaves for Badarikasrama. Krishna feigns flight from Jarasandha, leaps from burning Pravarsana and returns to Dvaraka. Pariksit asks about Rukmini; she sends a brahmana with a letter choosing Krishna and telling Him how to take her.

children.topic: My mind is fixed on her
children.note: Krishna tells the brahmana he cannot sleep for thinking of Rukmini and knows Rukmi blocks the marriage. (SB 10.53 2)
With the wedding at dawn and no sign of Krishna or the messenger, Rukmini laments her ill fortune. (SB 10.53 23)
Overjoyed at news of Krishna's arrival, Rukmini simply bows to the brahmana, having no fitting gift. (SB 10.53 31)
She bows to the goddess and her children and asks for one boon: that Krishna become her husband. (SB 10.53 46)
Krishna lifts Rukmini onto His Garuda-flagged chariot and drives slowly out through the ring of kings. (SB 10.53 56)

Krishna races to Kundina in one night while Balarama follows with an army. Rukmini waits in anguish, then rejoices when the brahmana returns. After praying to Ambika she steps out, and Krishna lifts her onto His chariot before the stunned kings.

children.topic: 54 · The Marriage of Kṛṣṇa and Rukmiṇī

children.note: Jarasandha says happiness and sorrow move by the Supreme Lord's will as a puppet moves by its master. (SB 10.54 12)

children.topic: Please do not kill my brother
children.note: Rukmini falls at Krishna's feet in terror and begs Him to spare Rukmi's life. (SB 10.54 33)
Krishna ties Rukmi and disfigures him by cutting patches of hair and moustache as a comic punishment. (SB 10.54 35)
Balarama tells Rukmini no one else causes our joy or grief; a person experiences his own actions. (SB 10.54 38)
The self neither joins nor leaves material things, as the sun is unaffected by sight and what is seen. (SB 10.54 46)

children.topic: Moon phases, not the moon, change
children.note: Birth and change belong to the body, not the self, as the new moon is called the moon's death. (SB 10.54 47)

The Yadus rout the pursuing kings; Jarasandha consoles Sisupala with talk of fate. Rukmi attacks alone, is defeated and shaved by Krishna at Rukmini's plea. Balarama rebukes Krishna and teaches Rukmini about the soul; the wedding is celebrated.
Sambara kidnaps Pradyumna before he is ten days old and casts the baby into the ocean. (SB 10.55 3)
Mayavati tells Pradyumna he is Narayana's son and Cupid himself, and she is his lawful wife. (SB 10.55 12)
Rati gives Pradyumna the mystic knowledge that overcomes every deluding spell of the demon. (SB 10.55 16)
After countering the demon's magical weapons, Pradyumna cuts off Sambara's head with his sword. (SB 10.55 24)

children.topic: A mother's heart knows her son
children.note: Rukmini senses the stranger is her lost child from her surging affection and quivering left arm. (SB 10.55 34)
Even palace women felt conjugal attraction, since Pradyumna looked exactly like Krishna and Cupid. (SB 10.55 40)

Cupid is reborn as Pradyumna to Rukmini, stolen by Sambara, thrown in the sea, swallowed by a fish and raised by Mayavati, who is Rati. She reveals his identity; he kills Sambara and flies home, where Rukmini and the palace women recognise him.

children.topic: Jewel yields gold, wards off calamity
children.note: The Syamantaka produces eight bharas of gold daily and keeps its home free from famine and disease. (SB 10.56 11)
Missing his brother, Satrajit rumours that Krishna killed Prasena for the jewel and the story spreads. (SB 10.56 16)
Krishna and Jambavan fight without rest with weapons, stones, trees and finally fists like thunderbolts. (SB 10.56 24)
Exhausted, the bear king realises his opponent is Vishnu, the strength and life of all beings. (SB 10.56 26)

children.topic: You built the bridge and burned Lanka
children.note: Jambavan identifies Krishna as Rama who tamed the ocean, crossed to Lanka and beheaded Ravana. (SB 10.56 28)

children.topic: Keep the jewel, We share its fruits
children.note: Krishna returns the gem to Satrajit, the sun-god's devotee, saying its benefits will reach the Yadus anyway. (SB 10.56 45)

Satrajit receives the Syamantaka jewel from the sun-god and refuses to give it to Ugrasena. Prasena is killed wearing it; Satrajit blames Krishna, who tracks it to Jambavan's cave, fights him 28 days, and gains the jewel, Jambavati and Satyabhama.
Persuaded by others, Satadhanva kills sleeping Satrajit for the jewel and thereby dooms himself. (SB 10.57 5)
He cites Kamsa's ruin and Jarasandha's seventeen defeats as proof that enmity to the Lords brings no good. (SB 10.57 12-13)
Akrura recalls how seven-year-old Krishna held up Govardhana as easily as a boy picks a mushroom. (SB 10.57 16)
Krishna, chasing on foot near Mithila, cuts off the murderer's head but finds no jewel on him. (SB 10.57 21)
Blaming Akrura's absence for the omens, the citizens forget that misfortune cannot dwell where the Lord resides. (SB 10.57 31)
Krishna displays the Syamantaka to His relatives to end the accusations, then hands it back to Akrura. (SB 10.57 41)

While Krishna is in Hastinapura, Satadhanva, urged by Akrura and Krtavarma, murders Satrajit for the jewel. Krishna kills him but finds no gem; Balarama stays in Mithila. Omens in Dvaraka bring Akrura back, and he produces the jewel Krishna leaves with him.
Kunti says the Lord, friend of all, still removes the miseries of those who constantly remember Him. (SB 10.58 10)

children.topic: Seen by fools, rare for yogis
children.note: Yudhishthira wonders what merit let them behold Krishna, whom perfected mystics seldom see. (SB 10.58 11)
The sun-god's daughter declares she will accept no husband but Vishnu and waits in the Yamuna for Him. (SB 10.58 21)

children.topic: A king begging, out of friendship
children.note: Krishna admits begging is condemned for kshatriyas, yet asks Nagnajit for his daughter to gain his friendship. (SB 10.58 40)
Krishna expands into seven and easily subdues the wild bulls that had broken many princes. (SB 10.58 45)

children.topic: Arjuna drives off the rival kings
children.note: Wielding Gandiva, Arjuna scatters the kings attacking Krishna's wedding party like a lion routing animals. (SB 10.58 54)

Krishna visits the Pandavas at Indraprastha, hears Kunti's gratitude, and with Arjuna meets Kalindi, whom He marries. He then weds Mitravinda, wins Satya by taming seven bulls, and marries Bhadra and Laksmana, before freeing Bhauma's captives.

children.topic: 59 · The Killing of the Demon Naraka

children.note: After shattering Mura's trident and club, Krishna slices off all five of the demon's heads with His disc. (SB 10.59 10)

children.topic: Bhauma's head falls to the cakra
children.note: Before the demon can throw his trident, Krishna's razor disc removes his head atop his elephant. (SB 10.59 21)
Bhumi says thinking the elements, senses and gods exist independently is illusion; all rest within the one Lord. (SB 10.59 30)

children.topic: Bhumi asks mercy for Bhauma's son
children.note: The earth-goddess presents the frightened boy and asks Krishna to place His sin-dispelling hand on his head. (SB 10.59 31)
Having got Aditi's earrings back, Indra still battles Krishna over the parijata; such is the gods' blindness. (SB 10.59 41)

children.topic: One form for each of 16,000 brides
children.note: Krishna expands into as many forms as princesses and marries them all at once, each in her own palace. (SB 10.59 42)

On Indra's request Krishna rides Garuda with Satyabhama to Pragjyotisapura, breaks its defences, kills Mura and his sons and beheads Narakasura. Bhumi prays for Bhauma's son; Krishna frees 16,000 princesses, takes the parijata and marries them all.
Krishna teases that He owns nothing and is dear only to those who have nothing, so the wealthy avoid Him. (SB 10.60 14)

children.topic: Rukmini faints like a felled plantain
children.note: Unable to bear His words, she drops her fan and bangles and collapses to the floor in grief. (SB 10.60 24)
Krishna assures Rukmini He knows her devotion and joked merely to hear what she would say. (SB 10.60 29)

children.topic: A husband is a corpse in skin
children.note: Rukmini says a woman who misses the fragrance of His feet accepts a body of flesh and waste as her lover. (SB 10.60 45)

children.topic: Hell for those who want only wealth
children.note: Krishna says people who gain Him yet crave riches, available even in hell, deserve that destination. (SB 10.60 53)
When Rukmi died at a wedding, Rukmini said nothing lest she lose Krishna; He says that silence won Him. (SB 10.60 56)

As Rukmini fans Krishna, He jokingly says she chose a poor, fearful husband and should pick a king. She faints in shock; He consoles her, saying He teased to hear her reply. Rukmini answers with deep philosophy and Krishna praises her unwavering love.
Because Krishna never seemed to leave her palace, every wife believed she was His most beloved. (SB 10.61 2)
Sixteen thousand queens' coy glances and gestures fail to agitate the Lord's senses. (SB 10.61 4)
Despite hating Krishna, Rukmi gives his granddaughter to Aniruddha to please his sister Rukmini. (SB 10.61 25)

children.topic: A voice from the sky: Rukmi lies
children.note: When Rukmi falsely claims the wager, a celestial voice declares Balarama the honest winner. (SB 10.61 33)
Insulted as a forest cowherd, Balarama strikes Rukmi dead in the midst of the wedding assembly. (SB 10.61 36)
To protect His bonds with both Rukmini and Balarama, Krishna stays silent at Rukmi's death. (SB 10.61 39)

Sukadeva lists the ten sons of each principal queen; Pradyumna marries Rukmi's daughter and Aniruddha his granddaughter Rocana. At that wedding Rukmi cheats Balarama at dice and mocks Him, so Balarama kills him with His club while Krishna stays silent.

children.topic: 62 · The Meeting of Ūṣā and Aniruddha
A thousand arms, no one to fight
children.note: Bana complains to Siva that his thousand arms are a burden since none in three worlds can match him. (SB 10.62 6)

children.topic: Siva predicts Bana's flag will fall
children.note: Angered, Siva says Bana's pride will be crushed when he meets a fighter equal to Siva himself. (SB 10.62 8)
Among Citralekha's drawings of the Vrishnis, Usa blushes and bows her head at Aniruddha's picture. (SB 10.62 18-19)

children.topic: Aniruddha carried off in his sleep
children.note: Citralekha uses yogic power to lift the sleeping prince from Dvaraka to Usa's chambers in Sonitapura. (SB 10.62 21)
Aniruddha with his iron club scatters Bana's guards, breaking their heads and limbs. (SB 10.62 32)
Bana captures Aniruddha with mystic serpent ropes, and Usa weeps in grief. (SB 10.62 33)

Banasura, Bali's son and Siva's devotee, begs for a worthy fight and Siva foretells his humbling. His daughter Usa dreams of a lover; Citralekha draws portraits, identifies Aniruddha and brings him from Dvaraka. Bana discovers them and binds Aniruddha.
Krishna counters brahmastra with brahmastra, wind with mountain, fire with rain and pasupata with narayanastra. (SB 10.63 13)
Krishna bewilders Siva with a yawning weapon and then cuts down Bana's army. (SB 10.63 14)
The Siva-jvara says all embodied souls suffer as long as they chase ambition and neglect the Lord's feet. (SB 10.63 28)
Siva says a mortal who abandons the Lord, his true self and friend, for sense objects chooses poison over nectar. (SB 10.63 42)

children.topic: Prahlada's descendants will not be killed
children.note: Krishna spares Bana because He promised Prahlada never to slay his line. (SB 10.63 47)

children.topic: Remember this victory, never be defeated
children.note: Whoever recalls Krishna's triumph over Siva at dawn will never meet defeat. (SB 10.63 53)

The Yadus besiege Sonitapura; Krishna battles Siva and his hosts, defeats the Siva-jvara with His own fever weapon and cuts off Bana's arms. Siva prays and asks mercy for Bana; Krishna leaves him four arms and brings Aniruddha and Usa home.
At Krishna's touch the creature sheds its lizard body and stands shining in golden celestial form. (SB 10.64 6)
A brahmana's cow wandered into Nrga's herd and he unknowingly donated it to another brahmana. (SB 10.64 16)
Nrga chooses to suffer his sin before enjoying his merit, and Yamaraja drops him into a lizard body. (SB 10.64 24)
Krishna says halahala has a cure, but stolen brahminical wealth has none in this world. (SB 10.64 33)

children.topic: Kings blinded by opulence court hell
children.note: Rulers who childishly crave a brahmana's property are really hankering for hell. (SB 10.64 36)

children.topic: Bow to brahmanas even when they curse
children.note: Krishna tells His followers never to mistreat a learned brahmana, even one who strikes or abuses them. (SB 10.64 41)

Yadu boys find a giant lizard in a well; Krishna lifts it out and it becomes King Nrga, who explains he fell for unknowingly giving away a brahmana's cow. After Nrga departs to heaven, Krishna warns rulers never to take a brahmana's property.
The parents lift Balarama onto their laps and ask that He and Krishna protect them always. (SB 10.65 3)

children.topic: We gave up everything for Him
children.note: The gopis say they abandoned family for Krishna, yet He left them, though who could distrust His promises? (SB 10.65 11-12)
Balarama consoles the gopis by relaying confidential words Krishna sent, which touch their hearts. (SB 10.65 16)

children.topic: I'll drag you here in a hundred streams
children.note: Angry that Yamuna ignores His call, Balarama threatens to pull her with the tip of His plough. (SB 10.65 26)
Frightened, the river-goddess admits she did not know His supremacy and begs release. (SB 10.65 29)
Sukadeva says the Yamuna's many branches still show where Balarama dragged her. (SB 10.65 33)

Balarama visits Vraja, is embraced by Nanda and Yasoda and questioned by the cowherds and gopis, who complain of Krishna's neglect. He stays two months, enjoys varuni liquor with the gopis, and drags the disobedient Yamuna with His plough.
Childish courtiers convince Paundraka that he is the Supreme Lord descended to earth. (SB 10.66 2)
Seeing Paundraka wearing imitation conch, disc, Kaustubha and yellow silk, Krishna laughs aloud. (SB 10.66 15)
Krishna wrecks his chariot with arrows and removes his head like Indra lopping a mountain peak. (SB 10.66 21)
By always thinking of Krishna, even as a mimic, Paundraka broke his bonds and became Krishna conscious. (SB 10.66 24)

children.topic: Do not fear, I shall protect you
children.note: When the fire demon nears Dvaraka, Krishna simply laughs and assures the citizens of safety. (SB 10.66 37)
Repelled by the disc, the fiery creature returns to Varanasi and burns Sudaksina and his priests. (SB 10.66 40)

Paundraka, flattered into believing he is Vasudeva, orders Krishna to surrender His symbols. Krishna laughs, beheads him and the king of Kasi. Kasi's prince Sudaksina invokes a fire demon against Dvaraka, but Sudarsana repels it and burns Varanasi.

children.topic: Dvivida burns the land for Naraka
children.note: The ape Dvivida sets fire to towns and villages to avenge his slain friend Narakasura. (SB 10.67 3)
Dvivida insults the girls with crude gestures right in front of Balarama, provoking him. (SB 10.67 13)
Unmoved like a mountain, Balarama grabs the falling tree and strikes back with his club Sunanda. (SB 10.67 18)

children.topic: One bare-handed blow ends the fight
children.note: Throwing aside his weapons, Balarama smashes Dvivida's collarbone with his fist and the ape collapses. (SB 10.67 25)
Sages and demigods shower flowers and shout praise as the world's disturber is slain. (SB 10.67 27)

Pariksit asks about Balarama. Sukadeva tells of the gorilla Dvivida, Naraka's friend, who ravages kingdoms and then mocks Balarama and his girlfriends on Raivataka Hill. After a furious tree-and-boulder duel, Balarama kills him with a bare-handed blow.

children.topic: Samba seizes Laksmana at her svayamvara
children.note: Jambavati's son carries off Duryodhana's daughter, sparking the Kuru-Yadu confrontation. (SB 10.68 1)
Cooling the armed Yadus, Balarama travels to Hastinapura hoping to settle the quarrel peacefully. (SB 10.68 14-15)

children.topic: Kurus call the Yadus a mere shoe
children.note: The proud Kurus sneer that the Yadus rule only by Kuru favor and dare not give orders. (SB 10.68 24)

children.topic: Even Brahma and Siva carry Krishna's foot-dust
children.note: Balarama asks how Krishna, worshiped by all demigods, could be unfit for a royal throne. (SB 10.68 37)

children.topic: Balarama drags Hastinapura with his plow
children.note: Enraged, Balarama hooks the city with his plow and starts pulling it toward the Ganges. (SB 10.68 41)

children.topic: Your anger is for teaching, not hatred
children.note: The Kurus admit Balarama's wrath is meant to instruct and protect the world, not to punish out of envy. (SB 10.68 47)

Krishna's son Samba abducts Duryodhana's daughter Laksmana and is captured by the Kurus. Balarama goes to Hastinapura to negotiate, is insulted, and drags the whole city toward the Ganges with his plow until the Kurus surrender and bless the couple.

children.topic: 69 · Nārada Muni Visits Lord Kṛṣṇa’s Palaces in Dvārakā
Narada wonders at sixteen thousand marriages
children.note: Hearing Krishna wed thousands of brides in one body, Narada sets out to see it for himself. (SB 10.69 1-6)
Though the water from Krishna's own feet is the Ganges, he honors Narada by bathing his feet. (SB 10.69 15)

children.topic: Narada asks only to remember Krishna
children.note: Narada's single request is the power to keep the Lord in mind wherever he wanders. (SB 10.69 18)

children.topic: In every palace, the same Krishna
children.note: Krishna greets Narada afresh in each home as if seeing him for the first time, astonishing the sage. (SB 10.69 20-22)

children.topic: I follow dharma to teach the world
children.note: Krishna tells Narada he both speaks and practises religion so that others will learn from him. (SB 10.69 40)
Anyone who hears or appreciates Krishna's inimitable activities gains devotion to the Lord. (SB 10.69 45)

Curious how Krishna lives with sixteen thousand wives at once, Narada tours the palaces of Dvaraka and finds Krishna in every one, busy with a different household or royal duty. Krishna explains he practises dharma to teach the world; Narada leaves in wonder.

children.topic: Krishna meditates on himself at dawn
children.note: Rising in the brahma-muhurta, Krishna fixes his mind on the one self-luminous Supreme Truth. (SB 10.70 4-5)

children.topic: Daily gift of thousands of cows
children.note: Each morning Krishna worships elders and gives decorated cows to learned brahmanas. (SB 10.70 7-9)

children.topic: Imprisoned kings surrender out of fear
children.note: The captive kings admit their separatist mentality yet take shelter of Krishna. (SB 10.70 25)
The kings recall Krishna's victories and beg him to end Jarasandha's pride. (SB 10.70 30)
Narada reports that Yudhisthira wants to worship Krishna with the greatest of sacrifices. (SB 10.70 41)
Calling Uddhava his best eye and friend, Krishna asks him to decide the course of action. (SB 10.70 46)

Sukadeva describes Krishna's daily routine, from dawn meditation and charity to court in the Sudharma hall. A messenger from kings imprisoned by Jarasandha begs for rescue; Narada announces Yudhisthira's Rajasuya, and Krishna asks Uddhava's advice.
Uddhava argues that defeating Jarasandha both frees the kings and qualifies Yudhisthira for the Rajasuya. (SB 10.71 3)

children.topic: Bhima should beg a duel as a brahmana
children.note: Since Jarasandha never refuses brahmanas, Bhima in disguise can obtain single combat and kill him. (SB 10.71 7)

children.topic: Captive queens sing of their rescuer
children.note: Wives of the imprisoned kings, the gopis and sages alike glorify Krishna as the slayer of enemies. (SB 10.71 9)
Holding Krishna, the king is flooded with bliss and forgets he is in the material world. (SB 10.71 26)

children.topic: City women rush to see Krishna
children.note: Women of Indraprastha abandon their chores and husbands to glimpse Krishna on the road. (SB 10.71 33)
During the stay Krishna and Arjuna feed Agni the forest and save Maya, who builds Yudhisthira's assembly hall. (SB 10.71 44-45)

Uddhava advises that Bhima killing Jarasandha in a duel will free the kings and enable the Rajasuya. Krishna sets out with army and queens, is welcomed with overwhelming love by the Pandavas and Kunti at Indraprastha, and stays several months.

children.topic: 72 · The Slaying of the Demon Jarāsandha
Serving your feet frees one from bondage
children.note: Yudhisthira says those who serve Krishna's feet gain liberation and even their worldly wishes. (SB 10.72 4)

children.topic: No one can defeat my devotee
children.note: Krishna assures that neither demigod nor king can overcome his devotee by strength, fame or wealth. (SB 10.72 11)

children.topic: What will the generous not give?
children.note: The disguised guests hint at their request with a verse on tolerance, generosity and equal vision. (SB 10.72 19)

children.topic: Jarasandha will give even his body
children.note: Recognizing royal guests in disguise, Jarasandha still resolves to grant whatever they ask. (SB 10.72 23)
Krishna shows Bhima how to kill his opponent by splitting a small branch in half. (SB 10.72 41)
Krishna installs Jarasandha's son as king of Magadha and releases all the imprisoned rulers. (SB 10.72 46)

Yudhisthira gets Krishna's blessing for the Rajasuya; the Pandavas conquer the directions. Krishna, Bhima and Arjuna visit Jarasandha as brahmanas and beg a duel. Bhima fights him to a stalemate until Krishna splits a twig, and Bhima tears the king in two.

children.topic: 73 · Lord Kṛṣṇa Blesses the Liberated Kings

children.note: Drunk on opulence, a ruler loses self-restraint and mistakes fleeting assets for permanent ones. (SB 10.73 10)
The kings confess they once fought each other in arrogance; now they only wish to remember Krishna's feet. (SB 10.73 12-13)

children.topic: A mirage kingdom, no longer wanted
children.note: The kings renounce both worldly rule and heavenly rewards as empty enticements. (SB 10.73 14)

children.topic: Ravana and Naraka fell from pride
children.note: Krishna lists rulers who lost everything through infatuation with material opulence. (SB 10.73 20)

children.topic: Keep your mind on me amid family life
children.note: Krishna tells the kings to raise families and face joy and sorrow while fixing their minds on him. (SB 10.73 22)
Hearing of the victory, the king is so moved by Krishna's mercy that he cannot speak. (SB 10.73 35)

The freed kings, emaciated from prison, praise Krishna and admit that pride in power caused their fall; they ask only to remember his feet. Krishna blesses them with devotion, tells them to rule righteously and sends them home, then returns to Indraprastha.

children.topic: 74 · The Deliverance of Śiśupāla at the Rājasūya Sacrifice
Sahadeva names Krishna for first worship
children.note: Sahadeva declares that Krishna embodies all the demigods and everything used in sacrifice. (SB 10.74 19)
Worshiping the complete Soul of all returns unlimited honor to the giver. (SB 10.74 24)

children.topic: Sisupala: why worship a cowherd boy?
children.note: Sisupala rages that exalted sages are passed over for a cowherd, like a crow eating sacred rice. (SB 10.74 33-34)

children.topic: Walk out on blasphemy or fall
children.note: One who stays where the Lord or his devotee is criticized loses all pious credit. (SB 10.74 40)
Restraining his devotees, Krishna himself kills the attacking Sisupala with his disc. (SB 10.74 43)

children.topic: Three lifetimes of hatred, then liberation
children.note: By constantly thinking of Krishna, even in enmity, Sisupala attains the Lord's own nature. (SB 10.74 46)

At the Rajasuya, Sahadeva proposes Krishna be honored first and all agree. Sisupala abuses Krishna; the Lord tolerates him, then beheads him with the Sudarsana disc, and Sisupala's soul merges into Krishna. The sacrifice ends, but Duryodhana burns with envy.

children.topic: Family members serve at the sacrifice
children.note: Bhima runs the kitchen, Duryodhana the treasury, and Krishna himself washes guests' feet. (SB 10.75 4-7)

children.topic: A bath that frees the worst sinner
children.note: All citizens bathe at the sacred spot where even grave sins are instantly washed away. (SB 10.75 21)
By Krishna's grace the king's burning ambition is finally satisfied. (SB 10.75 30)
Fooled by Maya's illusions, Duryodhana hitches his robe on dry floor and then tumbles into a pool. (SB 10.75 37)
Krishna stays silent at the laughter, for the insult serves his plan to relieve the earth's burden. (SB 10.75 39)

Pariksit asks why only Duryodhana was unhappy at the Rajasuya. Sukadeva describes the joyful closing bath in the Yamuna. Later, in Maya Danava's magic hall, Duryodhana mistakes floor for water and falls in; Bhima and the women laugh, and he leaves humiliated.

children.topic: 76 · The Battle Between Śālva and the Vṛṣṇis
Salva vows to destroy the Yadus
children.note: Defeated at Rukmini's wedding, Salva swears before all the kings to wipe out the Yadu race. (SB 10.76 3)

children.topic: Maya Danava builds the airship Saubha
children.note: Siva grants Salva's wish and Maya constructs an unassailable flying iron city. (SB 10.76 7)
Like sunlight dissolving night, Pradyumna's divine weapons destroy all of Salva's illusions. (SB 10.76 17)

children.topic: The ship that is many and then one
children.note: Saubha multiplies, vanishes and reappears so the Yadus cannot tell where it really is. (SB 10.76 21)

children.topic: No Yadu has ever fled battle
children.note: Pradyumna laments that his driver's rescue has stained his family honor. (SB 10.76 29)

children.topic: A driver's duty is to protect his master
children.note: The charioteer defends his act: he was bound to save his unconscious lord. (SB 10.76 32)

Salva, humiliated at Rukmini's wedding, worships Siva and wins the flying iron city Saubha. He attacks Dvaraka while Krishna is away; Pradyumna leads the defense and shatters Salva's illusions, but is knocked out and carried off by his driver, to his shame.

children.topic: 77 · Lord Kṛṣṇa Slays the Demon Śālva

children.note: Pradyumna methodically strikes down Dyuman's horses, driver, bow, flag and finally his head. (SB 10.77 3)

children.topic: Heroes act, they do not boast
children.note: Krishna tells Salva that death stands beside him and real warriors show their power in deeds. (SB 10.77 19)
Through Maya Danava's illusion Salva appears to cut off Krishna's father's head. (SB 10.77 27)

children.topic: Krishna sees through the demon's trick
children.note: After a moment of human-like grief, Krishna recognizes the whole scene as magic. (SB 10.77 28)
Sukadeva rejects the idea that fear or illusion could touch the all-knowing Supreme Lord. (SB 10.77 31)
As Indra once beheaded Vrtra, Krishna cuts off the magician's head with his disc. (SB 10.77 36)

Pradyumna kills Dyuman; the battle lasts twenty-seven days. Krishna returns and fights Salva, whose magic makes Krishna seem to see his father Vasudeva beheaded. Krishna sees through the illusion, smashes Saubha and beheads Salva; Dantavakra then attacks.

children.topic: 78 · The Killing of Dantavakra, Vidūratha and Romaharṣaṇa

children.note: Unmoved by the demon's club, Krishna strikes him in the chest and he falls dead. (SB 10.78 8)
Only those of beastly vision imagine that the Lord of the universe can lose. (SB 10.78 16)

children.topic: Balarama leaves on a neutral pilgrimage
children.note: To stay out of the Kuru-Pandava war, Balarama departs to bathe at holy places. (SB 10.78 17)
Balarama says Romaharsana's scholarship is like an actor's part, since he never conquered his mind. (SB 10.78 25-26)

children.topic: A blade of grass kills Romaharsana
children.note: Balarama merely touches the reciter with a grass tip and he dies. (SB 10.78 28)

children.topic: The son will speak the Puranas
children.note: Balarama grants that Romaharsana's son will inherit the role of Purana reciter with long life. (SB 10.78 36)

Krishna kills Dantavakra with his club and beheads his brother Viduratha; their souls merge into him. Balarama, avoiding the Kurukshetra war, goes on pilgrimage, kills the proud reciter Romaharsana with a blade of grass, and agrees to atone by killing Balvala.

children.topic: Plow hooks Balvala from the sky
children.note: Balarama catches the flying demon with his plow and crushes his head with his club. (SB 10.79 5)

children.topic: Blessings from Agastya at the southern sea
children.note: On pilgrimage Balarama gives cows, bows to Agastya and visits Kanyakumari. (SB 10.79 16-17)
Balarama tells Bhima and Duryodhana they are too evenly matched for either to win. (SB 10.79 27)

children.topic: Enmity too deep to be pacified
children.note: Both fighters ignore the advice, each remembering the insults suffered from the other. (SB 10.79 28)

children.topic: Balarama gives the sages divine vision
children.note: The sages learn to see the whole universe within Balarama and him within everything. (SB 10.79 31)

children.topic: Remember Balarama at dawn and dusk
children.note: Regularly recalling Balarama's deeds makes one dear to Lord Visnu. (SB 10.79 34)

Balarama kills the demon Balvala and tours India's holy rivers and shrines, from Prayaga to Rameswaram. He fails to stop the club duel between Bhima and Duryodhana at Kurukshetra, then returns to Naimisaranya to perform sacrifices and teach the sages.

children.topic: 80 · The Brāhmaṇa Sudāmā Visits Lord Kṛṣṇa in Dvārakā
Real hands work for the Lord
children.note: Pariksit defines true speech, hands, mind and ears as those engaged in Krishna's service. (SB 10.80 3)
Sudama's wife begs rice from neighbors and ties it in a rag as his gift for Krishna. (SB 10.80 14)

children.topic: Krishna weeps embracing his poor friend
children.note: Touching the emaciated brahmana, the Lord sheds tears of love. (SB 10.80 19)

children.topic: The guru who gives knowledge is like me
children.note: Krishna ranks the spiritual teacher above one's parents and even equal to himself. (SB 10.80 32)

children.topic: Serving the guru pleases me most
children.note: Krishna says faithful service to one's teacher satisfies him more than rituals or austerity. (SB 10.80 34)

children.topic: A disciple owes his guru everything
children.note: Sandipani teaches that true students repay their teacher even with their lives. (SB 10.80 41)

Pariksit asks for more of Krishna's deeds. Sukadeva tells of Sudama, a poor brahmana whose wife urges him to visit his old schoolmate Krishna. Bringing only flat rice, Sudama is received with tearful love, and Krishna recalls their days at Sandipani's school.

children.topic: A leaf, flower, fruit or water
children.note: Krishna says he accepts even the simplest offering when it is given with love. (SB 10.81 4)
Krishna delights in the flat rice, declaring it will satisfy him and all the worlds. (SB 10.81 9)
One palmful is already enough wealth for both worlds, Rukmini says, holding Krishna's hand. (SB 10.81 11)

children.topic: Riches might make me forget him
children.note: Sudama assumes Krishna withheld wealth out of compassion, lest prosperity intoxicate him. (SB 10.81 20)
Sudama marvels that the Lord treats his gifts as trivial and a devotee's small offering as great. (SB 10.81 35)
Krishna denies wealth to the unwise devotee, knowing pride causes the fall of the rich. (SB 10.81 37)

Krishna asks Sudama what gift he brought and joyfully eats his flat rice until Rukmini stops him. Sudama goes home without asking for wealth, praising Krishna's humility, and finds his hut turned into a palace. He enjoys it unattached and reaches Krishna.

children.topic: 82 · Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma Meet the Inhabitants of Vṛndāvana
May we have devotion to Krishna
children.note: Bathing at Samanta-pancaka, the Yadus pray only for devotion to the Lord. (SB 10.82 10)
Kunti observes that even close family forget one whom Providence has abandoned. (SB 10.82 19)

children.topic: You cared for them like eyelids
children.note: Devaki thanks Yasoda for protecting her sons before they ever knew their real parents. (SB 10.82 38)

children.topic: Gopis embrace Krishna through their eyes
children.note: Seeing Krishna after long separation, the gopis draw him into their hearts in ecstatic trance. (SB 10.82 39)

children.topic: Your special love has won me
children.note: Krishna tells the gopis their unique loving mood has obtained him completely. (SB 10.82 44)

children.topic: Let your feet awaken in our hearts
children.note: The gopis pray that Krishna's lotus feet, sought by yogis, may shine in their household hearts. (SB 10.82 48)

During a solar eclipse the Yadus travel to Kurukshetra and meet the Pandavas, Kunti and at last Nanda and the cowherds. Vasudeva and Nanda embrace, Devaki thanks Yasoda, and Krishna meets the gopis privately, teaching them to see him within and beyond all.

children.topic: 83 · Draupadī Meets the Queens of Kṛṣṇa
Nectar of your feet through the ears
children.note: The Pandavas say hearing Krishna's glories from devotees destroys forgetfulness of God. (SB 10.83 3)

children.topic: Rukmini: a lion taking his prey
children.note: Rukmini recalls how Krishna snatched her from the armed kings gathered for Sisupala. (SB 10.83 8)

children.topic: Kalindi, now a sweeper in his palace
children.note: Won by austerity, Kalindi counts herself a humble servant in Krishna's home. (SB 10.83 11)
In Laksmana's svayamvara Krishna hits the target seen only by its reflection with a single glance. (SB 10.83 25-26)
The queens reject heaven, mystic power and even liberation for the dust of Krishna's feet. (SB 10.83 41-42)
The queens long for the dust Krishna leaves on the grass while herding cows in Vraja. (SB 10.83 43)

Krishna's relatives praise him at Kurukshetra. Draupadi asks each of Krishna's queens how she was married, and Rukmini, Satyabhama, Jambavati, Kalindi, Mitravinda, Satya, Bhadra and Laksmana tell their stories. All wish only for the dust of Krishna's feet.
Krishna says holy rivers and stone images purify slowly, but sages do so immediately. (SB 10.84 11)

children.topic: No better than a cow or an ass
children.note: One who identifies with the body and ignores the wise is compared to a beast. (SB 10.84 13)

children.topic: The Lord pretends to be controlled
children.note: The sages marvel that Krishna hides himself in human behavior and feigns subordination. (SB 10.84 16)
Narada notes Vasudeva treats Krishna as a mere boy, like one who lives by the Ganges yet seeks other water. (SB 10.84 31)

children.topic: Renounce desire by fulfilling it wisely
children.note: The sages teach how sacrifice, family life and reflection on time cure the three great desires. (SB 10.84 38)

children.topic: May no one gain kingly wealth
children.note: Vasudeva regrets that opulence blinded him to friends like Nanda. (SB 10.84 64)
Srila Prabhupada's recorded class: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 10.84.13. Tap the link to read the transcript and play the audio.
Recorded classes on this chapter, with transcript and audio on vedabase.io. Oldest first.

Great sages arrive at Kurukshetra and Krishna, playing humble host, declares that saints purify instantly, unlike holy waters or images. The sages praise the Lord's hidden majesty, answer Vasudeva's question on karma and run his sacrifices. Nanda lingers.

children.topic: 85 · Lord Kṛṣṇa Instructs Vasudeva and Retrieves Devakī’s Sons
Everything is created in you, by you
children.note: Vasudeva sees that all existence arises within, from and for the Supreme Lord. (SB 10.85 4)
Vasudeva admits the Lord's illusion makes people think 'this is me' and 'these are mine'. (SB 10.85 17)

children.topic: Enough of calling you my child
children.note: Vasudeva surrenders to Krishna's feet and renounces the bodily idea of the Lord as his son. (SB 10.85 19)
Krishna compares Paramatma to the elements, which look varied in different objects yet remain one. (SB 10.85 25)

children.topic: Bali begs escape from the blind well
children.note: Bali asks to leave family life and wander freely at the feet of charitable trees. (SB 10.85 45)

children.topic: Devaki's milk awakens the six sons
children.note: Nursed by Devaki, the six recover their identities, bow to all and return to heaven. (SB 10.85 55-56)

Vasudeva, convinced of his sons' divinity, praises Krishna and Balarama as the source of every element and power. Krishna replies that all beings share one spiritual truth. Devaki asks them to restore her six sons killed by Kamsa; they fetch them from Bali.

children.topic: 86 · Arjuna Kidnaps Subhadrā, and Kṛṣṇa Blesses His Devotees

children.note: During a temple festival Arjuna abducts Subhadra, with her parents' and Krishna's consent. (SB 10.86 9)
Accepting both invitations, Krishna visits the king and the brahmana at the same moment. (SB 10.86 26)

children.topic: The devotee dearer than Laksmi or Brahma
children.note: Bahulasva cites Krishna's own words that his unalloyed devotee is dearest to him. (SB 10.86 32)

children.topic: Near in the heart, yet far away
children.note: Srutadeva says the Lord within is remote from minds absorbed in material work. (SB 10.86 47)
Krishna explains temples and rivers purify gradually, but the look of a saint does so at once. (SB 10.86 52)

children.topic: A brahmana dearer than my four-armed form
children.note: Krishna declares the learned brahmana contains all the Vedas as he contains all the gods. (SB 10.86 54)

Arjuna, disguised as a renunciant, carries off Subhadra with Krishna's approval. Krishna then visits Mithila with sages, staying at once in the homes of King Bahulasva and the poor brahmana Srutadeva, and teaches that a devotee brahmana is dearer than himself.

children.topic: 87 · The Prayers of the Personified Vedas

children.note: Pariksit asks how scripture, limited to material qualities, can speak of the transcendent Lord. (SB 10.87 1)

children.topic: Clay stays clay through every pot
children.note: The Vedas say the Supreme remains unchanged as the world is made from and dissolved into him. (SB 10.87 15)

children.topic: Without you, breathing is just a bellows
children.note: Only those who follow the Lord are truly alive; he is the reality beneath all coverings. (SB 10.87 17)
People ignore the Lord who is their own Self and wander through degraded bodies chasing the unreal. (SB 10.87 22)

children.topic: The mind is a wild horse
children.note: Those who abandon the guru while trying to tame the mind are like sailors without a helmsman. (SB 10.87 33)

children.topic: Universes drift in you like dust
children.note: Even the Lord cannot reach the end of his glories; the Vedas conclude by pointing to him alone. (SB 10.87 41)

Pariksit asks how the Vedas can describe the qualityless Absolute. Sukadeva relates Narayana Rsi telling Narada the personified Vedas' prayers, which awaken the Lord after annihilation and teach that the world rests on Brahman and devotion alone reaches him.

children.topic: My favor takes away your wealth
children.note: Krishna says he gradually impoverishes those he specially loves, so friends and relatives desert them. (SB 10.88 8)
Frustrated in making money, the person befriends devotees and receives Krishna's special mercy. (SB 10.88 9)
Those who get boons from easily satisfied deities become proud and even offend their benefactors. (SB 10.88 11)
Vrka asks Siva for a boon that anyone he touches on the head will die. (SB 10.88 21)
Chased by the demon, Siva runs in terror to the ends of the universe. (SB 10.88 24)

children.topic: The demon touches his own head
children.note: Charmed by the disguised Lord's words, Vrka tests the boon on himself and dies instantly. (SB 10.88 35)

Pariksit asks why Siva's worshipers grow rich while Visnu's stay poor. Krishna explains he strips wealth from those he favors. Vrkasura wins from Siva the power to kill by a head-touch and chases Siva, till Visnu as a student tricks him into touching his own.

children.topic: 89 · Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna Retrieve a Brāhmaṇa’s Sons

children.note: Visnu responds to the kick by rising, bowing and welcoming the sage with apologies. (SB 10.89 8-9)

children.topic: The sages conclude Visnu is supreme
children.note: From Visnu come peace, fearlessness and dharma; goodness is his dearest form. (SB 10.89 14-17)

children.topic: Arjuna vows to protect the child or burn
children.note: Arjuna promises the brahmana to save his next son or enter fire in atonement. (SB 10.89 29)
When the tenth child vanishes, the brahmana mocks Arjuna's boasting and his bow. (SB 10.89 41)

children.topic: Maha-Visnu wanted to see you both
children.note: The Lord of the causal ocean took the boys only to bring Krishna and Arjuna, his expansions, before him. (SB 10.89 58)

children.topic: All power comes from Krishna's mercy
children.note: Arjuna concludes that any extraordinary ability is simply a gift of Krishna's grace. (SB 10.89 62)

Bhrgu tests Brahma, Siva and Visnu; only Visnu tolerates his kick, so the sages declare Visnu supreme. In Dvaraka a brahmana loses nine sons at birth; Arjuna vows to save the tenth and fails. Krishna takes him past the universe to Maha-Visnu, who returns them.

children.topic: The queens question the kurari bird
children.note: Sleepless with love, the queens ask the crying bird if Krishna's glances pierced her heart too. (SB 10.90 15)

children.topic: Swan, tell him to come without Laksmi
children.note: The queens send a message through a swan, jealous that the goddess of fortune is not the only devoted one. (SB 10.90 24)
Krishna maintains over 16,100 wives while modeling perfect householder dharma. (SB 10.90 29)

children.topic: The Vrsnis forgot their own bodies
children.note: So absorbed were the Yadus in Krishna that they lost body-consciousness in every activity. (SB 10.90 46)
A famous benediction: may Krishna, son of Devaki and Yasoda, destroyer of evil, be ever glorious. (SB 10.90 48)
Regular hearing and chanting of Krishna's topics leads to the kingdom where death has no power. (SB 10.90 50)

Sukadeva closes the Tenth Canto: Krishna sports with his queens in Dvaraka's lakes, and in love-madness they address birds, ocean, moon and clouds. He fathers ten sons by each wife; the Yadu dynasty is immeasurably vast. Hearing his pastimes conquers death.
Krishna’s own pastimes: His advent, Vrindavan childhood, the gopis and the rasa dance, Mathura, Dvaraka, His queens and His glories. 90 chapters.

children.topic: 1 · The Curse upon the Yadu Dynasty
Fire from friction within the bamboo grove
children.note: Krishna resolves to end the Yadu dynasty through an internal quarrel, since no outside force could. (SB 11.1 4)
All beauty flows from Krishna; his form, words and footprints drew everyone to follow him. (SB 11.1 6-7)

children.topic: Samba disguised as a pregnant woman
children.note: Yadu boys mock the sages by asking whether the 'woman' Samba will bear a boy or girl. (SB 11.1 13-15)

children.topic: An iron club to destroy the dynasty
children.note: The angered sages curse that the pregnant 'woman' will bear a club that will end the Yadus. (SB 11.1 16)
The iron lump swallowed by a fish becomes the arrow tip of the hunter Jara. (SB 11.1 23)
Though able to reverse it, Krishna in his form as time gladly permits the curse to unfold. (SB 11.1 24)

Having relieved the earth through the Kurukshetra war, Krishna decides his own Yadu dynasty must also go. Yadu boys dress Samba as a pregnant woman to mock sages, who curse them with an iron club that will destroy the family; its remains become Jara's arrow.

children.topic: 2 · Mahārāja Nimi Meets the Nine Yogendras
Death stalks every step of life
children.note: Sukadeva opens by asking who, seeing death at every turn, would not serve Mukunda, whom even liberated souls worship. (SB 11.2 2)

children.topic: Half a moment with pure devotees
children.note: Nimi says that even a fleeting meeting with saintly devotees is a priceless treasure in this world of birth and death. (SB 11.2 30)
Kavi says even the ignorant can easily know God by following the method the Lord Himself prescribes: devotional service. (SB 11.2 34)
Every action of body, speech, mind or intelligence should be dedicated with the thought that it is for the Lord's pleasure. (SB 11.2 36)

children.topic: The first-class devotee sees Krishna everywhere
children.note: Havir defines the topmost devotee as one who perceives the Supreme Lord within all beings and all beings within Him. (SB 11.2 45)
The intermediate devotee loves the Lord, befriends devotees, shows mercy to the innocent and avoids the envious. (SB 11.2 46)

Narada visits Vasudeva in Dvaraka and retells how King Nimi questioned the nine Yogendras. Kavi explains bhagavata-dharma as the fearless path, and Havir describes the first-, second- and third-class devotee.

children.topic: Wealth is death for the soul
children.note: Prabuddha argues that money brings only distress, is hard to earn, and that home and family bought with it give no lasting joy. (SB 11.3 19)

children.topic: Seek a guru who knows the scriptures
children.note: Anyone wanting real happiness must take shelter of a spiritual master who has realized scripture and can convince others. (SB 11.3 21)

children.topic: The Lord gives Himself to sincere servants
children.note: The disciple should learn service without duplicity, for Hari is inclined to offer Himself to a faithful devotee. (SB 11.3 22)

children.topic: Chant together and encourage each other
children.note: Gathering with devotees to glorify the Lord purifies and lets them help one another give up sense gratification. (SB 11.3 30)

children.topic: Love of God crosses insurmountable maya
children.note: By learning and practising bhakti one reaches love of Narayana and easily crosses the illusory energy that is otherwise unbeatable. (SB 11.3 33)

children.topic: Candy so the child takes medicine
children.note: Avirhotra says the Vedas promise fruitive rewards only to lure the immature toward the real goal of liberation. (SB 11.3 44)
Srila Prabhupada's recorded class: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 11.3.21, Initiations. Tap the link to read the transcript and play the audio.
Srila Prabhupada's recorded class: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 11.3.27. Tap the link to read the transcript and play the audio.
Recorded classes on this chapter, with transcript and audio on vedabase.io. Oldest first.

Antariksa describes how maya entangles souls and how the universe dissolves; Prabuddha teaches taking shelter of a guru and associating with devotees; Pippalayana explains the Supreme; Avirhotra explains karma-yoga and Deity worship.

children.topic: 4 · Drumila Explains the Incarnations of Godhead to King Nimi
Counting dust before counting His qualities
children.note: Drumila says one might count every grain of earth sooner than enumerate the unlimited qualities of the Lord. (SB 11.4 2)
Untouched by Indra's plot, the Lord reassures the trembling Cupid and celestials and invites them to sanctify His asrama. (SB 11.4 8)
The demigods admit that ascetics who cross the ocean of the senses still sink over a trifle when overcome by anger. (SB 11.4 11)
The Lord descends as teachers of self-realization and as Hayagriva, who rescued the Vedas from Patala after slaying Madhu. (SB 11.4 17)
