The Lord will appear among the Yadus, bewilder sacrificers as Buddha, and as Kalki remove false rulers at Kali's end. (SB 11.4 22)

Drumila answers Nimi about the Lord's incarnations: the universal Purusa, Brahma-Visnu-Rudra, and Nara-Narayana Rsi, who calmly defeats Indra's Cupid and produces Urvasi. He then lists Hamsa, Matsya, Varaha, Nrsimha, Vamana, Rama, Krishna and Kalki.

children.topic: 5 · Nārada Concludes His Teachings to Vasudeva
Scripture permits but never encourages vice
children.note: Camasa explains that allowances for sex, meat and wine in ritual are restrictions meant to lead one toward renunciation. (SB 11.5 11)

children.topic: Turning from Vasudeva, dragged to darkness
children.note: Those absorbed in illusory family and possessions lose them unwillingly and sink into the darkest regions. (SB 11.5 18)

children.topic: The golden avatar worshiped by sankirtana
children.note: Karabhajana foretells that in Kali-yuga intelligent people worship Krishna Himself, not blackish, through congregational chanting. (SB 11.5 32)
Enlightened persons value this fallen age because all perfection comes easily through sankirtana. (SB 11.5 36)

children.topic: The surrendered soul owes no other debt
children.note: One who fully takes shelter of Mukunda is freed from obligations to demigods, sages, relatives and forefathers. (SB 11.5 41)

children.topic: Vasudeva and Devaki are already perfect
children.note: Narada tells Vasudeva that intimate parental love for Krishna has fully purified him and his wife. (SB 11.5 47)

Camasa warns that those who ignore Hari fall, and exposes materialistic Vedic ritualists. Karabhajana describes the Lord's forms and worship in each yuga, glorifying Kali-yuga's sankirtana. Narada then assures Vasudeva and Devaki they are already perfect.

children.topic: 6 · The Yadu Dynasty Retires to Prabhāsa

children.note: The demigods say that ordinary worship, study and austerity cannot cleanse a soul the way strong faith in the Lord's glories does. (SB 11.6 9)

children.topic: Two rivers that purify the worlds
children.note: Narrations about the Lord and the waters from His feet both destroy contamination, one heard and one bathed in. (SB 11.6 19)

children.topic: Hearing Krishna's deeds crosses Kali's darkness
children.note: Brahma declares that saintly people who hear and chant Krishna's pastimes easily pass beyond the ignorance of Kali-yuga. (SB 11.6 24)

children.topic: Like a shore holding back the ocean
children.note: Krishna explains He must check the Yadus, whose swelling strength threatened to overwhelm the whole world. (SB 11.6 29)
Uddhava declares he cannot bear separation from Kesava even for a moment and begs to be taken to the Lord's abode. (SB 11.6 43)

children.topic: Conquering maya with the Lord's remnants
children.note: Uddhava says servants who wear the Lord's used garlands and eat His leftovers will surely defeat the illusory energy. (SB 11.6 46)

Brahma, Siva and the demigods come to Dvaraka, praise Krishna and ask Him to return to His abode. Krishna agrees, explains why the Yadus must be withdrawn, and sends the dynasty to Prabhasa. Uddhava privately begs to accompany the Lord.

children.topic: Give up attachments, fix your mind on Me
children.note: Krishna instructs Uddhava to abandon friends and relatives, see everything equally and travel the earth conscious of Him. (SB 11.7 6)

children.topic: The human form is dear to Me
children.note: Among all the bodies with any number of legs, Krishna says He especially cherishes the human form. (SB 11.7 22)
The avadhuta lists his teachers, from earth, air and sky to the pigeon, python, honeybee, Pingala, the child and the wasp. (SB 11.7 33-35)
A sober person sees attackers as helpless instruments of providence and stays undistracted on his path. (SB 11.7 37)
A self-realized soul lives in various bodies without becoming entangled, as the wind never mixes with the scents it carries. (SB 11.7 41)
Human life opens liberation's door, but one who buries himself in family life like the pigeon has climbed up only to tumble. (SB 11.7 74)

Krishna tells Uddhava to wander with equal vision, then narrates King Yadu meeting an avadhuta who names twenty-four gurus. The brahmana draws lessons from the earth, the wind, the sky, water, fire, moon and sun, and the pigeon ruined by family attachment.

children.topic: The ocean neither swells nor dries
children.note: A devotee neither rejoices in sudden wealth nor grieves in poverty, just as the ocean stays steady through monsoon and drought. (SB 11.8 6)

children.topic: Take the essence like a honeybee
children.note: As a bee gathers nectar from every flower, an intelligent person collects the essence from all scriptures. (SB 11.8 10)

children.topic: Conquer the tongue, conquer all senses
children.note: Mastery of the other senses counts for nothing until the tongue is controlled; win the tongue and everything follows. (SB 11.8 21)

children.topic: Pingala neglected the Beloved in her heart
children.note: Pingala laments serving petty men while ignoring the Lord within, the true giver of love and prosperity. (SB 11.8 31)

children.topic: Buying the Lord with full surrender
children.note: Pingala resolves that total surrender is the price she will pay to win the Lord and enjoy with Him like Laksmi herself. (SB 11.8 35)

children.topic: Desire is misery, freedom is joy
children.note: Cutting off her hopes for lovers, Pingala sleeps peacefully, proving that giving up desire is the greatest happiness. (SB 11.8 44)

The avadhuta continues: the python accepts what comes, the ocean stays level, the moth, elephant, honeybee, deer and fish warn against sense objects. Then he tells of Pingala, a prostitute whose disappointed night turned into detachment and surrender.

children.topic: 9 · Detachment from All that Is Material

children.note: Just as the girl removed bracelets to stop the noise, a sage lives alone to avoid the quarrel that company brings. (SB 11.9 10)

children.topic: The arrow maker missed the king
children.note: Total absorption in the Supreme removes all sense of duality, like the craftsman who never noticed the passing king. (SB 11.9 13)

children.topic: The spider spins and swallows its web
children.note: The Lord expands the cosmos from His own potency, plays with it and finally withdraws it into Himself. (SB 11.9 21)

children.topic: The insect became a wasp by meditation
children.note: One attains the form one constantly meditates on, as the trapped insect fixed on the wasp took on its nature. (SB 11.9 23)

children.topic: Don't waste the rare human body
children.note: After countless births the human form arrives; a sober person hurries toward perfection, since only humans can know Krishna. (SB 11.9 29)
The one Truth is described in many ways by sages, so firm knowledge may not come from a single guru alone. (SB 11.9 31)

The avadhuta finishes his gurus: the hawk dropping its meat, the child, the girl's bracelets, the arrow maker, the snake, the spider and the wasp, and finally his own body. King Yadu becomes detached. Human life alone allows Krishna consciousness.

children.topic: Fire and firewood: soul and body
children.note: The illuminating soul differs from the body it lights up, as fire differs from the wood it burns. (SB 11.10 8)

children.topic: Guru, disciple and instruction as kindling sticks
children.note: Knowledge passed from guru to disciple ignites like fire from rubbing sticks and burns ignorance to ashes. (SB 11.10 12)
Since everyone is walking toward death, Krishna asks what real pleasure material things can offer. (SB 11.10 20)

children.topic: Falling from heaven when merit runs out
children.note: The sacrificer enjoys heaven only until his pious credit is spent, then time drags him back down against his will. (SB 11.10 26)

children.topic: Even Brahma fears Me as time
children.note: From heaven to hell, all beings, including long-lived Brahma, fear the Lord in His form of time. (SB 11.10 30)
Uddhava asks how to tell a liberated soul from a conditioned one in how each lives, eats, sits and moves. (SB 11.10 36-37)

Krishna tells Uddhava to follow varnasrama while sheltered in Him, distinguishes soul from body with the fire and firewood analogy, and exposes fruitive work: heaven is temporary, its enjoyers fall, and even Brahma fears time. Uddhava asks about bondage.

children.topic: 11 · The Symptoms of Conditioned and Liberated Living Entities

children.note: One bird eats the fruits while the other simply watches; the soul enjoys while the Lord stays superior by His potency. (SB 11.11 6)

children.topic: Neither angry when attacked nor pleased when praised
children.note: True intelligence shows in remaining unmoved whether one is suddenly assaulted or unexpectedly honored. (SB 11.11 15)
Scholarly Vedic study that never fixes the mind on the Lord yields only labor, like tending a cow that gives no milk. (SB 11.11 18)
If the mind cannot be fully absorbed in spirit, Krishna says to dedicate all activities to Him without wanting the results. (SB 11.11 22)

children.topic: Love matters more than knowing who I am
children.note: Devotees may not grasp Krishna's full nature, but if they worship with unalloyed love He counts them as the best. (SB 11.11 33)
Krishna is the shelter of the liberated; without loving service born of devotee association there is no real way out. (SB 11.11 48)

Krishna explains that the soul is neither truly bound nor freed; two birds in one tree illustrate the conditioned soul and the Lord. He describes the sage, warns that Vedic study without Him is barren, lists a saint's qualities and ways to worship Him.

children.topic: They reached Me by association alone
children.note: Prahlada, Bali, Hanuman and others never studied deeply or did austerities; devotee association alone brought them to Krishna. (SB 11.12 7)

children.topic: Yoga, charity and study cannot reach Me
children.note: Even strenuous mysticism, speculation, vows, sacrifice and renunciation fail to attain Krishna without love. (SB 11.12 9)

children.topic: Nights with Krishna passed in a moment
children.note: For the gopis, nights with the Lord flew by, but without Him each night stretched like a day of Brahma. (SB 11.12 11)

children.topic: The gopis attained Me as their lover
children.note: Unaware of His divinity, thousands of gopis wanted Krishna as a lover and by intimate association reached the Absolute. (SB 11.12 13)

children.topic: Leave the Vedas, take shelter of Me
children.note: Krishna tells Uddhava to set aside scriptural injunctions and surrender wholeheartedly to Him for freedom from all fear. (SB 11.12 14-15)

children.topic: Cut with knowledge, then drop the ax
children.note: Serve the guru, sever the subtle covering with the ax of knowledge, and once the Lord is realized, discard even that ax. (SB 11.12 24)

Krishna says association with devotees surpasses yoga, study and austerity, citing demons, animals and the gopis who attained Him by love alone. He tells Uddhava to drop Vedic formalities and take shelter of Him, then describes the tree of material existence.

children.topic: 13 · The Haṁsa-avatāra Answers the Questions of the Sons of Brahmā
Bamboo fire consumes its own forest
children.note: As friction between bamboos ignites a fire that burns the grove, cultivating knowledge with body and mind destroys their material cause. (SB 11.13 7)

children.topic: Why act like dogs, asses and goats?
children.note: Uddhava asks how people who know material life ends in misery still chase enjoyment like animals. (SB 11.13 8)

children.topic: Yoga is withdrawing the mind into Me
children.note: The real yoga taught by Sanaka is simply to pull the mind from all else and absorb it directly in Krishna. (SB 11.13 14)
The Hamsa avatar turns the sages' question back: if they meant the body, they should have asked the five elements. (SB 11.13 23)

children.topic: I am the fourth state of consciousness
children.note: Beyond waking, dreaming and deep sleep stands the Lord; fixed in Him, the soul drops the mind and its objects. (SB 11.13 28)

children.topic: A drunk man ignores his clothes
children.note: The self-realized soul no longer notices whether the body sits, stands, dies or gets replaced, as a drunkard ignores his dress. (SB 11.13 36)

Krishna explains how goodness conquers passion and ignorance, then recalls appearing as Hamsa to the Kumaras when Brahma could not answer them. He teaches that mind and sense objects are coverings and that He is the fourth state beyond waking, dream and sleep.

children.topic: 14 · Lord Kṛṣṇa Explains the Yoga System to Śrī Uddhava
Uddhava, dearer than My own self
children.note: Krishna says not Brahma, Siva, Sankarsana, Laksmi nor even His own self is as dear to Him as Uddhava. (SB 11.14 15)
Krishna walks behind His desireless devotees, wanting to purify the worlds with the dust of their feet. (SB 11.14 16)

children.topic: Only pure bhakti brings Me under control
children.note: Yoga, Sankhya, pious work, study, austerity and renunciation cannot control Krishna, but unalloyed devotion does. (SB 11.14 20)

children.topic: No melting heart, no purified consciousness
children.note: Without hair standing on end, tears and a melting heart, there is no loving service and no real purification. (SB 11.14 23)

children.topic: Gold smelted pure in bhakti's fire
children.note: The soul absorbed in devotion sheds karmic impurities as gold loses dross in fire and returns to serving the Lord. (SB 11.14 25)

children.topic: Meditate on the Lord in the heart-lotus
children.note: Krishna describes fixing the four-armed, smiling Lord within the fire on the eight-petaled lotus of the heart. (SB 11.14 36-42)

Uddhava asks which path is supreme. Krishna says human opinions vary but pure devotion alone controls Him, that Uddhava is dearer than Brahma or Laksmi, and that bhakti burns sin like fire. He then details posture, breath and meditation on His form.

children.topic: 15 · Lord Kṛṣṇa’s Description of Mystic Yoga Perfections
Eighteen perfections: eight primary, ten secondary
children.note: Yoga masters count eight siddhis sheltered in the Lord and ten more that arise from the mode of goodness. (SB 11.15 3)
The primary siddhis let a yogi become tiny, huge or weightless, obtain anything, enjoy anything and control maya. (SB 11.15 4-5)

children.topic: Entering another body like a bee
children.note: A perfected yogi leaves his gross body through the pathways of air and enters another as a bee moves between flowers. (SB 11.15 23)

children.topic: Fire, water and poison cannot harm him
children.note: A yogi pacified by devotion is untouched by fire, sun, water or poison, as fish are unharmed by water. (SB 11.15 29)

children.topic: Siddhis are a waste of time
children.note: Experts in bhakti call mystic powers impediments for one practising the supreme yoga that brings all perfection from Krishna. (SB 11.15 33)

children.topic: Devotion grants what herbs and mantras promise
children.note: Every power achievable by birth, herbs, austerity or mantras comes through devotional service, the only real perfection. (SB 11.15 34)

Krishna lists eighteen mystic perfections, eight primary and ten secondary, and explains the meditation that yields each, from anima to entering other bodies. He concludes that siddhis are obstacles for a devotee, since bhakti gives every perfection.
Krishna notes that Uddhava's question about His opulences is the same one Arjuna raised before the battle. (SB 11.16 6)

children.topic: Om, the letter a, the Gayatri
children.note: Among mantras Krishna is the omkara, among letters the first letter, and among meters the Gayatri. (SB 11.16 12)

children.topic: I am samadhi and the science of self
children.note: Among yoga stages Krishna is the final trance, and among discriminative sciences He is knowledge that separates spirit from matter. (SB 11.16 24)
Among those called Bhagavan Krishna is Vasudeva, and among devotees He names Uddhava as His representative. (SB 11.16 29)

children.topic: All power and beauty expand from Me
children.note: Whatever strength, fame, opulence, renunciation, fortune or knowledge exists is just an expansion of the Lord's opulence. (SB 11.16 40)

children.topic: Water leaking from an unbaked pot
children.note: Without control of speech and mind, a transcendentalist's vows, austerity and charity drain away like water from raw clay. (SB 11.16 43)

Uddhava asks about the Lord's opulences, and Krishna, recalling Arjuna's same question at Kuruksetra, names His representatives: om, Brahma, Indra, Prahlada, the Ganges, samadhi, spring, Vyasa, Uddhava among devotees. He ends urging control of speech and mind.

children.topic: 17 · Lord Kṛṣṇa’s Description of the Varṇāśrama System

children.note: At first all humans belonged to a single order of natural devotees, so the age is called Krta, where duties are complete. (SB 11.17 10)

children.topic: The natural qualities of a brahmana
children.note: A brahmana is marked by calm, sense control, austerity, purity, contentment, tolerance, honesty, devotion to Krishna, mercy and truthfulness. (SB 11.17 16)
Every person in society must practise nonviolence, truth, honesty and goodwill toward all, staying free of lust, anger and greed. (SB 11.17 21)
Krishna warns never to disrespect or envy the guru as an ordinary man, for he represents all the demigods. (SB 11.17 27)
Wife, children and friends are like fellow travelers; each new body separates one from them as waking ends a dream. (SB 11.17 53)

children.topic: Live at home like a guest
children.note: A liberated householder stays without proprietorship or false ego and so is never bound by domestic affairs. (SB 11.17 54)

Uddhava asks how people attain devotion through prescribed duties. Krishna traces varnasrama from Satya-yuga's single hamsa class, lists the natural qualities of each varna, details brahmacari life and guru service, and gives householder duties.
One who endures the vanaprastha's severe austerities merely to gain sense enjoyment is called the greatest fool. (SB 11.18 10)
Fearing the renunciant will surpass them, demigods appear as his former wife and attractions; he should ignore them. (SB 11.18 14)

children.topic: Sticks alone do not make a sannyasi
children.note: Without restraint of speech, activity and breath, carrying a bamboo staff does not qualify one as a renunciant. (SB 11.18 17)
Though wise, expert and learned, the paramahamsa behaves like a child, an incompetent or a madman, unbound by rules. (SB 11.18 29)
Sannyasis practise equanimity and nonviolence, vanaprasthas austerity, householders shelter and sacrifice, brahmacaris guru service. (SB 11.18 42)

children.topic: Varnasrama offered in love brings perfection
children.note: Duties followed by authorized tradition award the highest goal when dedicated to Krishna in loving service. (SB 11.18 47)

Krishna describes the vanaprastha's forest austerities and the sannyasi's begging, silence and equal vision, warning against demigods' temptations and false renunciants. He states each asrama's chief duty and says duties offered to Him bring perfection.

children.topic: Surrender knowledge and its means to Me
children.note: The enlightened soul who sees the world as illusion should offer both his knowledge and the process that produced it to Krishna. (SB 11.19 1)

children.topic: Your feet, an umbrella raining nectar
children.note: Uddhava sees no shelter on the fearful path of birth and death except the Lord's feet, which shower relief. (SB 11.19 9)

children.topic: Seeing the cause, not the elements
children.note: Vijnana means no longer perceiving twenty-eight separate elements but directly seeing their single source, the Lord. (SB 11.19 15)
Faith in His pastimes, chanting, worship, honoring devotees, seeing Him in all beings and offering everything lead to love. (SB 11.19 20-24)
Religion leads to devotion, knowledge reveals His all-pervading presence, detachment shuns sense objects, opulence is siddhi. (SB 11.19 27)
Krishna redefines virtues: tolerance is enduring distress, austerity is renouncing lust, heroism is conquering material urges. (SB 11.19 36-39)

Krishna tells Uddhava to surrender even his knowledge to Him, recalls Yudhisthira hearing from Bhisma, explains realization beyond the twenty-eight elements, and lists the limbs of bhakti. He then defines yama, niyama, tolerance, charity, wealth and wisdom.

children.topic: 20 · Pure Devotional Service Surpasses Knowledge and Detachment

children.note: Krishna says He offers jnana-yoga, karma-yoga and bhakti-yoga for human perfection, and no fourth means exists. (SB 11.20 6)

children.topic: Faith in hearing marks the devotee's path
children.note: One who by good fortune develops faith in His glories, neither disgusted nor too attached, should follow bhakti. (SB 11.20 8)

children.topic: The boat, the captain and the wind
children.note: The human body is a boat, the guru its captain, Krishna's words the wind; not using it makes one a killer of the soul. (SB 11.20 17)

children.topic: Taming the mind like a wild horse
children.note: As a rider lets a headstrong horse run before reining it in, a yogi watches the mind's urges and slowly controls them. (SB 11.20 21)

children.topic: Seeing Me cuts the heart's knot
children.note: Once the Lord is directly seen, the heart's knot is cut open, doubts are shredded and the chain of karma ends. (SB 11.20 30)
Krishna's devotees want nothing but Him and decline freedom from birth and death even when He offers it. (SB 11.20 34)

Uddhava asks how piety and sin fit with surrender. Krishna gives three paths: jnana for the detached, karma for the desirous, bhakti for the faithful. The human body is a boat, the guru its captain; the devotee gains everything and refuses even liberation.

children.topic: 21 · Lord Kṛṣṇa’s Explanation of the Vedic Path
Piety is staying in your position
children.note: Steadiness in one's own prescribed position is real piety, while deviating from it is impiety. (SB 11.21 2)
Bathing, charity, austerity and rituals cleanse the self, but remembrance of the Lord is the highest purifier. (SB 11.21 14)
Accepting sense objects as desirable breeds attachment, attachment breeds lust, and lust creates conflict among men. (SB 11.21 19)

children.topic: Fruitive promises are candy for children
children.note: Scriptural rewards are mere inducements to perform beneficial duties, like sweets offered so a child takes medicine. (SB 11.21 23)
Ritualists bent on enjoyment cannot see that the Lord dwells in every heart and that the universe emanates from Him. (SB 11.21 28)

children.topic: I am the sacrifice, the Deity, the conclusion
children.note: Krishna is the ritual, the worshiped form and the philosophy; the Vedas finally negate duality and rest in Him. (SB 11.21 43)

Krishna explains purity and impurity of place, time, objects and self, and how attachment breeds lust, quarrel, anger and ignorance. Vedic promises of heaven are candy for children; ritualists miss His presence. He alone knows the Vedas' purpose: Himself.

children.topic: 22 · Enumeration of the Elements of Material Creation

children.note: Differences of opinion arise from Krishna's energies, but for those absorbed in Him the very cause of argument is gone. (SB 11.22 6)

children.topic: The mind travels; the soul follows
children.note: Shaped by karma, the mind and five senses move from body to body, and the soul, though different, goes along. (SB 11.22 37)
Absorbed in a new body's sensations, the soul forgets its previous body entirely; that forgetting is called death. (SB 11.22 39)

children.topic: Birth is identifying with a new body
children.note: What is called birth is simply full acceptance of a new body, like taking a dream or fantasy for reality. (SB 11.22 40)

children.topic: Watching a tree grow and die
children.note: One who observes a tree from seed to decay stays separate from it; likewise the witness of bodily birth and death is apart. (SB 11.22 50)

children.topic: Stay steady though beaten and spat upon
children.note: Even if insulted, tied up, spat on or defiled by ignorant people, the seeker uses intelligence to stay on the spiritual platform. (SB 11.22 58-59)

Uddhava asks why sages count the elements differently; Krishna validates each system by His energies. He shows nature and soul are distinct, describes how the mind carries the soul between bodies, birth and death as forgetting, and urges tolerance of insults.

children.topic: 23 · The Song of the Avantī Brāhmaṇa
Harsh words cut deeper than arrows
children.note: Krishna says insults from uncivilized men lodge in the heart and hurt more than arrows piercing the chest. (SB 11.23 3)

children.topic: Wealth brings labor, fear, anxiety, delusion
children.note: Earning, keeping, spending, losing and enjoying money all torment a man, the brahmana realizes. (SB 11.23 17)

children.topic: Suffering was Hari's gift of detachment
children.note: The brahmana concludes the Lord must be pleased with him, having forced on him the detachment that ferries him across. (SB 11.23 28)

children.topic: The mind alone causes joy and sorrow
children.note: Not people, demigods, body, planets, karma or time, but the mind produces happiness and distress and turns the wheel of life. (SB 11.23 42)

children.topic: Master the mind, master every sense
children.note: The mind has ruled the senses forever and bows to nothing; whoever controls it commands all the senses. (SB 11.23 47)

children.topic: Crossing nescience by serving Krishna's feet
children.note: The brahmana vows to cross the ocean of ignorance by fixed service to Krishna, as the previous acaryas approved. (SB 11.23 57)
Srila Prabhupada's recorded class: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 11.23.57, Initiations and Sannyāsa of Sudāmā. Tap the link to read the transcript and play the audio.
Recorded classes on this chapter, with transcript and audio on vedabase.io. Oldest first.

Krishna tells of a miserly Avanti brahmana who lost all his wealth, became detached and took sannyasa. Tormented by rowdies, he sang that neither people, gods, body, planets, karma nor time cause suffering, only the mind, and resolved to serve Krishna's feet.

children.topic: One Truth becomes nature and enjoyer
children.note: The Absolute, beyond speech and mind, splits into two: matter on one side and the souls who try to enjoy it on the other. (SB 11.24 3)

children.topic: My glance stirs the three modes
children.note: When Krishna glances on nature, goodness, passion and ignorance appear to fulfil the conditioned souls' pending desires. (SB 11.24 5)

children.topic: Yoga reaches Maharloka; bhakti reaches Me
children.note: Austerity and renunciation win the higher planets, but only devotional yoga brings one to the Lord's transcendental abode. (SB 11.24 14)

children.topic: Gold before and after the bracelet
children.note: The ingredient exists before and after its product, so it must be present in between; names like bracelet are conveniences. (SB 11.24 17)
Body merges into food, food into earth, earth into fragrance and water, on through the elements, senses and mind. (SB 11.24 22-27)

children.topic: Sunrise dispels the dark of duality
children.note: Knowing how the cosmos dissolves removes illusory duality from a serious student's mind as the sun clears the sky. (SB 11.24 28)

Krishna teaches Sankhya: the one Absolute divides into nature and enjoyer, the modes yield mahat-tattva, false ego, elements and demigods, and Brahma builds the worlds. Gold and clay show substance outlasting form; annihilation reverses creation step by step.

children.topic: 25 · The Three Modes of Nature and Beyond

children.note: Krishna lists the character marks of each mode, from self-control and mercy in goodness to anger, laziness and violence in ignorance. (SB 11.25 2-5)
Alert wakefulness comes from goodness, dreaming from passion, dreamless sleep from ignorance, while a fourth transcendental state pervades them all. (SB 11.25 20)
Dying in goodness leads to heaven, in passion to a human birth, in ignorance to hell, but one beyond all modes reaches Krishna. (SB 11.25 22)

children.topic: Forest, town, gambling den, Krishna's abode
children.note: Places carry modes too: forest life is goodness, city life passion, a gambling house ignorance, and living where Krishna dwells is transcendental. (SB 11.25 25)

children.topic: Use the human form to transcend
children.note: Having gained a human body fit for knowledge, an intelligent person should shed the modes' contamination and serve Krishna with love. (SB 11.25 33)
After defeating passion and ignorance with goodness, the fixed devotee lets go of goodness itself through indifference and reaches Krishna. (SB 11.25 35)

Krishna tells Uddhava how goodness, passion and ignorance shape a person's traits, faith, food, work, happiness and next birth, then urges him to rise above all three modes through devotional service and attain pure love for Him.
Following materialists devoted to belly and genitals drags one into the darkest pit, like one blind man led by another. (SB 11.26 3)

children.topic: What use is learning if lust wins?
children.note: Pururava asks what education, austerity, scripture and solitude are worth when a woman can still carry off one's mind. (SB 11.26 12)
Years of enjoying Urvasi never satisfied Pururava; his desire kept flaring like a fire fed with ghee. (SB 11.26 14)
Pururava admits the fault was his own ignorance and lack of sense control, like mistaking a rope for a snake. (SB 11.26 17)
An intelligent person drops bad company and keeps company with devotees, whose words sever the mind's excessive attachments. (SB 11.26 26)
Peaceful devotees fixed in knowledge are the shelter for souls drowning in the fearful ocean of material life. (SB 11.26 32)

Krishna warns against bad association and relates the song of King Pururava, who after losing Urvasi laments how lust wasted his years and stole his intelligence; he turns to detachment and Krishna praises the saintly devotees as a rescuing boat.

children.topic: 27 · Lord Kṛṣṇa’s Instructions on the Process of Deity Worship

children.note: A twice-born person may worship Krishna sincerely in the Deity, on the ground, in fire, the sun, water or within the heart. (SB 11.27 9)
The Lord's Deity may be made of stone, wood, metal, earth, paint, sand, jewels or conceived within the mind. (SB 11.27 12)

children.topic: A little water offered with faith
children.note: Whatever a devotee offers with faith, even a few drops of water, is most dear to Krishna. (SB 11.27 16-17)
Lavish gifts from nondevotees do not please Krishna, but a loving devotee's tiny offering does. (SB 11.27 18)

children.topic: Sing, dance and enact His pastimes
children.note: The devotee should spend time in festivity, chanting loudly, dancing, acting out and narrating Krishna's pastimes. (SB 11.27 44)
Whoever serves without seeking rewards attains Krishna Himself, and this worship ripens into pure devotion. (SB 11.27 53)

At Uddhava's request Krishna explains Deity worship: the eight kinds of Deity forms, bathing and decorating, mental meditation, offering foods, fire sacrifice, singing and dancing, and building temples; He is pleased by any small offering made with love.
Krishna opens by telling Uddhava to stop judging others' conditioned behavior and see everything as nature and soul resting in the Absolute. (SB 11.28 1)
As a waking person is no longer troubled by a nightmare, the enlightened soul is untouched by material experiences. (SB 11.28 14)
False ego shows up as mind, speech and life air, but a sage cuts it off with knowledge sharpened by serving the guru. (SB 11.28 17)
Just as gold alone persists through its ornaments, Krishna alone exists before, during and after the universe. (SB 11.28 19)
Realization of Krishna removes the darkness covering consciousness, as sunrise reveals objects that were always present. (SB 11.28 34)
One who takes refuge in Krishna tastes the soul's happiness, stays free of hankering and overcomes every obstacle in yoga. (SB 11.28 44)

Krishna teaches jnana-yoga: avoid praising or blaming others, see the world as illusion resting on the one Absolute Truth, and cut false ego with the sword of knowledge; He answers Uddhava on who really suffers and dismisses bodily mystic perfections.
Uddhava says no poet could repay Krishna, who delivers souls in two ways, as the acarya outwardly and as the Supersoul inwardly. (SB 11.29 6)
The truly wise person honors all, seeing Krishna equally present in the brahmana and outcaste, the gentle and the cruel. (SB 11.29 13-14)

children.topic: Bow even to dogs and asses
children.note: Ignoring ridicule, one should drop bodily shame and offer prostrated obeisances to every creature. (SB 11.29 16)
Krishna calls this path the highest intelligence, since it uses the temporary to reach the eternal reality in one lifetime. (SB 11.29 22)
One who abandons fruitive work and offers himself fully to Krishna escapes birth and death and shares His opulences. (SB 11.29 34)
Overcome by fear of separation, Uddhava bows again and again, places his master's sandals on his head and departs. (SB 11.29 46)

Uddhava asks for an easier path, and Krishna gives bhakti-yoga: do everything for Him, see Him in all beings, honor everyone, and share this knowledge with the faithful. Uddhava weeps in gratitude and is sent to Badarikasrama as Krishna concludes His teaching.

children.topic: 30 · The Disappearance of the Yadu Dynasty

children.note: Krishna tells the Yadu leaders that terrible signs have appeared in Dvaraka and they must leave at once. (SB 11.30 5)
Intoxicated and arrogant at Prabhasa, the Yadu heroes are bewildered by Krishna's own potency and a deadly quarrel erupts. (SB 11.30 13)
Grasping reeds that turn to thunderbolt-hard clubs, the Yadus beat each other and even attack Krishna. (SB 11.30 21)
With His dynasty destroyed, Krishna reflects that the earth's burden has finally been removed. (SB 11.30 25)
The hunter Jara mistakes the Lord's foot for a deer and pierces it with an arrow made from Samba's iron club. (SB 11.30 33)

children.topic: Do not fear, it was My wish
children.note: Krishna reassures the terrified hunter, says the act was His own desire, and sends him to the spiritual world. (SB 11.30 39)

Seeing evil omens, Krishna sends the Yadus to Prabhasa, where they drink, quarrel and slaughter each other with cane stalks turned iron. Balarama departs, the hunter Jara pierces Krishna's foot, and Krishna forgives him and dispatches Daruka to Dvaraka.

children.topic: 31 · The Disappearance of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa

children.note: Krishna does not use fire meditation to destroy His body but simply enters His own abode with it. (SB 11.31 6)
The demigods cannot follow Krishna's movements any more than men can track a bolt of lightning leaving a cloud. (SB 11.31 9)
Sukadeva tells Pariksit the Lord's coming and going only resemble a conditioned soul's; they are a performance staged by His energy. (SB 11.31 11)

children.topic: This world has no real value
children.note: Krishna, cause of everything, simply chose not to keep His body here, showing that the mortal world is not worth clinging to. (SB 11.31 13)
Once the Lord leaves, the sea floods Dvaraka on every side, sparing only His palace. (SB 11.31 23)
Anyone who clearly recites the Lord's childhood and incarnation pastimes gains loving service to Krishna. (SB 11.31 28)

Brahma, Siva and the demigods gather at Prabhasa as Krishna withdraws into His own abode without burning His body. Sukadeva explains the departure as a show of His potency; Krishna's parents and wives pass away, Dvaraka floods, and Arjuna moves the survivors.
The curse on the Yadu dynasty, the Uddhava-gita: Krishna’s final teachings, the avadhuta’s 24 teachers, and Krishna’s disappearance. 31 chapters.

children.topic: Nanda, son of a sudra woman
children.note: Mahanandi fathers the mighty Nanda, who crushes the ksatriyas; from then on kings are mostly irreligious sudras. (SB 12.1 6-8)
A brahmana betrays Nanda and his eight sons and destroys them, ushering in the Maurya dynasty. (SB 12.1 11)
The brahmana installs Candragupta, whose line continues through Varisara and Asokavardhana. (SB 12.1 12)
Future rulers will prey on their own people, kill women, cows and brahmanas, and be short-lived slaves of passion and ignorance. (SB 12.1 39-40)
People governed by low-class kings copy their character and speech, harass each other and are ruined together. (SB 12.1 41)

Sukadeva foretells the Kali-yuga dynasties after Pariksit: the Pradyotanas, Sisunagas, Nanda, Candragupta and the Mauryas, the Sungas, Kanvas, Andhras and many barbarian lines, ending with degraded rulers whose citizens copy their vices and are ruined.
Religion, truth, cleanliness, mercy, lifespan, strength and memory all decline day by day under Kali's influence. (SB 12.2 1)
In Kali-yuga money alone marks good birth and character, and justice goes to whoever has power. (SB 12.2 2)
The Lord will appear as Kalki in the home of the brahmana Visnuyasa in the village of Sambhala. (SB 12.2 18)

children.topic: Kalki on horseback slays false kings
children.note: Riding Devadatta with sword in hand, Kalki kills by the millions the thieves posing as rulers. (SB 12.2 19-20)
As long as Krishna's feet touched the earth, the Age of Kali could not take hold of the planet. (SB 12.2 30)

children.topic: King today, worms and ashes tomorrow
children.note: A body called king ends as worms, stool or ashes; harming others for its sake only leads one to hell. (SB 12.2 41)
Srila Prabhupada's recorded class: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 12.2.1. Tap the link to read the transcript and play the audio.
Recorded classes on this chapter, with transcript and audio on vedabase.io. Oldest first.

Sukadeva describes Kali-yuga's decay: religion, lifespan and memory shrink, wealth decides status, and rulers become thieves. Lord Kalki then appears from Sambhala to kill the impostor kings and restart Satya-yuga; kings who claimed the earth all turn to dust.
Seeing kings scheme to possess her, the earth mocks them as toys in the hands of death. (SB 12.3 1)
Sukadeva explains he told royal histories only to teach knowledge and detachment, not as the goal itself. (SB 12.3 14)
In Satya-yuga religion stands on all four legs: truthfulness, mercy, austerity and charity. (SB 12.3 18)
Misled by atheism, people of Kali will rarely offer anything to the Lord whom even the rulers of the worlds honor. (SB 12.3 43)
Though Kali is an ocean of faults, simply chanting Hare Krishna frees one from bondage and lifts one to the spiritual kingdom. (SB 12.3 51)

children.topic: One chant equals all past practices
children.note: What meditation, sacrifice and temple service achieved in earlier ages is gained in Kali just by chanting the maha-mantra. (SB 12.3 52)

The earth laughs at kings who try to conquer her yet die helpless. Sukadeva then describes the four ages and religion's shrinking legs, Kali's ugly symptoms, and the age's one great virtue: chanting the Hare Krishna mantra frees one from bondage.

children.topic: 4 · The Four Categories of Universal Annihilation

children.note: One thousand cycles of four ages make a kalpa, Brahma's single day, during which fourteen Manus rule. (SB 12.4 2)
As annihilation nears, drought lasts a century, famine spreads, and starving people devour each other. (SB 12.4 7)
Water loses taste to fire, fire form to air, air touch to ether, ether sound to ego, and all merge back into the mahat-tattva. (SB 12.4 15-19)
When knowledge severs false ego and one realizes the Supersoul, that is the final end of material existence. (SB 12.4 34)
Time works through continuous, occasional, elemental and ultimate dissolution. (SB 12.4 38)
For one burning in miseries, taste for hearing the Lord's pastimes is the only boat across the ocean of existence. (SB 12.4 40)

Sukadeva explains four annihilations: the occasional one at Brahma's night, the elemental one at Brahma's death when all dissolves into pradhana, the continuous erosion by time, and the ultimate one when knowledge cuts false ego. Devotion is the only boat.

children.topic: 5 · Śukadeva Gosvāmī’s Final Instructions to Mahārāja Parīkṣit

children.note: Sukadeva tells the king to abandon the animal-like thought of dying, since the soul never took birth and cannot be destroyed. (SB 12.5 2)

children.topic: Sky remains when the pot breaks
children.note: As space inside a pot is unaffected when the pot shatters, the soul resumes its own identity when the bodies die. (SB 12.5 5)
The snake-bird's poison will not touch Pariksit's true self, for he has already conquered every danger on the path home. (SB 12.5 10)

children.topic: You will not notice the bite
children.note: Absorbed in the Supreme Soul, Pariksit will not perceive Taksaka's fangs, his dying body or the world around him. (SB 12.5 11-12)

Sukadeva gives his final lesson: Pariksit should drop the animal fear of dying, since the soul is unborn and separate from the body like fire from fuel. Fixed on Vasudeva, he will not even notice Taksaka's bite.
Pariksit declares he no longer fears the snake-bird or repeated death, having absorbed himself in the Absolute Truth. (SB 12.6 5)
The snake-bird buys off the sage who could cure the poison, disguises himself as a brahmana and bites the king. (SB 12.6 12)
Brhaspati tells Janamejaya that each soul's life, death and next destination come from his own acts, not another agent. (SB 12.6 25)
The three-sound omkara arises from subtle transcendental vibration and represents the Absolute in all three phases. (SB 12.6 39)

children.topic: Vyasa sorts the Veda into four
children.note: Like sorting mixed jewels into piles, Vyasa separates the mantras into the Rg, Yajur, Sama and Atharva Vedas. (SB 12.6 50)
Yajnavalkya vomits up his master's mantras, and fellow disciples as partridges collect them, forming the Taittiriya-samhita. (SB 12.6 64-65)

Pariksit thanks Sukadeva, meditates by the Ganges and is bitten by Taksaka. Brhaspati halts Janamejaya's snake sacrifice. Suta then explains how omkara and the Vedas arose from Brahma, how Vyasa divided them, and how disciples like Yajnavalkya spread them.
Authorities define a great Purana by ten subjects from creation through annihilation to the supreme shelter; lesser ones cover five. (SB 12.7 9-10)

children.topic: The Lord appears in every age
children.note: In each age the infallible Lord descends among animals, humans, sages and gods to protect the universe and defeat Vedic culture's enemies. (SB 12.7 14)

children.topic: The Absolute is the unique shelter
children.note: The Supreme Truth pervades waking, dream and deep sleep and every illusory phenomenon, yet stands apart as the ultimate refuge. (SB 12.7 19)
Suta lists the eighteen great Puranas, from Brahma and Padma to Kurma and Brahmanda, including Srimad-Bhagavatam. (SB 12.7 23-24)

Suta names the teachers of the Atharva Veda and the Puranas, defines a Purana by ten topics (creation, secondary creation, maintenance, sustenance, Manus, dynasties, their deeds, annihilation, motivation, supreme shelter), and lists the eighteen major Puranas.
While Markandeya sat absorbed in yoga, the enormous span of six Manu lifetimes slipped by. (SB 12.8 14)
Fearing the sage's growing power, Indra dispatches Cupid, dancing girls, spring, scented breezes, greed and intoxication. (SB 12.8 16)
Cupid shoots thinking he has won, but every effort to seduce Markandeya proves as futile as an atheist's endeavors. (SB 12.8 28)
Cupid's party feel scorched by the sage's potency and give up their mischief, as children who have roused a sleeping serpent. (SB 12.8 29)
Markandeya prays that Brahma himself dreads time's passage, so only the Lord's feet can relieve conditioned souls' fear. (SB 12.8 43)
Though the Lord uses all three modes for creation, He frees souls specifically through goodness; passion and ignorance bring suffering. (SB 12.8 45)

Suta tells how Markandeya practiced celibacy and austerity for six Manu ages, resisted Indra's Cupid and Apsaras unmoved, and was visited by Nara-Narayana Rsi; overwhelmed, he offers prayers on the Lord's power, fear of time and the mode of goodness.

children.topic: 9 · Mārkaṇḍeya Ṛṣi Sees the Illusory Potency of the Lord

children.note: Offered any benediction, Markandeya says the Lord's darsana is all he wants. (SB 12.9 4)
Satisfied but curious, the sage asks to witness the illusory energy that makes the world seem materially varied. (SB 12.9 6)
Water covers earth, sky and heaven, and Markandeya wanders the deluge alone, hair loose, as if blind and dumb. (SB 12.9 15)
On a small island's banyan tree he sees a glowing baby lying on a leaf, its effulgence swallowing the darkness. (SB 12.9 21)
The child breathes in and Markandeya enters His body, finding the entire universe intact within. (SB 12.9 27)
When the Lord vanishes, the deluge and banyan disappear too and the sage instantly finds himself home as before. (SB 12.9 34)

Narayana offers Markandeya a boon and the sage asks only to see the Lord's maya. A cosmic deluge sweeps him alone through darkness for ages until he finds an infant on a banyan leaf, is inhaled into the child to see the whole universe, then returns home.

children.topic: 10 · Lord Śiva and Umā Glorify Mārkaṇḍeya Ṛṣi

children.note: Siva tells Uma the sage desires no boon, not even liberation, having attained pure devotion to the Lord. (SB 12.10 6)
Siva still wishes to speak with the sage, since keeping company with saintly devotees is the highest achievement. (SB 12.10 7)
Seeing Markandeya unaware of his visitors, Siva uses mystic power to pass into the sky of his heart like wind through an opening. (SB 12.10 10)
Holy rivers and statues purify slowly, but saintly devotees purify immediately, just by being seen. (SB 12.10 23)
Markandeya's single request is unfailing devotion to the Supreme Lord and to His devotees, especially Siva. (SB 12.10 34)
Siva grants that the sage will keep pious fame and freedom from aging and death until the end of the creation cycle. (SB 12.10 36)

Siva and Uma find Markandeya in trance and Siva enters his heart to rouse him. Siva praises devotees who purify by mere sight; the sage asks only for unfailing devotion to the Lord and His devotees, and Siva grants him fame, deathlessness and Puranic mastery.

children.topic: Earth His feet, sun His eyes
children.note: In the universal person the earth is His feet, sky His navel, sun His eyes, wind His nostrils and the clouds His hair. (SB 12.11 6-8)
The gem on the Lord's chest represents the spirit soul, and the Srivatsa mark is that gem's spreading radiance. (SB 12.11 10)

children.topic: Meaning of club, conch, disc, bow
children.note: The club is prana, the conch water, the Sudarsana disc fire, the sword ether, the shield ignorance and the bow Sarnga time. (SB 12.11 14-15)

children.topic: Umbrella is Vaikuntha, Garuda the Vedas
children.note: The Lord's parasol is His fearless spiritual abode, and His carrier Garuda embodies the threefold Veda. (SB 12.11 19)
One who quietly recites this description each morning with a purified mind realizes the Mahapurusa within the heart. (SB 12.11 26)
All the sun's associates are Visnu's expansions, and remembering them at dawn and dusk removes sinful reactions. (SB 12.11 45)

Suta describes the Lord's universal form and what each ornament and weapon represents: the Kaustubha is the soul, the disc fire, the bow time, the umbrella Vaikuntha. He then names the seven companions who ride along with the sun-god month by month.
Even an involuntary shout of obeisance to Hari when falling, sneezing or in pain frees one from sinful reactions. (SB 12.12 47)
Speech about temporary matters is false and empty; only words revealing the Lord's qualities are truthful and auspicious. (SB 12.12 49)
Literature that ignores the Lord's glories is a crow's resort, shunned by the wise, while devotees relish only Krishna-katha. (SB 12.12 51)
Writing full of the Lord's names and pastimes sparks a revolution in misdirected civilization and is accepted even if flawed. (SB 12.12 52)
Constant recitation, or faithfully hearing just one verse, a line or half a line, purifies the self. (SB 12.12 59)
Suta bows to his guru Sukadeva, who left Brahman absorption when attracted by Krishna's melodious pastimes and spoke this Purana. (SB 12.12 69)

Suta recaps the whole Bhagavatam canto by canto, from creation and Kapila to Krishna's pastimes, the Uddhava-gita and Pariksit's passing. He then praises words that glorify the Lord and the fruits of hearing this Purana, and bows to Sukadeva.
Among the Puranas' verse counts, Srimad-Bhagavatam contains eighteen thousand verses. (SB 12.13 4-9)
The Lord spoke the full Bhagavatam to Brahma as he sat afraid on the navel lotus. (SB 12.13 10)
The Bhagavatam is Vedanta's essence, and whoever tastes its nectar is never again drawn to other literature. (SB 12.13 15)
As Ganga leads the rivers, Acyuta the deities and Siva the Vaisnavas, so the Bhagavatam leads all Puranas. (SB 12.13 16)

children.topic: The chain from Brahma to Pariksit
children.note: The Lord gave this torch of knowledge to Brahma, who passed it to Narada, Vyasa, Sukadeva and finally Pariksit. (SB 12.13 19)
Suta honors Sukadeva, who rescued Pariksit from the serpent of material existence. (SB 12.13 21)

Suta lists the verse counts of the eighteen Puranas, tells how the Lord first spoke the Bhagavatam to a frightened Brahma, and glorifies it as the essence of Vedanta and greatest of Puranas, ending with prayers for pure devotion and obeisances to Sukadeva.
The age of Kali: degraded dynasties, the symptoms of the age, Pariksit’s passing, and the glories of the Bhagavatam itself. 13 chapters.

Sacinandana descends in Kali-yuga to bestow what no earlier incarnation offered, the mellow of conjugal love. (CC Adi 1 4)

children.topic: Radha and Krishna united as Caitanya
children.note: The once-separated Radha and Krishna have joined as one in Caitanya, who is Krishna with Radha's mood and complexion. (CC Adi 1 5)

children.topic: The guru is nondifferent from Krishna

The two brothers lead one to the book Bhagavata and the person bhagavata, the devotee immersed in loving mellows. (CC Adi 1 99)

Krsnadasa Kaviraja opens with fourteen invocation verses to Caitanya, Nityananda and Advaita, then explains six features of one truth: guru, devotees, incarnations, expansions, energies and Krishna Himself. Caitanya and Nityananda are Gauda's sun and moon.

children.topic: 2 · Śri Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Supreme Personality of Godhead

children.note: Krishna, the original Personality of Godhead, is all-perfect knowledge and bliss, the source of all-pervading Visnu. (CC Adi 2 8)
As a single sun reflects in many jewels, Govinda appears as the Supersoul in every heart. (CC Adi 2 19)
Brahma explains 'nara' as all living beings and 'ayana' as their refuge, so Krishna is the original Narayana. (CC Adi 2 38)
Every incarnation is a portion of the purusa-avataras, but Krishna is the Supreme Lord and the source of them all. (CC Adi 2 70)
Just as one candle from which many are lit is the original, Krishna is the origin of all expansions. (CC Adi 2 89)
The author concludes that Lord Caitanya is Krishna Himself, Vraja's own prince. (CC Adi 2 120)

Explaining his third verse, Krsnadasa shows from scripture that Brahman, Paramatma and Bhagavan are features of one Krishna. Brahma proves Krishna is the original Narayana, and 'krsnas tu bhagavan svayam' is defended by grammar. That Krishna is Caitanya.

children.topic: 3 · The External Reasons for the Appearance of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu
Without love the world is useless
children.note: Krishna reflects that He has long withheld pure loving service, without which material existence has no purpose. (CC Adi 3 14)

children.topic: Awe and reverence do not attract Him
children.note: Worship weakened by veneration of Krishna's opulence fails to win Him the way Vraja's intimate love does. (CC Adi 3 16)
Krishna resolves to personally start congregational chanting and make the world dance in the four mellows of love. (CC Adi 3 19)
The Bhagavatam verse says intelligent people in Kali worship through sankirtana a non-blackish Krishna who constantly sings His name. (CC Adi 3 52)
Advaita recalls that Krishna gives Himself to a devotee who offers only a tulasi leaf and a palmful of water. (CC Adi 3 104)
The principal cause of Caitanya's descent is Advaita's loud petition; the Lord appears by His devotee's desire. (CC Adi 3 110)

Explaining the fourth verse: Krishna descends as Caitanya to launch nama-sankirtana and teach Vraja's loving devotion by His own example; scripture foretells a golden Kali-yuga avatara; and Advaita Acarya's loud calls with tulasi and water draw Him down.

children.topic: 4 · The Confidential Reasons for the Appearance of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu
Two inner motives for Krishna's coming
children.note: Beyond killing demons, Krishna descends to relish the sweetness of loving devotion and to spread spontaneous, attraction-based bhakti in the world. (CC Adi 4 15-16)

children.topic: Krishna becomes controlled by intimate love
children.note: When a devotee loves Krishna as son, friend or beloved, seeing himself as equal or superior, Krishna willingly becomes subordinate to that love. (CC Adi 4 21-22)

children.topic: Radha and Krishna united in one body
children.note: Radha and Krishna, one identity split into two, have joined again as Caitanya, who is Krishna wearing Radha's feelings and complexion. (CC Adi 4 55)

children.topic: Lust versus love: the key difference
children.note: Wanting to please one's own senses is kama; wanting to please Krishna's senses is prema, and the two are as different as iron and gold. (CC Adi 4 165)
To grasp the greatness of Radha's love, what she relishes in him, and her joy in his sweetness, Krishna appeared from Saci's womb in her mood. (CC Adi 4 230)

children.topic: Krishna decides to take Radha's mood
children.note: Krishna concludes that his three longings can be fulfilled only by adopting Radha's emotions and golden luster, and resolves to descend as Caitanya. (CC Adi 4 268)

Krishnadasa explains the hidden reasons for Caitanya's descent: Krishna wants to taste Radha's love, see his own sweetness through her eyes, and feel the joy she gets from him, so he appears in her mood and golden color. Radha's love and the gopis' selfless devotion are analysed.

children.topic: 5 · The Glories Of Lord Nityānanda Balarāma

children.note: Krishna and Balarama share one identity but differ in form; Balarama is Krishna's first bodily expansion and assists in all his pastimes. (CC Adi 5 5)
Krishna is the true cause of the cosmos; inert prakriti alone is as useless as the milkless nipples on a goat's neck. (CC Adi 5 61)
Brahma marvels that he is enclosed in one universe while countless universes drift through the pores of the Lord's body like dust through a window. (CC Adi 5 72)
Ananta Sesa is called Sesa because he reaches the limit of servitude, becoming Krishna's bed, slippers, umbrella and throne. (CC Adi 5 124)
Accepting Caitanya while disrespecting Nityananda is as absurd as wanting a hen for eggs but cutting off the half that eats. (CC Adi 5 176)

children.topic: Nityananda's dream order: go to Vrindavana
children.note: In a dream Nityananda tells Krishnadasa not to fear but to go to Vrindavana, where he will attain everything; he leaves that very moment. (CC Adi 5 195)

Krishnadasa explains verses seven to eleven on Nityananda as Balarama, the source of Sankarsana, Sesa and the three Vishnu purushas who create the universes. He then tells his own story: rebuking his brother, Nityananda's dream order to go to Vrindavana, and the mercy he found there.

children.topic: 6 · The Glories of Śrī Advaita Ācārya
Why he is called Advaita Acarya
children.note: He is Advaita because he is non-different from Hari, and Acarya because he teaches the path of devotion; he is both Lord and devotee incarnation. (CC Adi 6 5)

children.topic: Tulasi and Ganges water summon Caitanya
children.note: Advaita worshiped Krishna with tulasi leaves and Ganges water and called aloud until Caitanya appeared on earth with his associates. (CC Adi 6 34)

children.topic: Servitude outweighs oneness ten million times
children.note: The joy of serving Krishna is an ocean; the bliss of merging with Brahman multiplied ten million times cannot match one drop of it. (CC Adi 6 44)
Love for Krishna has a unique effect: it fills superiors, equals and inferiors alike with the wish to serve him. (CC Adi 6 53)

children.topic: Devotees dearer than Krishna's own self
children.note: Being a devotee is higher than being equal to Krishna, since Krishna holds his devotees dearer than himself. (CC Adi 6 100)

children.topic: Krishna needs a devotee's heart to taste himself
children.note: Even Krishna cannot relish his own sweetness without adopting a devotee's emotions, which is why he came as Caitanya. (CC Adi 6 108)

Krishnadasa glorifies Advaita Acarya as the incarnation of Maha-Vishnu who is the material cause of creation and whose loud prayers brought Caitanya down. Though Caitanya honors him as guru, Advaita calls himself Caitanya's servant, and the chapter shows that even Nanda, the gopis and Balarama feel this servitude.
Krishna manifests as a devotee, a devotee's expansion, a devotee incarnation, a pure devotee and the devotional energy: the Panca-tattva. (CC Adi 7 6)

children.topic: Breaking open the storehouse of love
children.note: Krishna's love came sealed in a storehouse; Caitanya and his associates broke the seal, tasted freely, and thirsted for more the more they tasted. (CC Adi 7 20-21)

children.topic: Guru calls him a fool: just chant
children.note: Caitanya's guru tells him he is unfit for Vedanta study and must always chant Krishna's name, the essence of all mantras. (CC Adi 7 72)
The verse Caitanya keeps in his throat: in this age there is no alternative to the holy name, repeated three times for emphasis. (CC Adi 7 76)

children.topic: Brahman bliss is a shallow canal
children.note: Compared with the ocean of joy from chanting Hare Krishna, the pleasure of impersonal Brahman realization is like canal water. (CC Adi 7 97)

children.topic: Sambandha, abhidheya, prayojana in every sutra
children.note: Caitanya sums up Vedanta: relationship with God, action in that relationship, and love of God as the goal run through every aphorism. (CC Adi 7 146)

Krishnadasa explains the Panca-tattva who plunder and freely distribute the storehouse of love of God. Caitanya takes sannyasa to catch the Mayavadis, then at a feast in Varanasi tells Prakasananda how his guru ordered him to chant, refutes Sankara's indirect readings of Vedanta, and converts the sannyasis.

children.topic: 8 · The Author Receives the Orders of Kṛṣṇa and Guru
Panca-tattva makes the dumb a poet
children.note: Remembering the Panca-tattva's feet, a mute can compose poetry, a lame man can cross mountains and a blind man can see the stars. (CC Adi 8 5)

children.topic: Krishna hides pure bhakti, gives the rest
children.note: Krishna readily grants liberation or sense pleasure to anyone who asks, but keeps pure devotional service concealed. (CC Adi 8 18)

children.topic: Iron heart: no tears while chanting
children.note: If the heart does not change and tears do not flow while chanting, the heart is hard as iron because of offenses to the holy name. (CC Adi 8 25)

children.topic: Caitanya and Nityananda's names clear offenses
children.note: Chanting Caitanya's and Nityananda's names with even a little faith quickly removes offenses, so Hare Krishna then gives ecstasy. (CC Adi 8 31)
When Krishnadasa prays for permission to write, a garland slips from Madana-mohana's neck and the priest places it on him. (CC Adi 8 75)
The author says the book is not his but is dictated by Madana-mohana; he merely repeats it like a parrot. (CC Adi 8 78)

Krishnadasa urges everyone to worship Caitanya and Nityananda, explains why chanting with offenses fails while their names cleanse quickly, praises Vrindavana dasa's Caitanya-mangala, and tells how the Vrindavana Vaishnavas ordered him to write; Madana-mohana's garland fell as the Deity's permission.

children.topic: 9 · The Desire Tree of Devotional Service
Living up to the name Visvambhara
children.note: Caitanya reasons that his name, maintainer of the universe, will be true only if he fills the whole universe with love of God. (CC Adi 9 7)

children.topic: Seed first sprouts in Madhavendra Puri
children.note: Madhavendra Puri is the storehouse of devotion where the seed of the bhakti tree first fructified, before Isvara Puri and Caitanya. (CC Adi 9 10)

children.topic: Fruit given without checking who is fit
children.note: The gardener hands out the fruit of devotion without asking who wanted it or who deserved it. (CC Adi 9 29)

children.topic: Order to everyone: distribute this movement
children.note: Caitanya commands every person in the universe to take up Krishna consciousness and spread it everywhere. (CC Adi 9 36)

children.topic: Duty of one born in India
children.note: A person born as a human in Bharata-varsha should perfect his own life and then work for the welfare of all others. (CC Adi 9 41)
Whoever eats his fill of Caitanya's fruit becomes maddened, chanting, dancing and laughing on his own. (CC Adi 9 49)

Krishnadasa describes Caitanya as gardener, seed and trunk of the desire tree of devotion, rooted in Madhavendra Puri, Isvara Puri and nine sannyasi roots. The gardener distributes the fruit of love of God to everyone free of charge and orders every branch to spread it across the world.

children.topic: 10 · The Trunk, Branches and Subbranches of the Caitanya Tree

children.note: Caitanya had many associates, but none should be called higher or lower; the difference cannot be judged. (CC Adi 10 4)

children.topic: Vasudeva Datta offers to suffer for all
children.note: Vasudeva Datta wished to take on the sins of every soul in the world so that Caitanya could deliver them all. (CC Adi 10 42)
Haridasa Thakura, the twentieth branch, chanted Krishna's name three hundred thousand times every day without fail. (CC Adi 10 43)

children.topic: Even a dog of Kulina-grama is dear
children.note: Caitanya declares that even a dog from the village of Kulina-grama is his dear friend. (CC Adi 10 82)
Raghunatha dasa spent over twenty-two and a half hours a day in devotional practice and slept less than two. (CC Adi 10 102)

children.topic: Jagai and Madhai prove the Lord's name
children.note: The two brothers were living evidence that Caitanya is rightly called Patita-pavana, savior of the fallen. (CC Adi 10 120)

Krishnadasa lists the branches of the Caitanya tree: Srivasa, Gadadhara, Vakresvara, Jagadananda, Raghava and his bags, Vasudeva Datta, Haridasa Thakura, Murari Gupta, Sivananda Sena, Rupa and Sanatana, Raghunatha dasa and dozens more from Bengal, Puri and Varanasi.
Though Virabhadra Gosani was the Supreme Lord, he presented himself as a devotee and strictly kept the Vedic rules. (CC Adi 11 9)
All of Nityananda's associates were formerly cowherd boys in Vraja, shown by their horns, sticks, cowherd dress and peacock feathers. (CC Adi 11 21)

children.topic: Kirtana that melts wood and stone
children.note: When Vasudeva Ghosa sang about Caitanya and Nityananda, even wood and stone would soften on hearing it. (CC Adi 11 19)

children.topic: Vrindavana dasa, the Vyasa of Caitanya-lila
children.note: As Vyasa recorded Krishna's pastimes in the Bhagavatam, Vrindavana dasa is the Vyasa of Caitanya's pastimes. (CC Adi 11 55)

children.topic: Power to give Krishna to anyone
children.note: Nityananda's followers had unlimited strength to deliver ceaseless love of Krishna and could offer Krishna himself to anyone. (CC Adi 11 59)

Krishnadasa names the chief followers of Nityananda, headed by Virabhadra Gosani, along with the twelve gopalas such as Ramadasa, Gadadhara dasa, Sundarananda and Uddharana Datta, and dozens of others, all of whom freely distributed love of Krishna.

children.topic: 12 · The Expansions of Advaita Ācārya and Gadādhara Paṇḍita

children.note: The spiritual master's instruction is the living principle of spiritual life; whoever disobeys it becomes useless at once. (CC Adi 12 10)
Young Acyutananda objects that Caitanya, guru of the fourteen worlds, cannot have Kesava Bharati as his guru, and Advaita is delighted. (CC Adi 12 16)
When mantras fail to revive fainted Gopala, Caitanya touches his chest and tells him to rise and chant, and he wakes. (CC Adi 12 25)

children.topic: Punished by the Lord: great fortune
children.note: Advaita consoles Kamalakanta that being chastised by Caitanya is a rare blessing, like the punishment given to Mukunda and Saci. (CC Adi 12 38)

children.topic: A guru must not take from the rich
children.note: Caitanya teaches that a spiritual master who accepts money or grain from materialists pollutes his mind and loses remembrance of Krishna. (CC Adi 12 50)

children.topic: Remembering these Vaishnavas fulfills all desires
children.note: Simply recalling the names of these devotees brings one to Caitanya's feet and fulfills every wish. (CC Adi 12 92)

Krishnadasa lists Advaita Acarya's followers, praising the loyal line of his son Acyutananda and warning that those who left Caitanya's path withered. He tells how Caitanya banned Kamalakanta for calling Advaita a debtor, teaching that a guru must not beg from the rich, then lists Gadadhara's branches.

children.topic: 13 · The Advent of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu

children.note: Caitanya appeared in Saka 1407 (AD 1486) and left the world in Saka 1455 (AD 1534), visible for forty-eight years. (CC Adi 13 9)

children.topic: Every stage a pretext for chanting
children.note: From birth through boyhood and youth, Caitanya used one excuse after another to make people chant the names of Hari. (CC Adi 13 22)

children.topic: Advaita resolves to bring Krishna down
children.note: Seeing the world sunk in sense enjoyment, Advaita concludes that only Krishna's own appearance can deliver everyone. (CC Adi 13 69)

children.topic: Rahu's eclipse makes the world chant
children.note: Rahu covers the moon at the birth moment, and the cries of Krishna and Hari flood the three worlds. (CC Adi 13 92)

children.topic: Sita Thakurani names the child Nimai
children.note: Advaita's wife blesses the newborn with long life and, to ward off ghosts and witches, gives him the name Nimai. (CC Adi 13 117)
One who gets a human body but ignores Caitanya's path drinks from a poison pit instead of the nectar river and had better not have lived. (CC Adi 13 123)

Krishnadasa gives an outline of Caitanya's forty-eight years, then narrates his birth: Advaita's loud prayers draw Krishna down, Saci loses eight daughters and bears Visvarupa, and on the Phalguna full moon of 1486 a lunar eclipse makes all Navadvipa chant Hari as Gaurahari appears. Sita Thakurani names him Nimai.

children.topic: Named Visvambhara, maintainer of the world
children.note: Nilambara Cakravarti reads the marks on the child and predicts he will protect the whole world, so he is called Visvambhara. (CC Adi 14 19)
Caught eating dirt, the child argues that sweets and rice are also transformations of earth, so what difference does it make. (CC Adi 14 28)
Saci replies that earth turned into grain nourishes the body while raw dirt sickens it, refuting his Mayavada-style argument. (CC Adi 14 31)

children.topic: Worship me, the Ganges is my maidservant
children.note: Among girls worshiping demigods, the boy claims Ganga, Durga and even Siva are his servants and promises good husbands. (CC Adi 14 50)
Meeting Vallabhacarya's daughter Lakshmi by the Ganges, Nimai tells her to worship him as the Supreme Lord and accepts her devotion. (CC Adi 14 66)

children.topic: Even if he is Narayana, I must teach him
children.note: In a dream Jagannatha Misra insists that a father's duty is to instruct his son, whoever the son may be. (CC Adi 14 89)

Krishnadasa sketches Nimai's childhood: Vishnu marks on his feet, the name Visvambhara, eating dirt and arguing philosophy with Saci, misleading thieves, demanding worship from girls at the Ganges, meeting Lakshmi, ankle-bell sounds, and a brahmana's dream telling Jagannatha Misra who his son is.
As his one requested gift, Nimai asks Saci to stop eating grains on Ekadasi, and she begins fasting from that day. (CC Adi 15 9)
Caitanya comforts his parents that his elder brother's renunciation has delivered the family lines of both father and mother. (CC Adi 15 14)

children.topic: I will stay and serve my parents
children.note: In a trance Nimai tells Visvarupa he is too young for sannyasa and will serve his helpless parents as a householder, pleasing Narayana. (CC Adi 15 20)
Deciding to marry, Caitanya reflects that a house without a wife is not a home, and together the couple fulfills life's purposes. (CC Adi 15 27)

Between ages five and ten Nimai masters grammar under Gangadasa, asks Saci to fast from grains on Ekadasi, consoles his parents when Visvarupa takes sannyasa, reports meeting Visvarupa in a trance, performs his father's funeral rites, and marries Lakshmidevi.

children.topic: 16 · The Pastimes of the Lord in His Childhood and Youth

children.note: Reading endless scriptures and commentaries and hearing many teachers only produces doubt; it cannot settle the goal of life. (CC Adi 16 11)

children.topic: Chanting is the basis of success
children.note: Caitanya instructs Tapana Misra that the goal of life and the way to reach it both rest on chanting the holy name. (CC Adi 16 15)
While Nimai preaches in East Bengal, the snake of separation bites Lakshmidevi and she departs for the spiritual world. (CC Adi 16 21)
Nimai announces that the champion's verse contains five defects and five literary ornaments and asks him to hear and judge. (CC Adi 16 54)

children.topic: One spot of leprosy spoils the body
children.note: A single fault ruins a whole poem, just as one patch of white leprosy makes a jewelled body repulsive. (CC Adi 16 70)
After Sarasvati reveals Nimai's identity in a dream, Kesava Kasmiri surrenders at his feet and is freed from material attachment. (CC Adi 16 107)

At eleven Nimai begins teaching, visits East Bengal spreading the holy name and sends Tapana Misra to Varanasi. Lakshmidevi dies of separation; he marries Vishnupriya. On a full-moon night he asks the proud poet Kesava Kasmiri to explain his Ganges verse and exposes five faults, and the poet surrenders.

children.topic: 17 · The Pastimes of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu in His Youth
Harer nama: the only way in Kali
children.note: Caitanya explains the Purana verse: in this age chanting Hari's name, repeated thrice for emphasis, is the sole path to self-realization. (CC Adi 17 21)

children.topic: Lower than grass, more tolerant than a tree
children.note: The humble, tolerant devotee who honours others and seeks no honour himself can chant the holy name without interruption. (CC Adi 17 31)

children.topic: I came to kill the pasandis
children.note: Angry at Gopala Capala's offence against Srivasa, Caitanya says His mission is to destroy demons and then preach devotion. (CC Adi 17 53)

children.topic: Light torches; let us see the Kazi
children.note: Caitanya answers the Kazi's ban by ordering a city-wide evening kirtan procession under His personal protection. (CC Adi 17 134)
Caitanya challenges the Kazi: since cow and bull are like parents, on what religious principle can one kill and eat them? (CC Adi 17 154)
Converted by Caitanya, the Kazi binds all his descendants never to obstruct the chanting movement in Nadia. (CC Adi 17 222)

Caitanya's youth in Navadvipa: initiation at Gaya, nightly kirtan at Srivasa's house, the Kazi's ban on chanting overturned by a mass procession and debate, the offending students, and His decision to take sannyasa to save them.
Adi-lila: the spiritual masters, Lord Caitanya as Krishna Himself, Nityananda and Advaita, and His early life in Navadvipa.

children.topic: 1 · The Later Pastimes of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu

children.note: The Lord's life is arranged as adi, madhya and antya lila; the madhya covers His six years of travel across India. (CC Madhya 1 21)

children.topic: The same lover, yet longing for the Reva
children.note: Caitanya's mysterious dancing verse expresses Radha meeting Krishna at Kuruksetra while yearning for Vrindavana's atmosphere. (CC Madhya 1 58)
Rupa Gosvami's verse unlocks the meaning: meeting Krishna in royal opulence cannot replace the forest, the Yamuna and the flute. (CC Madhya 1 76)
Rupa and Sanatana, straw in their teeth, plead that they are lower than Jagai and Madhai and the fittest objects of mercy. (CC Madhya 1 190)

children.topic: Your names are now Rupa and Sanatana
children.note: Caitanya renames Dabira Khasa and Sakara Mallika, calls them His old servants and begs them to stop their humility. (CC Madhya 1 208)
Heeding Sanatana's advice, the Lord decides a pilgrimage to Vrindavana should be made alone or with a single companion. (CC Madhya 1 230)

Krishnadasa surveys the last twenty-four years: the adi, madhya and antya divisions, the Gosvamis' books, the South India tour, Ratha-yatra with Bengal devotees, and the meeting at Ramakeli where Rupa and Sanatana receive the Lord's mercy.

children.topic: 2 · The Ecstatic Manifestations of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu

children.note: Caitanya's state during His last years mirrors Radharani's condition when Uddhava visited the grieving gopis. (CC Madhya 2 4)

children.topic: Eyes that never see Krishna are useless
children.note: Without seeing Krishna's moonlike face the eyes are worthless; each sense unfilled by Krishna is declared dead weight. (CC Madhya 2 29)

children.topic: I have no love; my tears are show
children.note: In deep humility Caitanya claims His crying merely pretends good fortune and that He lives purposelessly like an insect. (CC Madhya 2 45)

children.topic: Love of God is hot sugarcane
children.note: Real love of Krishna burns the mouth yet cannot be given up; it is poison and nectar mixed together. (CC Madhya 2 51)
By tasting love of God Himself, Caitanya freely hands its touchstone to anyone, deserving or not. (CC Madhya 2 81)
Even if these pastimes are unclear at first, repeated hearing awakens love for Krishna and reveals the Vrindavana affairs. (CC Madhya 2 87)

A synopsis of the antya-lila: for twelve years Caitanya, in Radha's mood, shows madness of separation from Krishna, His body transformed, lamenting before Svarupa Damodara and Ramananda Raya and reciting verses of longing.

children.topic: 3 · Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu’s Stay at the House of Advaita Ācārya

children.note: The true purpose of renunciation is to devote oneself to Mukunda's service, which alone frees one from material bondage. (CC Madhya 3 8)
Advaita explains to the bewildered Lord that His presence makes any place Vrindavana, and that He now stands on the Ganges bank. (CC Madhya 3 33)

children.topic: Feed Krishna well, and I bow to you
children.note: Delighted by Advaita's offering, Caitanya vows to carry on His head the feet of anyone who cooks so nicely for Krishna. (CC Madhya 3 65)
Nityananda tells Advaita that treating the thrown prasadam as common food is an offence, turning the joke into a lesson. (CC Madhya 3 99)

children.topic: This body belongs to you, mother
children.note: Caitanya assures weeping Saci that He can never repay her and will obey whatever she asks of Him. (CC Madhya 3 145)

children.topic: Let Nimai stay at Jagannatha Puri
children.note: Saci decides Puri is close enough for news and visits while letting her son keep his sannyasa duties. (CC Madhya 3 182)

After sannyasa Caitanya wanders Radha-desa for three days; Nityananda leads Him to Santipura, where Advaita feeds Him, holds nightly kirtan, mother Saci meets Him, and it is agreed He will live at Jagannatha Puri.
In a dream Gopala says He has waited in the bush for Madhavendra and will appear to deliver all fallen souls. (CC Madhya 4 40)

children.topic: Gopala eats yet the food remains
children.note: At the Annakuta the hungry Deity consumes everything offered while by His touch the mountain of food stays intact. (CC Madhya 4 77)

children.topic: Gopinatha stole this sweet rice for you
children.note: The priest searches the marketplace calling for Madhavendra to receive the pot the Deity hid behind His curtain. (CC Madhya 4 133)

children.topic: My body and Gopinatha's are one
children.note: Gopala tells Madhavendra to smear the sandalwood on Gopinatha at Remuna, since anointing Him cools Gopala as well. (CC Madhya 4 160)
Caitanya draws the lesson: a devotee in love serves the Lord in all circumstances without weighing hardship. (CC Madhya 4 186)

children.topic: Master of Mathura, when shall I see You?
children.note: Madhavendra's famous verse of separation, spoken in Radha's mood, which Caitanya cannot finish reciting without collapsing. (CC Madhya 4 197)

At Remuna Caitanya tells Madhavendra Puri's story: Gopala appears to him as a cowherd boy, is dug out at Govardhana and installed with an Annakuta feast, Gopinatha steals sweet rice for him, and he carries sandalwood from Puri.
The young brahmana explains he serves the elder only for Krishna's satisfaction, which enriches his devotion, not for reward. (CC Madhya 5 24)
Torn between his promise and his family's threats, the old man simply asks Gopala to protect his religion and his kin. (CC Madhya 5 47)

children.topic: A silent witness shares the sin
children.note: The young brahmana argues that one who knows the truth yet refuses to testify becomes implicated in the wrong. (CC Madhya 5 90)

children.topic: You are not a statue but Nanda's son
children.note: When Gopala objects that Deities do not walk, the brahmana replies that Krishna Himself can do what was never done. (CC Madhya 5 96)
Gopala agrees to follow the sound of His ankle bells but warns He will stop wherever the brahmana turns to see Him. (CC Madhya 5 98)

children.topic: The breaking of the staff is deep
children.note: Only a devotee fixed on both Lords can grasp why Nityananda broke the danda and why Caitanya seemed angry. (CC Madhya 5 158)

Nityananda narrates Saksi-gopala: an old brahmana promises his daughter to a young one before the Deity, then wavers under family pressure, so Gopala walks from Vrindavana to Vidyanagara to testify. Nityananda later breaks the Lord's staff.
Gopinatha Acarya quotes that a trace of the Lord's favour teaches more than years of studying the Vedas by guesswork. (CC Madhya 6 84)
Caitanya says Vyasa's sutras shine by their direct meaning; imaginative commentary only covers that light. (CC Madhya 6 138)

children.topic: Touchstone makes gold yet stays unchanged
children.note: The Lord manifests the cosmos through His inconceivable potency while His own transcendental form is never transformed. (CC Madhya 6 171)
The atmarama verse: Krishna's attractive qualities draw even liberated souls into loving devotional service. (CC Madhya 6 186)

children.topic: You melted an iron bar of logic
children.note: Sarvabhauma confesses that dry argument had hardened him and that only Caitanya's power could soften his heart. (CC Madhya 6 214)
The former Mayavadi now prefers the word bhakti, since the very sound of liberation evokes fear and dislike. (CC Madhya 6 276)
