Caitanya faints before Jagannatha and is carried to Sarvabhauma's home. Gopinatha Acarya argues the Lord's divinity; after seven days of Vedanta lectures Caitanya refutes Sankara, explains the atmarama verse in eighteen ways and reveals His Krishna form.

children.topic: 7 · The Lord Begins His Tour of South India
Begging leave to tour South India
children.note: Caitanya asks His dearest devotees for one favour: permission to travel south by Himself. (CC Madhya 7 10)

children.topic: Calling their virtues faults to spare them
children.note: The Lord paints His devotees' love as obstacles only so they will stay behind and not suffer on the road. (CC Madhya 7 32)

children.topic: Soft as a flower, hard as thunder
children.note: Great souls seem contradictory: Caitanya walks away from a fainting Sarvabhauma yet loves him deeply. (CC Madhya 7 72)

children.topic: One empowered person converts a village
children.note: Each person the Lord embraces returns home and turns everyone he meets into a chanter of Krishna's name. (CC Madhya 7 101)

children.topic: Stay home, teach Gita and Bhagavatam
children.note: Caitanya tells Kurma not to follow Him but to become a guru at home and free the people of his land. (CC Madhya 7 128)

children.topic: The leper Vasudeva healed by embrace
children.note: The Lord returns to hug the worm-covered brahmana, and his leprosy and misery vanish at His touch. (CC Madhya 7 141)

Caitanya insists on touring South India alone, pretending to seek Visvarupa; Nityananda gets Him to take Krishnadasa. He leaves a grieving Sarvabhauma, converts village after village by embrace, teaches Kurma to preach at home, and heals the leper Vasudeva.

children.topic: 8 · Talks Between Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Rāmānanda Rāya

children.note: Caitanya brushes aside Ramananda's first answer, pushing him past ritual duty toward deeper truths. (CC Madhya 8 59)

children.topic: Pure love costs only intense greed
children.note: Devotion to Krishna cannot be earned by lifetimes of piety; its one price is burning eagerness to have it. (CC Madhya 8 70)

children.topic: Anyone who knows Krishna is guru
children.note: Caste and dress do not matter; whoever truly knows the science of Krishna is qualified to teach. (CC Madhya 8 128)

children.topic: Radha is the essence of ecstatic love
children.note: The innermost part of Krishna's pleasure potency is mahabhava, and that ecstasy is Radharani herself. (CC Madhya 8 160)

children.topic: Enter Radha-Krishna's pastimes through the gopis
children.note: Only by following the gopis' mood of service can one approach the Divine Couple's confidential play. (CC Madhya 8 204-205)
The Lord reveals to Ramananda that He is Krishna clothed in Radha's feelings and golden hue. (CC Madhya 8 282)

On the Godavari bank Caitanya meets Ramananda Raya and questions him for ten nights. Ramananda climbs from duty to surrender to spontaneous love, ending at Radha's love and the gopis' mood. The Lord reveals His Radha-Krishna form and calls him to Puri.

children.topic: 9 · Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu’s Travels to the Holy Places
One Krishna equals three thousand Vishnu names
children.note: The Rama-chanting brahmana explains why Krishna's name pulled him from his lifelong practice. (CC Madhya 9 33)

children.topic: Chant loudly to revive the Buddhist teacher
children.note: Caitanya tells the frightened disciples to chant Krishna's name into their guru's ear, and he awakens. (CC Madhya 9 60)

children.topic: The stammering Gita reader knows its purport
children.note: A brahmana who sees Krishna driving Arjuna's chariot while reading is praised as a true Gita authority. (CC Madhya 9 102)
Though the forms are one in truth, Krishna's conjugal charm gives Him a special superiority. (CC Madhya 9 146)

children.topic: Ravana stole only a shadow Sita
children.note: Caitanya comforts Ramadasa Vipra: material senses cannot touch Sita, so only an illusory form was taken. (CC Madhya 9 192)
To the Tattvavadi acarya, Caitanya says the nine devotional processes, not liberation, are life's goal. (CC Madhya 9 258)

Caitanya sweeps through South India turning Buddhists, Saivites and Tattvavadis into chanters. He debates Venkata Bhatta on Krishna versus Narayana, consoles Ramadasa about Sita, finds the Brahma-samhita and Krishna-karnamrita, and rescues Krishnadasa.

children.topic: 10 · The Lord’s Return to Jagannātha Purī
Saints travel to purify the holy places
children.note: Sarvabhauma tells the king a Vaisnava visits tirthas to cleanse them and reclaim fallen souls. (CC Madhya 10 13)

children.topic: Bhavananda's family: servants birth after birth
children.note: Caitanya accepts Bhavananda Raya's surrender as that of an eternal relative, not an outsider. (CC Madhya 10 58)

children.topic: Svarupa screens all writings for the Lord
children.note: Nothing was recited before Caitanya until Svarupa Damodara had checked it for correct conclusions. (CC Madhya 10 112)

children.topic: Bound by the rope of mercy
children.note: Svarupa confesses he abandoned the Lord, but the Lord dragged him back by the neck with His grace. (CC Madhya 10 125)
Defending Govinda's low birth, Caitanya says loving dealings with God far exceed reverent ones. (CC Madhya 10 140)
Brahmananda Bharati realises his ascetic skin was for prestige and drops it for sannyasi robes. (CC Madhya 10 159)

King Prataparudra asks Sarvabhauma about the Lord and offers Kasi Misra's house. Caitanya returns to Puri, meets the local devotees and Bhavananda Raya, dismisses Krishnadasa, and welcomes Paramananda Puri, Svarupa Damodara, Govinda and Brahmananda Bharati.

children.topic: 11 · The Beḍā-kīrtana Pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu
For a sannyasi a king is poison
children.note: Caitanya covers His ears: meeting a king or a woman is as deadly for a renunciant as drinking poison. (CC Madhya 11 7)

children.topic: The servant's devotee is truly Mine
children.note: Because the king loves Ramananda, Caitanya says Krishna will accept him as His real devotee. (CC Madhya 11 28)

children.topic: The king will die without His mercy
children.note: Prataparudra vows to give up his life if Caitanya will not see him; his resolve moves Sarvabhauma. (CC Madhya 11 48)

children.topic: Chanting is the religion of Kali-yuga
children.note: Sarvabhauma explains that Caitanya came to teach congregational chanting as this age's dharma. (CC Madhya 11 98)
Fasting rules yield when the Lord Himself hands out prasadam; neglecting that gift is a fault. (CC Madhya 11 114)

children.topic: Haridasa outranks any brahmana or sannyasi
children.note: Caitanya tells the humble Haridasa that constant chanting makes him greater than all Vedic scholars. (CC Madhya 11 191)

Caitanya refuses to meet King Prataparudra, calling a king poison; Sarvabhauma plans a Ratha-yatra encounter. Ramananda retires to Puri. Two hundred Bengal devotees arrive, are named to the king from his roof, meet Haridasa, feast, and chant in four parties.

children.topic: 12 · The Cleansing of the Guṇḍicā Temple
Independent yet ruled by devotees' love
children.note: Damodara admits the Lord answers to no one, but affection from His devotees always moves Him. (CC Madhya 12 29)

children.topic: A drop of liquor spoils the milk
children.note: Caitanya says the title 'king' contaminates even a good man, as one drop taints a whole pot of milk. (CC Madhya 12 53)

children.topic: The prince reminds everyone of Krishna
children.note: Seeing the dark, lotus-eyed boy in yellow, the Lord embraces him and he trembles and chants. (CC Madhya 12 61)
After washing every room with a hundred pots, the devotees' hearts feel as spotless as the temple. (CC Madhya 12 105)
Pleased inside, Caitanya scolds the Bengali who drank His foot water inside the temple to set a standard. (CC Madhya 12 124)

children.topic: He turned a crow into Garuda
children.note: Sarvabhauma marvels that the Lord changed him from a barking logician into a chanter of Krishna's names. (CC Madhya 12 182)

The king gets the Lord's old cloth, and his Krishna-like son is embraced. Before Ratha-yatra Caitanya leads hundreds of devotees in washing the Gundica temple, scolds a Bengali who drinks His foot water, revives Gopala, feasts, and gazes at Jagannatha.

children.topic: 13 · The Ecstatic Dancing of the Lord at Ratha-yātrā
Jagannatha moves only by His own will
children.note: Though burly carriers haul the Deity, the narrator says the maintainer of the universe travels purely by His own desire, for the sake of His pastimes. (CC Madhya 13 13)

children.topic: The King's broom wins the Lord's mercy
children.note: By sweeping the road before Jagannatha, the mighty King Prataparudra becomes a fit candidate for the Lord's grace through humble, menial service. (CC Madhya 13 17)

children.topic: Servant of the servant of Krishna
children.note: Caitanya declares He is no brahmana, no sannyasi, nothing but the servant of the servant of the servant of Krishna, the gopis' keeper. (CC Madhya 13 80)

children.topic: Same lover, longing for the Reva bank
children.note: In Radha's mood Caitanya recites a poem of reunion that still aches for Vrindavan; only Svarupa Damodara grasps what He means. (CC Madhya 13 121)
Speaking as Radha, Caitanya tells Krishna that Her mind and Vrindavan are one, so He should place His feet there and grant full mercy. (CC Madhya 13 137)
Krishna assures the gopis that their love is the sole reason He returns, and that devotional service is the only way to reach Him. (CC Madhya 13 160)

Caitanya dances before Jagannatha's chariot at Ratha-yatra: King Prataparudra sweeps the road, seven kirtan parties roar, the Lord shows ecstatic symptoms and, in Radha's mood, recites the Kurukshetra verse begging Krishna to return to Vrindavan.

children.topic: Krishna's words are life for the suffering
children.note: The verse the King recites: narrations of Krishna revive those who suffer, wipe out sin, and those who spread them are the greatest benefactors. (CC Madhya 14 13)
Asked who he is, the King answers only that he wishes to be accepted as the most obedient servant of the Lord's servants. (CC Madhya 14 18)

children.topic: The chariot moves at the Lord's touch
children.note: After wrestlers and elephants fail, Caitanya pushes the car with His head and it rolls forward on its own toward Gundica. (CC Madhya 14 55)

children.topic: Logic is a dry oil cake
children.note: Gopinatha Acarya jokes that Sarvabhauma spent his life chewing the dry cake of logic until the Lord gave him the nectar of Krishna's pastimes. (CC Madhya 14 87)

children.topic: Only the gopis enter Vrindavan pastimes
children.note: Svarupa Damodara explains that Lakshmi is left behind because no one but the gopis can attract Krishna's mind in Vrindavan. (CC Madhya 14 123)
The gopis are super goddesses of fortune, the trees grant wishes, speech is song and walking is dance; hence Vrindavan alone is worth savoring. (CC Madhya 14 227)

King Prataparudra, dressed as a Vaishnava, recites the tava kathamrtam verse and receives Caitanya's embrace; the Lord pushes Jagannatha's stuck chariot with His head, sports in lakes, and at Hera-pancami hears Svarupa Damodara explain the gopis' jealous moods.

children.topic: 15 · The Lord Accepts Prasādam at the House of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya
Give Krishna even to the lowest
children.note: Caitanya asks Advaita Acarya to distribute devotion to Krishna to everyone in Bengal, right down to the outcaste candalas. (CC Madhya 15 41)
Defining a Vaishnava for Satyaraja Khan, the Lord says whoever utters Krishna's name even once is the best of humans and deserves honor. (CC Madhya 15 106)
Mukunda calls his own son Raghunandana his father because the boy gave him devotion; Caitanya confirms this as correct. (CC Madhya 15 117)
Praising Murari Gupta, who refused to switch from Rama to Krishna, Caitanya says a true servant clings to his Lord even when told to leave. (CC Madhya 15 154)

children.topic: Let me suffer for all souls
children.note: Vasudeva Datta begs to take on the sins of every living being and rot in hell so that everyone else can be freed. (CC Madhya 15 163)
Placing His hand on the dying blasphemer's chest, Caitanya tells him to rise and chant Hare Krishna, and Amogha revives and dances. (CC Madhya 15 277)

Caitanya celebrates Janmashtami and Vijaya-dasami, sends the Bengal devotees home with personal instructions, praises Raghava Pandita, Murari Gupta and Vasudeva Datta, then eats at Sarvabhauma's house, where son-in-law Amogha blasphemes and is later forgiven and converted.

children.topic: 16 · The Lord’s Attempt to Go to Vṛndāvana
You are the life, I the body
children.note: Nityananda accepts Caitanya's order to remain in Bengal, saying the two are inseparable like life and body, with life the more important. (CC Madhya 16 66)

children.topic: The best Vaishnava makes others chant
children.note: Caitanya grades devotees: the topmost Vaishnava is one whose very presence inspires others to chant Krishna's name. (CC Madhya 16 74)

children.topic: Seen from afar, one is overwhelmed
children.note: The palace ladies fall into ecstasy just by glimpsing the Lord; no one in the three worlds is as merciful as Caitanya. (CC Madhya 16 121)

children.topic: Why was I born a Muslim?
children.note: The converted governor laments his low birth, wishing he had been born where he could stay near the Lord's feet. (CC Madhya 16 181)
Caitanya tells Raghunatha dasa to go home, stay faithful inside, act like an ordinary man outside, and wait for Krishna's mercy. (CC Madhya 16 238)

children.topic: No one goes to Vrindavan with a parade
children.note: Reflecting on Sanatana's words, the Lord decides that arriving with a huge crowd would look like a magician's show, and resolves to go alone. (CC Madhya 16 272)

Devotees delay Caitanya's Vrindavan trip; Nityananda is ordered to stay in Bengal; the Lord teaches degrees of Vaishnavas, converts a drunken Muslim governor at the Orissa border, meets young Raghunatha dasa, then turns back at Kanai Natasala after Sanatana's hint about crowds.
Touched by the Lord's foot and told to chant Krishna's name, a tiger sleeping on the path rises and dances, chanting. (CC Madhya 17 29)
Seeing tigers and deer walk together, Caitanya recites that in Vrindavan there is no hunger or anger, and natural foes live as friends. (CC Madhya 17 39)
The Lord tells Balabhadra that Krishna used Sanatana's words to steer Him away from the crowds onto the quiet forest road. (CC Madhya 17 74)
Explaining why Mayavadis cannot say 'Krishna', Caitanya teaches that the Lord's name, form and self are absolutely identical. (CC Madhya 17 131)
Accepting food from the Sanodiya brahmana, the Lord says scriptures disagree, so the behavior of a pure devotee like Madhavendra Puri sets the standard. (CC Madhya 17 185)

children.topic: Love multiplies a hundred thousand times
children.note: The narrator measures the Lord's ecstasy: a thousandfold at Mathura, a hundred-thousandfold once He walks in Vrindavan's forests. (CC Madhya 17 227)

Caitanya slips away from Puri with Balabhadra Bhattacarya, makes tigers, elephants and deer chant and dance in the Jharikhanda forest, stays with Tapana Misra in Kashi where Prakasananda mocks Him, and reaches Mathura and Vrindavan, where cows, deer, parrots and trees greet Him.

children.topic: 18 · Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu’s Visit to Śrī Vṛndāvana

children.note: Praying at Radha-kunda, the Lord says Krishna grants love like Radha's to anyone who bathes there even once in a lifetime. (CC Madhya 18 10)
Because Caitanya, thinking Himself a devotee, will not climb Govardhan, Gopala arranges a pretext to come down and meet Him. (CC Madhya 18 25)
Dancing at the hill, the Lord recites how Govardhan serves Krishna and Balarama with water, grass, caves and fruit, and glows from Their touch. (CC Madhya 18 34)

children.topic: A jiva can never be Krishna
children.note: When people call Him God, Caitanya cries 'Vishnu! Vishnu!' and insists no living being ever becomes the Supreme Lord. (CC Madhya 18 111)

children.topic: The spark is not the flame
children.note: The Lord compares the soul to a spark and God to the fire: a fragment can never equal the original whole. (CC Madhya 18 113)

children.topic: The Koran ends in a personal God
children.note: Debating the Muslim saint, Caitanya argues that the Koran raises impersonalism only to reject it and establish a personal Lord and devotion. (CC Madhya 18 189)

Caitanya rediscovers Radha-kunda in a paddy field, refuses to climb Govardhan so Gopala comes down to Him, tours the twelve forests, exposes a fisherman's torch mistaken for Krishna at Kaliya lake, and converts Pathan soldiers by debating the Koran before leaving for Prayag.

children.topic: 19 · Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Instructs Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī
The pure devotee outranks the scholar
children.note: Krishna says caste and learning count for nothing; a pure devotee even from a low family is as worshipable as He is. (CC Madhya 19 50)

children.topic: The lucky soul gets the bhakti seed
children.note: Among countless wandering souls, one fortunate person meets a real guru and receives the seed of devotion by Krishna's grace. (CC Madhya 19 151)

children.topic: Water the seed by hearing and chanting
children.note: The devotee becomes a gardener, planting the seed in the heart and watering it daily with hearing and chanting until it sprouts. (CC Madhya 19 152)
An offense against a Vaishnava is like a rampaging elephant that tears up the creeper and dries its leaves. (CC Madhya 19 156)
Top-class devotion is free of material desire, monistic knowledge and fruitive motive, and serves Krishna favorably as He wishes. (CC Madhya 19 167)
Devotees relate to Krishna in five chief moods: neutrality, service, friendship, parental love and conjugal love. (CC Madhya 19 185)

Rupa and Anupama give up their wealth and meet Caitanya at Prayaga, where Vallabha Bhatta hosts Him. At Dasasvamedha-ghata the Lord teaches Rupa the bhakti creeper, the rare pure devotee, and the five rasas, then sends him to Vrindavan.

children.topic: 20 · Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Instructs Sanātana Gosvāmī in the Science of the Absolute Truth
Who am I, why do I suffer?
children.note: Sanatana's humble question opens the whole teaching: he asks his real identity and why the threefold miseries keep tormenting him. (CC Madhya 20 102)

children.topic: The soul is Krishna's eternal servant
children.note: The living being is Krishna's marginal energy, one with Him yet different, like a spark of fire, and by nature His servant. (CC Madhya 20 108-109)
Having turned to the external energy since time immemorial, the soul is beaten by maya with every kind of suffering. (CC Madhya 20 117)
Scripture gives the relationship with Krishna, the practice that follows from it, and the goal of returning home to Godhead. (CC Madhya 20 124)

children.topic: Three principal forms of the Lord
children.note: Krishna appears as His own original form, expansions of that same self, and living beings He invests with His power. (CC Madhya 20 165)
In this age Krishna comes in a golden hue with His companions and starts congregational chanting to give people love of God. (CC Madhya 20 340)

Sanatana bribes his way out of prison, escapes to Varanasi and trades his blanket for a torn quilt. Caitanya then teaches him the soul's identity, Krishna's energies, the three tattvas, the avataras, Maha-Vishnu, the yuga incarnations and Kali's golden avatar.

children.topic: 21 · The Opulence and Sweetness of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa

children.note: Brahma admits Krishna's opulences lie completely beyond his body, mind and words, whatever others may boast about knowing. (CC Madhya 21 27)

children.topic: Which Brahma is at the door?
children.note: When Brahma comes to Dvaraka, Krishna asks the doorman which Brahma has arrived, startling the four-headed creator. (CC Madhya 21 60)
Seeing Brahmas with millions of heads bow to Krishna, this universe's Brahma feels tiny and humbled. (CC Madhya 21 69)

children.topic: The cowherd boy is the supreme form
children.note: Of all Krishna's pastimes, His humanlike form as a young flute-playing dancer from Vraja is the highest and sweetest. (CC Madhya 21 101)
Krishna's body beautifies the jewels He wears, and His sidelong glances pierce the hearts of Radha and the gopis like arrows. (CC Madhya 21 105)

children.topic: Sweet body, sweeter face, sweetest smile
children.note: Krishna's form is sweet, His face sweeter, and His honey-scented soft smile is the sweetest of all. (CC Madhya 21 136)

Caitanya tells Sanatana of the measureless Vaikuntha planets and Krishna's unlimited qualities, retells Brahma meeting countless other Brahmas at Dvaraka, and then, lost in ecstasy, describes Krishna's beauty, smile and flute that steal the gopis' hearts.

children.topic: Krishna is sunlight, maya is darkness
children.note: Illusion cannot stand where Krishna consciousness shines, just as darkness vanishes before the sun. (CC Madhya 22 31)

children.topic: A moment with a devotee brings success
children.note: All scriptures agree that even a brief association with a pure devotee can give a person every perfection. (CC Madhya 22 54)

children.topic: Think of Me, become My devotee
children.note: Krishna's most confidential promise to Arjuna: always remember Him, worship Him and bow to Him, and you will surely reach Him. (CC Madhya 22 57-58)
Accept the favorable, reject the unfavorable, trust Krishna's protection, take Him as master, give yourself fully and stay humble. (CC Madhya 22 100)
Associate with devotees, chant the holy name, hear the Bhagavatam, live in Mathura and worship the Deity with faith. (CC Madhya 22 128)
Spontaneous loving service means following Krishna's dear Vraja associates and serving Him constantly within the mind. (CC Madhya 22 159)

Caitanya explains abhidheya to Sanatana: souls are liberated or conditioned, only bhakti frees them, and it comes through devotee association, surrender and a guru. He lists sixty-four practices, the five most potent, then spontaneous raganuga bhakti.

children.topic: 23 · Life’s Ultimate Goal — Love of Godhead

children.note: The journey begins when a fortunate soul develops faith in Krishna and starts keeping the company of devotees. (CC Madhya 23 9)

children.topic: Nine steps from faith to prema
children.note: Faith, association, initiation, freedom from bad habits, steadiness, taste, attachment, emotion and finally love: the ladder of bhakti. (CC Madhya 23 14-15)
Forgiveness, not wasting time, detachment, humility, hope, eagerness, relish for chanting, love of Krishna's qualities and of His places. (CC Madhya 23 18-19)
Though claiming no love, qualification or pedigree, the devotee clings to a painful, unshakable hope in Krishna's mercy for the fallen. (CC Madhya 23 29)
Radharani is Krishna's direct feminine counterpart, the source of all goddesses of fortune, who alone attracts the all-attractive Lord. (CC Madhya 23 68)
Caitanya commissions Sanatana to spread devotional scriptures and rediscover the lost holy places of the Mathura district. (CC Madhya 23 103)

Caitanya teaches Sanatana the goal, prema: faith grows through devotee association, practice, taste and attachment into love of God, shown by nine signs. He covers the rasas, Krishna's 64 and Radha's 25 qualities, then tells Sanatana to write and restore Vrindavan.

children.topic: 24 · The Sixty-One Explanations of the Ātmārāma Verse

children.note: Even sages fully satisfied in the self are drawn to serve Krishna, because His qualities pull everyone toward Him. (CC Madhya 24 5)
Pure devotion is so sweet that material pleasure, liberation and yogic powers all fade from the devotee's memory. (CC Madhya 24 39)

children.topic: Other paths are like a goat's neck nipples
children.note: Without devotion, every other method of self-realization is useless decoration; the wise choose bhakti alone. (CC Madhya 24 93)
Those who think themselves liberated but neglect the Lord's feet slip from their hard-won Brahman position. (CC Madhya 24 131)
Devotee association, serving Krishna, hearing Bhagavatam, chanting the holy name and living in Vraja awaken dormant love. (CC Madhya 24 193)
Narada tells the reformed hunter that gentleness is no surprise, since those serving the Lord never wish to hurt others. (CC Madhya 24 273)

At Sanatana's request, Caitanya unpacks the atmarama verse word by word into sixty-one meanings, all pointing to Krishna's service, tells how Narada turned the hunter Mrgari into a devotee, and outlines the Vaishnava rulebook Sanatana should write.

children.topic: 25 · How All the Residents of Vārāṇasī Became Vaiṣṇavas
Follow the mahajanas, not dry philosophy
children.note: Prakasananda admits the six philosophical systems cannot reach the Absolute; one must walk the path of the great authorities. (CC Madhya 25 56)

children.topic: Need the dust of great souls' feet
children.note: Until people accept the feet of selfless mahatmas, their attention cannot turn to Krishna, who ends material misery. (CC Madhya 25 85)
Caitanya concludes that Vyasa's own commentary on Vedanta is the Bhagavatam, whose meaning matches the Upanishads. (CC Madhya 25 100)
In every land, time and circumstance, one's duty is to find a bona fide spiritual master and inquire about devotional service. (CC Madhya 25 122)
Caitanya's parting advice to Prakasananda: constant Bhagavatam discussion and chanting bring easy liberation and love of God. (CC Madhya 25 154)

children.topic: Let your mind swim like a swan
children.note: Krishnadasa invites readers to treat Caitanya's pastimes as an eternal lake of nectar and let the mind play there. (CC Madhya 25 271)

Prakasananda's disciple and then Prakasananda himself accept Caitanya, who shows that the Bhagavatam is Vyasa's own Vedanta commentary; Varanasi turns to chanting, the Lord returns to Puri, and Krishnadasa reviews the whole Madhya-lila.
Madhya-lila: sannyasa, Jagannatha Puri, South India, the teachings to Sarvabhauma, Ramananda Raya, Rupa and Sanatana, the Ratha-yatra.

children.topic: 1 · Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī’s Second Meeting with the Lord

children.note: Caitanya has a dog chant Hare Krishna and it goes to Vaikuntha, showing the holy name saves any creature. (CC Antya 1 33)

children.topic: Never take Krishna out of Vrindavana
children.note: Caitanya instructs Rupa that the son of Nanda never leaves Vraja, so the Vrindavana and Dvaraka pastimes need separate plays. (CC Antya 1 66)

children.topic: How did you know My heart?
children.note: Reading Rupa's verse on Radha at Kurukshetra, the Lord embraces him for grasping His most confidential mood. (CC Antya 1 84)

children.topic: Nectar of the two syllables Krish-na
children.note: Rupa's verse says chanting the name makes one crave countless mouths and ears, and hearing it makes one long for endless senses. (CC Antya 1 99)

children.topic: Ashamed to hear His own praise
children.note: Caitanya objects to Rupa's verse glorifying Him as alkali in nectar; Ramananda calls it a pinch of camphor instead. (CC Antya 1 181)

children.topic: Preach and excavate lost holy places
children.note: The Lord sends Rupa to Vrindavana to write devotional literature, uncover forgotten sites and establish Krishna's service. (CC Antya 1 218)

Sivananda Sena's dog chants Krishna's name before Caitanya; Rupa Gosvami reaches Puri, is told to split his drama and keep Krishna in Vrindavana, and amazes Ramananda and the devotees with verses from his two plays before being sent back to Vraja.

children.topic: Three ways the Lord delivers souls
children.note: Caitanya frees people by meeting them directly, by empowering pure devotees, and by appearing before them Himself. (CC Antya 2 4)
Wherever pure devotion exists, Gaurasundara is conquered by it and shows Himself to His devotees. (CC Antya 2 81)

children.topic: Mayavada's word jugglery bends even devotees
children.note: Svarupa Damodara warns that reading Sankara's commentary can shake a devotee who has made Krishna his life. (CC Antya 2 96)

children.topic: A renunciant must avoid intimacy with women
children.note: Caitanya cannot bear to see a sannyasi who chats familiarly with a woman, and so bans Junior Haridasa. (CC Antya 2 117)

children.topic: Even a wooden woman attracts a sage
children.note: The senses cling so strongly to their objects that even a statue can capture the mind of a great saint. (CC Antya 2 118)
Krishnadasa notes the episode teaches renunciant discipline, the glories of holy places and how the Lord accepts a faithful devotee. (CC Antya 2 169)

Caitanya delivers people by entering Nakula Brahmacari and appearing to eat Nrsimhananda's offerings, then bans Junior Haridasa for begging rice from a woman; after a year of rejection Haridasa drowns himself at Prayaga and sings for the Lord in a spiritual body.

children.topic: 3 · The Glories of Śrīla Haridāsa Ṭhākura
Yavanas saved by saying ha rama
children.note: Haridasa assures the Lord that even the Muslims' habitual cry of Rama's name is a shadow of chanting that liberates them. (CC Antya 3 53)

children.topic: The name works even uttered improperly
children.note: Once the holy name touches the tongue, mind or ear, it frees one from bondage regardless of correct pronunciation or intent. (CC Antya 3 60)

children.topic: I stayed three days to deliver you
children.note: Haridasa tells the reformed prostitute he knew Ramacandra Khan's plot but remained only to save her. (CC Antya 3 134)

children.topic: The real fruit is love, not liberation
children.note: Haridasa corrects the scholars: freedom from sin and liberation are side effects; offenseless chanting awakens love for Krishna. (CC Antya 3 178)
A pure devotee overlooks insults, but the Lord Himself cannot tolerate blasphemy of His devotee, as Gopala Cakravarti learns. (CC Antya 3 213)

children.topic: Rama's name liberates, Krishna's gives love
children.note: Maya confesses that Rama's name grants liberation, while Krishna's name carries one across nescience into ecstatic love. (CC Antya 3 257)

Caitanya sends the strict Damodara Pandita to guard mother Saci, then hears Haridasa Thakura explain how namabhasa saves even yavanas and all beings; Haridasa converts a prostitute sent by Ramacandra Khan, wins a debate on the holy name, and is tested by Maya herself, who begs for Krishna's name.

children.topic: 4 · Sanātana Gosvāmī Visits the Lord at Jagannātha Purī
Krishna is reached by bhakti, not suicide
children.note: Caitanya tells Sanatana that throwing away the body wins nothing; devotional service is the only road to Krishna. (CC Antya 4 56)

children.topic: Low birth is no bar to bhakti
children.note: Neither humble nor aristocratic birth decides fitness for devotion; only the practice itself matters. (CC Antya 4 66)

children.topic: Chanting is chief of the nine
children.note: Among the nine limbs of bhakti, constant offenseless chanting most easily yields love of God. (CC Antya 4 71)

children.topic: Your body is My property now
children.note: Caitanya argues a surrendered devotee has no right to destroy a body that belongs to the Lord. (CC Antya 4 76)
Even a purifier of the universe should guard Vaishnava etiquette; Caitanya prizes Sanatana for walking the hot sand. (CC Antya 4 129-130)

children.topic: A mother never hates her child's mess
children.note: Caitanya likens Sanatana's oozing sores to a child's soiling, which a loving parent cleans without disgust. (CC Antya 4 186)

Sanatana arrives at Puri with oozing sores, planning to die under Jagannatha's cart; Caitanya embraces him anyway, forbids suicide, claims his body as His own tool for Vrindavan, praises his etiquette, and finally heals him with a hug.

children.topic: 5 · How Pradyumna Miśra Received Instructions from Rāmānanda Rāya
Duty without taste for Krishna is wasted
children.note: Performing varnashrama duties yet never relishing hearing and chanting about Krishna is fruitless labor. (CC Antya 5 10)

children.topic: Even a sannyasi is moved by women
children.note: Caitanya admits a woman's mere name stirs Him, to highlight how extraordinary Ramananda's steadiness is. (CC Antya 5 35-36)
One who faithfully hears Krishna's pastimes with the gopis quickly loses material desire, the heart's disease. (CC Antya 5 48)

children.topic: I am only the Lord's instrument
children.note: Ramananda says Caitanya speaks through him like a musician plays a stringed instrument. (CC Antya 5 73)
Caitanya humbles proud scholars and renunciants by teaching religion through a so-called sudra householder. (CC Antya 5 84)

children.topic: God's body and self are one
children.note: Svarupa Damodara insists the Lord's form and identity are both spiritual bliss; separating them is a grave offense. (CC Antya 5 122)

Caitanya sends Pradyumna Misra to hear about Krishna from Ramananda Raya, whose training of temple dancers shows a mind untouched by lust. Later Svarupa Damodara corrects a Bengali poet who called Jagannatha a body and Caitanya its soul.

children.topic: 6 · The Meeting of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī
Feed My men yogurt and chipped rice
children.note: Nityananda 'punishes' Raghunatha by ordering the famous Panihati festival, which Caitanya secretly attends. (CC Antya 6 51)

children.topic: Krishna's mercy pulled you from the ditch
children.note: Caitanya greets the arriving Raghunatha, crediting Krishna's mercy for lifting him out of materialistic life. (CC Antya 6 193)

children.topic: A renunciant must not depend on others
children.note: Caitanya approves Raghunatha's begging, saying a vairagi who leans on patrons loses Krishna's favor. (CC Antya 6 224)

children.topic: Don't talk, eat or dress like others
children.note: The Lord's brief code for Raghunatha: avoid worldly talk, rich food and fine clothes. (CC Antya 6 236)

children.topic: Chant and serve Radha-Krishna in mind
children.note: Expect no honor, respect everyone, always chant, and mentally serve the divine couple in Vrindavan. (CC Antya 6 237)

children.topic: This stone is Krishna's own form
children.note: Caitanya hands over the Govardhana sila, telling Raghunatha to worship it with simple water and tulasi. (CC Antya 6 294)

Raghunatha dasa escapes wealthy family life: Nityananda makes him host the chipped-rice feast at Panihati, he slips away to Puri, and Caitanya entrusts him to Svarupa Damodara, teaches strict renunciation, and gives him a Govardhana stone.

children.topic: 7 · The Meeting of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Vallabha Bhaṭṭa
I learned bhakti only from devotees
children.note: Caitanya calls Himself a Mayavadi sannyasi who learned devotion from Advaita, Nityananda, Ramananda and others. (CC Antya 7 16)

children.topic: Krishna is won by spontaneous love
children.note: Yasoda's son is reached by loving service, not by speculation, austerity or bodily identification. (CC Antya 7 27)
Asked to hear many meanings of the holy name, Caitanya says He knows only two and needs no more. (CC Antya 7 85)

children.topic: A chaste wife obeys her husband's order
children.note: Vallabha says wives shouldn't utter the husband's name; Caitanya replies Krishna's order is to chant it. (CC Antya 7 107)

children.topic: Sridhara Svami is guru of the world
children.note: Caitanya honors Sridhara's Bhagavatam commentary and warns that writing to surpass it is false pride. (CC Antya 7 133)
Caitanya tells Gadadhara that his silent tolerance of apparent neglect has won the Lord completely. (CC Antya 7 162)

The scholar Vallabha Bhatta visits Puri. Caitanya humbly credits His devotees for everything He knows, refuses to hear Vallabha's proud commentary, and defends Sridhara Svami until Vallabha's pride breaks and he surrenders; Gadadhara's patience is tested too.
Told to stop crying and remember Brahman, the dying Madhavendra drives Ramacandra Puri away as a rascal. (CC Antya 8 22)

children.topic: One blessed, one cursed by guru
children.note: Isvara Puri became an ocean of love while Ramacandra Puri became a dry critic; the guru's mood decides fate. (CC Antya 8 31)

children.topic: O master of Mathura, when again?
children.note: Madhavendra's dying verse of separation from Krishna is the seed of love that grew into Caitanya's mission. (CC Antya 8 34)

children.topic: Only a quarter pot of prasadam
children.note: Stung by the ant accusation, Caitanya orders Govinda to cut His food to a fraction of the usual. (CC Antya 8 53)

children.topic: A critic ignores a hundred virtues
children.note: Paramananda Puri explains that fault-finders overlook countless good qualities to hunt for one flaw. (CC Antya 8 81)

children.topic: Rejected by guru, one offends God
children.note: The author's lesson: a disciple cast off by his spiritual master can sink to offending even the Lord. (CC Antya 8 99)

Ramacandra Puri, once rebuked by his guru Madhavendra Puri, comes to Puri and faults everyone's eating, even accusing Caitanya over ants. The Lord halves His meals, the devotees starve in sympathy, and peace returns only when the critic leaves.

children.topic: Pay the king, then spend the rest
children.note: Caitanya sides with the king, saying a sensible servant clears government dues before spending anything. (CC Antya 9 33)

children.topic: Pray to Jagannatha, not to Me
children.note: Calling Himself a mere beggar, Caitanya tells the devotees to petition Lord Jagannatha for Gopinatha. (CC Antya 9 43)

children.topic: Serving God for money is foolishness
children.note: Kasi Misra says worship meant to please the Lord awakens love, while worship for material gain is stupid. (CC Antya 9 69)
Prataparudra values a moment with Caitanya above millions of gems and cancels Gopinatha's entire debt. (CC Antya 9 96)

children.topic: Wealth is only a glimpse of mercy
children.note: Restored and honored, Gopinatha says flickering fortune is not the real fruit of remembering the Lord's feet. (CC Antya 9 137)
Caitanya's single order to the five brothers: pay the treasury first, and waste nothing on sin. (CC Antya 9 142)

Gopinatha Pattanayaka, Ramananda's brother, is set to be executed for unpaid revenue. Caitanya refuses to intervene and even threatens to leave Puri, yet Kasi Misra's hints lead King Prataparudra to forgive the debt and double Gopinatha's salary.

children.topic: 10 · Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Accepts Prasādam from His Devotees
Breaking an order out of love pleases most
children.note: Nityananda defies the Lord's order to stay in Bengal; such loving disobedience delights Krishna far more than obedience. (CC Antya 10 8)
Caitanya relishes Damayanti's plain bitter leaves because He accepts the affection behind the gift. (CC Antya 10 18)

children.topic: Let my head fall at Jagannatha's feet
children.note: One Oriya line sung by Svarupa Damodara sends Caitanya into hours of ecstatic dancing. (CC Antya 10 68)

children.topic: Offend for service, never for self
children.note: Govinda reasons that countless offenses in the Lord's service are fine, but even one for his own sake is fearful. (CC Antya 10 96)
Stored offerings from many devotees remain unspoiled and Caitanya eats enough for a hundred people. (CC Antya 10 125-126)
Young Caitanya dasa serves simple yogurt, lime and ginger, and the Lord is happier than with a lavish feast. (CC Antya 10 150)

The Bengal devotees return with Raghava Pandita's bags of Damayanti's pickles and sweets. Caitanya dances wildly at the Jagannatha temple, Govinda climbs over the sleeping Lord to serve Him, and the Lord eats a month of stored offerings in one sitting.

children.topic: You may reduce your rounds now
children.note: Caitanya suggests the elderly liberated Haridasa can chant less, but Haridasa treats his vow as life itself. (CC Antya 11 24)

children.topic: Let me go before You do
children.note: Haridasa's one wish: to die in the Lord's presence rather than witness the close of His pastimes. (CC Antya 11 32)
Eyes fixed on the Lord's face, feet on his heart, Haridasa leaves his body by his own will. (CC Antya 11 56)

children.topic: The Lord dances with Haridasa's body
children.note: Overwhelmed, Caitanya lifts the corpse onto His lap and dances in the courtyard. (CC Antya 11 59)

children.topic: Blessing for all who joined the festival
children.note: Anyone who saw, chanted, offered sand or ate at Haridasa's farewell will soon gain Krishna's favor. (CC Antya 11 91-93)

children.topic: World has lost its crown jewel
children.note: Caitanya declares that without Haridasa the world is stripped of its most precious ornament. (CC Antya 11 97)

Aging Haridasa Thakura asks to leave his body before the Lord's pastimes end. Amid kirtan, gazing at Caitanya's face and chanting His name, he departs; Caitanya dances with the body, buries it by the sea, begs prasadam and holds a festival.

children.topic: 12 · The Loving Dealings Between Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Jagadānanda Paṇḍita

children.note: Sivananda thanks Nityananda for the kick, saying the dust of those feet has made his whole life successful. (CC Antya 12 28)

children.topic: Nityananda's anger works for one's good
children.note: The author notes the Lord's contradictory nature: when He kicks someone in anger, it benefits them. (CC Antya 12 33)

children.topic: My body is now your property
children.note: Unable to repay the devotees' yearly journeys, Caitanya surrenders His own body for them to sell as they like. (CC Antya 12 74)

children.topic: Perfumed oil would shame a sannyasi
children.note: Caitanya fears passersby would take a scented head as the sign of a tantric sannyasi who keeps women. (CC Antya 12 114)
Denying he ever brought oil, Jagadananda hurls the pot down in the courtyard and locks himself in his room. (CC Antya 12 119)

children.topic: Even cooked in anger, it is delicious
children.note: Eating Jagadananda's lunch, Caitanya says Krishna makes his food nectar because Krishna Himself will eat it. (CC Antya 12 131)

Nityananda kicks Sivananda Sena, who counts it a blessing; Caitanya tearfully offers His body to the departing Bengal devotees; and Jagadananda smashes his gift of sandalwood oil when the Lord refuses it, then cooks a lunch that ends the quarrel.

children.topic: 13 · Pastimes with Jagadānanda Paṇḍita and Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī
A renunciant sleeps on the floor
children.note: Caitanya rejects Jagadananda's quilt and pillow, saying bedding would disgrace one in the renounced order. (CC Antya 13 15)

children.topic: Respect Vrindavan residents from a distance
children.note: The Lord warns Jagadananda not to mix freely with Mathura locals, whose practices differ from his own path. (CC Antya 13 37)
Sanatana wore another sannyasi's cloth only to witness Jagadananda's fierce exclusive love for Caitanya. (CC Antya 13 60)
Halted a step from a woman singer, Caitanya says touching her body would have killed Him. (CC Antya 13 85)
Caitanya forbids Raghunatha Bhatta to marry and sends him home to serve his parents and learn from a realized Vaishnava. (CC Antya 13 113)
Raghunatha Bhatta refuses to listen to any fault-finding, seeing everyone as engaged in Krishna's service. (CC Antya 13 133)

Jagadananda's quilt is refused, so he goes to Vrindavan, nearly beats Sanatana over a stranger's cloth, and returns with gifts. Caitanya chases a devadasi's Gita-govinda song until Govinda stops Him. Raghunatha Bhatta serves the Lord and is sent to Vrindavan.

children.topic: 14 · Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu’s Feelings of Separation from Kṛṣṇa
His mood mirrors the grieving gopis
children.note: Caitanya's condition in separation matches exactly what the gopis of Vrindavana felt once Krishna left for Mathura. (CC Antya 14 12)

children.topic: Envying a woman's eagerness for Jagannatha
children.note: Caitanya calls the woman who stepped on His shoulder fortunate and begs her to share her intense hunger to see the Lord. (CC Antya 14 30)

children.topic: My mind became a wandering yogi
children.note: Having found and lost Krishna, Caitanya says His mind abandoned body and home to wander Vrindavana as a mendicant with His senses as disciples. (CC Antya 14 41)
Separation from Krishna brings anxiety, sleeplessness, agitation, thinness, dirtiness, raving, disease, madness, illusion and death. (CC Antya 14 53)
Found unconscious by the gate, Caitanya's limbs are elongated and every joint separated by inches, held together only by skin. (CC Antya 14 65-66)
Running toward the sand dune, Caitanya recites the gopis' praise of Govardhana Hill, which supplies Krishna and His friends with everything they need. (CC Antya 14 86)

Caitanya's separation-madness begins: He dreams of the rasa dance, praises an eager Orissan woman at the temple, calls His mind a begging yogi, collapses at the Simha-dvara with joints pulled apart, then races toward Cataka-parvata as if it were Govardhana.

children.topic: 15 · The Transcendental Madness of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu
Bodily duties turn like a potter's wheel
children.note: Though always absorbed inside, Caitanya's bathing, temple visits and meals continued automatically, like a wheel spinning without the potter's hand. (CC Antya 15 6)

children.topic: One mind, five senses, five directions
children.note: Caitanya compares His mind to a single horse that five sense-riders each drag a different way until it must die. (CC Antya 15 17)

children.topic: The senses are not to blame
children.note: Told to control His senses, Caitanya replies that Krishna's beauty, sound, touch, scent and taste are irresistible by nature, so the fault is not theirs. (CC Antya 15 18)

children.topic: Asking the trees where Krishna went
children.note: In the gopis' mood Caitanya begs the mango, kadamba and other Yamuna-bank trees to reveal Krishna's whereabouts before the searchers die. (CC Antya 15 32)

children.topic: The noose of Krishna's smiling face
children.note: Caitanya explains that Krishna traps the doe-like gopis with His face and baits them with a smile until they abandon home and honor to serve Him. (CC Antya 15 71)

children.topic: Why Krishna vanished from the rasa dance
children.note: Krishna disappeared to curb the gopis' pride in their fortune and to show them a deeper favor. (CC Antya 15 81)

Seeing Jagannatha as Krishna, Caitanya's five senses are pulled in five directions like a horse ridden by five riders. He then mistakes a seaside garden for Vrindavana and, in the gopis' mood, questions trees, creepers and deer about where Krishna has gone.

children.topic: 16 · Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Tastes Nectar from the Lips of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa
A dog-eater devotee outranks a scholar
children.note: Krishna says a pure devotee born in the lowest family is dearer to Him than a learned non-devotee and deserves worship like Himself. (CC Antya 16 25)
Caitanya's daily prayer: wherever He looks, inside or outside, He sees Lord Nrisimha and takes shelter of Him. (CC Antya 16 53)

children.topic: Three powerful substances of a devotee
children.note: A Vaishnava's foot-dust, foot-water and food remnants are named as three things that grant love of Krishna. (CC Antya 16 60)
Asked to recite, the seven-year-old praises Krishna as a lotus for the ears, ointment for the eyes and a jewel necklace for the chest. (CC Antya 16 74)
Raghunatha dasa's verse recalls Caitanya madly demanding the gatekeeper lead Him to the Lord of His heart. (CC Antya 16 87)

children.topic: Ordinary spices made nectar by Krishna's lips
children.note: Caitanya reasons that familiar ingredients taste and smell extraordinary only because Krishna's lips have touched them. (CC Antya 16 112)

Kalidasa, who licks the food remnants of every Vaishnava in Bengal even Jhadu Thakura's, receives Caitanya's foot-water and prasadam. Seven-year-old Puri dasa composes a verse, a doorkeeper shows Caitanya Krishna, and the Lord relishes prasadam touched by Krishna's lips.

children.topic: 17 · The Bodily Transformations of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu

children.note: Lying unconscious among the cows, Caitanya's arms and legs retract into His trunk while foam and tears flow. (CC Antya 17 16)

children.topic: What woman could resist the flute?
children.note: The gopis ask Krishna which woman in the three worlds could keep her chastity after hearing His flute, when even cows and trees are stunned. (CC Antya 17 31)

children.topic: Flute, words and ornaments kill the gopis
children.note: The gopis complain that the nectar of Krishna's flute, speech and tinkling jewelry together seize their ears, minds and lives. (CC Antya 17 38)

children.topic: Four sounds that give ears their purpose
children.note: Caitanya says only the most fortunate hear Krishna's words, ankle bells, voice and flute; other ears are like useless holed shells. (CC Antya 17 48)
In Radha's mood Caitanya tries to stop talking of Krishna, yet He lies in the heart like Cupid and cannot be forgotten. (CC Antya 17 51)

children.topic: Worship Caitanya to gain love of Krishna
children.note: The author urges everyone to worship Caitanya's feet, the one way to reach the treasure of ecstatic love for Krishna. (CC Antya 17 69)

Hearing Krishna's flute, Caitanya passes through locked doors and is found among Tailanga cows, His limbs drawn in like a tortoise. Revived by chanting, He explains the gopis' 'ka stry anga te' verse and a Krishna-karnamrita verse on the ear's thirst for Krishna's sound.

children.topic: 18 · Rescuing the Lord from the Sea
Krishna becomes a devotee to taste love
children.note: Because even Krishna cannot gauge His devotees' ecstatic emotions, He takes the role of a devotee to experience them fully. (CC Antya 18 16-17)

children.topic: Love, Krishna and devotee dance together
children.note: Ecstatic love makes Krishna and His devotees dance and dances itself, so all three dance in one place. (CC Antya 18 18)

children.topic: Leaping into the sea as the Yamuna
children.note: Seeing moonlit waves shine like the Yamuna, Caitanya runs and plunges into the ocean unnoticed. (CC Antya 18 28)
The fisherman reports catching a long, slack-jointed body he takes for a ghost that has possessed him. (CC Antya 18 47)
Svarupa explains that touching Caitanya stirred the fisherman's dormant love for Krishna, though fear made him think it a ghost. (CC Antya 18 66)

children.topic: Gopis with thousands of eyes and hands
children.note: In the water fight the gopis seem to see, approach, kiss and embrace Krishna with thousands of eyes, legs, faces and bodies. (CC Antya 18 88)

On an autumn full-moon night Caitanya mistakes the sea for the Yamuna and jumps in. A fisherman nets His elongated body, thinks it a ghost, and is calmed by Svarupa Damodara. Revived, Caitanya narrates Krishna and the gopis' water sports and forest picnic.

children.topic: 19 · The Inconceivable Behavior of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu
A sannyasi still depends on his mother
children.note: Caitanya asks Saci not to take offense at His renunciation, saying He remains entirely dependent on her. (CC Antya 19 10)

children.topic: Advaita's riddle: rice no longer sells
children.note: Advaita's cryptic message says everyone has gone mad in love and the market for rice has collapsed, a hint understood only by Caitanya. (CC Antya 19 20)

children.topic: Where is the moon of Nanda's dynasty?
children.note: In Radha's voice Caitanya asks Visakha where the peacock-crowned, flute-playing Krishna has gone and curses Providence. (CC Antya 19 35)
Caitanya quotes the gopis rebuking Providence for uniting lovers and then parting them like a child's cruel prank. (CC Antya 19 45)

children.topic: Face bloodied searching for the door
children.note: Caitanya explains He could not find the exit and kept striking the walls with His face until it bled. (CC Antya 19 64)
Krishna is likened to a perfume seller whose free fragrances blind His female customers so they cannot find the way home. (CC Antya 19 98)

Caitanya sends Jagadananda to console mother Saci and receives Advaita's cryptic sonnet, after which His separation doubles. He blames Providence like Radha, rubs His face bloody on the Gambhira walls, and in the Jagannatha-vallabha garden chases Krishna's fragrance.
The first Siksastaka verse praises the holy name for polishing the heart, quenching material fire and giving nectar at every step. (CC Antya 20 12)

children.topic: All power in the name, no attachment in me
children.note: Krishna has invested full potency in His many names with no rules for chanting, yet Caitanya laments His own lack of taste for them. (CC Antya 20 16)

children.topic: Lower than grass, tolerant as a tree
children.note: One who feels humbler than grass, tolerates like a tree and honors others without seeking honor can chant constantly. (CC Antya 20 21)

children.topic: No wealth, followers or wife, only service
children.note: Caitanya asks Krishna for nothing but unmotivated devotional service, birth after birth. (CC Antya 20 29)

children.topic: Your eternal servant, drowning in ignorance
children.note: Caitanya prays as a fallen servant of Nanda's son to be counted as a dust particle at Krishna's feet. (CC Antya 20 32)

children.topic: Embrace Me or trample Me, still My Lord
children.note: Radha's mood: whether Krishna holds her or breaks her heart by staying away, the debauchee alone remains the Lord of her heart. (CC Antya 20 47)

Caitanya recites and explains His own eight Siksastaka verses to Svarupa Damodara and Ramananda Raya, from the glories of chanting through humility and servitude to Radha's unconditional love. Krishnadasa then reviews every Antya-lila chapter and closes the book.
Antya-lila: the last years in Puri, Haridasa Thakura, Jagadananda, Raghunatha dasa, the Lord’s ecstasies and the Siksastaka prayers.

children.note: Two armies face each other. Seeing his own family on the other side, Arjuna loses heart and puts down his bow. 46 verses.
The blind king asks Sanjaya what his sons and the Pandavas did on the field of dharma.
Seeing kinsmen on both sides, his limbs shake, his mouth dries, his bow slips.
Overwhelmed by grief, he casts aside his bow and arrows in the chariot.

children.topic: Chapter 2 · Contents of the Gita Summarized
children.note: Krishna begins to teach. The soul is eternal; the body changes; duty must be done without attachment to results. 72 verses.
Confused about duty, Arjuna asks Krishna to instruct him.
As the soul passes through the changing body, so it passes into another body at death.

children.topic: The soul is never born, never dies
children.note: Unborn, eternal, ever-existing; it is not slain when the body is slain.
A person gives up old clothes for new; the soul gives up old bodies for new ones.

children.topic: Right to work, not to its fruits
children.note: Act as duty, never for the result, and never cling to inaction.
From attachment comes lust, from lust anger, from anger delusion and loss of memory.
What is night to the world is the time of waking for the self-controlled sage.

children.topic: Chapter 5 · Karma-yoga – Action in Krishna Consciousness
children.note: Renouncing work versus working in devotion; the second is easier and better. 29 verses.
Both renunciation and devoted work liberate, but devotional work is superior.

One who engages in full devotion at once transcends the modes and comes to the level of Brahman.

The living entities are eternal fragments of Krishna, struggling with the six senses including the mind.
From Krishna come remembrance, knowledge and forgetfulness; He is the knower and compiler of the Vedas.
Beyond the fallible and the infallible, He is celebrated as the Supreme Person.

maps.title: Gita Week — the teaching in one map

nodeData.topic: Gita Week — the teaching in one map
nodeData.note: Sri Gauranga Das's 7-day overview of the Bhagavad-gita As It Is, arranged by his own frame: why read it, Arjuna's crisis, the five truths (soul, work, the Lord, nature and the modes, time), the mind, knowledge and the guru, and devotion as the essence. Every bubble is a moment from the classes with its minute and a verbatim line; the link plays it. Tap Orbit for 3D; the story 'The Gita in 12 steps' is ready under ⋯ → Stories.

children.topic: The Gita is like an ocean
children.note: Like the ocean off Durban's beach, the Gita gets deeper the further you go in. Seven days can only be a brief overview, not an in-depth study. — "the Gita is like an ocean. You have a nice beach here in Durban, right? And so the ocean is very deep."

children.topic: Spoken by Krishna to Arjuna at Kurukshetra
children.note: The audience recalls the basics: Krishna spoke the Gita to Arjuna on the battlefield of Kurukshetra, 5,000 years ago. — "I'm just trying to remember who actually spoke the Gita. Can anyone help me with that? Krishna. Lord Krishna."

The one truly unique feature: the Gita gives fresh meaning every time you open it, at whatever level you are. — "But there is one very unique characteristic of the Gita and that is the Gita is alive."

children.topic: Gandhi: fresh joy from it every day
children.note: Gandhi's words from the book's back cover: when doubts and disappointments come, he found comfort in the Gita and new meaning daily. — "I turn to the Bhagat Gita and find your words to comfort me. And I immediately begin to smile in the midst of overwhelming sorrow."

children.topic: Open any page and find your answer
children.note: When something is bothering you, open the Gita anywhere and the answer will be there. — "open the Gita. Any page, anyhow. Not that you have to go to a specific chapter, you have to go to a specific page. No, just open it and you will actually find that the answer you're seeking is in those pages."

children.topic: Gita Mahatmya: why read the Gita
children.note: Prabhupada includes Shankaracharya's verses on the glories of the Gita; these give the reasons to read it. — "Shankar Achara was a great acharia for the adita school and he wrote on the Bhagat Gita. He wrote about the glories of the Gita."

children.topic: Choosing soap: why choose this book
children.note: Just as we pick soap by quality, fragrance and ingredients, the Mahatmya tells us the qualities that make the Gita worth choosing. — "Let's say you're buying some soap and then you have a whole bunch of options. There's many many types of soaps."

children.topic: Context is war, content is life
children.note: Though spoken on a battlefield, the Gita is about how to live, not about warfare. — "So the context is war but the content is life. It's all about life. It's not about war."

Mahatmya verse 1: following the Gita frees one from bhaya (fear) and shoka (lamentation) now, and gives a spiritual next life. — "If one properly follows the instructions of how to one can be free from all miseries and anxieties in this life and one's next life will be spiritual."

children.topic: Two kinds of punya: material and spiritual
children.note: Material piety takes you to heavenly planets; spiritual piety takes you out of the material world altogether. — "There is material puna and spiritual puna. So material puna puna means pious activities."

children.topic: Gita is the milk of the Vedas
children.note: Mahatmya verse 6: the Upanishads are the cow, Krishna the milker, Arjuna the calf, and the Gita is the milk for devotees to drink. — "Just like if the if you if they take the shape of a cow, then the essence of the cow is milk. And so Gita is that milk."

children.topic: One scripture, one God, one mantra, one work
children.note: Mahatmya verse 7: one scripture (Gita), one God (Krishna), one mantra (Hare Krishna) and one work (service to the Lord). — "Let there be one scripture only. One common scripture for the whole world."

children.topic: What aspect of my life needs clarity?
children.note: A reflection exercise: write down the one area of your life you want the Gita to clarify. — "If the Gita could clarify one aspect of my life today, what aspect would that be?"

Although the Gita holds all answers, they open only to someone submissive to Krishna and willing to accept him as the Supreme. — "there is a qualification that is needed and that qualification is submissiveness. We have to be submissive to the Lord."

All knowledge is online, but without a connection you cannot reach it; submissiveness is our connection to the Gita. — "in order to access that you need the internet connection isn't it without internet connection you cannot access Wikipedia so the same way"

The 18 chapters divide into three sets of six: karma yoga (1-6), bhakti yoga (7-12) and jnana yoga (13-18); the essence is kept in the middle. — "front cover of Bhagat Gita is the first six chapters and that is known as karm yoga. The back cover is the last six chapters that is known as ghani yoga. But the middle is known as bakti yoga."

children.topic: Medicine bottles packed in the middle
children.note: We hide what is precious in the middle of the suitcase; Krishna put bhakti, the essence, in the middle six chapters. — "If you're carrying some glass bottles of medicine or whatever in your suitcase, you don't keep it on the edge, right? You keep it in between"

The Gita deals with five subjects: prakriti (material nature), isvara (God), kala (time), karma (activities) and jiva (the soul). — "Priti means material nature. Ishwara. Ishwara means God. Kala Kala means time."
The fourth topic, karma, covers our activities and duties. — "karma means activities or prescribed duties."

children.topic: Four yogas: linking with the Supreme
children.note: Wherever the word yoga appears it means connecting with the Supreme; the Gita covers four kinds and its essence is bhakti. — "Yoga means connection or linking to the supreme."
When the linking process is mainly work or physical activity. — "requiring some action on our part then that is known as karma yoga."
When the process is empirical, working things out with the mind. — "We're trying to figure things out with our mental capacities. Then that process is known as ghana yoga"

children.topic: Bhakti yoga: I am your servant
children.note: Engaging with the Lord in a devotional mood of service. — "you are the supreme lord I am your servant and that's why I'm engaging in your service then that is known as baki yoga"

children.topic: Essence of the Gita is bhakti yoga
children.note: Of the four, devotion is the heart of the Gita. — "the essence of Bhagat Gita is actually bakti yoga."

children.topic: Arjuna: draw my chariot between the armies
children.note: Arjuna knew exactly who he would fight; he asked to see them to gauge how determined they were. — "This is in text 22 of chapter 1. He said, "Oh infallible one, please draw my chariot between the two armies so that I may see those present here who desire to fight"

No boxing match is advertised with an unknown opponent; Arjuna certainly knew his opponents. — "Muhammad Ali versus then a question mark. He'll know when he gets into the ring. Does that happen? No. So Arjuna didn't know who he was going to fight. He knew."
Like boxers staring each other down at the weigh-in, Arjuna wanted to read his cousins' faces. — "So Arjuna wanted to see how determined are my cousins to fight with me. He wanted to see their face."

children.topic: Bhishma: a devotee on the wrong side
children.note: Bhishma, a pure devotee with an unbeaten record, fought for Duryodhana because Krishna wanted to show that even the greatest lose on the wrong side. — "Bishma Dave is a devotey of the Lord. He he is a devotey of Krishna. Lord Krishna is the charioteer of Arjuna on the other side and he's on this side."

children.topic: On the wrong side, you lose
children.note: However great a person is, being on the wrong side means game over. — "even if you're as good as Bishma as powerful as Bishma on the battlefield if you're on the wrong side you're going to lose."

children.topic: Last verse: where Krishna and Arjuna are, victory
children.note: Dhritarashtra's real question was 'who will win?'; Sanjaya answers it in the Gita's final verse. — "wherever Lord Krishna and Arjuna are that party will win."

children.topic: Arjuna's bodily symptoms on seeing family
children.note: Instead of warriors, Arjuna sees grandfather, uncle, cousin, teacher; he breaks down with about nine physical symptoms. — "So in text 28 to 30 Arjuna he is describing what he's going through when he saw the opposite party."

children.topic: Krishna points out family, not warriors
children.note: Krishna cleverly reframed the enemy as relatives, and Arjuna's attachment took over. — ""Oh see there is your grandfather, there is your uncle, there is your cousin, there is your friend, right? There's your teacher.""

children.topic: Trembling, dry mouth, hair standing on end
children.note: The list read out: limbs curling, dry mouth, trembling, hair on end, bow slipping, skin burning, unable to stand, forgetting himself, seeing only misfortune. — "My mouth is drying up. My whole body is trembling. My hair are standing on end."

We all know Arjuna's breakdown: knowing the subject yet freezing when the exam paper is turned over. — "as soon as you flip the paper, you have a heart attack. You you you forget even what what the spelling of your own name is. Your pen is shaking."

Arjuna admits he has all his strength, skill and strategy but cannot use any of it; this miserly weakness is what he brings to Krishna. — "my lord I have been afflicted by karpa karpa dsha means miserly weakness"

A wealthy company owner who came to the temple in torn socks: a true story of having but not using. — "That's a miser miser. You have the ability, you have the facilities, you have the requirements, but you don't use them."
Gujaratis keeping the plastic wrap on a new remote: a lighter example of miserliness. — "they don't take out the plastic. No, it has to, you know, it has to remain perfect."

children.topic: Arjuna surrenders: I am your disciple
children.note: Not knowing what to do, Arjuna knew where to go; he surrendered to Krishna as a disciple and asked to be told what is best. — "I am your disciple shish and I am surrendered onto you I have come to you tell me what is best"

We want someone to say yes to our yes; Arjuna instead said 'I don't know, you tell me'. — "See nowadays when we go to people, we're looking for validation. We're not really looking for some advice or some guidance."

children.topic: Guru takes us from confusion to clarity
children.note: The Gita teaches that we need to approach a guru, someone in knowledge who can show the way. — "guru can take us out from confusion to clarity otherwise we remain in confusion"

children.topic: Take-home: when stuck, ask for help
children.note: The first lesson of the Gita and today's take-home: be intelligent enough to know you cannot figure it out alone. — "So when the problem is too big for us to solve, we should approach for help. Otherwise we get stuck."

Once Arjuna finally asks what to do, Krishna smiles and then tells him his arguments make no sense. — "And so Lord Krishna he smiled a little bit at first right it wasn't a very big smile and it wasn't a laugh also."

children.topic: Wise lament neither for living nor dead
children.note: The verse on the board: Krishna says Arjuna speaks learned words but grieves for what is not worth grieving. — "Therefore he's saying the wise lament neither for the living nor for the dead."

children.topic: In crisis we forget who we are
children.note: Seeing relatives on the other side, Arjuna lost sight of his identity and his duty. — "he went into lamentation he forgot who he was he forgot what he was supposed to do he forgot his identity"

children.topic: Like a student who thinks exam is everything
children.note: A student in an exam feels it is the end of the world and forgets there is more to them than being a student. — "and we discussed just like the student at that moment when They're sitting the exam."

children.topic: Arjuna: my illusion is gone, I will act
children.note: After knowledge, duty and devotion, Arjuna surrenders and declares he will do as Krishna says. Krishna consciousness means acting according to Krishna's desire. — "my illusion is gone. My illusion is finished. I know who I am now. I know I am supposed to do what you say."

children.topic: Surrender means doing what Krishna says
children.note: Surrender is not sitting and doing nothing; Krishna's desire is already stated: think of Me, become My devotee, worship, bow down. — "No surrender means you do as Krishna is saying."
Arjuna is not fighting in the ordinary sense; he is doing Krishna consciousness, taking action with no personal want. — "Win, lose, doesn't matter. Krishna said fight so I'm fighting."

Love is not lip service or forgotten birthdays; a mother gives the child milk, not the Fanta she wants. Krishna has said clearly what pleases Him, so no speculation. — "So love means we do something for someone in the way that they want it to be done."

Arjuna did not run away or stop fighting; the same activity continued but for Krishna instead of for himself. — "He surrendered torishna. The surrender to Krishna changed what? Tell the devotey next to you. What do you think changed? Consciousness."

children.topic: Radio station WIFM: what's in it for me
children.note: Everyone is tuned to this station; Arjuna entered the battle asking what he would get and saw only dead relatives and sin. He then switched it off for what does Krishna want. — "It's called W I FM. Has anybody heard of it? W I FM? It's called What's in it for me?"

children.topic: Don't remove anything, just add Krishna
children.note: Arjuna came to fight and simply added Krishna; then there was victory, peace and happiness. — "Krishna consciousness or path of devotional service is not no no no no no. It's just add Krishna plus Krishna."

children.topic: You are the soul, not the body
children.note: This is Krishna's first instruction in the Gita: remember your real identity. — "Lord Krishna immediately starts by reminding Arjuna who he is and he says you are the soul not the body."

children.topic: Krishna speaks of the soul only once
children.note: These key verses in Chapter 2 are the only place the Gita describes the soul; Arjuna understood in one shot. — "Lord Krishna speaks about the soul only once in the Gita. You will not find any information about the soul later on."

The father's body is lying right there, yet the child says he is gone; what has gone is the soul. — "there was a small child crying and [snorts] a sadhu was walking there and the sadhu asked him my dear child why are you crying"

The body itself is always dead matter; it moves only because the soul is present. — "so the difference between a living body and a dead body is consciousness. Actually the body is dead. See what moves the body is the soul."

children.topic: iPhone without a battery is useless
children.note: The phone is the body, the battery is the soul; however good the phone, without the battery it does nothing. — "can be the best iPhone but there's no battery inside it's useless isn't it? So the same way the body may be very strong, maybe very attractive but if there's no soul inside the body then it is useless."
Our own language already admits that the body is a possession, separate from the self. — "We don't say I hand we don't say I ear right we say my hand my ear my body we don't say I body."

children.topic: Soul passes from boyhood to youth to old age
children.note: The body is a container; the same person passes through changing bodies and at death into another one. — "The soul passes from boyhood to youth to old age, right? I'm sure we all have family albums"

children.topic: Old photos: 'where did the hair go?'
children.note: Family albums show totally different bodies, yet everyone knows it is the same person. — "This was you. Where did the hair disappear? [laughter] And you're like, yeah, yeah, that was me."

children.topic: Soul cannot be destroyed, body cannot be saved
children.note: Two conclusions of the seers of truth; Arjuna wanted to save bodies that can never be saved. — "One soul can never be destroyed. And number two, the body can never be saved."

children.topic: If no one kills them, time will
children.note: No amount of gym or diet buys a guaranteed extension; every body must be destroyed by time. — "And even if someone else doesn't kill them, time will kill them. No matter how strong you are, how much gym hours you put in"

Old clothes are the old body; death is only a change of dress for the soul, which is never born and never dies. — "Just like we change old clothes and we put on new clothes, the soul similarly accepts new bodies after giving up old ones."

children.topic: No weapon can cut, burn, drown or dry the soul
children.note: Krishna speaks to the warrior in Arjuna's own language: no physical or elemental weapon can touch the soul. — "that the soul cannot be cut. That means no shastra can work acuh to the soul cannot be burnt cannot be drowned cannot be dried up by the wind."

Arjuna knew both kinds of weapon, so the analogy of cutting, burning and drowning was tailored to him. — "So astra means it's elemental. Shastra means it's physical, right? Like swords and maces. These are shastras."

children.topic: The soul can never be killed. Full stop.
children.note: Krishna's last words on the soul in the Gita; no lamentation is needed for any living being. — "He says the soul can never be killed. Full stop. Right? And therefore you do not need to lament for any living being."

children.topic: Moving house: nobody laments the old one
children.note: Grandfathers and teachers leave old bodies for new ones, an upgrade; it is cause for happiness, not grief. — "So, they had a one-bedroom house, they'll get a two or a three, right? So, nobody laments, oh, why did you leave your old house?"

children.topic: Say it to your neighbour: body never alive, soul ever alive
children.note: The two-sentence conclusion each listener repeats to the devotee beside them. — "the bad news is body never alive. Body is dead. It's never alive. But the good news is soul is ever alive. Soul never dies."

Every body, human, animal or plant, goes through the same six changes; whatever is born must die. — "Birth, growth, stay for some time, produce byproducts, dwindle and then die. So everybody goes through this"

children.topic: A flower: bud, bloom, seed, wither
children.note: The flower shows all six transformations in miniature. — "Take a flower for example. It's in a bud form, then it blooms. Once it blooms, it stays for some time, then it starts producing a seed."

children.topic: After death, birth again: a cycle
children.note: Birth and death repeat; the cycle is no reason to lament or abandon duty. — "But then he's saying after death there's also birth. So this is a cycle and he's telling Arjuna you should not be disturbed by this cycle."

children.topic: If not the body, why do we suffer?
children.note: The answer drawn from the audience: because of the senses and because of attachment to the body. — "But then if we know this, why do we still suffer? If I go and slap someone, will they feel pain? But they're not the body."

children.topic: BMW hit on the highway: 'why did you hit me?'
children.note: The car stands for the body; nothing touched us, but attachment makes us feel every dent as pain. — "why did you hit me? Isn't it? Why did you hit me? He didn't hit you. He hit the car."

children.topic: Street kids vs your own kid
children.note: We ignore many street children but suffer for our own; the only difference is bodily relation and attachment. — "But if your kid ends up in the street, what happens? It's a lot of pain, isn't it?"

children.topic: Body is the field, soul the knower
children.note: Arjuna asks about kshetra and kshetrajna; Krishna answers that the body is a field of activities and the soul living inside it is the knower of that field. — "this body or son of counti is called the field and one who knows this body is called the knower of the field"

children.topic: Dehi: the one who lives in the body
children.note: The soul is the dweller, the body the dwelling; this distinction has run through all the earlier chapters. — "Dehi means one who lives in Deha. Deha is body. So the soul lives in the body."

Just as a farmer knows his own farm but not others', the soul knows its own body: its pains and pleasures, not those of the person beside it. — "But you as a farmer you know right here I've planted carrots. Here I've planted peas. Here I've planted some beans."

children.topic: We are imperfect knowers even of ourselves
children.note: We know we are sick but not why; we do not know how food becomes blood or how many hairs are on our head. Our knowledge of our own field is partial. — "we ate the food we got food poisoning do we know what exactly caused the food poisoning we can't know"

children.topic: Eternal fragmental parts, struggling in the modes
children.note: The living entities are Krishna's eternal parts, but conditioned by the modes they struggle with the mind and senses. — "mango mame wango means you are my part you and I are connected we we are so connected with the lord even though we are here he is with us"

Conditioning has engineered us into something we are not; the Gita is Krishna's mercy to undo it. This is not our natural place. — "Is reverse engineering. We have been engineered into something we are not. So but Lord Krishna is giving the knowledge by which we can reverse engineer come out right."

Arjuna asks why fight if bodies die anyway; Krishna answers that nobody can avoid work. — "Lord Krishna is saying to Arjuna, everyone has to work. Everyone is forced to work. There was uh I also do you know sessions"

children.topic: Nobody can sit still for two minutes
children.note: If we cannot stay idle for two minutes, giving up work altogether is impossible. — "just sit still for 2 minutes and I've even tried this with adults. 2 minutes people they they go crazy."

children.topic: Marshmallow experiment: mind on the object
children.note: Children who did not touch the marshmallow still thought of it constantly; not acting while dwelling on sense objects is pretending. — "And after like 4 minutes or so, most of them just ended up eating it."
Renouncing action before the heart is purified is a show; better to work. — "If you artificially stop your activities when that purification has not happened then it is called pretention."

children.topic: Yoga: duty without attachment to results
children.note: Arjuna's refusal to fight is itself an attachment; real yoga is doing prescribed work equipoised in success and failure. — "perform your duty equipoed abandoning All attachment to success and failure that is called yoga."

children.topic: Nobody sits an exam hoping to fail
children.note: Exams and interviews show how naturally we are attached to results; even Arjuna found this hard. — "Did anyone go and sit the exam and say it doesn't matter if I pass or fail?"

children.topic: Four results: no reaction, indifference to Vedas, no birth-death, samadhi
children.note: Working without expecting results brings freedom from reaction, from ritual, from rebirth, and leads to trance. — "Number two you become indifferent to the vedas. Whatever has been said, whatever has been written, it doesn't make a difference. Number three, there is no birth and no death."

children.topic: Musk and Buffett: working not for the money
children.note: The billionaire still going to work is a picture of acting where the result is not the motive. — "that someone like Jeff Bezos or Alon Musk they go to work it's not for the money whether the money is there or not there it's really makes no difference"

children.topic: Confectioner surrounded by sweets, no craving
